Spearman's conventional t test and Kendall's normal approximation are asymptotically invalid, with rejection probabilities tending to one under process independence.

title: Dynamic Shaping: Acquiring Interfaces and Constructing Execution over Frozen Pretrained Components
abstract: We introduce Dynamic Shaping, a method for constructing executable neural arrangements through acquired response and partial-derivative interfaces over frozen pretrained components. The method learns local descriptions of available computation, ranks component rebindings using task-gradient alignment, transports the current interface across a rebinding, and retains changes through behavioral feedback. Continuous interface acquisition uses proximal policy optimization; the source coefficients remain fixed. We derive an exact identity relating transport error in component responses and partials to changes in action logits and their sensitivities. A pixels-only ViZDoom Basic study evaluates first task acquisition without a competent reference controller, demonstrations or intact response targets. Across three initializations and 100 shared held-out game seeds, initial arrangements succeed on 86/300 controller/episode pairs; joint interface-and-binding construction succeeds on 295/300. Fixed-binding interface acquisition also reaches 295/300. Each policy executes four source fragments, with 110 acquired interface values and fixed random visual and action projections. The artifact includes all candidate trials, interventions and costs; all 1,200 recorded initial/retained outcomes replay exactly. The contribution is an explicit profile, rebind, transport and retain procedure and a reproducible reference-free acquisition case over frozen pretrained computation.

title: ExtremeDrive: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Critical Driving
abstract: Existing autonomous driving datasets and benchmarks provide extensive resources for routine driving, yet real-world data covering safety-critical scenarios and extreme environmental conditions remain limited. To address this gap, we present ExtremeDrive, a real-world dataset and benchmark covering emergency maneuvers, complex traffic interactions, and adverse conditions such as slippery or snow-covered roads, alongside routine driving. The dataset comprises 589 driving scenes curated from a larger pool of real-world driving recordings, with calibrated and aligned multisensor data and reviewed annotations of road structure and traffic participants. We further establish a benchmark to evaluate planned trajectories through simulated vehicle execution, measuring safety-related metrics and driving performance. Experiments at equal training set sizes show that incorporating critical driving data reduces trajectory prediction errors and improves mean critical-success rates in critical scenarios. ExtremeDrive provides a unified resource for learning and evaluating autonomous driving in safety-critical scenarios and extreme environmental conditions.

title: PerturbJEPA: Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning of Cellular Perturbation Responses
abstract: Identifying the drug and dose that produced a cellular response requires preserving treatment effects within each cellular background. A joint-embedding predictor can match its targets while ignoring the intervention if its encoder preserves differences across backgrounds but erases differences between treated and control populations within each one. We call this failure interventional contrast collapse. PerturbJEPA encodes the difference in mean gene expression between treated and control populations as an effect vector. It aligns the displacement between their latent centroids with this vector and regularizes the vectors to preserve variation across population pairs. We show that the measured displacements cannot all coincide within a batch when effect-vector variation exceeds the root-mean-square alignment error. Trained with separate drug and dose ranking objectives, the model predicts candidate responses from a common control population and matches them to the observed response without cell pairing or expression reconstruction. We evaluate 3,592 Tahoe-100M queries on held-out combinations of known interventions and cellular backgrounds, each with over 700 drug-dose candidates in a fixed, background-specific catalog. PerturbJEPA achieves 91.46% macro joint drug-dose Recall@1, exceeding STATE by 3.40 percentage points (95% drug-cluster bootstrap interval of 1.72 to 5.07 points). Controlled diagnostics show that treatment-control differences can shrink even when representations remain globally dispersed. With the drug ranking objective fixed, adding effect-vector regularization to alignment raises joint Recall@1 from 18.57% to 87.47%.

title: Partial Borrows in Rust
abstract: Rust ensures memory safety by requiring exclusive access to mutably borrowed data. However, a borrow can prevent access to more data than necessary. For example, a method with an &mut self parameter borrows the entire struct, even when the method uses only some of its fields. Calling the method can therefore conflict with an existing borrow of a field the method never uses, causing Rust to reject the program. Resolving such conflicts can require programmers to compromise useful abstractions, make non-local changes to their programs, or worse, resort to unsafe code. We introduce view types, a backward-compatible refinement of reference types that specifies which fields a reference may access. This allows methods to partially borrow a struct, accessing only the fields they need without blocking access to the rest. We establish the first fully mechanized foundation for Aeneas in Rocq. Along the way, we uncover and fix gaps in the original semantics and proofs. Building on this foundation, we formalize partial borrows and prove the extended borrow checking sound. We implement view types in rustc and extend the Aeneas interpreter to support partial borrows. Our evaluation shows how view types systematically resolve borrowing conflicts across method boundaries at no runtime cost.

title: Global Strong Solutions and Large-Time Behavior for the Two-Dimensional Compressible Flow with General Bulk Viscosity
abstract: The global existence of a unique strong solution to the two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations with general density-dependent bulk viscosity is established for large initial data allowing vacuum. Both the periodic problem and the Cauchy problem with far-field vacuum are considered under a common logarithmic derivative bound and growth condition on the viscosity primitive. A time-independent density upper bound and uniform low-order estimates are obtained in both domains. The admissible coefficients include every superlinear power law and near-linear laws with logarithmic gains. Exponential relaxation to the positive equilibrium is proved in the periodic setting. In the whole space, uniform relaxation toward vacuum and algebraic decay of the pressure, velocity gradient, material acceleration, and relative kinetic energy are established.

title: The 1/4-power law for bounded variation of wall turbulence from the Kármán-Howarth equation
abstract: By applying the Kármán-Howarth (KH) equation to turbulent channel flows, we derive the $1/4$-power bounded laws for the peak dissipation and the normalized mean-square streamwise velocity fluctuation. The analysis requires two additional inputs, both standard in the study of turbulent wall flows: the logarithmic mean velocity profile and the near-isotropy of the spatial velocity derivatives. Self-similarity of KH equation yields, for the profile of the mean-square streamwise velocity, the form $c_1 - c_2 (y/δ)^{1/4}$ in the overlap region (Chen and Sreenivasan, 2023), where $δ$ is the half-channel height; it also provides the basis for constructing self-similar profiles for high-order moments of streamwise velocity (Chen and Sreenivasan, 2025). Furthermore, the analysis yields the form $c_1' - c_2' Re^{-1/4}_τ$ for the inner peak of the streamwise mean-square velocity (Chen and Sreenivasan, 2022), and a similar bounded relation for a characteristic wall dissipation (Chen and Sreenivasan, 2021).

title: Language Models Meet Vibration Testing for LEO Constellation Satellites with Calibrated Response Prediction from Few-show Sweeps
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly drive engineering analysis end to end, turning textual records into the inputs of numerical programs, but a plausible and wrong value can pass silently into a decision. We propose deterministic validation gates for LLM-driven engineering analysis, a general paradigm in which a typed configuration produced by LLMs is consumed only after it passes deterministic checks on units, physical consistency, verbatim quotes, agreement between independent models, consistency with measurement exports and the applicability of trained models. The gates target hallucinations from two directions, since quote checking catches fabricated content while agreement between models catches errors of omission that quote checking misses. We instantiate the paradigm on sine vibration acceptance testing for low Earth orbit mega-constellation satellites, where DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Qwen-plus read Chinese test records and extract a configuration of 76 fields. Fact-level F1 ranged from 0.98 to 1.0 on five input variants, with all repairs frozen on development inputs and evaluated on held-out inputs. With all gates, 20 of 20 configurations produced notching results bit for bit identical to the gold run, and all 17 real and injected errors in consumed fields were stopped, of which 16 would have run without gates. Retraining the bound model on a dataset built from an LLM configuration reproduced its results within GPU nondeterminism. We also report a negative result of practical value. Direct LLM curve forecasting only matches linear extrapolation, whereas a small physics-structured network reduces the over-notched bandwidth by 86% to 89% at calibrated coverage c = 0.90, which delineates where direct LLM prediction should give way to a trained model.

title: multiCAsp: Spatially Informed Canonical Association Analysis of Multi-Omic Data
abstract: Simultaneous profiling of multiple molecular layers at spatially resolved locations creates opportunities to identify shared cross-modal biological variation in its tissue context. We present multiCAsp (multi-omic Canonical Association informed by spatial graph), a probabilistic latent-factor model for integrating $M \geq 2$ spatially resolved omic modalities. It incorporates spatial dependence through a graph-Laplacian prior on shared latent factors and uses an expectation-maximization algorithm to estimate factor scores and modality-specific feature loadings. Because the prior is defined on a neighborhood graph rather than on Euclidean distances, it accommodates irregular tissue geometries and extends naturally to multiple tissue sections. Simulations show that multiCAsp consistently achieves higher mean latent subspace and loading recovery than alternative methods across varying sample sizes, feature dimensions, and noise levels, with the largest gains under high noise. Compared with an existing Gaussian process-based spatial factor model, it is also less sensitive to how the spatial coordinates are represented, produces spatially smoother factors, and has lower computational cost. Applied to metabolomic-proteomic data from macaque cortex and gene-protein data from human renal carcinoma, multiCAsp recovers spatially coherent multi-omic factors with interpretable biological signatures. In the macaque data, transferred factors retain broad spatial patterns across animals and support cross-modal prediction of protein abundances from metabolomic measurements.

title: Relaxation Critical Dynamics of Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking
abstract: Strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB) is unique to mixed states: strong symmetry is broken while weak symmetry is preserved, requiring two order parameters. We study the critical relaxation of both order parameters in a monitored $\mathbb{Z}_2$ circuit, which maps exactly onto two nested bond-percolation problems. The initial state acts as a temporal boundary condition for each problem, wired if the state is ordered in the corresponding order parameter and free otherwise. An SW-SSB initial state wires only the strong-symmetry order parameter, a configuration that no pure state realizes. Each autocorrelation exponent is the sum of an initial scaling dimension, set by the initial state, and an observation dimension, set by the observation time, whereas the equal-time correlator gives only the observation dimension. For the SW-SSB state, the initial dimension is $1/3$ for the weak-symmetry order parameter and $0$ for the strong-symmetry one, each at its own critical point. These initial dimensions also set how fast a stored bit is lost. The probability of decoding the initial value of a single qubit from the system alone decays as a power law, whereas system and environment together retain it. Stabilizer simulations confirm the theoretical prediction, and we propose an experimental protocol that measures these exponents without postselection. Our results reveal a form of boundary criticality inaccessible to pure states.

title: SCoRe: Support-Calibrated Role Fusion for Training-Free Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation
abstract: We present SCoRe (Support-Calibrated Role fusion), a framework to utilize two complementary vision foundation model-based (VFM) segmenters for training-free cross-domain few-shot segmentation (CD-FSS). Our approach is based on the observation that current VFMs for CD-FSS possess capabilities where one model locates the correct object, while another model computes the better contour. Our approach uses: 1. a method to identify a VFM segmenter to lead Few-Shot Segmentation (FSS) task for a given concept, 2. a novel deterministic boundary correction method using bands of near- and far-pixels at the lead segmenter's predicted boundary of an object, and 3. a region correction mechanism for the other segmenter to conservatively prune components, fill holes, and bridge short gaps on the lead segmenter's predicted masks to improve accuracy. We evaluate SCoRe using RSRM and FSS-SAM3 across 3,314 matched five-shot episodes from 10 datasets. SCoRe achieves 72.738% foreground mIoU averaged across datasets, a gain of 5.210 percentage points over RSRM (paired 95% CI [4.618, 5.972]), with per-dataset gains up to 8.461 points over the strongest standalone method and the best point estimate on 7 of 10 datasets.

title: State-Machine Governance of Adaptive Enforcement: Evidence from a Paired-Scenario Evaluation
abstract: AI-assisted security systems can recommend rapid policy changes, but governing their execution requires explicit authorization, evidence, and recovery rules. This study evaluated a machine-verifiable, state-machine-governed transition procedure implemented in ZTGuard using 36 matched scripted scenarios and deterministic vendor-connector simulations. Each pair held the starting state, telemetry, AI recommendation, and scheduled vendor condition constant. The sole dependent variable, Control, was the equal-weight mean of traceability, accountability, audit-chain completeness, and reliable rollback capability. Mean Control was 0.720 (SD = 0.218) for the scripted operator-driven baseline and 0.972 (SD = 0.131) for the governed procedure. A two-tailed paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test yielded V = 359, p < .001, with a matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation of .899. Twenty-six pairs favored treatment, nine were tied, and one favored baseline. The findings support controlled artifact utility, not production readiness. Interpretation is limited by purposive sampling, scripted operators, simulated connectors, overlapping components, and arm-specific scoring rules.

title: A Self-Evolving Agent Runs Like a Gas: Describing and Predicting Its Evolution with Fluid Dynamics
abstract: A self-evolving LLM agent improves in service by rewriting its own plugin library under a validation gate. Agent engineering is converging on exactly such agents: single systems in continuous operation, carrying populations of runtime instances (plugins, skills, tools) past the point where anyone can read the library and still predict what the system will do. Yet the run itself, the aggregate motion of that population across hundreds of edit rounds, is unstudied: no theory says whether it relaxes, oscillates, or freezes. A recent kinetic theory supplies the missing level: under four architectural properties, the plugin instances of one agent behave as identical hard spheres whose density obeys a master equation, and the theory is candid that its gate injects and drains credit, momentum is not conserved, and waves are excluded by construction. We argue the boundary is architectural; keeping the four safety theorems, we stack conservation axioms on top. A closed-credit ledger makes credit a collision invariant and unlocks acoustic waves at a measurable, engineerable speed; a zero-sum projection gate conserves centroid momentum unconditionally, for any proposal stream. Both layers are proven and executed: the axis total is conserved to the digit over 66 interventions under a live gate, and the pre-registered decisive probe returns the theory's directional verdict: linear wavefronts where the ledger holds, dissipation where it does not, replicated across two population sizes. For agents that must never stop, the gas description is not a metaphor: it is the measurement interface through which their future becomes readable.

title: Scaling a Universal Graph Neural Network Force Field to Billions of Atoms on Desk-Side GPUs
abstract: Machine-learning force fields are capable of simulating billions of atoms, but usually require high-performance supercomputing clusters. We show that a universal graph neural network force field, ALIGNN-FF, evaluates energies and forces of more than one billion atoms on desk-side computers such as the NVIDIA GB10, which has 128 GB of unified memory, by using a cube-and-halo decomposition. The halo contains every atom within the model's 20 Å receptive field, which makes the result exact. One GB10 holds 216,000 atoms with forces as a single graph. The cube-and-halo decomposition removes this limit, enabling an evaluation of 2 billion atoms on nine GB10s. We also demonstrate three case studies: a billion-atom polycrystal, a 102-million-atom microelectronic gate stack and a 1.07-million-atom satellite tobacco mosaic virus in water. This brings single-point evaluations at experimentally relevant sizes within reach of one research group. The code is available at: https://github.com/atomgptlab/scalingmat.

title: $G$-Hilbert schemes of canonical abelian quotient threefolds
abstract: Ishida and Iwashita showed that the canonical abelian quotient singularities of dimension three that are not Gorenstein fall into four families. For the two families that have not been treated before, we extend a method of Kędzierski and compute the toric charts of the $G$-Hilbert scheme explicitly. As a result, we show that the $G$-Hilbert scheme has at worst conifold singularities. Combined with known results, this shows that for every three-dimensional canonical abelian quotient singularity, the $G$-Hilbert scheme has at worst conifold singularities, every essential divisor over the singularity appears on it as a prime divisor, and its limit F-blowup is a resolution of the singularity. These results also hold for every three-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial canonical toric singularity in any characteristic, if we replace the $G$-Hilbert scheme by the limit F-blowup of the singularity.

title: Stability Principle Inherent in Wheel Gait of Planar X-shaped Walker Generated Using Constant Torque Drive and Mechanical Stoppers
abstract: Since the late 19th century when the first walking toys were developed, it has been known that mechanical stoppers at the hip joint are crucial for generating stable passive dynamic walking. Recent research on passive-dynamic and limit-cycle walkers has also confirmed that mechanical stoppers at the hip and knee joints are effective for generating stable walking motion, but theoretical research on how this mechanical constraint enhances the overall gait stability remains insufficient. This paper introduces a planar X-shaped walker equipped with mechanical stoppers at the hip joint, and investigates the effect of the mechanical constraint on the stability of the wheel gait generated by constant torque drive on a downslope. By simply falling forward while using the stoppers to constrain itself to the target impact posture, the robot can generate a highly stable wheel gait. We divide the motion of one step into four phases, derive approximate analytical solutions for the state error transition function matrix in each phase using a linearized model, and analyze the increase or decrease in the state error norm using metrics such as its maximum singular value. Numerical simulations demonstrate that while two phases are unstable in terms of the increase in the state error norm, the remaining two phases are stable, resulting in overall asymptotic stability.

title: Doubly strange tetraquark as a $KK^*$ virtual state: quark-model study with harmonic traps
abstract: We extract hadron--hadron scattering information from quark-level interactions using an artificial harmonic trap and a four-quark basis that includes both meson--meson and compact diquark--antidiquark configurations. Combining the Busch--Englert--Rzażewski--Wilkens formula with the effective range expansion (ERE), we determine phase shifts, scattering lengths, effective ranges, and pole positions from the trapped spectrum. We control uncertainties from basis truncation, finite trap frequencies, truncation of ERE, and quark-model parameters. The extracted $DD^*$ and $BB^*$ binding energies agree with direct calculations, providing benchmarks. For the doubly strange $T_{ss}$ with $I(J^P)=0(1^+)$, we predict a $KK^*$ virtual-state pole about 30--35~MeV below threshold in the stable-$K^*$ approximation. Both the AL1 model and its modified version that better reproduces the measured $T_{cc}^+$ binding energy yield this result. This finding differs from earlier predictions of a bound state and motivates searches for the $T_{ss}$ at facilities such as the High Intensity heavy Ion Accelerator Facility (HIAF). This framework could be extended to other hadron-hadron channels to extract scattering observables and pole positions.

title: Beyond Marginal Risk: ESG and Multidimensional Fragility in Equity Markets
abstract: Do ESG characteristics provide financial resilience beyond conventional risk, and is that inference stable to the financial state and ESG score being measured? We study a point-in-time panel of nonfinancial S&P 500 constituents from January 2019 through November 2025. Once ex ante return, volatility, and liquidity exposures are modeled explicitly, the broad downside-resilience pattern attenuates and none of the three primary marginal ESG $\times$ Down tests survives Holm adjustment under either conventional or wild-cluster-bootstrap inference. A post-primary exact decomposition then shows that the negative Return+RVOL coefficient is almost entirely allocated to observations that also breach the CHL trading-cost tail, while the mutually exclusive Return+RVOL-only component is essentially zero. Finally, a paired standardized comparison on an identical sample shows that MSCI's downstream Industry Adjusted Score and upstream Weighted Average Key Issue Score imply materially different fitted associations in adverse market states: at a 5% market decline, the difference is about one probability percentage point per score standard deviation. Sector-time, leave- one-month-out, and observed-change timing diagnostics preserve most of this contrast, although the result remains exploratory and inference is sensitive to multiplicity and market-state support. The evidence therefore favors a narrower interpretation of ESG resilience: the apparent association weakens once conventional risk is modeled, while the remaining relation depends on both the adverse state and the MSCI score field used to represent ESG.

title: A widely-tunable printed-circuit-board-based resonant electro-optic modulator
abstract: We present a simple, printed-circuit-board (PCB)-based resonant electro-optic modulator (EOM) featuring a wide operational frequency range. By utilizing a low-loss, high-frequency variable capacitor, the resonant frequency can be continuously tuned by typically 30% within a single band, e.g., from 161.0 MHz to 233.5 MHz. Furthermore, by swapping a radio-frequency transformer, the EOM's resonance is reconfigurable across the 17.7-489.7 MHz range, with quality factors ranging from 46 to 109. Using this design, we demonstrate the EOM's applicability by generating strong 228 MHz sidebands to verify its utility for ^6Li laser cooling and by locking a 780 nm laser to the Rb D2 transition using retroreflected modulation transfer spectroscopy at 20 MHz resonance. The device's reconfigurable wide frequency range and high quality factors make this EOM versatile for laser cooling of multiple atomic species, including ^6Li, ^39K, and ^41K, as well as for laser frequency locking. This design offers a flexible, robust, and practical solution for undergraduate teaching laboratories and quantum optics research groups.

title: GPRidge: Gaussian-process Accelerated Calculations of Minimum Energy Paths and First-order Saddle Points
abstract: GPRidge, a Gaussian-process (GP) library for accelerating calculations of minimum energy paths and first-order saddle points with compiled-language and Python bindings, is presented. An evaluation controller uses GP predictions to iteratively adjust the Cartesian coordinates of the atoms. The fitted GP energy surface and measured energies and forces pass from the path calculation to local refinement of the saddle point. New evaluations improve the surrogate and check the candidate geometry. For the molecular calculations, acceptance requires measured-force convergence and an independent Hessian with only one negative eigenvalue. A second negative eigenvalue triggers an escape and renewed refinement. The controller supports a joint inverse-distance GP for molecules and local GP residuals on periodic systems. Applications to the 24 Baker-Chan and 20 Birkholz-Schlegel molecular reactions using the Universal Model for Atoms (UMA-S-1.1), and to 72 Pt heptamer and island rearrangements on Pt(111) using a Morse potential, are presented. On matched Baker-Chan reactions, GPRidge uses 7.8- and 7.0-fold fewer energy-and-force evaluations than climbing-image nudged elastic band (CI-NEB) and off-path climbing-image nudged elastic band (OCI-NEB), respectively, reducing validation-inclusive CI-NEB time by 41%. All 20 Birkholz-Schlegel saddle points pass the independent index-one check, compared with 17 for the classical dimer method started from the same path maxima; on those 17 reactions, the GP dimer stage uses 6.4-fold fewer evaluations. All 72 Pt(111) paths meet the OptBench force criterion, with median evaluation counts of 30 and 23 for the heptamer and island problems, against 778 and 443 for CI-NEB.

title: Distribution of Primes in Galois Extensions of Global Fields with Explicit Constant Terms
abstract: We study the distribution of primes among Frobenius conjugacy classes in finite Galois extensions of global fields. In earlier work, the author and Koyama proved that the existence and nonvanishing of the limit of partial Euler products on the critical line for Artin $L$-functions (the Deep Riemann Hypothesis (A), or DRH(A)) are equivalent to an asymptotic formula for weighted prime counting functions with an unspecified constant term. In this article, we prove that a refined asymptotic formula is equivalent to the full version of DRH, namely the convergence of the Euler products on the critical line (DRH(A)) and the determination of their limiting values (DRH(B)). Here, the constant term is given explicitly in terms of the residue of the zeta function, central derivatives of Artin $L$-functions, ramified primes, and higher prime-power contributions.

title: JEPTERA: A Platform Agnostic JEPA-Assisted Model Predictive Planner for Urban UAV Navigation
abstract: Urban navigation for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) requires planning that accounts for environmental geometry, vehicle dynamics, and moving obstacles. This paper presents JEPTERA, a navigation architecture that integrates a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA), Model Predictive Control (MPC), PID control, and a safety layer. JEPA predicts the UAV's motion response to candidate commands for MPC action selection, while the safety layer checks trajectories against occupied space and predicted obstacle motion. Simulator adapters and platform-specific YAML configurations separate the planning core from simulator interfaces. An ablation study evaluated six configurations across three gym scenarios, totaling 180 runs. The complete architecture achieved the highest aggregate success rate, completing 28 of 30 runs. Additional tests completed one route across three city maps without collisions. Separate integration tests demonstrated operation in Gazebo/ROS 2, MuJoCo, and CARLA without modifying the core planning logic. These results support the feasibility of the integrated architecture for simulated urban UAV navigation and its portability across simulator interfaces.

title: Experience: ENTRAP - An IaC Enterprise Cyber Range for Reproducible Security Assessment and Dataset Generation
abstract: An enterprise breach causes most of its damage after the perimeter is crossed. Once an attacker gains a foothold, they can move laterally to other hosts, take over the trusted services of the network, and encrypt the backups needed for recovery. Defenders, on the other hand, need to study this post-compromise stage, but they cannot rehearse it on a production enterprise network. Building such an enterprise network manually is time-consuming, and resetting it to its clean state between runs is still harder. As a result, security experiments are difficult to perform, compare and reproduce. We develop Enterprise Network Testbed for Reproducible Attack and Defense Practices (ENTRAP), an Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) cyber range that defines a fully segmented enterprise as version-controlled automation. ENTRAP uses Ansible, KVM/Libvirt, and Cloud-init to provision the environment and reset it to a clean state whenever necessary. The enterprise network includes several entities such as a gateway, an internal Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), DNS, DHCP, a backup server, a web server, and clients. On this network, a user can learn to assemble the entities, launch attacks, and write rules or defensive measures that harden its security. We launch three attacks: a Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS)-backed ransomware campaign, a Layer-2 DHCP starvation and rogue DHCP attack, and perimeter web exploitation. Each attack runs from a clean state, and ENTRAP acts as a reproducible generator of labeled attack datasets. Using the collected dataset, we train a Random Forest classifier for ransomware detection and present its evaluation results. We publicly release the codebase, collected logs, and datasets to facilitate further research.

title: Invariant-Aware Harness Enforcement to Protect LLM Agents from Silent API Failures
abstract: LLM agents answer questions by calling APIs and trusting the results. An API can fail silently. It ignores part of a request, such as a misnamed filter, yet returns HTTP 200 and a plausible but wrong result. Current fixes, such as checklists, reviewer models and LLM judges, ask the model to catch it. But models often see the problem and answer anyway. We present SilentGuard, which moves the decision from the model to the harness running tool calls. It tests each result against invariants that any correct API must satisfy and withholds values that break one. We find silent failures in 11 of 15 public research APIs, with counts inflated up to 691 times. Current fixes leave over 70% of answers wrong, and agents report 77.4% of counts a judge flags. Across 7 open models, SilentGuard cuts wrong answers on its target faults from 74.0% to 1.7%, with no loss on fault-free tasks. On three frontier models they fall from 70.2% to 0.5%. A warning from the same check leaves 70.1% wrong, so enforcement is the key. On new fault types, the harness alone cuts wrong answers from 61.1% to 24.5%. It avoids wrong answers by abstaining rather than recovering.

title: Finite-time blowup in a one-dimensional magnetohydrodynamics model
abstract: We prove finite-time blowup of both the velocity and magnetic field in a one-dimensional magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) model starting from smooth odd initial data. The construction combines the dynamical rescaling approach with weighted stability estimates. Both the velocity and magnetic field remain in $L^2$ before the blowup time.

title: Solutions concentrating on spheres for Hamiltonian elliptic systems with supercritical growth
abstract: We study positive solutions of the singularly perturbed Hamiltonian elliptic system \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} -\varepsilon^2Δu+u=|v|^{q-2}v &\text{in }A,\\ -\varepsilon^2Δv+v=|u|^{p-2}u &\text{in }A,\\ u,v>0\text{ in }A,\qquad u=v=0 &\text{on }\partial A, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $A=\{x\in\mathbb R^{2m}:a<|x|<b\}$, $0<a<b$, $m\geq2$, and $2<p,q<2(m+1)/(m-1)$. We prove the existence of a family of solutions whose two components concentrate around the same $(m-1)$-dimensional sphere on the inner boundary as $\varepsilon\to0$. The two spheres of maxima are at distance $o(\varepsilon)$ from each other, and both components decay exponentially away from these spheres. The admissible range of $(p,q)$ includes critical and supercritical exponent pairs in dimension $2m$. The proof uses a reduction to a weighted system in dimension $m+1$. We establish foliated Schwarz symmetry of its ground states with a common axis via reduction by inversion and polarization. A uniform estimate on generalized Nehari fibers gives the upper energy bound. A half-space nonexistence result and the corresponding lower bound then determine the concentration location and the limiting profiles.

title: Neural Operator Approximation for Yau--Yau Nonlinear Filtering: Stability, Approximation, and Fast Computation
abstract: Since the introduction of the Kalman filter, nonlinear state estimation has become an important topic in areas such as aerospace engineering, sensor design, and target tracking. Within the optimal filtering framework described by the Duncan-Mortensen-Zakai (DMZ) equation, Yau-Yau filtering (YYF) employs an offline-online decomposition: the Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov (FKE) equations, initialized by a prescribed set of basis functions, are solved offline, and the prior density is projected onto these basis functions during the online stage. However, this approach still faces two computational challenges: solving multiple FKEs offline can be computationally expensive, and the online projection becomes costly when filtering is performed repeatedly or in high-dimensional settings. To address these limitations, we develop a neural operator filter (NOF) that directly learns the mapping from the prior density to the posterior density, thereby eliminating both the expensive offline FKE solves and the online projection. The underlying operator is approximated using a Fourier neural operator (FNO). Numerical experiments on several challenging filtering systems verify both the effectiveness and accuracy of our method, and we further provide a rigorous theoretical analysis of its stability and approximation error.

title: Full $t$-Linkage, Cancellation, and Almost Krull Domains
abstract: Motivated by open questions of Kabbaj and Mimouni, we determine the position of full $t$-linkage among the standard classes of integral domains and its relationship with almost Krullness. Full linkage for a star operation is equivalent to cancellation in the monoid of all nonzero fractional star ideals. For the $t$-operation, this full cancellation law, denoted by $\mathrm{TCL}$, lies strictly between the $t$-almost Dedekind and completely integrally closed classes; on the $\mathrm{PvMD}$ locus, we recover the known $t$-almost Dedekind characterization. We prove that $\mathrm{TCL}$ and almost Krullness are incomparable. A monoid algebra arising from Reinhart's example satisfies $\mathrm{TCL}$ but is neither almost Krull nor a $\mathrm{PvMD}$. In the opposite direction, we construct a locally factorial almost Krull domain with a maximal ideal $0\ne M=M_t=(M^2)_t\subsetneq D$. For this domain the canonical locally divisorial operation $κ$ is cancellative and $κ_f=t$, but cancellation does not descend to $t$. In contrast, finite valuation patching proves that the Heinzer--Ohm and Arnold--Matsuda almost Krull non-$\mathrm{PvMD}$s satisfy $\mathrm{TCL}$ with $t<κ$; in the latter example $κ=v$. Class-monoid, residual, and support criteria identify the obstruction to descent. Thus the missing $t$-linkage node is governed by cancellation in the entire fractional $t$-ideal monoid, rather than by local Krullness alone.

title: Liouville theorems for nonlinear polyharmonic equations with indefinite nonlinearities
abstract: We establish a Liouville theorem for nonnegative bounded solutions of the indefinite polyharmonic equation $(-Δ)^m u=x_1u^p$ in $\mathbb R^n$, for all integers $m\ge2$, $n\ge1$, and all $p>1$. The main difficulty lies in extending the moving-plane method to a higher-order equation with a sign-changing coefficient. We first combine sublinear growth estimates with reflection arguments to establish the super-polyharmonic property in the right half-space, without prescribing boundary conditions on the separating hyperplane. We then use a doubling and rescaling argument to obtain relative first- and second-derivative estimates on strips, replacing the scalar Harnack estimates used in the second-order case. These estimates allow us to establish monotonicity in the $x_1$-direction within the right half-space $\{x_1>0\}$, and a cutoff argument then yields the desired nonexistence result.

title: Cold stellarator coils that outlast power plant lifetime
abstract: We show that a two order-of-magnitude reduction in stellarator coil peak neutron flux and heating can be achieved by moving coils much farther from the plasma if the plasma shape may change slightly and the vessel shielding is increased. Alternating coil and plasma optimizations move the closest coils of our main design over 25 cm out, without substantial degradation in key engineering and physics requirements. The field error decreases and the plasma boundary moves about 1 cm on average. Such coils would be at 4.2 K, use only one third to half the superconducting tape of the original, and require no replacement during the plant's lifetime. This reduced coil flux and heating could significantly enhance the viability of stellarator power plants.

title: Quantum Computing-Based Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Networks for Airfoil Parameterization
abstract: Airfoil geometry parameterization is essential in aerodynamic design optimization. Optimization search in the large space suffers from low efficiency and modest feasible region, which could further incur failures to convergence. Generative adversarial networks (GAN), aiming to learn the statistical distribution of existing data, pave a new avenue for shape generation and airfoil parameterization. GAN manages to implicitly reduce design space by generating only smooth, realistic airfoils. Meanwhile, quantum computing has been emergingly exhibiting great potential for achieving superior performance in specific types of engineering problems but has not been introduced to airfoil parameterization. To fill this gap, this work develops quantum computing-based Wasserstein GAN (Q-WGAN) and investigates the performance for airfoil parameterization. The Q-WGAN adopts parameterized quantum circuits as the generator to promote the generative performance, while the discriminator remains classical. The developed Q-WGAN is demonstrated on a dataset of optimal airfoils parameterized by free-form deformation (FFD) control points, resulting from 992 airfoil aerodynamic design optimizations. Results show that Q-WGAN achieves 92.1% mean fitting accuracy on the optimal FFD control points and 99.2% accuracy on airfoil coordinates, comparable with the classical WGAN performance of 92.28% on FFD control points and 99.26% on airfoil coordinates. Q-WGAN achieves lower Jensen-Shannon divergence, Fréchet distance, and Wasserstein distance than the classical WGAN, indicating an improved agreement with the reference airfoil distribution. Therefore, this work presents a convincing evidence that Q-WGAN makes a viable option for parameterizing airfoils and possesses a great potential for other relevant engineering applications.

title: BiGSyn: A Bi-Level Heterogeneous Graph Contrastive Learning Framework for Interpretable Drug Synergy Prediction
abstract: Drug combination therapy has become a mainstream of modern medicine, with the potential to enhance efficacy, reduce toxicity, and overcome drug resistance. However, identifying synergistic drug combinations remains challenging, as it requires modeling complex interactions across multiple biological scales---from atom-level molecular structures to entity-level relations in biological networks. Existing approaches typically model these levels in isolation, overlooking complementary signals and long-range dependencies. To address these limitations, we propose BiGSyn, a Bi-level heterogeneous Graph contrastive learning framework for drug Synergy prediction. Specifically, BiGSyn leverages heterogeneous graph transformers to extract high-order dependencies from molecular graphs and biological networks, and introduces a bi-level contrastive learning objective to bridge the cross-level semantic gap. Extensive experiments on two benchmark datasets show that BiGSyn consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Moreover, its attention mechanism highlights key molecular substructures and biological interactions driving synergy, providing interpretable insights.

title: A new class of Manin triples of compatible Lie algebras
abstract: This paper introduces a new class of Manin triples of compatible Lie algebras and investigates the corresponding bialgebra structures. To this end, we first study an invariant-c$2$c form on a compatible Lie algebra, namely a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form that is invariant with respect to one Lie bracket and is a commutative $2$-cocycle with respect to the other, which naturally arises from a quadratic differential Novikov algebra. Then we introduce the notion of compatible Lie-anti-pre-Lie algebras (compatible LAPL algebras in short), which serve as the underlying algebra structures of compatible Lie algebras endowed with invariant-c$2$c forms. Furthermore, we introduce the notion of a compatible LAPL bialgebra, which is shown to be equivalent to a Manin triple of compatible Lie algebras with respect to the invariant-c$2$c form. We investigate triangular compatible LAPL bialgebras, which are obtained from antisymmetric solutions of the compatible LAPL Yang-Baxter equation. We also use $\mathcal{O}$-operators of compatible LAPL algebras to construct such solutions. Finally, we show that every differential Novikov bialgebra gives rise to a compatible LAPL bialgebra and that this construction preserves triangularity.

title: AdMem: Expectation-Grounded Procedural Memory for Long-Horizon Task-Solving Agents
abstract: An agent that carries memory across tasks is only as good as the entries it keeps. We begin from an observation that is easy to reproduce and uncomfortable for the field: naively accumulating cross-task experience can make an agent \emph{worse} than one with no memory at all. On AgentBoard, a workflow-induction memory solves fewer tasks than a memoryless ReAct agent in seven of eight domains, and a per-step procedural store with no surrounding structure loses half of ReAct's completions on Jericho. We argue that the missing ingredients are per-action credit assignment and an explicit life cycle for stored entries, and present AdMem, which supplies both. Before each action the actor commits to an expected outcome; a concurrently running critic scores the realized outcome against that expectation and writes a procedural entry carrying a binary reward and a reflection, so credit lands on the action that earned it and no environment reward is required. Each entry then carries a scalar utility, updated online under a noisy-OR reward model, that ranks retrieval jointly with context similarity and drives eviction and merging, giving the store a forgetting and consolidation policy instead of unbounded growth. Across 707 tasks in eight AgentBoard domains AdMem solves 441 against 388 for ReAct and 312 for the workflow-induction baseline --- a pooled gain significant under a two-sided Fisher exact test, concentrated in the domains that supply transferable cross-task structure. All memory stays human-readable text, which is what makes the failures above diagnosable --- and, as we discuss, also makes the store an auditable but attackable surface.

title: Necessary for What? Auditing Demographic Disclosure to LLM Synthetic Respondents
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly answer surveys on behalf of real panelists, and each panelist's recorded demographic attributes (e.g., age, education, ethnicity) are often placed in the prompt on the premise that richer profiles make more faithful synthetic respondents. While data minimization limits personal data to what a purpose requires, a synthetic survey serves several purposes at once, from predicting individual answers to estimating how opinions are distributed and comparing groups. We ask which of these purposes require the respondent's record, and whether improved estimates support sound conclusions about groups. We vary whose profile a model receives, where it comes from, and how many fields it contains, in two U.S. surveys with eleven open-weight and three hosted models, and compare each model with a statistical model fit to the same information. We make four contributions. First, we show that the record adds little to individual predictions and that, for the open-weight models, most of its gain in population estimates remains when it is replaced by census data or a synthetic persona. Second, we find that group comparisons improve only with the respondent's own record, and that even then the models' group differences rest more on the demographic label in the prompt than on the individual respondent, which the usual check of reproducing known group differences does not reveal. Third, we find that the models make groups look more alike than they are, keeping differences in circumstances while flattening or reversing differences in attitudes, most sharply for religious affiliation and ethnic origin, both special categories of personal data. Fourth, we outline an audit that a survey organization can run on questions it has already fielded to decide which estimates may use the record.

title: DNA: A Double-Helix Hierarchical Deep Interaction Network Architecture for Industrial Digital Twin
abstract: High-fidelity modeling is fundamental to industrial digital twin, yet a trade-off persists between the physical transparency of mechanistic models and the superior predictive power of data-driven approaches. Existing hybrid methods often fail to bridge this gap, suffering from shallow integration and rigid one-shot modeling strategies that struggle with complex industrial systems. To address these issues, we propose a \textbf{Double-Helix Hierarchical Deep Interaction Network Architecture (DNA)}. Inspired by the double-helix structure of biological \textit{DNA}, our architecture intertwines mechanistic and data-driven modeling strands through two novel interaction strategies, forming a symbiotic architecture in which the two strands mutually enhance predictive capability. Furthermore, the hierarchical structure of DNA allows it to model complex systems in a multi-stage manner through two tailored deep learning frameworks. We evaluate the proposed approach on two distinct industrial systems, where DNA achieves reductions in MAE of 3.704\% and 3.175\%, respectively, compared to the strongest baseline. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of DNA and suggest its potential to provide new insights for the development of industrial digital twins.

title: Same Papers, Different Verdicts: Tracing Version Drift in LLM Peer Review
abstract: Venues and benchmarks read LLM review scores as measurements of a paper, while providers replace their models within months. We audit twenty frontier models from OpenAI, Google and Anthropic on ICLR 2027 submissions while they were under review, with tests registered before the decisions. Between an earlier and a later version of Claude Opus and of Gemini, the share of papers placed on the accept side falls by 52 and 53 percentage points on 183 and 60 randomly drawn submissions, and by 43 to 79 points in six further paired comparisons, with no paper moving up in any of them. Stating a 30% acceptance rate in the prompt leaves a gap of 79 points between the two Opus versions. When score-stripped critiques are swapped between versions, the later critiques alone lower the accept share by 35 points for Opus and 51 for Gemini; for Opus the drop is 35 points under a third-party scorer and 24 after a rewrite that keeps each technical point and removes evaluative wording. On 57 papers, the percentiles of Opus 4.6 and 5.5 correlate at 0.73 while their accept shares differ by 44 points. On 99 to 119 submissions, the self-estimated percentiles of three models correlate with two human reviewers more strongly than a third reviewer does (point estimates 0.17 to 0.21, 95% intervals between -0.04 and +0.42). All twenty models give a 2 or a 3 in 473 of their 475 reviews, against 60 of 72 human reviews. Retrospective tests on decided papers can draw on memory. Claude Opus 5.5 names the true first author of 27 decided ICLR 2026 papers from their titles alone, with no wrong name, and Claude Opus 4.6 accepted all 11 decided papers it said it recognized, against 5 expected. Thresholds on LLM-reviewer scores therefore have to be validated against human decisions for each model version; our tests against the ICLR 2027 decisions follow on 16 December 2026.

title: Newton-PINet: A fast physics-informed neural network with Newton linearization for meta-learning nonlinear PDEs
abstract: Scientific machine learning has opened new avenues for solving parameterized partial differential equations (PDEs), enabling models to learn a family of PDEs and generalize to unseen instances. In this context, data-driven operator learning methods typically require large training datasets, while physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) suffer from difficult optimization and limited generalization, especially for nonlinear PDEs. We propose Newton-PINet, a physics-informed network enhanced by Newton linearization, offering an effective meta-learning framework for nonlinear PDEs. Newton-PINet (i) employs a physics-informed multilayer network with skip connections, where the output-layer weights are solved by least squares; (ii) adopts a two-stage learning strategy that first leverages gradient-based training to learn robust representations from the available training tasks, and then performs gradient-free fine-tuning on the output layer for fast task-specific generalization; and (iii) incorporates a Newton linearization method to speed up the least-squares iteration for nonlinear PDE problems. On a challenging nonlinear reaction-diffusion benchmark, Newton-PINet achieves up to three orders of magnitude lower relative error than recent neural solvers, while using 16x fewer training tasks and over an order of magnitude less training time (about 5 minutes versus several hours). This work advances the meta-learning of PINNs toward data-efficient, fast, and generalizable physics solvers. The code and datasets are publicly available at: https://github.com/fycAIwj/Newton-PINet.

title: Quantum Sensor of Mechanical Vibrations
abstract: We report the use of a single trapped-ion motional mode as a probe of mechanical vibrations of the Paul trap structure. By exciting vibrations of the trap using an ultrasonic transducer mounted outside the vacuum chamber and probing the ion motion through motional sideband interactions, we observe a clear resonance response of the axial mode. We further demonstrate detection of trap vibrations with amplitudes as low as 0.6 picometers. These measurements show direct coupling between macroscopic mechanical motion and trapped-ion dynamics, providing a route toward vibration sensing using quantum control of motional states.

title: Folding of d-invariants via F-invariants with applications to quiver Hecke KR-modules
abstract: The \(\de\)-invariant measures the interaction between two simple modules and controls the behavior of their convolution product. Using categorical interpretations of Cao's tropical and \(F\)-invariants, we establish folding formulas for the \(Λ\)-invariants between determinantial modules in arbitrary symmetrizable type and derive the corresponding \(\de\)-formula by symmetrization. We apply the \(\de\)-formula to quiver Hecke Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules and show that, in every finite type, their \(\de\)-invariants are completely determined by the coefficients of the symmetrized inverse \(t\)-quantized Cartan matrix. We obtain explicit formulas in all finite types, including closed formulas in the classical types \(A\), \(B\), \(C\), and \(D\).

title: Learning Design Taste through Verifiable Synthetic Environments and Agentic Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Code-generating language models produce user interfaces that build and run, but the pages are often weak in hierarchy, spacing, typography and composition. We study whether a small code model can learn design taste through reinforcement learning in verifiable synthetic environments. The method has three components. First, a layered verification framework splits design quality into hard gates, render-grounded metrics, rubric judges, within-group relative preference and a blinded expert panel. A signal enters the reward only if it passes an admission protocol that tests agreement with experts, causal sensitivity, resistance to hack traps and stability. Second, following SCALER [1], synthetic design environments are parameterised generators with measured difficulty ladders: base pages are written once by an agentic coder, and instances are produced by syntax-tree perturbation operators and constraint samplers, scheduled by an adaptive curriculum with a quarantine rule against reward over-optimisation. Third, a 4B code model is trained with agentic reinforcement learning over multi-turn episodes in which it edits and builds a repository and reads a textual report of its own render, while hidden graders compute the reward. The admission protocol admits 7 of 16 render signals and 6 of 10 rubric dimensions. On TD-Bench, agentic training raises the Taste Index from 0.630 to 0.795 in-family and from 0.598 to 0.700 on held-out families, and wins 0.600 of blinded expert comparisons against the base model and 0.569 against a single-turn control. Most of the advantage depends on the inference-time loop, and cross-brief distinctiveness falls slightly below that of the base model, the only success criterion not met.

title: Noise-Aware Testing of NISQ Quantum Programs: Self-Baseline Oracle with a Controlled False-Positive Rate
abstract: Testing quantum programs on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices faces a test-oracle problem: hardware noise and finite-shot sampling make the runs of a correct program vary as much as those of a faulty one, so oracles with a fixed acceptance threshold produce false positives that depend on the program and the backend. We present a noise-aware testing framework built on self-baseline calibration: each run of the program under test is compared with repeated executions of a trusted reference program on the same backend, and the acceptance threshold is the $(1-α)$ quantile of the finite-shot null distribution of the Jensen-Shannon divergence, so the oracle's false-positive rate is a level set in advance. A noncentral chi-square model predicts detection power, a homogeneity test and a two-run sentinel detect drift, a mutation engine labels every mutant exactly within a three-class noise-aware taxonomy, and zero-noise extrapolation attributes rejections to faults or noise. In simulation on nine core benchmarks, 32 QASMBench programs, ten real bugs, seven noise regimes and three device snapshots, the oracle's false-positive rate is 0.0011 at $α= 10^{-3}$ over 9,000 correct runs, against 36-74% for fixed thresholds, 8.9% for a QOIN-style filter and 10.8% for a globally calibrated threshold, while attaining the highest F1 on non-equivalent faults (0.941). On an IBM Heron device, using about 14 minutes of QPU time, it rejected none of 82 correct runs and detected 120 of 121 faults and semantic mutants, and a two-run sentinel reduced drift-induced false positives from 27.4% to 1.8%.

title: Nitrogen Defect Coupling in Epitaxial LaFeO3 From Structural Reconstruction to Water Oxidation
abstract: Earth-abundant ABO3-type perovskite oxides provide a versatile platform for understanding how anion chemistry and defects govern electrocatalytic behavior. Here, we use epitaxial LaFeO3-xNy thin films to reveal how dilute N incorporation (<0.8% N/O) couples to defect formation, structural reconstruction, and water oxidation. Nitrogen-plasma-assisted pulsed laser deposition introduces N and is accompanied by reduced oxygen content, localized Fe-metal exsolution, and pronounced lattice expansion, while preserving predominantly Fe3+ in the bulk of the film. Ab initio calculations identify a plausible charge-balanced extended defect configuration involving coupled oxygen and Fe vacancies with substitutional N incorporation, reproducing the experimentally observed lattice expansion while preserving the bulk-average Fe oxidation state. The resulting electronic-state redistribution is accompanied by substantially modified electrical transport and nearly two orders of magnitude higher initial oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity than undoped LaFeO3. Under OER conditions, however, the highly active as-grown state is metastable: near-surface N depletion and Fe0 oxidation/removal accompany rapid initial activity decay toward a quasi-steady state. pH-dependent kinetics and post-OER anion redistribution are consistent with possible lattice-oxygen participation. These results establish relationships among dilute anion incorporation, coupled defect reconstruction, electronic properties, and electrochemical behavior in perovskite oxides.

title: Hyperbolic string vertices as geometric chains
abstract: For 0<L<=2arcsinh(1), the hyperbolic string vertices of Costello and Zwiebach consist of the bordered hyperbolic surfaces with geodesic boundary of length L whose interior simple closed geodesics have length at least L. We show that the corresponding regions in moduli space are compact oriented orbifolds with corners whose boundaries are, including orientations and automorphism groups, the spaces of twisted sewings. Hence their generating chain satisfies the master equation without the bracket term exactly in a complex of geometric chains. The usual connected form cannot hold exactly for geometric chains; we determine its exact form, show that it holds modulo gluing and covering relations in a complex computing the homology of the moduli spaces, and that the vertex currents are the unique top-dimensional solution. Finally we compare with Costello's homotopical framework. In a strict model given by hyperbolic surfaces with marked boundary points, every solution of his master equation with his initial condition integrates exactly to the vertex currents, up to the sign (-1)^(3g-3+n); such solutions exist, are unique up to homotopy, and correspond to the hyperbolic vertices. Under a continuity assumption on the comparison map and granting the inputs of Costello's homology computation, the hyperbolic vertices represent his homotopy class of solutions, for a completed notion of homotopy.

title: GEAR$^2$: Pruned Experts Live On through Gated Reuse of Activated Experts and a Missing-Mass Residual
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Large Language Models (LLMs) activate only a few experts per token while generally keeping all the experts in GPU memory for high efficiency. Expert pruning reduces this GPU memory footprint cost, yet discards the contribution of pruned experts. Existing remedies either rely on static substitutes, merge experts at the cost of altering their functions, or require costly recovery training. In this paper, we find that the functionalities of pruned experts can be efficiently reconstructed from the activated remaining experts. We propose GEAR (Gated Expert Activation Reuse), which reuses the scaled outputs of reliable activated experts without any training or additional expert computation. In addition, we propose GEAR$^2$ to further recover what reuse cannot express with an ultra-lightweight residual. On five MoE LLMs from 16B to 106B parameters with 25% and 50% of experts pruned, GEAR improves over its training-free counterparts in nearly every setting (up to 4 pp.) in terms of accuracy, and GEAR$^2$ outperforms baseline approaches (up to 2.75 pp.) in every setting on nine zero-shot benchmarks, with larger advantages (up to 2.72 pp. higher) under more aggressive pruning (up to 50%).

title: Complex Interplay between Outer Disk Dynamics and Inner Water Reservoir
abstract: We present a homogeneous characterization of outer disk dust and gas properties for 51 protoplanetary disks from the JWST/MIRI Cycle 1 programs, combining new ALMA observations with archival data. Visibility fitting with frank recovers more and higher-contrast substructures in the mm continuum than image-plane analysis, placing the innermost features of several disks at 4-5 au and leaving only three disks featureless at the current resolution. CO gas disk sizes span $\sim$60-1000 au and correlate strongly with mm continuum sizes, with $R_{\rm CO}/R_{\rm mm}$ ranging from 1.4 to 9.7 (median 2.95). We then connect these outer disk properties to JWST/MIRI inner disk water diagnostics. We find no global correlation between the cold-to-hot water flux ratio ($F_{\rm cold}/F_{\rm hot}$), a proposed proxy of cold water enrichment by pebble transport, and any single outer disk parameter, including $R_{\rm mm}$, $R_{\rm CO}/R_{\rm mm}$, and innermost substructure location. Three compact ($R_{\rm mm}<30$ au), structureless disks with $R_{\rm CO}/R_{\rm mm}>4$ show both elevated $F_{\rm cold}/F_{\rm hot}$ and cold water emission near the snowline temperature, consistent with unimpeded inward drift of icy pebbles. For structured disks, the water properties instead vary widely at fixed gap location, reflecting the sensitivity of the inner disk water content to multiple factors, including gap leakiness, grain size, and thermal history. Linking outer disk dust evolution to inner disk water content thus requires carefully selected samples with detailed constraints on these additional parameters.

title: One Mean Can't Rule Them All
abstract: There has been extensive debate on how to summarize performance results, especially within the computer architecture community. This article presents a systematic approach to choosing the correct mean, aiming to answer this question for all computer scientists once and for all.

title: From Joint Risk to Decision Invariance: Decision-Preserving Regularization for Exemplar-Free Class-Incremental Learning
abstract: Exemplar-free continual learning seeks to minimize joint risk over all seen tasks, yet historical data are unavailable for direct optimization. We observe that, for classification, preserving the model's decisions on previously learned classes helps retain old knowledge. This motivates Decision-Preserving Regularization (DPR). Penalizing changes in all pairwise old-class logit margins reduces algebraically to a centered relative-logit penalty. We further apply spectral whitening to remove the classifier's spectral scale bias. Because the global classifier supplies the decision constraints for the next stage, it must remain calibrated across all seen classes despite the drift of stored old-class statistics during representation updates. We therefore fit a closed-form affine map from paired current-task features to transport old-class Gaussian means and covariances into the updated feature space, then calibrate the global classifier using these distributions and current-task features. Across CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, ImageNet-Subset, and ImageNet-1K under cold-start protocols, comparisons with state-of-the-art methods show that DPR achieves higher accuracy in most settings while remaining highly efficient. Code is available at https://github.com/bnufw/dpr.

title: Cycles on the universal moduli of rank 2 bundles over the hyperelliptic locus
abstract: We establish a strong Franchetta property for the universal moduli stack of rank two vector bundles over smooth hyperelliptic curves and identify the image of the Chow ring in the cohomology of a fiber via restriction and the cycle class map as precisely the monodromy invariant cohomology classes. More precisely, for every genus $g\geq 2$, degree $d$, and hyperelliptic curve $C$ of genus $g$, we show that the restriction and the cycle class map identifies the Chow ring of the universal moduli stack with the subring of $H^* (Bun_{2,d}(C),\mathbb Q)$ generated by twisted $κ$-classes, which coincides with $H^{*}(Bun_{2,d}(C), \mathbb Q)^{π_1(\mathcal H_g,[C])}$. We use this viewpoint to give an alternative proof to a theorem of Larson in (arXiv:2404.12607), and verify a conjecture of the second author in (arXiv:2604.11958) in the rank $2$ case.

title: GPromptShield: Elevating Resilience in Graph Prompt Tuning against Adversarial Attacks
abstract: The paradigm of ``pre-training and prompt-tuning", with its effectiveness and lightweight characteristics, has rapidly spread from the language field to the graph field. Several pioneering studies have designed specialized prompt functions for diverse downstream graph tasks based on various graph pre-training strategies. These prompts concentrate on the compatibility between the pre-training pretext and downstream graph tasks, aiming to bridge the gap between them. However, designing prompts blindly to adapt to downstream tasks based on this concept neglects crucial security issues. By conducting covert attacks on downstream graph data, we find that even when the downstream task data closely matches that of the pre-training tasks, it is still feasible to generate highly misleading prompts using simple deceptive techniques. In this paper, we shift the primary focus of graph prompts from compatibility to vulnerability issues in adversarial attack scenarios. We design a highly extensible shield defense system for the prompts, which enhances their robustness from two perspectives: Direct Handling and Indirect Amplification. When downstream graph data contains unreliable biases, the former directly combats invalid information by incorporating hybrid multi-defense prompts to the input graph's feature space, while the latter adopts a training strategy to bypass the invalid components and amplifies valid part. We provide a theoretical derivation that proves their feasibility, indicating that unbiased prompts exist under certain conditions on unreliable data. Extensive experiments across various scenarios of adversarial attacks indicate that the prompts within our defense system exhibit enhanced resilience and superiority. This paper explores a new perspective in graph prompt learning, offering a novel option for robust prompt tuning in downstream tasks.

title: Observable Spectral Framework for Noisy Amplitude Amplification: Stopping Stability and Correction
abstract: Stopping rules for noisy amplitude amplification often rely on channel-specific success-probability formulas, limiting their transfer across noise mechanisms. We develop an observable spectral framework for stationary noisy standard amplitude amplification under explicit leading-mode, spectral-separation, and residual-control conditions. Within this class, the first amplification lobe has a damped-oscillatory leading component and a bounded non-leading contribution. We derive how frequency shift, damping, and observable phase offset displace the leading peak, and establish sampled-gap criteria for retaining the ideal integer stopping depth, certifying recalibration, or selecting a robust candidate window. In single-target Grover search, frequency and damping errors have stopping-coordinate sensitivities proportional to the search-space size, whereas phase offsets scale with its square root; residual modes can independently reverse the ordering of neighbouring depths. Analytical constructions, circuit simulations, finite-shot inference, and calibration-derived device-like trajectories examine these predictions and their operational limits. For a 64-element search, an a posteriori sampled-set check selects depth five over six, with success probability increasing from 0.595 to 0.626. The resulting theory links observable spectral dynamics to conditional integer stopping guarantees without requiring a separate microscopic channel solution.

title: Example-Based Spatial Guidance for Training-Free Concept Erasure in Diffusion Models
abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models often synthesize policy-violating content, necessitating robust safeguards and rigorous evaluation frameworks. However, current approaches remain largely monolithic in both execution and evaluation, limited to coarse-grained categorization within broad unsafe concepts. Such approaches fail to account for the specific constituent factors of a violation, resulting in weak learning signals and allowing model collapse to bypass safety checks. To overcome these limitations, we propose Example-Based Spatial Guidance (EBSG), a training-free method that utilizes user-editable exemplar packs to provide granular spatial guidance for precise concept steering. Unlike existing methods that coarsely steer the entire image away from a broad concept, EBSG decomposes these categories into specific sub-concepts via exemplar text-image pairs, providing explicit, localized steering signals for more robust safety control. Furthermore, we introduce a vision language model (VLM)-based evaluation protocol that provides a fine-grained assessment, avoiding the pitfall of conventional binary evaluators that permit model collapse to bypass safety checks. Empirically, EBSG achieves state-of-the-art erasure performance across diverse safety datasets and concept categories, spanning four nudity benchmarks, seven I2P harmful-concept slices, and four MJA metaphor categories, while supporting multi-concept removal and transferring to a modern backbone, SD3.

title: Miniaturized Low-Cost 3-D Printed High-Permittivity Dielectric Transmissive LP-to-CP Converter for L-Band Satellite Communications
abstract: A low-cost, miniaturized, additively manufactured transmissive linear-to-circular polarization converter for L-band air and space communication systems is presented. The proposed polarizer employs an in-house-fabricated high-permittivity dielectric medium, realized using a 3-D printed polylactic acid (PLA) enclosure filled with a TiO$_2$--water mixture. Variation in the effective permittivity is achieved by adjusting the mixture filling fraction. The selected 60\% filling fraction corresponds to an effective relative permittivity of 11.3 at 1 GHz. The high-permittivity loading enables miniaturization of the polarizer height and area by reducing the anisotropic dielectric unit-cell dimensions to $\boldsymbol{0.037λ_0 \times 0.037λ_0 \times 0.22λ_0}$. An additively manufactured polarizer with overall dimensions $\boldsymbol{0.83λ_0 \times 0.77λ_0 \times 0.22λ_0}$ is experimentally validated using a compact linearly polarized feed source. The measured results demonstrate LP-to-CP conversion, with a 3 dB axial ratio of 12\% and insertion loss of less than 0.6 dB. Radiation-pattern measurements at 1 GHz show LHCP-to-RHCP discrimination levels of 19 and 24 dB in the \textbf{\textit{xz}}- and \textbf{\textit{yz}}-planes, respectively. The proposed configuration combines miniaturization, LP-to-CP conversion, and low-cost additive manufacturing, making it promising for UAV-mounted and other size-constrained L-band satellite communication terminals.

title: ASCG: Adaptive Spatial Classifier Guidance for Surgical Concept Suppression in Diffusion Models
abstract: While text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models achieve remarkable quality, they risk producing harmful content. Existing safety mechanisms often rely on indiscriminate, global interventions that induce unintended semantic drift and degrade image quality. To address this, we propose Adaptive Spatial Classifier Guidance (ASCG), a necessity-driven framework that employs probabilistic monitoring to activate guidance selectively upon harm detection. By leveraging Grad-CAM for localized suppression, ASCG effectively removes harmful concepts while preserving superior semantic fidelity compared to conventional methods. Furthermore, we overcome the limitations of traditional metrics like NudeNet---which fails to assess semantic integrity---by introducing a VLM-based evaluation framework to provide a fine-grained, robust analysis of both safety and context preservation. Our results demonstrate that ASCG not only balances safety and fidelity but also exhibits remarkable plug-and-play synergy with existing frameworks to establish state-of-the-art performance.

title: Two-Stage Staffing with Random Arrival Rate: A Simulation Optimization Approach
abstract: In service systems, the arrival rate in the same time period and day of the week exhibits randomness, yet can be more accurately estimated or forecast right before that period, which motivates a two-stage staffing scheme with advance base staffing and pre-shift surge staffing. Existing approaches usually impose strong assumptions on the arrival process and service systems' operational logic and other further approximations (i.e., stylized models) to derive explicit staffing policies. This paper proposes a simulation optimization approach (SOA) for more general arrival processes and service systems by effectively addressing some intertwined challenges. By recasting the original formulation into computationally tractable structures and designing an efficient coordinate-search algorithm, it constructs a two-stage staffing lookup table offline, which allows managers to make real-time surge staffing decisions without any further simulation. Comprehensive numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed SOA has significantly better staffing performance and substantially broader applicability compared to existing approaches. Even under the stylized models, the cost savings delivered by our SOA compared with existing approaches range from the low tens to several tens of percent, depending on different problem parameters; the advantage further amplifies when the actual problem deviates from the stylized models. In a nurse-staffing case study grounded in real-world data, the proposed SOA delivers approximately 8% to 13% cost savings over a state-of-the-art benchmark.

title: Quasinormal modes of Kerr--de Sitter black holes in semi-open systems
abstract: We investigate the gravitational quasinormal mode spectrum of Kerr--de Sitter black holes with a partially reflective inner boundary near the event horizon, by reducing the angular and radial Teukolsky equations to Heun equations. We vary different parameters and study the $s=-2$, $\ell=m=2$ modes numerically. As the reflectivity $\mathcal{R}_0$ increases, QNMs develop echo branches approaching the real axis with approximately regular spacing, while others approach $\operatorname{Re}ω=mΩ(r_+)$. As the rotation $a$ increases, some QNMs approach the real axis or retain finite damping, while others exhibit approximately horizontal shifts with real parts tracking $mΩ(r_+)$. Two mechanisms driving the instabilities are identified in complementary regimes, namely superradiant amplification and energy injection from the reflective wall. We derive the ratio between Teukolsky amplitude and energy reflectivities, finding that the latter can diverge at $mΩ(r_+)$ even when the former is small, which accounts for an active wall in this regime. We also find that formulating the reflective boundary condition in terms of asymptotic amplitudes gives rise to resonances near each pole of the ingoing connection coefficient, extending to arbitrarily large positive imaginary parts. An exact finite radius Robin condition imposed on the Sasaki--Nakamura variable removes these pole-born frequencies. These results show how the inner boundary prescription controls the spectrum structure and stability of semi-open Kerr--de Sitter systems.

title: PixelBench: Evaluating Language Models for Pixel-Art Creation
abstract: Pixel art is widely used in games and digital content creation, requiring readable forms, coherent spatial relationships, and harmonious colors under limited resolution and palette constraints. Language models show growing promise in visual creation, yet their pixel art creation capabilities lack systematic evaluation. We introduce PixelBench, formalizing text-to-image generation and instruction-guided editing for pixel art and providing a benchmark for these tasks. We further present a creation environment in which language model agents invoke drawing tools through code to generate and edit pixel art. We assess the quality of generated artwork through human evaluation and employ a multimodal large language model as a judge, validating the agreement between its automated assessments and human preferences. We compare language models and configurations across diverse subjects and canvas sizes. In our experiments, GPT-6 Astra achieves both the highest average judge score and the best average human rank, highlighting the potential of general-purpose language models for pixel art creation. We release the tasks, all artworks, the human rankings, and the judge protocol.

title: Event-Guided Stereo Video Super-Resolution
abstract: Stereo Video Super-Resolution (SVSR) aims to reconstruct high-resolution stereo videos by exploiting temporal cues across consecutive frames and complementary spatial cues between stereo views. However, existing methods struggle to recover high-frequency texture details under rapid motion and complex illumination, compromising reconstruction quality and stereo consistency. Event cameras provide valuable motion and texture cues with high temporal resolution and wide dynamic range, yet their potential for SVSR remains underexplored. To bridge this gap, we present the first investigation of event-guided SVSR and propose a novel framework.
