abstract: On sufficiently large scales the galaxy overdensity field is approximately Gaussian, so its information can be losslessly compressed into the power spectrum. Standard power spectrum estimators are nevertheless suboptimal on the largest scales, where the survey window induces significant coupling between different modes. Optimal power spectrum analysis typically requires an inverse of the covariance matrix, which can be overly expensive. Here we develop an alternative field level approach, which is significantly faster. We assess its impact on constraining primordial non-Gaussianity of the local type, which is particularly sensitive to these largest scales. Relative to the standard power spectrum analysis, our field level likelihood forecasts a $14\%$ improvement in constraining power. For the DESI DR2 LRG and QSO samples, our approach forecasts $σ(f_{\rm NL})=4.1$, compared to $σ(f_{\rm NL})=4.8$ from the power spectrum based analysis. The field level approach also enables efficient implementations of additional non-cosmological contributions to the signal. As an example, we present a novel non-parametric method to mitigate angular systematics, enabling efficient deprojection of contaminated modes.

title: Feebly-Interacting Particle Searches
abstract: In the last several years, feebly-interacting particles (FIPs) have moved from "exotica" to the mainstream of particle physics. This development is fueled by three motivations: FIPs are one of two broad possibilities for new particles, FIPs are as well motivated by dark matter as WIMPs, and FIPs are connected to important problems in particle physics. I review these motivations and then briefly highlight recent progress in a few areas, including axion-like particles, dark photons and other gauge bosons, the X17 anomaly, quirks, and the Forward Physics Facility.

title: Constraints on the volume enclosed by Fermi surfaces
abstract: A fundamental property of a Fermi liquid (FL) is that the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by $ρ$, the total density of electrons. In a fractionalized Fermi liquid (FL*), the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by the same expression after $ρ$ has been shifted by a quantized amount, most commonly to $ρ-1$ (we assume spin rotation invariance, for simplicity). The FL* shift is related to the quantized symmetry fractionalization data of a quantum spin liquid, whose fractionalized spinon excitations are present alongside the Fermi surface quasiparticles. In this review article, we establish the FL* Fermi volume by generalizing the original Luttinger proof for FL to parton gauge theories of the quantum spin liquid and FL*. We also discuss Oshikawa's flux insertion arguments for FL, and their extension to FL*, including a discussion of gapless spin liquids.

title: Velocity Reconstruction from kSZ with SPT-3G and DESI-LS
abstract: We reconstruct the large-scale radial velocity field from the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect for the first time with the South Pole Telescope, and measure the galaxy-velocity correlation and the velocity power spectrum. We cross-correlate the SPT-3G D1 maps at 95, 150, and 220 GHz with luminous red galaxies from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys over the SPT-3G Main field. For the extended galaxy sample, we detect the galaxy-velocity correlation at signal-to-noise ratio $11.2$ and the velocity power spectrum at $8.1$, combining the three frequencies. We detect the reconstructed velocities for the first time at 220 GHz with signal-to-noise ratios of 4.2 and 3.1 from the galaxy-velocity correlation dipole and monopole, and at 3.8 from the velocity power spectrum. We model and estimate foreground contributions to the monopole, detecting both the thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect and the cosmic infrared background contribution separately. On the around five percent of sky jointly covered by SPT-3G and DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys, reconstructed velocities give new constraints on local-type primordial non-Gaussianity at $f_{\rm NL}=-38^{+61}_{-61}$, and adding galaxy clustering gives $f_{\rm NL}=-20^{+40}_{-46}$. The galaxy-velocity correlation is consistent between the three frequencies.

title: Cosmic Censorship in the Landscape of SUSY-Broken AdS Vacua
abstract: We investigate signatures of weak cosmic censorship in non-supersymmetric vacua of both IIA and IIB string theory. In particular, we examine the Penrose Inequality, which can be proven holographically using Ryu-Takayanagi, and can be independently proven in SUSY AdS vacua for spherically symmetric initial data. We prove that any EFT of scalars coupled to gravity in AdS, including in particular those of string compactifications, satisfies both the Penrose Inequality and a positive mass theorem if a function that we call a "weak fake superpotential" exists. We demonstrate that this condition is satisfied globally for the DGKT skew-whiffed vacua in IIA. Since there is no known nonperturbative instability in this DGKT vacuum, this provides evidence that the IIA SUSY-broken AdS vacua may be absolutely stable. We also find the weak fake superpotential exists locally in field space in some SUSY-broken AdS vacua in a KKLT construction in IIB. Thus, within the framework considered here, some false SUSY-broken KKLT AdS vacua are stable against vacuum decay. Conversely, we find that some KKLT vacua do not have a weak fake superpotential, and correspondingly violate the Penrose Inequality and fail to have a positive mass theorem; the DGKT vacua only violate the Penrose Inequality in the presence of designer gravity boundary conditions. In all cases studied, this is due to false vacuum decay. We discuss the implications of these violations for holography and black hole thermodynamics in these SUSY-broken AdS vacua.

title: Black holes as black boxes: a query lower bound on python's lunch decoding
abstract: The python's lunch conjecture relates the complexity of bulk reconstruction in holographic tensor networks to an exponential cost associated with post-selection. We establish a tight query lower bound for this decoding problem in a Haar random oracle model, with a python's lunch circuit that applies Haar random unitary $U$ to a logical input and fixed ancillas, followed by post-selection on $m$ output qubits. Given one copy of the normalized encoded state and coherent oracle access to $U$ and $U^\dagger$, including controlled queries, we prove that recovering even a single logical bit with constant average advantage requires $Ω(2^{m/2})$ queries. Together with the state-independent amplitude amplification upper bound for approximately isometric encodings, this establishes query complexity $Θ(2^{m/2})$ at constant decoding accuracy. We also comment on the decoding cost for other "admissible'" ensembles of unitaries $U$ which give rise to families of approximately isometric holographic maps.

title: Localization identities for spectral determinants: two-dimensional QCD and Ising field theory
abstract: Spectral determinants encode the meson spectra of planar two-dimensional QCD and of Ising field theory in the two-particle Bethe-Salpeter approximation. We derive localization identities for these determinants which express their logarithmic derivatives with respect to the spectral parameter in terms of Baxter $Q-$functions evaluated at special points, proving previously conjectured relations. Our derivation uses finite-rank commutation relations and virial identities of the underlying integral spectral operators. We identify a sufficient rational closure condition on the symbol of these operators that extends localization to a broader class of spectral problems and determines the evaluation points. Applications include generalized two-dimensional QCD with a quartic gauge-field potential and symbols interpolating between the QCD and Ising cases. We also give a general construction of the spectral operators and establish conditions for the finite-rank reduction on which localization relies.

title: All-Genus 2D $\mathcal{N}=1$ Superconformal Blocks
abstract: We develop a numerical algorithm for two dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal blocks at arbitrary genera, in arbitrary plumbing channels, and for arbitrary spin structures. The algorithm utilizes two commuting copies of Virasoro subalgebras of the direct sum of the $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal algebra with an auxiliary free fermion algebra, which allows us to reduce the $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal blocks to Virasoro conformal blocks.

title: Not All Holographic Entropy Inequalities Are Free of Area Law Ultraviolet Divergences
abstract: In the AdS/CFT correspondence, linear constraints on subsystem entropies, which are necessary conditions for the validity of the Ryu-Takayanagi proposal, define the holographic entropy cone. We disprove a prior claim that all holographic constraints of this type are free of area law divergences (superbalanced). We analyze one explicit counterexample and explain how to easily find more; we report signatures of $\mathcal{O}(10^5)$ counterexamples. Our findings invalidate multiple prior claims and conjectures.

title: Supersymmetric warped AdS$_3$ solutions in eleven-dimensional supergravity
abstract: We construct new families of supersymmetric solutions of eleven-dimensional supergravity by deforming the half-BPS $\mathrm{AdS}_3\times \mathrm{S}^3_+\times \mathrm{S}^3_-\times\mathbb R^2$ background. We consider lightlike, spacelike and timelike warpings of the anti-de Sitter factor, accompanied by deformations of the two three-spheres, and determine the supporting four-form fluxes and the constraints imposed by the equations of motion. In particular, the deformation parameters of the two spheres are necessarily equal, although their radii need not coincide. We compute the conserved charges and determine the preserved supersymmetries and Killing superalgebras. Generic lightlike solutions preserve four real supercharges, whereas spacelike and timelike solutions preserve eight, with a Killing superalgebra containing a single exceptional $\mathfrak d(2,1;α)$ factor.

title: Plugging the Pion Chimney
abstract: Heavy QCD axions and other gluon-coupled axion-like particles (ALPs) with masses from MeV to GeV are well motivated and have been searched for extensively. However, a window around the neutral pion mass, the so-called pion chimney, has escaped every search. There the ALP mixes strongly with the $π^0$ and therefore shares its experimental signatures. We show that the chimney can be closed with existing LHC data. The key point is that mixing changes the lifetimes of the two mass eigenstates but does not make them equal, and at LHC energies the states are boosted enough for the lifetime to decide whether they escape the detector or decay inside it. The ATLAS monojet search constrains the first case and the ATLAS inclusive photon measurement the second, and together they exclude the chimney up to the cutoff of the ALP effective theory. Above the cutoff, LHC searches for the colored states of the simplest ultraviolet completions exclude the rest. We also show that the bound from the $K^+$ width does not reach the chimney, because an ALP passes the same selection as a $π^0$, and we derive an independent, purely kinematic constraint from the measured $π^\pm$-$π^0$ mass splitting.

title: Supernova Bounds on Neutrino Dipole Moments from a Modern Perspective
abstract: Neutrinos may have nonstandard magnetic dipole moments $μ_ν$. In the dense cores of supernovae (SNe), these would convert part of the neutrinos into sterile, right-handed states through the electromagnetic fluctuations of the charged plasma. The streaming sterile neutrinos with 100-MeV energies can convert back to standard neutrinos in the Galactic magnetic field, leading to a high-energy neutrino flux unobserved from the historical SN 1987A. We reassess the production rates, including scattering on both protons and electrons, and, building upon advances in SN simulations and in the description of the Milky Way magnetic field, we revisit the bounds on magnetic dipole moments. We find for Dirac electron neutrinos $μ_{ν_e} \lesssim 4.8 \times 10^{-13} μ_B$, superseding all existing terrestrial and astrophysical constraints.

title: Gravity/Thermodynamics Correspondence for Generic Dynamical Spacetimes
abstract: Working within covariant phase space formalism, we establish \textit{gravity-thermodynamics correspondence} for generic dynamical spacetimes. We derive local first and second laws of thermodynamics on general null boundaries, for generic non-stationary solutions to Einstein gravity {with minimally coupled matter} for physical observers that we carefully specify. Entropy variation, which receives contribution only from the gravitational sector, is the surface charge variation associated with a vector field generating the null boundary, and temperature is its non-affinity parameter (divided by $2π$). The statement of the second law in our setting is that the entropy variation evaluated along the null vector field is strictly non-negative for the admissible positive-non-affinity clock and matter satisfying the null energy condition. Our dynamical entropy variation, which is non-integrable for generic non-stationary solutions, becomes integrable in near-stationary configurations, reproducing the Hollands--Wald--Zhang dynamical entropy formula. Strikingly, this local second law holds even when the boundary area is decreasing, disentangling thermodynamic irreversibility and the second law from standard area theorems. Our first-principles construction demonstrates that gravitational thermodynamics requires neither a stationary background, teleological event horizons, nor an exact entropy state function on individual codimension-1 spacelike slices of the null boundary (codimension two in spacetime).

title: ASAS-SN Rates V: Tidal Disruption Event Volumetric Rates and Luminosity Functions by Optical Spectroscopic Type, X-ray Luminosity, and Host-Galaxy Properties
abstract: We present volumetric rates and luminosity functions (LFs) of tidal disruption events (TDEs) based on 21 TDEs from the All-Sky Automated Survey for Supernovae (ASAS-SN) between 2014 and 2024. We calculate completeness corrections from injection-recovery simulations of the ASAS-SN light curves using individual TDE templates. We find a total volumetric rate of $\log_{10}(R_{\rm tot}[{\rm yr}^{-1}{\rm Gpc}^{-3}h_{70}^3]) = 2.32^{+0.15}_{-0.23}$ for $z \leq 0.12$. We also measure the rates of two growing TDE subpopulations. The one off-nuclear TDE in our standard sample implies $\log_{10}(R_{\rm off\text{-}nuclear}) = 0.39^{+0.52}_{-0.76}$ ($1.2^{+3.4}_{-1.0}$% of the total rate). We measure the rate of recurrent TDEs (rTDEs) to be $\log_{10}(R_{\rm recurrent}) = 1.26^{+0.23}_{-0.62}$ ($9^{+8}_{-6}$% of the total rate) from the four rTDEs in our standard sample, increasing to $1.45^{+0.20}_{-0.35}$ ($13^{+10}_{-7}$%) when the well-studied ASASSN-14ko is included. Galaxies with substantial (>0.1%) burst-mass fractions and steeply falling star-formation histories host the majority of TDEs. We recover the known overrepresentation of TDEs in post-starburst galaxies, by a factor of $15^{+16}_{-11}$ relative to matched control galaxies, and a weaker enhancement of $5^{+5}_{-4}$ in quiescent Balmer-strong galaxies. TDE-H+He events dominate the volumetric TDE rate, with TDE-H, TDE-He, and TDE-Featureless events comprising <15% of nearby TDEs. The $g$-band LFs are statistically indistinguishable when split at the median X-ray to UV/optical blackbody luminosity ratio of $\sim$1%, corroborating unification models where the observed multi-wavelength emission is set primarily by viewing angle effects. Extrapolating the measured TDE LFs to higher luminosities and more massive black holes supports a TDE origin for luminous ambiguous nuclear transients and extreme nuclear transients.

title: The meaning of Milky Way mass estimates in the presence of the LMC
abstract: The LMC's recent arrival perturbs the observed kinematics of the Milky Way's (MW) stellar halo, complicating equilibrium-based MW mass estimates at Galactocentric distances $r\gtrsim 30$ kpc. Using N-body MW+LMC simulations, we show that the MW stellar halo can be used to disentangle the total MW+LMC, current LMC, and pre-infall MW mass profiles, by exploiting the LMC's orbital path and the LMC-induced motion of the MW's center of mass ("reflex motion"). Tracers in regions crossed by the LMC longest ago (Galactic coordinates $\ell >0^\circ, b>0^\circ$) are approximately relaxed and trace the total MW+LMC mass. Since the reflex motion is primarily latitudinal, a radial-velocity-only estimator ($M_{v_r}$) recovers the total MW+LMC mass with $\lesssim 5\%$ errors across $30<r/{\rm kpc}<200$, without any reflex-motion correction. Subtracting mass estimates in the region of the LMC's future orbit ($\ell < 0^\circ, b >0^\circ$) from those in its recent-orbit region ($\ell > 0^\circ, b <0^\circ$), which maximizes the LMC-induced velocity dipole, recovers the LMC's current mass profile with $10-20\%$ errors, but this requires tracers at $r\gtrsim 100-120$ kpc. Subtracting this from the total MW+LMC mass recovers the MW's pre-LMC infall mass at $r\gtrsim 80$ kpc with $5-10\%$ errors. Applying $M_{v_r}$ to DESI-MWS DR1 BHBs at $\ell >0^\circ, b>0^\circ$ and $50<r/{\rm kpc}<60$, we obtain a total MW+LMC mass $M(r<60\,{\rm kpc}) \approx 7.5^{+3.0}_{-2.2}\times 10^{11}\,M_\odot$. Observationally, recovering the LMC and pre-infall MW mass profiles requires 6D samples at $r\gtrsim100$ kpc, and a virial mass to within $\sim10-20\%$ requires $r\gtrsim120$ kpc, both achievable with Gaia DR5 astrometry for halo giants targeted by DESI Run 2 and 4MOST. Rather than treating the LMC-induced disequilibrium as an obstacle, our framework exploits it to weigh both galaxies.

title: Baryonification V: Thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich maps from dark-matter-only lightcones
abstract: Baryonic feedback is a major theoretical uncertainty for Stage-IV weak lensing (WL) surveys. The thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) effect traces the hot gas redistributed by feedback, so combining it with WL can calibrate feedback and improve cosmological constraints. Doing so with simulation-based inference requires correlated lensing and Compton-$y$ maps across many cosmologies and feedback scenarios. We present two methods to generate Compton-$y$ maps from dark-matter-only $N$-body light cones using the component-wise baryonification (BFC) model, which produces separate gas and stellar fields and computes the gas pressure from hydrostatic equilibrium. The two methods, painting pressure profiles onto halos or redistributing the signal along the baryonified gas, agree to within a few per cent. We calibrate the model to the fiducial and strongest AGN feedback FLAMINGO simulations by jointly fitting gas mass fractions and thermal pressure profiles, measuring the non-thermal pressure from the simulated gas velocities rather than treating it as a free parameter. The predicted Compton-$y$ profiles match FLAMINGO within halo-to-halo scatter, and when painted onto the FLAMINGO halos we reproduce the tSZ power spectrum of both feedback models to $\sim5\%$ for $500\lesssim\ell\lesssim3000$. Applied to a \emph{CosmoGridV1-like} $N$-body simulation, our maps agree with FLAMINGO within $\sim10\%$ for $300\lesssim\ell\lesssim8000$; the remaining differences come from the few hundred most massive clusters, and removing them from both halo catalogs brings the two into agreement. Our method thus enables accurate and efficient tSZ forward models from $N$-body simulation suites such as CosmoGridV1, an important step towards joint WL and tSZ simulation-based inference for Euclid, LSST, and the Simons Observatory.

title: Cyclic Boson Stars with Quantum Vortex Molecules
abstract: We find a new type of stationary boson star with cyclic rotational symmetry in the minimal model of complex scalar field coupled to gravity. Unlike conventional axisymmetric spinning boson stars, these configurations can carry noninteger angular momentum per particle in units of the reduced Planck constant, revealing a new way for boson stars to carry angular momentum. We identify the vortex assemblies within these stars as self-gravitating quantum vortex molecules, in which gravity supports a stationary vortex arrangement despite internal circulation. These structures provide a relativistic realization of quantum vortex molecules studied in condensates and motivate possible laboratory analogues.

title: Gravitational Mode Instabilities in Kerr-like Black Holes
abstract: We identify exponentially growing modes of a homogeneous gravitational Teukolsky-like operator on highly spinning Kerr-like black holes subject to quasinormal mode boundary conditions. Specifically, we compute electromagnetic and gravitational quasinormal modes of a spacetime proposed by Konoplya, Rezzolla, and Zhidenko that parametrizes deformations from the Kerr geometry, including configurations with black hole spin parameter $a/M > 1$ that retain an event horizon. Using the continued fraction method, we find that the spin-weight $s=-2$ operator develops exponentially growing modes when the black hole spin and deformation parameters are sufficiently large, while the electromagnetic modes remain damped throughout the parameter space. We further compare the quasinormal mode predictions with an agnostic analysis of the GW250114 ringdown, identifying regions of the parameter space that are compatible with the spectrum inferred from the data.

title: Active Galactic Nuclei as Beyond the Standard Model Laboratories: a White Paper
abstract: Multi-messenger and multi-wavelength observations of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) can provide otherwise inaccessible knowledge about physics Beyond the Standard Model (BSM), and may even lead to its discovery. Realizing this potential hinges on two parallel efforts: advancing our understanding of AGN and of the dark matter around them, and identifying the BSM signatures that are at once promising and robust against the gaps in that understanding. These fields have attracted growing interest in recent years, also motivated by the IceCube association of neutrinos to individual AGN, yet we have only begun to explore their cross-fertilization. This white paper offers a new perspective on this interdisciplinary endeavor. It concisely reviews the state of the art in each field and at their interface, and identifies the key open questions that must be addressed to strengthen our prospects for learning about BSM physics with AGN.

title: Thermal Composite Dark Matter at LZ
abstract: We show that stable fermionic resonances of Composite Higgs models provide a thermal inelastic Dark Matter interpretation of the high-energy nuclear-recoil event LZ230616. Their stability follows from an exact accidental parity of the strong sector. Annihilation channels from composite interactions link the thermal relic mass to the strong coupling, allowing masses well beyond the pure electroweak prediction. We identify three scenarios in which the neutral states form a split pseudo-Dirac pair, distinguished by the origin of the inelastic coupling to the $Z$ boson. In the pure electroweak regime, the pair consists of the neutral components of a complex Higgsino-like doublet. Its unsuppressed inelastic $Z$ coupling requires Dark Matter masses above 20 TeV. In the pure strong regime, the suppressed $Z$ coupling of neutral states with vanishing hypercharge arises from strong interactions alone, allowing for smaller splittings and TeV-scale masses. In the third regime, which interpolates between the previous two, the neutral components of multiplets with different hypercharge are mixed. This enhances their inelastic coupling, accommodating the LZ event for masses of a few TeV and splittings around 300 keV, with mixing angles of order $10^\circ$. All three cases provide a thermal Dark Matter candidate able to explain the LZ event, consistently with the solar-capture bounds, the LZ high-energy sideband, and gamma-ray indirect searches.

title: Shocks and Trails in the Circumgalactic Medium Driven by Runaway Supermassive Black Holes
abstract: Runaway supermassive black holes (SMBHs) have long been predicted. RBH-1, discovered with HST and confirmed by JWST, provides the strongest evidence yet for a runaway SMBH: a bow shock and linear trail in the circumgalactic medium (CGM) of a $z=0.96$ galaxy. The bow shock is $\sim$kpc wide, the trail is $\sim 60$ kpc long, and the SMBH apparently moves at $\sim 1,000$ km s$^{-1}$. Using controlled hydrodynamic simulations, we show that the SMBH's gravity alone cannot produce a significant bow shock, but a comoving wind source can sustain one similar to RBH-1's. The wind must either be active or have shut off less than $\sim 3$ Myr ago. The required recent wind momentum flux is $6\times10^{32}\,{\rm dyn}\,(n_{\rm CGM}/10^{-3}\,{\rm cm}^{-3})$, where $n_{\rm CGM}$ is the CGM density. Assuming the wind reaches peak strength only during the last $\sim 6$ Myr, the minimum integrated wind mass is $3.5\times10^5\,M_\odot\,(n_{\rm CGM}/10^{-3}\,{\rm cm}^{-3})$. A $2\times10^7\,M_\odot$ SMBH accreting at $1\%$ Eddington could power the wind. Supernova feedback from a star cluster carried by the SMBH is an alternative, although the required mass and momentum fluxes $\gtrsim 60$ Myr after ejection are difficult to reconcile with a standard initial mass function. For a hot ambient CGM at $\sim 10^6$ K, the quasi-linear trail constrains the 1D velocity dispersion to $σ_{\rm 1D}\lesssim 30$ km s$^{-1}$, above which it becomes strongly disturbed. Runaway SMBH trails therefore offer a new probe of turbulence in the diffuse CGM, in regimes where its kinematics are otherwise inaccessible.

title: Modular Hamiltonian and modular flow of a massive scalar in an interval
abstract: We obtain the vacuum modular Hamiltonian of a free massive scalar in an interval, for any $mL$. Its eigenvectors are superpositions of massive plane waves emitted from the two end points, with amplitudes given by a linear integral equation whose Neumann series is an expansion in reflections, and a normalization fixed by a Painlevé V transcendent. We follow the modular flow of initially localized wave packets inside the causal diamond. The flow is not geometric: the commutator profiles spread and can develop peaks ahead of the conformal trajectory.

title: A Proposal for Quantum Reference Frames in Quantum Field Theory and their Experimental Exploration
abstract: We construct quantum reference frames (QRFs) in quantum field theory, using localized modes of a scalar field as frames for its shift symmetry. We import tools from relativistic quantum information to explicitly compute entropies and correlation measures of relational observables, investigating their frame dependence and the new features arising from the field-theoretic character of the system. Unlike QRFs for systems with finitely many degrees of freedom, localized field-theoretic QRFs are necessarily mixed in physically relevant states and generically correlated with the subsystems they describe. These aspects of QRFs for fields affect the properties of relational observables in a subtle way. Furthermore, we put forward a proposal for testing these predictions with existing quantum simulators based on ultracold atoms and quantum fluids, thus connecting QRF physics with analogue gravity platforms.

title: Smuggling baryon asymmetry through strong washout
abstract: We propose a scheme in which a primordial net baryon number generated at or around the unification scale may survive subsequent strong washout phases associated with active sphalerons and interactions of right-handed neutrinos inherent to thermal leptogenesis. A simple realization of this, namely, a long-lived scalar population injecting the net $B-L$ it carries into the Standard Model matter sector late enough to be safe from a strong washout, is constructed and studied in the context of a simple Pati-Salam scalar sector with a heavy $SU(4)_C$ sextet scalar.

title: Flash UV Spectroscopy: Decoding the Ultraviolet Diversity of Young Core-Collapse Supernovae with the Hubble Space Telescope
abstract: We present multi-wavelength observations and modeling of the largest sample to date of core-collapse supernovae (SNe) with Hubble Space Telescope (HST) ultraviolet (UV) spectroscopy within < 2 weeks of first light. Our total sample contains early-time UV spectroscopy from 12 Type II SNe (SNe II), 3 Type IIb SNe (SNe IIb), 3 Type IIn SNe (SNe IIn) and 1 Type I super-luminous SN (SLSN-I). This sample includes 11 objects with unpublished UV spectroscopy from HST Cycles 31 and 32 "Flexible Thursdays" target of opportunity programs, increasing the number of core-collapse SNe with early-time HST UV spectra by a factor of 2.4. The early-time near-UV spectra of most sample SNe II show similar Doppler-broadened P-Cygni profiles of metals (Mg, Fe, Ti, Cr), though with notable diversity in line velocities and absorption strengths. Comparison to non-Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (nLTE) radiative transfer model grids at similar phases indicates that most sample SNe II are consistent with low circumstellar material (CSM) densities at the time of UV observations (e.g., $\dot M = 10^{-6}$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$, $v_w = 50$ km/s) and standard kinetic energies (e.g., $E_k = 0.6-1.2$ B), while two objects, SNe 2024faq and 2023ixf, show UV/optical evidence for interaction with more confined, higher-density CSM. SN 2023ixf and sample SNe IIn exhibit relatively featureless early-time UV spectra despite displaying prominent optical Lorentzian emission lines from electron scattering in optically thick CSM -- this being attributed to differing properties of UV resonance versus optical recombination transitions as well as intrinsic CSM asymmetries. These results demonstrate the potential of early-time UV spectroscopy to constrain the outermost SN ejecta structure, explosion energetics/composition, and progenitor mass-loss histories of core-collapse SNe.

title: Center anomalies without twists: torsion, exact degeneracies, and condensates
abstract: Mixed center anomalies are usually exposed by 't Hooft's twisted boundary conditions in a Hamiltonian formalism. On $\mathbb {RP}^3$, torsion makes the twist unnecessary: a center operator on the untwisted $SU(2)$ Hilbert space anticommutes with time reversal in Yang-Mills theory at $θ=π$ and with the chiral symmetry of super Yang-Mills theory, so every level is at least doubly degenerate. The relevant semiclassical object is the BPST instanton, which descends to a charge-$\tfrac12$ saddle on the orbifold $\mathbb R^4/\mathbb Z_2$. We complete it in two ways: applying a conformal transformation maps the orbifold to $\mathbb R\times\mathbb {RP}^3$, with the saddle describing the tunneling event between the two center sectors; by resolving the orbifold singularity, we obtain the Eguchi-Hanson space, which gives the gaugino condensate at its weak-coupling value.

title: Parametric and Universal Thouless Invariants in Matrix Product States
abstract: We investigate the classification of continuous families of translation-invariant injective matrix product states on an infinite chain, parametrized by a paracompact Hausdorff space $X$ and subject to a compact Hausdorff symmetry $G$. We construct an invariant for phases of such families, valued in $\check{H}^1(X;\widehat{G})$, that generalizes the known $\widehat{G}$ phase invariant for $G$-symmetric Thouless pumps. The phase invariant is constructed as the pullback to $X$ of a single universal Čech cohomology class on a classifying space of $G$-symmetric translation-invariant injective matrix product states. Several examples are given over various parameter spaces where this invariant is nontrivial.

title: Tunable Topological Charge Order in Magnetic Moiré Systems
abstract: Two-dimensional electrons in a strong magnetic field exhibit two seemingly incompatible ground states: incompressible quantum Hall liquids with a quantized Hall conductance, and electron crystals in which interactions drive the charge into ordered patterns. Moiré superlattices in transition-metal-dichalcogenide bilayers offer a tunable arena for this competition. Using neural quantum states (NQS) together with several methodological advances, we show how this competition unfolds. In particular, we demonstrate that the two end points are separated by an extended regime in which molecular charge order coexists with a quantized Hall response. We map the ground-state phase diagram of electrons at Landau-level filling $ν_B=1$ in the presence of a moiré superlattice potential, with three electrons per moiré cell. In the deep triangular potential limit, the electrons form the topologically trivial "Wigner molecular crystal'' of three-electron artificial atoms, a state recently imaged at zero magnetic field in moiré bilayers. As the potential depth is lowered, molecular charge order remains while quantized Hall response emerges. At the honeycomb point, where each cell contains three electrons and two degenerate moiré minima, wells are either singly or doubly occupied and the doublons provide an emergent Ising degree of freedom. Starting from modest interaction strength, we find short-range doublon correlations within the Chern insulator which grow with interaction strength and eventually break sublattice symmetry, forming a Néel CDW with long-range order between doublons. The topological molecular regime lies at twist angles and magnetic fields directly accessible to current experiments. The methodological advances presented provide a scalable framework for exploring a broad range of questions in correlated quantum matter in the presence of magnetic fields.

title: From active nests to fast wind gusts: Nested flux emergence as a precursor of persistent non-axisymmetric coronal holes
abstract: Recurring flux emergence within active nests reshapes the Sun's large-scale magnetic field and creates unipolar magnetic regions that can support coronal holes. The fast solar wind emerging from coronal holes drives space weather across the heliosphere. We investigated how the emergence of active nests at the peak of solar cycle 25 drove changes in global magnetic topology, coronal hole formation, and solar wind speed. Coronal holes were identified from composite SDO/AIA maps and their magnetic field properties were extracted from SDO/HMI magnetograms. Spherical harmonic decomposition quantified how magnetic flux was distributed at different spatial scales and was used to extrapolate the coronal field. We compared coronal structure with SOHO/LASCO-C2 observations and the solar wind measured at 1 au. Emerging magnetic flux within active nests rapidly surpassed the pre-existing magnetic flux in 2024, strengthening the non-axisymmetric field and shifting the corona into a tilted-dipole state. This dipolarisation stabilised the large-scale magnetic field, with the heliospheric current sheet anchored above active nests. Unipolar magnetic regions from the edges of active nests sustained non-axisymmetric coronal holes covering 6 to 14% of the solar surface in 2025, comparable to the 12% covered by polar coronal holes at solar minimum. Flux emergence near the tilted-dipole's negative pole returned the corona to a quadrupole-dominated state in 2026. Active nests helped stabilise the coronal magnetic field, while the decay and transport of unipolar magnetic flux sustained persistent, non-axisymmetric coronal holes. Differential rotation between unipolar regions triggered episodic expansion and contraction of the largest coronal holes. Early identification of specific active nest configurations, combined with the solar cycle phase, could improve the forecasting of coronal holes and fast solar wind.

title: Perturbative QCD Analysis for the Electric Dipole Moment of $Ξ$ and $Σ$ Hyperons from CP-Violating Dipole Interactions
abstract: Hyperon electric dipole moments (EDMs) probe CP-violating interactions beyond the Standard Model. Motivated by the recent BESIII measurement [Ablikim et al., Science 393, 1027] and the perturbative QCD analysis of the $Λ$ EDM form factor $d_Λ$ [Chen et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 051902], we extend the perturbative QCD calculation of the EDM form factor to the $Ξ$ and $Σ$ hyperons. We derive factorization formulas from quark EDM and chromoelectric dipole moment contributions in terms of leading-twist light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs). Using lattice-QCD results for the LCDAs and the strange-quark dipole moment ranges inferred from the BESIII $d_Λ$ bound and neutron EDM constraints, we obtain the conditional estimates $-4.8 \times 10^{-18} < d_{Ξ^-} < 1.8\times10^{-18}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $-6.1\times10^{-19} < d_{Σ^+} < 2.4\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ at the scale of ${J/ψ}$ mass. Dedicated searches at BESIII and the future Super Tau-Charm Factory could further constrain these quark-level sources of CP violation.

title: Restoring quantum neural network trainability through reusable calibration
abstract: Quantum neural networks (QNNs) rely on measured quantum observables to guide optimization, but hardware noise can suppress the parameter-dependent signals essential for learning. Here, we develop a structure-preserving error-mitigation framework that improves QNN trainability through reusable calibration of the quantum circuit's effective noise response. By calibrating a reference circuit with the same gate architecture as the trainable circuit, we construct regularized estimators of local quantum features that remain fixed throughout training. We quantify how calibration errors and response mismatches affect the recovery of both observables and their derivatives. Numerical simulations demonstrate enhanced loss-landscape contrast, faster convergence, and improved classification performance, and an IBM Quantum experiment confirms improved closed-loop variational optimization under hardware noise. We further demonstrate calibration reuse in a modular QNN comprising 25 independent four-qubit channels, corresponding to 100 qubits in aggregate. Our results establish reusable feature calibration as a practical approach to improving noise-limited quantum machine learning without repeated calibration at every training step.

title: Robust Passive Quantum Memory in Three Dimensions, Part I: Thermal and Zero-Temperature Perturbative Stability
abstract: Whether a three-dimensional quantum many-body system with geometrically local, bounded-degree interactions can passively protect encoded quantum information has remained a central open question since Kitaev introduced topological quantum computation. Passive protection requires stability against both thermal noise at nonzero temperature and generic static Hamiltonian perturbations Balasubramanian, Davydova, and Lin (BDL) recently established unperturbed three-dimensional thermal self-correction using a recursively defined family of stabilizer Hamiltonians. However, they left open whether their construction remains stable against quantum perturbations, even at zero temperature. In this paper, we show that a slight variant of the BDL code family achieves stability along both boundary axes of the perturbation-temperature phase diagram as the system size grows. Following BDL, in the absence of perturbation it is thermally stable below a critical temperature, achieving a stretched-exponentially long memory lifetime when coupled to any local Markovian thermal bath generated by single-site system-bath interactions satisfying detailed balance with bounded coupling rates. At zero temperature under arbitrary weak, superpolynomially decaying quantum perturbations, the family maintains a uniform bulk spectral gap, superpolynomially small ground-space splitting, and a superpolynomially long closed-system unitary memory lifetime for quasi-locally dressed logical observables. To prove this zero-temperature stability, we establish local topological quantum order across the multiscale hierarchy using a linearly dilated relaxation of the usual Bravyi-Hastings-Michalakis criteria. In the companion paper, we combine the tools developed here with finite-temperature worldline cluster expansions to establish passive self-correction throughout the phase diagram's positive-temperature perturbed interior.

title: Modular conjugations for thermal states and second worlds
abstract: The modular conjugation $J$ maps an algebra of observables onto its commutant. For the vacuum on a Rindler wedge it is a spacetime reflection, but for thermal states in two-dimensional CFTs the known expressions involve chiral fields at the complex points $x\pm iβ/2$, interpreted as belonging to a ``second world''. Here we compute $J$ for the geometric thermal state in explicit cyclic purifications, using either the vacuum vector, through the conformal map to a Rindler wedge, or a vector in the natural cone of a local algebra. The modular images are then fields at real points, and complex coordinates arise only when operators of the commutant outside the image of the thermal representation are written as fields on the original spacetime. For the chiral $U(1)$ current we also purify by doubling the Fock space, obtain explicit formulas for $J$, show that this purification coincides with Sorce's canonical purification, and treat all primary thermal states.

title: From Top to Bottom: Quark Mass Hierarchies in Heterotic String Theory
abstract: Standard Model fermion masses exhibit large hierarchies, spanning more than five orders of magnitude in the quark sector alone. In this paper, we study whether these hierarchies can be generated perturbatively at tree level in smooth heterotic Calabi-Yau compactifications, where the supergravity approximation remains under computational control. In such backgrounds, physical Yukawa couplings combine holomorphic superpotential integrals with matter field Kahler metrics. The former can be computed algebraically, while the latter require solving a coupled system of partial differential equations for the Ricci-flat metric, Hermitian Yang-Mills connections, and harmonic bundle-valued forms. Within this framework, we identify two new tree-level mechanisms by which complex structure moduli can generate fermion mass hierarchies and show analytically and numerically that both mechanisms are obstructed for previously studied tetra-quadric models. Motivated by these obstructions, we scan the existing databases of tens of thousands of complete intersection Calabi-Yau line bundle models and find a unique smooth quotient admitting a rank-three up-quark Yukawa matrix at tree level. Evaluating the physical couplings on this manifold and evolving them under the renormalization group, we obtain realistic mass hierarchies for the top, charm, up, and bottom quarks in the smooth supergravity regime.

title: Mapping the multimessenger horizon for $γ$-ray counterparts of cosmic neutrinos
abstract: The joint detection of high-energy neutrinos and $γ$-rays offers a powerful probe of the most energetic astrophysical accelerators, linking hadronic interactions to observable signatures across cosmic distances. Understanding the conditions under which these two messengers can be simultaneously observed is essential for identifying and characterizing the sources of cosmic neutrinos. In this work, we examine the detectability of $γ$-ray cascades associated with neutrino production in source environments that are gamma-ray transparent, focusing on how electromagnetic cascades evolve as $γ$-rays propagate through intergalactic space. By modeling photon interactions with the extragalactic background light and deflections in intergalactic magnetic fields, we determine the minimum neutrino fluence for transient emission and neutrino flux for steady emission required to produce a $γ$-ray counterpart detectable by $γ$-ray observatories, such as Fermi-LAT, HAWC, or LHAASO. This defines a ``multimessenger horizon" -- the region in flux-distance parameter space where neutrinos and $γ$-rays are jointly observable. We consider both energy-binned injection tied to IceCube's sensitivity and a continuous power-law spectrum extending from TeV to PeV energies. Our results reveal that detectability depends strongly on redshift, magnetic field strength, and photon energy, with higher-energy cascades suffering greater attenuation inside filamentary structures. The framework provides new constraints on source opacity, baryon loading, and neutrino production mechanisms, offering a predictive tool for interpreting current events and guiding future multimessenger campaigns.

title: Loss-Tolerant Quantum Correlations Between Atomic and Photonic Qubits
abstract: Quantum physics forbids cloning of a qubit. Therefore, a qubit is irreversibly lost upon loss of the information carrier. To mitigate this physical loss, it has been proposed to distribute the logical information across an entangled set of physical qubits, some of which can be lost. Previous experiments illustrated this concept, but failed to demonstrate a gain in the information-retrieval efficiency. Here we address this challenge with photons for which the total loss, from generation to detection, is below the loss-tolerance threshold of $50\%$. Using two single-atom emitters in an optical cavity, we encode information into the photons of a graph state and observe an efficiency gain for retrieving quantum correlations between the atoms and the photons for single-qubit measurements in the Pauli $X$ and $Z$ bases. Although technical errors reduce the probability to obtain the \textit{correct} result, we achieve average fidelities as high as $\gtrsim\!70\%$ without and $\gtrsim\!75\%$ with error detection, demonstrating entanglement between the atomic and encoded photonic qubits. Lowering the encoding errors is a next natural step toward loss-tolerant photonic quantum-information processing.

title: Giant gravitons without giant gravitons
abstract: We demonstrate that the partition function of a free bosonic $U(N)$ multi-matrix model admits a giant graviton expansion. For $d$ matrices, there are $d$ distinct giant gravitons, and the expansion can be characterized by a $d$-node quiver with bifundamentals connecting the nodes. This suggests the intriguing possibility of a more generalized holography where models without any obvious gravitational dual can nevertheless be given a dual brane interpretation. The giant graviton expansion of this multi-matrix model is somewhat unconventional though, as the giant graviton partition functions will necessarily have intrinsic $N$-dependence.

title: XQR30: ALMA Observations Reveal the Diverse Structure of Cold Gas within z>6 Quasar Host Galaxies
abstract: We present 0.25(~1.5kpc) ALMA observations of the [CII] and dust continuum emission from the host galaxies of 24 luminous z~6 quasars. Together with archival data from 17 quasars, this constitutes a nearly complete sample of all quasars with J-band magnitudes of J_AB<20.0 and redshifts between 5.8 and 6.6, which are the limits defined in the VLT/XSHOOTER legacy survey, XQR-30. For the full sample of 41 quasars, we find that 39(95%) of the quasar host galaxies are detected in [CII] emission with [CII] luminosities ranging between (0.3 and 9.2)x10^9Lsun, and 39(95%) of the quasar host galaxies are detected in continuum emission with continuum flux densities ranging between 0.22 and 16.3mJy. We detect eight [CII]-emitting companion galaxies, which is consistent with the expected number of galaxies based on clustering results. We find that z~6 quasar host galaxies have a range of morphologies, and by defining a new parameter, the kinematic position angle alignment parameter, Delta_PA_{kin-CII}, we show that most quasar host galaxies deviate from a standard disk model. This suggests that [CII] emission probes structures beyond simple disk rotation, such as bars, tidally disturbed gas, etc. We show that the dust emission is more compact than the [CII] emission independent of the morphology of the galaxy. Finally, we provide rough dynamical mass estimates within twice the [CII] half-light radius for the majority of the galaxies, and show that the average dynamical mass within the inner few kpc is consistent with estimates of the average mass in stars, gas and the SMBH.

title: The Impact of Seeding Threshold on Wandering Black Hole Populations and Merger Rates
abstract: Cosmological simulations following massive black holes (MBHs) with dynamical friction subgrid models predict hundreds to thousands of off-centre, wandering MBHs in massive galaxies. We investigate how the wandering MBH population changes with halo mass seeding threshold. We present cosmological zoom-in simulations of a $(15\,\mathrm{cMpc})^3$ volume to $z=2$, using the halo mass seeding thresholds of ASTRID, EAGLE and Illustris-TNG $(5\times10^{9}-5\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}/h)$, with a fixed MBH seed mass of $m_\mathrm{seed}=2\times10^{6}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}/h$. The subgrid dynamical friction model for MBHs switches to accurate integration around MBHs using the \textsc{ketju} module above $m_{\bullet} \geq 2\times10^{7}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}/h$. We find that the seeding threshold greatly affects the MBH population: the number of seeded MBHs varies by a factor of ten and the number of wandering MBHs in the most massive galaxy ($M_\star=4.4\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) varies from 2 to 115. An MBH can become a wanderer in two ways. Interactions with other galaxies can offset a central MBH in low-mass galaxies ($M_\star\sim10^{8}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) if seeded in low mass halos $(\lesssim10^{10}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot/h)$. Alternatively, wandering MBHs can be added through mergers. The growth of the most massive MBHs is insensitive to the seeding threshold. While the total number of MBH mergers varies by an order of magnitude, the number of massive dynamically resolved MBH mergers differs by most a factor of $\sim3$ between seeding thresholds. The dynamically resolved binaries coalesce typically on timescales of $\sim10-250\,\mathrm{Myr}$ after becoming bound.

title: Analytic next-to-leading order electroweak corrections to Higgs boson pair production in the forward limit
abstract: We calculate next-to-leading order electroweak corrections for Higgs boson pair production in the gluon fusion channel, in the forward limit. We perform an analytic calculation and obtain a final result for the partonic cross section that depends explicitly on all kinematic parameters and particle masses. We describe our method, which can be readily applied to similar processes. We observe rapid convergence within the validity range of the forward expansion. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the entire phase space can be covered when this approach is combined with the high-energy expansion.

title: NEMESIS: Exoplanet TraNsit SurvEy of Nearby M-dwarfs in TESS FFIS II - 262 Transiting Planet Candidates from the TESS Primary Mission
abstract: We present NEMESIS II, a blind transit search of nearby M-dwarfs in TESS Primary Mission full-frame images (Sectors 1-26), including stars lacking 2-minute observations. Using the open-source NEMESIS pipeline, we extracted, detrended, and searched 213,658 single-sector light curves of 113,047 M-dwarfs within 100 pc, yielding 23,339 threshold crossing events. Automated LEO-Vetter vetting, applied identically to the survey and its injection-recovery and orbit-scrambling controls, retains 558 detections corresponding to 525 distinct signals with converged transit fits and periods of 0.51-9.10 days. Of these, 482 lie on stars without TOI, CTOI, or NASA Exoplanet Archive transiting-planet entries. Orbit-scrambling predicts 329 false alarms among the 558 detections, all but 14 of them among the 408 below Multiple Event Statistic 8. Assuming an astrophysical signal, TRICERATOPS favors a planetary origin for 262 of 525 candidates (232 new), which we classify as planet candidates; it also excludes resolved-neighbor eclipses for 105. Known planets and TOI candidates survive vetting at 1.01 +/- 0.07 of the injection-predicted rate. Correcting for each light curve's sensitivity, false alarms, and astrophysical false positives, we infer 0.81 +/- 0.44 planets per star for periods between 1.0-10.0 days and planet radii between 0.5-11.0 Earth radii. This is a lower limit, because our injections recover few or no planets near and below 1 Earth radii and assume central transits. Light curves, catalogs, vetting reports, and injection-recovery results will be released as a High Level Science Product at MAST upon publication. Documentation for the NEMESIS pipeline is available at https://nemesis-tess.readthedocs.io/.

title: Distrustful entanglement-based Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is the one of the most explored application of quantum information theory. While practical QKD systems are being deployed around the world, a major issue of these setups are that one has to trust the measurement devices of both parties. On the other hand, the most secure among such schemes are called device-independent (DI) QKD protocols, where no component of the setup is assumed to be trusted. However, due to their high technological demand, their loophole-free version currently remain out of practical reach. Inspired by the real world, we consider the traditional QKD in a distrustful measurement setting, that is, the measurement devices can only be trusted upto some level of confidence, which might still be large but not completely trusted. We then derive a general lower bound on the asymptotic key rate in this scenario. Then considering perfect detectors and source, and the entanglement-based BB84 (BBM) protocol, we show that to obtain secure keys one needs to trust their devices more than 92 %. However, we observe that such a protocol can not be realised with any level of distrust using the realistic detectors and sources at the current technology. Finally, we also consider the BBM protocol with arbitrary dimensional systems and observe that they are more robust to distrust than qubit systems. Consequently, with the same level of distrust, along with same detector and source efficiences, one can get better key rates with high-dimensional systems.

title: The phase gradient spectrum: probing the squeezed bispectrum of the 21-cm signal during reionization
abstract: The 21-cm signal from the epoch of reionization is highly non-Gaussian. Standard analyses rely on the power spectrum, which is blind to the Fourier phases, while higher-order statistics such as the bispectrum are computationally expensive and spread information across triangle configurations. As an efficient alternative, we develop the \textit{phase gradient spectrum}, which measures the circular coherence of phase differences between Fourier modes separated by a long-wavelength mode. We show analytically that this statistic measures the angle-averaged normalised squeezed bispectrum, which describes the response of small-scale power to long-wavelength fluctuations. Applied to reionization simulations with different ionizing source properties, the phase gradient spectrum of the 21-cm signal shows a characteristic non-monotonic evolution. At early times, the spectrum tracks the non-Gaussianity of the matter density field. Once the mean neutral fraction $\langle x_\mathrm{HI}\rangle \lesssim 0.9$, the spectrum follows the ionization topology. The phase coherence reaches a minimum midway through reionization and rises again as the remaining neutral regions shrink into isolated islands. Statistics that keep the sign of the squeezed bispectrum show that this minimum marks its sign change. This evolution holds for different reionization models and simulation frameworks. A Fisher forecast for a 1000-h Square Kilometre Array (SKA)-Low observation, combining five redshifts across reionization, shows that the phase gradient spectrum alone constrains the astrophysical parameters, and these constraints tighten by a factor of $\gtrsim 2$ for a 10,000-h observation. Combining the phase gradient spectrum with the power spectrum tightens the marginalised constraints by up to $\sim$20 per cent relative to the power spectrum alone.

title: Diverse Stellar Components Resolved by JWST in the Massive Galaxy SPT0311-58
abstract: SPT0311$-$58 is comprised of two clumpy dusty star-forming galaxies inhabiting a $z=6.9$ protocluster core. Within a $16$ kpc diameter, there are 26 spectroscopically confirmed members. The 12 highly dust-obscured clumps were identified by their rest-frame [CII] emission, and the 14 less obscured clumps in the rest-frame ultraviolet (UV). We present new NIRCam and MIRI imaging from JWST of the central regions, which respectively trace the rest-frame UV and near-infrared. Combining this imaging with supplementary data from the Hubble Space Telescope and Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) provides the most complete picture of SPT0311$-$58 to date. Using 14 photometric bands and ALMA dust continuum to model the spectral energy distribution of SPT0311$-$58, we present well-informed stellar masses and star-formation rates (SFR) on local ($\sim1.5$ kpc) and global scales. We find that SPT0311$-$58 has a total stellar mass of $M_\star=3.2^{+3.2}_{-1.6}\times10^{11}\, M_\odot$ and SFR of $1.5^{+0.89}_{-0.53}\times10^3\, M_\odot\, \text{yr}^{-1}$. We compare these measurements to simulations and known, rare classes of high-redshift objects observed by JWST, namely massive $z\approx6$--$8.5$ Lyman-break galaxies, $z>6$ quasars, and other merging/clumpy $z\sim6$--$7$ systems. SPT0311$-$58 is comparable to $z>6$ quasars in both stellar mass and SFR, but is more extreme than the other reference populations for both quantities. Additionally, we compare our measurements with the star-formation histories (SFH) of five massive quiescent galaxies from the Early eXtragalactic Continuum and Emission Line Science (EXCELS) survey. We find that SPT0311$-$58 has a higher SFR than expected from the SFHs of the EXCELS galaxies at $z=6.9$, but is otherwise a plausible progenitor to massive quiescent galaxies.

title: Radiation Response of NbN Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detectors Under $^{210}$Po Alpha-Particle Irradiation
abstract: Superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) are attractive for space applications because they combine high detection efficiency, low noise, and fast timing, but their radiation tolerance remains less established than that of conventional semiconductor detectors. Here we study NbN SNSPDs exposed to alpha-particle $^{210}$Po irradiation by combining cryogenic electrical and photon-counting measurements with SRIM and Geant4 radiation-transport calculations. For the estimated fluence corresponding to the 200-hour $^{210}$Po exposure, the air-inclusive Geant4 calculation predicts an average ionizing dose of 8.49 Mrad in the active NbN layer and a displacement-damage estimate of $5.67 \times 10^{-7}$ displacements per atom. Measurements before and after irradiation show no systematic degradation of the superconducting transition, switching current, retrapping current, dark-count behavior, or photon-count response. These results indicate radiation resilience of thin-film NbN SNSPDs under a multi-Mrad alpha-particle exposure and support their use in photon-counting systems for radiation environments.

title: A new angle on coherence-violating logarithms in color-singlet processes
abstract: We introduce a new formulation for the resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the transverse energy flow in rapidity gaps in the Drell-Yan process. Our formalism allows us to resum coherence-violating logarithms in the gap cross section in the phenomenologically important regime where the gap size is comparable to the logarithm of the transverse energy. In the formal small gap limit, our result reduces to the known state-of-the-art resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the Drell-Yan process. However, we identify sizable new corrections even for moderate gap widths that significantly modify the phenomenological picture for LHC applications. This work will form an important element of future extensions to a range of global and non-global observables.

title: $B\to K a$ decays in QCD factorization and revised bounds on ALP couplings
abstract: Rare flavor-changing processes such as $B\to K a$ offer sensitive probes of axion-like particles (ALPs) for masses below a few GeV. We study this process in the framework of QCD factorization and ALP effective theory, in which the ALP couples to the Standard Model (SM) fermions through shift-invariant derivative interactions. In contrast to previous studies, where flavor violation arises solely from flavor-changing ALP couplings, we also include the contributions proportional to flavor-conserving ALP couplings, in which the flavor change is mediated by the weak interactions of the SM. Based on this analysis, we derive upper bounds on both flavor-changing and flavor-conserving ALP couplings at low energies. Then we consider the UV scenario of a "minimally flavor-violating ALP", which features flavor-universal ALP-fermion couplings at very high energies, and evaluate the resulting constraints on the UV couplings.

title: AI Scientist Discovered Robust Quantum Control
abstract: Protecting quantum coherence is a central theme of modern quantum technologies. Carefully designed control pulses can extend coherence by suppressing disorder and unwanted interactions. However, designing robust pulse sequences remains challenging in interacting multi-level systems, where multiple independent error channels must be controlled in the presence of experimental imperfections. Here we introduce QORA, a multi-agent artificial intelligence framework that integrates theoretical reasoning, automated experimental calibration and control for closed-loop discovery of quantum control sequences. Applied to a dense ensemble of spin-1 nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond, QORA discovers AID-ROD, a series of AI-discovered sequences that nearly double the measured spin coherence time relative to the state-of-the-art human-designed sequence DROID-C3PO. Subsequence analysis by human researchers reveals a hierarchy of error suppression: 18-pulse blocks suppress linear and quadratic onsite disorder and common-mode drive-amplitude errors, while their arrangement over a longer cycle reduces dipolar interactions, providing a physical explanation for the observed improvement and robustness in AID-ROD. These results demonstrate AI-guided experimental discovery of robust quantum control and identify a design strategy for protecting coherence in interacting multi-level systems beyond qubits.

title: Margin Dynamics for Large Language Model Alignment
abstract: Practitioners choose among LLM alignment methods largely by trial and error. We provide a theoretical foundation: each pairwise method defines a vector field on the probability simplex that governs how the model redistributes mass between preferred and dispreferred completions. Projecting onto a single preferred/dispreferred pair reduces this to a one-dimensional margin ODE with a closed-form solution. These solutions reveal that DPO margins grow without bound (logarithmically as $O(\log t)$ in the gradient-flow limit) while IPO margins converge to a finite $1/(2τ)$; that label noise induces a qualitative phase transition in DPO (unbounded $\to$ bounded) but affects IPO only quantitatively; and that gradient concentration under asymmetric weighting governs trainability at scale. We confirm all three predictions across five model families spanning four benchmarks. The closed-form solutions also enable principled method design: we prove that adding any label smoothing $\varepsilon > 0$ to SimPO creates a finite margin attractor at $Δ^* = β^{-1}\log((1-\varepsilon)/\varepsilon)$, while $\varepsilon = 0$ (standard SimPO) has no attractor. We test this across three models (8B-9B) and confirm the prediction: the theory-derived configuration (TPO-S, $\varepsilon = 0.05$) is competitive with the strongest baselines, attaining the highest mean IFEval score among the compared methods on all three, validating that the predicted finite attractor is a usable operating point rather than proposing a new state-of-the-art loss.

title: Existence of a third self-similar solution of the Yang--Mills equation in high even dimensions
abstract: We prove that the spherically symmetric $SO(d)$ Yang--Mills equation admits a third smooth self-similar profile, in addition to the two known explicit profiles, in every even dimension $d\geq 12$. This complements the analogous existence theorem in odd dimensions $d\geq 11$ (arXiv:2610.36784). In contrast to the odd-dimensional case, where the classification of smooth self-similar profiles reduces to counting roots of an explicit resonance polynomial [Phys. Rev. D 114, 064021 (2026)], the even-dimensional proof requires solving a nonlinear connection problem. In $d=10$, where one explicit profile degenerates to the zero solution, we give a formal argument for the existence of a second nontrivial smooth profile in addition to the single nontrivial explicit one.

title: Quantum Reference Frames, Locality, and Microcausality in Quantum Field Theory
abstract: As a consequence of the relativistic spectrum condition, quantum reference frames for translations on Minkowski space are never described by projection-valued measures, and in many cases fail a weaker spacetime localisation property known as the norm-$1$ condition. This has several implications for the local and observable structure of quantum field theories described relative to even the best available frame: for a large class of frame states, strict locality is replaced by almost locality, and microcausality by commutators that decay rapidly with increasing separation, corresponding to an effective smearing of the light cone by the localisation density of the frame state. Operations built from finitely many almost local Kraus operators, for example nonselective measurements of relativised local observables, satisfy an approximate no-signalling bound, with a residue attributable to the localisation uncertainty of the frame. Whether causality in its strongest operational form -- non-disturbance under all physically realisable operations -- survives relativisation is left open. An upshot of our finding is that quantum field theories formulated relative to a quantum reference frame cannot rest on the traditional axioms, and some general relational axiomatisation must replace at least some of them by taking into account physically realistic properties of the frame.

title: Learning Calibrated and Samplable Predictive Distributions of Surface-Ocean $Δp$CO$_2$ Using Tabular Diffusion Models
abstract: The ocean absorbs almost 30% of anthropogenic CO$_2$ emissions, but quantifying this sink requires estimating surface-ocean CO$_2$ from observations that are sparse in space and time. Most existing machine-learning estimates of this field are deterministic, giving a single value per grid point, with uncertainty approximated post hoc via residuals, ensembles, or prescribed distributions. We instead learn a conditional predictive distribution for each observation: using Treeffuser, a conditional diffusion model with gradient-boosted-tree score functions, we estimate the full predictive distribution of $Δp$CO$_2$ (the sea-air $p$CO$_2$ difference) from 13 environmental, spatial, and temporal predictors. On a held-out SOCAT test set, Treeffuser attains the lowest continuous ranked probability score among the uncertainty-quantification methods evaluated (8.229 $μ$atm) and the coverage closest to the nominal 68% / 95% levels (0.686 / 0.930), while retaining point-prediction skill comparable to a deterministic XGBoost baseline (RMSE 18.4 vs. 17.7 $μ$atm; $R^2$ 0.77 vs. 0.79). These results show that conditional diffusion can provide well-calibrated, observation-level uncertainties while largely preserving point-prediction skill. Because Treeffuser is generative, its samples can support probabilistic analyses of $Δp$CO$_2$; extending this to spatially coherent field reconstruction will require modeling dependence across grid cells and evaluation on spatially held-out data.

title: A Science Traceability Matrix for Micro-arcsecond Resolution X-ray Imaging
abstract: Our ability to understand the highest energy processes and environments in astronomy is directly tied to our ability to probe their physical processes at the smallest scales. Despite transformative progress in high-angular resolution instruments across the radio through optical, angular resolution within the X-rays has plateaued around $\sim0.1-1''$, and therefore our window into the innermost regions of the high energy Universe lies primarily within spectral, timing, and/or polarimetric studies rather than direct imaging. This represents a significant barrier to gaining a robust understanding of key science questions, including the mechanisms of accretion and jet launching, the accretion activity and angular momentum losses of binary active galactic nuclei (AGN) leading to gravitational wave events, and the space weather events that may influence atmospheric evolution and prebiotic chemistry on potentially habitable exoplanets. The Accretion Explorer Interferometer (AEI) is a mission concept for X-ray imaging that could achieve up to $μ$as resolution, $\sim5-6$ orders of magnitude better than current instrumentation. Here we present the scientific discovery space enabled by such an advance, and highlight areas of uncertainty and open questions that are critical to investigate for future development of this concept.

title: An Open-Source da Vinci X/Xi Instrument Module for Laparoscopic Surgery Research
abstract: Studying electrosurgical tasks on a research robot requires control of both instrument motion and energy activation, along with a record of when each action occurs. This paper presents an open-source module for da Vinci X/Xi instruments on a UR5/UR5e robotic arm. Five motors transmit torque through timing belts to spring-loaded drive discs. An electrosurgical interposer accepts software commands, gives the surgeon's foot pedals priority, and records the source of each activation request. In bench testing, the interposer recorded all 12 activation and deactivation events from six pedal presses. Ex vivo demonstrations included monopolar and bipolar coagulation of splenic tissue and monopolar cutting during gallbladder dissection. Optical tracking of the Fenestrated Bipolar Forceps showed that calibration brought pitch and yaw gains from 0.904 and 1.14 to 1.00 and 1.02, respectively. The module enables researchers to record instrument motion, video, and the timing and source of electrosurgical commands during laparoscopic tasks.

title: Boxes in Infinite Words: Complexity, Automata, and Point Modules
abstract: Motivated by the geometry of point modules over monomial algebras, we introduce a box-counting function associated to a right-infinite word over a finite alphabet. An extendable box is a family of finite words obtained by choosing letters independently at each position, subject to the condition that all choices admit a common infinite right continuation in the associated subshift. We prove several results for these functions for words of linearly bounded complexity. For $k$-automatic words, we show using techniques from first-order logic that the total box-counting function is $k$-regular. Finally, we apply our results to prove eventual affine growth of the number of positive-dimensional irreducible components in finite projections of point-module spaces associated to semiprime monomial algebras of at most quadratic growth.

title: Hidden convexity of the Eliashberg condensation energy: existence, uniqueness and continuity of the superconducting state
abstract: Kiessling, Altshuler and Yuzbashyan conjectured the thermodynamic transition picture for the isotropic Eliashberg spin-chain functional with vanishing Coulomb pseudopotential: the normal state is the unique minimizer above and at a critical temperature, the superconducting minimizer below it is unique up to gauge, and the transition is continuous. We establish the nonlinear part of this picture. In the variables $ρ_n=\sin^2θ_n$, the condensation energy restricted to the first quadrant is strictly convex, and folding any admissible chain into that quadrant cannot increase its energy. For every positive, non-increasing interaction with power-law decay, hidden convexity and a compactness estimate give existence and uniqueness of the minimizer up to gauge. The normal state minimizes the energy exactly when its quadratic form is non-negative, including marginal stability. Among admissible chains, a positive solution of the nonlinear Eliashberg equations exists exactly when the normal state is linearly unstable and is then unique. For temperature-dependent families with pointwise continuity and locally uniform decay bounds, the minimizing density is continuous in a weighted $\ell^1$ norm. Together with uniqueness of the linear-stability temperature, these results prove the thermodynamic conjectures for the $γ$-model, Einstein phonons and general phonon spectra; the phonon applications use separately established spectral input. Finite-dimensional algebraic and convex-analytic components are machine-checked in Lean. The proofs were obtained independently of concurrent work that reaches overlapping conclusions.

title: Binary black-hole mergers with ultralight vector bosons
abstract: We simulate the inspiral, merger, and ringdown of equal-mass, nonspinning binary black holes coupled to a massive vector (Proca) field. Starting from constraint-consistent electric-field initial data, we find that the Proca field rapidly concentrates around the black holes. However, it continues to exhibit nontrivial dynamics. Orbital evolution depends on vector mass, while the dominant gravitational waveforms remain close to vacuum after time, phase, and amplitude alignment. This contrast highlights the limited imprint of the field on aligned merger-ringdown morphology at these resolutions.

title: Rule-based curation and validation in batch fermentation of a genome-scale metabolic model of the mycoprotein fungus Fusarium venenatum A3/5
abstract: Sustainable protein supply is a central food-system challenge, and mycoprotein from Fusarium venenatum is an established, low-impact option. Its production relies on refined glucose, and yields on lower-cost feedstocks are normally found by fermentation. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) can estimate these yields before any experiment, but to our knowledge none has been published for this fungus, and models transferred from related species inherit template errors. Here we built iJL1143, a GEM of strain A3/5, from an Aspergillus niger model and curated it with rules based on homology, thermodynamics and the literature. We compared it with the uncurated Draft model in four oxygen-enriched batch fermentations on glucose and fructose. Thermodynamic directionality rules and the direction of the mitochondrial GTP/GDP carrier brought the maximum ATP yield of the Draft model within the theoretical range. As a result, with sequential sugar uptake and no fitted parameters, the mean final-biomass discrepancy fell from 20% for the Draft model to 6% for iJL1143. Sequential uptake and a fitted lag time also reduced its biomass time-course error from 4.88 to 0.42 g/L. In oxygen-enriched batch fermentation, iJL1143 can therefore estimate obtainable biomass before fermentation, which could reduce the experiments needed to develop lower-cost mycoprotein.

title: Actions of quantum groups: the standard implementation and relatively invariant weights
abstract: We establish a characterisation of the standard implementation for actions of locally compact quantum groups on von Neumann algebras, extending results of Daws-Skalski-Viselter and Haagerup. As a consequence, we prove that taking the standard implementation respects morphisms of quantum groups. We also prove that several natural conditions expressing relative $ρ$-invariance for n.s.f. weights are equivalent.

title: LLMs as Validators for Cross-Chain Bridges: Evaluating Source-Level and Transaction-Level Attack Detection on Solana
abstract: Cross-chain bridges have suffered substantial asset losses due to vulnerabilities in their on-chain programs. On Solana, missing validation checks can enable exploits even when the underlying blockchain operates correctly. The ability of large language models (LLMs) to diagnose these flaws from source code or transaction records, rather than merely raise alarms, remains insufficiently understood. We implement a native Rust lock-and-mint bridge on a local Solana validator with four exploitable variants: two model flaws from the Cashio and Wormhole incidents, while the other two represent vulnerability classes documented in Solana security audits. Paired vulnerable and secure programs, together with successful attacks, benign sessions, and blocked attempts, allow us to distinguish correct diagnoses from unsupported alarms. We evaluate six configurations of five open-weight models across 16,800 responses, compare source inputs with and without comments, and grade 7,200 answers on vulnerable inputs using two blinded LLM graders. The results reveal substantial differences across conditions: without comments, models diagnose 24% of vulnerable source inputs while frequently flagging the secure bridge. Transaction diagnosis is high for the missing-signer scenario but averages 6% across the other three scenarios. Original comments, some of which describe the flaw, increase source diagnosis to 60%. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing correct vulnerability diagnoses from unsupported alarms in bridge security review.

title: Transient State Preservation of a Dissipative Qubit via Lyapunov Control
abstract: Preserving quantum states in the presence of environmental decoherence remains a fundamental challenge for quantum information processing. This work investigates whether Hamiltonian Lyapunov feedback can transiently preserve the state of an open qubit by reshaping its trajectory under Markovian dissipation. A state-error Lyapunov function is adopted to derive an analytical feedback law for Lindblad dynamics, ensuring a nonincreasing Lyapunov function whenever the control sensitivities are nonzero. The analysis identifies the geometric conditions under which the feedback becomes ineffective, showing that control authority vanishes when the current and target Bloch vectors are collinear. Numerical simulations are performed for amplitude damping and pure dephasing using selected target states. Performance is evaluated through fidelity, accumulated infidelity, dwell time above a fidelity threshold, coherence, and control effort. The results demonstrate that the proposed feedback cannot eliminate irreversible dissipation or achieve universal asymptotic stabilization, but it can provide transient benefits for selected target-channel combinations. In particular, under amplitude damping, the controller significantly reduces accumulated infidelity and substantially extends the interval during which the system remains above a prescribed fidelity threshold. In the pure dephasing cases examined, improvements in fidelity are generally limited, although transient coherence preservation is observed for the oblique target considered, revealing a trade-off between coherence and state fidelity.
