These findings indicate that Lyapunov-based Hamiltonian feedback is best suited as a transient preservation mechanism and motivate its application to gate operations and preservation of prepared states during finite time intervals before their use or readout.

title: Cross-correlating the SPHEREx extragalactic background light with CMB lensing I: theoretical predictions and forecasts
abstract: The near-infrared extragalactic background light (EBL), which SPHEREx maps in 102 spectral channels, holds the emission lines of galaxies on top of a much brighter continuum from the integrated galaxy light (IGL) and the intrahalo light (IHL). Cross-correlating these maps with the lensing of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) isolates the emission that traces the matter, unbiased by uncorrelated foregrounds. The lines face two obstacles. Filtering along the line of sight removes the long radial modes that carry the cross-correlation, and the extragalactic continuum, a signal in its own right, is a correlated foreground for the lines. We forecast the detectability of all EBL components, in a common halo-model framework, for the SPHEREx deep fields and all-sky survey with lensing maps at the sensitivity level of Planck and the Simons Observatory (SO). Without filtering, and with all amplitudes fitted jointly, the cross-correlation with Planck lensing detects the IGL at $9σ$ in the deep fields, but not the lines. In the all-sky survey, it measures the IGL and IHL amplitudes to $1.0\%$ and $3\%$ and detects the five lines, fitted as one template, at $4.6σ$. With SO lensing, these become $0.6\%$, $1.6\%$ and $7.4σ$. In these joint fits, a filter removing radial modes longer than about $600$ Mpc costs every component $90\%$ or more of its signal-to-noise ratio, so the lines are reached by fitting the continuum, not by filtering it. These values assume a known spectral shape of the continuum. Calibrating it with the continuum's auto-spectra keeps the lines at $7.3$--$7.4σ$; fitting it from the cross-spectrum alone leaves $1.4$--$2.3σ$. The line detections vary by a factor of seven to eleven across line models. The cross-correlation is thus a robust probe of the IGL and a viable route to the emission lines, provided the continuum is modeled across the channels.

title: Cross-correlating the SPHEREx extragalactic background light with CMB lensing II: theoretical predictions confronted with lightcone simulations
abstract: Cross-correlating intensity maps with the lensing of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) rejects the foregrounds and noise that do not trace the dark matter. In the near infrared, the remaining signal combines the integrated galaxy light (IGL), the intrahalo light (IHL) and several emission lines. Accurate modeling of all three is essential to forecast detectability and interpret measurements. We present simulated SPHEREx intensity maps of all three on a lightcone, painted on halos from the Hidden Valley $N$-body simulation, and the CMB-lensing convergence of the same lightcone, over $100\,{\rm deg}^2$ to $z \approx 6$. We assign each halo its lines and continuum by stellar-population synthesis, in two models whose metallicities are fixed or follow its stellar mass. Halo-model predictions from the simulation's luminosity-halo mass relations and measured clustering, without free parameters, match the auto-spectra of the IGL and lines, and their cross-spectra with lensing, across the band: at $2.2\,μ$m, to within $5\%$ above $\ell \approx 400$ and $7\%$ above $\ell = 200$, respectively. The agreement requires nonlinear clustering: linear theory describes the cross-spectrum of a line up to $\ell \approx 1000$-$1600$ at $2.2\,μ$m, but fails for the IGL and the convergence at multipoles of a few hundred. With the noise of a SPHEREx deep field and of Simons Observatory lensing, the unfiltered cross-spectra, each component taken alone, reach signal-to-noise ratios of $9$-$21$ for the lines, $20$ for the IGL and $15$ for the IHL. A filter that removes radial modes longer than about $600$ Mpc keeps $62\%$ of the IGL's signal-to-noise and at most $20\%$ of the lines', with fitted amplitudes within about $1σ$ of the predictions before and after filtering. The emission model changes a channel's intensity by up to a factor of three, but the line detectability only by tens of percent.

title: Beyond Reconstruction: A Unified Framework for Trustworthy and Explainable EEG Artifact Removal Evaluation
abstract: Deep-learning methods have achieved strong performance in EEG artifact removal, but evaluation remains dominated by reconstruction metrics such as error, correlation, and signal-to-noise ratio. Although these metrics assess similarity to clean EEG, they do not establish whether models effectively suppress artifacts, preserve neural activity, or provide reliable explanations. To address these limitations, we propose TriX-EEG, a three-level framework for trustworthy and explainable EEG artifact removal. Level 1, Signal Validity (SV), evaluates reconstruction quality and neural band-power preservation. Level 2, Removal Faithfulness (RF), assesses the removed component through artifact error and residual artifact/neural leakage. Level 3, Explanation Reliability (ER), examines model behavior through temporal alignment, causal relevance, and stability. We evaluate TriX-EEG using nine published neural denoisers across three public benchmarks derived from EEGDenoiseNet and the PhysioNet Motion Artifact Contaminated EEG Dataset, covering EOG, EMG, and motion artifacts. Results show that reconstruction metrics alone are insufficient for trustworthy denoiser assessment: RF complements it by revealing whether errors stem from residual artifact or suppressed neural activity, while ER captures distinct aspects of explanation behavior, supporting joint evaluation of three aspects within a unified framework rather than reliance on any single factor. External validation on an independent EEG/EOG dataset and the BCI Competition IV-2a motor-imagery dataset further demonstrates broadly consistent rankings under dataset shift. Higher-ranked denoisers generally preserve more task-relevant information or cause less downstream performance degradation. Overall, TriX-EEG provides a comprehensive basis for EEG denoiser assessment, encouraging models that are not only accurate but also faithful and explainable.

title: Every Camera Grows Up: Camera-Height Regression in Interactive Video World Models
abstract: Interactive video world models serve as simulators for embodied agents: from a starting image and an action trajectory, they generate the views the agent would see. The starting image fixes how high the camera is, for example 0.15 m for a floor robot or 2.2 m for an overhead camera, and a faithful simulator must keep this height as the camera moves. We show that six recent open-weight models fail to do so: as motion replaces the starting view with generated content, they move the camera toward human eye level, a failure we call camera-height regression. Our benchmark, EyeHeight, pairs six rendered elevations (0.15 m to 2.2 m) and four calibrated real-world rig heights with scale-free multi-view height estimation. All six models lose their initial height during a $180^\circ$ turn-and-walk rollout: initialized at 0.15 m, only 0-20% of clips end within $1.3\times$ of the starting height as inferred viewpoints converge to human heights of 1.1 m to 1.5 m, whereas ground-truth renders remain within a few percent. In Matrix-Game models, homography-tracked floor motion stays consistent with constant elevation during rotation even as newly outpainted room geometry yields a higher reconstructed viewpoint. Regression grows with rotation angle, begins while the start frame remains in context, and largely reverses in SANA-WM when a $360^\circ$ turn restores the initial view. We trace this pull to human-centric video priors in which floor-level views are nearly absent: in SANA-WM, textual height cues and dense floor-disparity maps do not prevent it, whereas classifier-free text guidance during the first half of denoising strengthens it. Combining unguided sampling with height-balanced fine-tuning recovers more retention but costs 5 MUSIQ points, a loss fixed during those same early steps. Viewpoint drift alone shifts the paths predicted by visual navigation policies.

title: Better Calibrated, Better Planned: Uncertainty-Aware Multi-ASV Informative Path Planning for Oil Spill Monitoring
abstract: Monitoring oil spills with fleets of Autonomous Surface Vehicles (ASVs) requires mapping a heterogeneous pollutant field from sparse, noisy measurements under tight time and energy budgets. Informative Path Planning (IPP) addresses this problem by coupling a reconstruction model, which infers the field and its uncertainty, with a planner that decides where to sample next. Prior work has focused on planning strategies and has largely relied on Gaussian Processes (GPs), leaving the calibration of the model's uncertainty underexplored. We study how uncertainty calibration conditions multi-vehicle IPP with a fleet of ASVs that coordinates online through a shared uncertainty map. We introduce Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) as an uncertainty-calibrated information model. We benchmark EDL, Monte Carlo Dropout and Deep Ensembles against a GP in closed loop with five planners on physics-based oil spill simulations. Across 60 maps, the choice of model dominates the outcome, explaining 80\% of the variance of the final reconstruction error, against 1\% for the planner among the deep models. EDL achieves the lowest error and the highest IoU under every planner, is the best calibrated model and runs at 3.9 ms per step. With 50 cells per vehicle it reconstructs the spill better than MC Dropout and Deep Ensembles with 150. Deep Ensembles become more confident as their error grows, whereas EDL is unaffected. Robustness of the information model to the data its own planner collects is therefore a requirement of uncertainty-aware IPP.

title: Revisiting the Survival of Agent-Attributed Code: How Measurement Choices Decide the Verdict
abstract: Studies of how long code from AI coding agents survives after it is merged reach conflicting verdicts: agent code is reported to be retained longer than human code, about as long, or modified sooner. Each study makes defensible measurement choices, but how much these choices decide the verdict is unknown. We revisit the survival of agent-attributed code in our earlier study: 854,139 lines that 2,802 merged pull requests (PRs) added to 215 repositories of the AIDev dataset. We vary nine measurement choices in five research questions and build a specification curve of 88 survival analyses, tested under three variance estimators, several observation windows, and permuted labels. For code from human-supervised agents, mostly GitHub Copilot, the choices change the size of the effect but not its direction. For code from the fully-autonomous agent Devin, they decide the verdict. Across repositories, 15 of 22 specifications report it modified sooner when lines are treated as independent, but only 3 when standard errors are clustered by repository, no more than permuted labels produce. Within repositories, no specification detects a difference. LLM intent classifiers agree with human labels about as well as two humans agree with each other, whereas keyword rules do not (kappa = 0.69 to 0.72 against 0.38), and the two reach different verdicts on why agent code is modified. Humans make most modifications to agent code under every unit and window. Re-run on our data, five published designs each change their result with a single choice. Whether agent code survives longer than human code is therefore decided as much by the measurement as by the code. We derive an operationalization checklist for post-merge studies.

title: Microwave-optical quantum transduction with quantum-well exciton polaritons
abstract: Linking superconducting quantum processors over optical fiber requires microwave-optical quantum transducers that are efficient, high-bandwidth, and low-noise. This combination has been out of reach because of the weak nonlinearities of conventional electro-optic (EO) materials. We propose a transducer with an engineered, strong EO nonlinearity using the quantum-confined Stark effect (QCSE) of quantum-well excitons. The QCSE transducer leverages the strong light-matter interactions and extreme polarizability of quantum well excitons. Strong coupling to an optical cavity forms exciton-polaritons whose vacuum EO coupling is up to five orders of magnitude larger than in a typical thin-film lithium niobate device. We describe a GaAs/AlGaAs stepped-quantum-well transducer design with predicted transduction efficiencies above 60% and fewer than 0.01 added noise quanta over a $\sim$60 MHz bandwidth, using pump powers below 10 $μ$W and loaded optical and microwave quality factors of only $3\times10^4$ and $10^3$. We further show that the cavity protection of the polariton provides robustness against inhomogeneous broadening of the quantum well excitons.

title: Connecting Calcium Depletion and Dust Evolution in the Rapid Accretor T28
abstract: We present a multi-wavelength case study of the star T28 in the Chamaeleon I star-forming region and investigate the dust evolution of its highly Ca-depleted protoplanetary disk. We combine new observations from the MIKE spectrograph on the Magellan Clay Telescope with archival IRS spectrum and photometry. We constrain the optical extinction using the hydrogen column density of the region, and apply ROTFIT to obtain stellar parameters. We estimate the mass accretion rate by fitting the excess flux above the photosphere with an accretion shock model. We model the line profiles of Ca II K and H$α$ with magnetospheric accretion models to infer Ca/H abundance, while the infrared excess is modeled with irradiated accretion disk models to get disk properties. We find that T28 is a high accretor with significant Ca depletion in its accretion flows. We find that the disk is best fit with a pre-transitional model with a disk mass of 0.12 $M_{\odot}$, where two optically thick disks are separated by a gap filled with optically thin dust extending to 16 au. This gap would not be resolved in the existing observations. T28 follows the trend of increasing depletion with increasing mass accretion rate. This trend can potentially be explained by preferential and early giant planet formation in massive disks, as suggested by recent planet formation simulations, leading to enhanced capture of refractory material in the massive disks of high accretors and thus depletion in the material reaching the star.

title: FLZ integrability in the 't Hooft model
abstract: We study the 't Hooft equation describing mesons in large-$N_c$ two-dimensional QCD with arbitrary unequal quark masses. Using its Fredholm formulation and the associated Baxter finite-difference equation, we investigate the relations between spectral determinants and canonical Baxter $Q$-functions. We derive special-point identities for the Baxter solutions by exploiting finite-rank commutator relations of the underlying integral operators. We also determine the spectral residues of the inhomogeneous solutions and obtain exact expressions for eigenfunction normalization factors in terms of values at distinguished complex points. These results establish the unit-residue property of the Baxter expressions entering the Fateev-Lukyanov-Zamolodchikov (FLZ) spectral-determinant identities. As a further application, we prove the nondegeneracy of the meson spectrum for arbitrary unequal quark masses. We further identify a broader class of integral operators exhibiting the same mechanism, which we refer to as FLZ integrability, and illustrate its applicability to the meson spectral problem in Ising field theory. Our approach reveals a connection between the analytic structure of Baxter equations and the theory of completely integrable Fredholm operators.

title: Neutron-Rich Disks, Nickel-Rich Ejecta: Can Direct-Horizon Collapsars Explain Early $r$-Process Enrichment?
abstract: Very massive stars above the pair-instability mass gap may collapse directly into black holes surrounded by massive disks. These "direct-horizon collapsars" accrete at $\dot{M} \gtrsim 10\,M_\odot\,{\rm s}^{-1}$ and have been proposed to eject a substantial amount of $r$-process material, powering "super-kilonovae". We present the first three-dimensional general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations of direct-horizon collapsars with M1 neutrino transport, following a $\approx 150\,M_\odot$ helium core from collapse through the escape of magnetically driven outflows. Extreme accretion rates neutronize the disks to $Y_{\rm e} \approx 0.1$-$0.25$ and, at early times, allow them to satisfy the gravitational-instability and cooling criteria for fragmentation. However, the strong poloidal fields needed to eject the neutron-rich gas promptly also drain the disks and lift their electron degeneracy. The neutron-rich ejecta composition is set in a brief phase, such that the ejecta carry $\sim 0.1$-$0.3\,M_\odot$ of nuclei with $A \geq 69$, including $\lesssim 2\times10^{-4}\,M_\odot$ of lanthanides, alongside $\sim 1$-$4\,M_\odot$ of $^{56}$Ni. Assuming proportional retention and mixing of Eu and Fe, these yields imply $[{\rm Eu/Fe}]\approx-0.4$ to $+0.3$, and simple dilution estimates permit enrichment at $[{\rm Fe/H}]\lesssim-2.6$. Direct-horizon collapsars are therefore potential prompt contributors to iron and $r$-process enrichment at low metallicity. Their predicted Eu/Fe ratios fall below those of strongly $r$-process-enhanced stars, but uncertainties in the relative yields, particularly of iron, may close this gap. The ${}^{56}{\rm Ni}$-rich ejecta would power luminous supernovae with rise times of weeks, potentially accompanied by exceptionally powerful gamma-ray bursts, rather than lanthanide-rich super-kilonovae.

title: ASTRA: ASV Simulator for Transferable Realistic Autonomy
abstract: Autonomy development for marine autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs) remains challenging because field testing is costly and difficult to reproduce. Existing marine simulation tools provide mature capabilities in vessel dynamics, robotics integration, and visual rendering, but these strengths are emphasized differently across platforms. This paper presents ASTRA, an ASV simulation framework built in NVIDIA Isaac Sim that combines marine vehicle dynamics, photorealistic perception, and Robot Operating System (ROS 2) autonomy interfaces within a common environment. ASTRA incorporates a Fossen-style marine dynamics model together with geometry-based buoyancy and programmable spectral wave disturbances, enabling non-planar hydrostatic and wave-induced motion. The simulator reproduces the sensor configuration of a physical BlueBoat testbed, including GPS, IMU, LiDAR, and RGB-D sensing exposed through ROS 2. This allows localization, perception, planning, and control software to be developed against interfaces consistent with the physical platform. The BlueBoat's existing ROS 2 localization and perception modules were ported directly into ASTRA, while targeted zero-propulsion experiments were used to verify the implemented wave-body coupling. The simulated roll response was consistent with the expected non-oscillatory hydrostatic behavior, and heave remained highly coherent with the generated wave field, with approximately unity gain at the dominant wave frequency in the tested sea states. ASTRA is intended as an open-source testbed for marine autonomy development, simulation-based benchmarking, and sim-to-real experimentation.

title: Multicomponent Adaptive Sampling Configuration Interaction method in openLOWDIN: positronic and quantum nuclear systems
abstract: We present a multicomponent Selective Configuration Interaction (SCI) method based on the deterministic Adaptive Sampling CI (ASCI) algorithm for computing energies and wavefunction properties of molecular systems containing leptons of variable masses, or quantum nuclei. Near-FCI accuracy is achieved by incorporating second-order Epstein-Nesbet perturbation theory or by dressing the Hamiltonian via Davidson's and co-workers shifted-Bk method. We validate the approach through benchmark positronic (e$^+$LiH, e$^+$OH$^-$, e$^+$Mg) and quantum nuclear systems (HCN), establishing a novel protocol for accurate convergence, based on the iterative adaptation of natural orbitals starting from those obtained by considering only cross-particle CISD excitations, to those obtained from SCI variational space, surpassing the accuracy of previous SCI studies. Overall, we show that the present multi-component SCI framework offers a simple, systematically improvable, and cost-effective alternative to traditional CI approaches.

title: Regularized Score Centering
abstract: Asynchronous reinforcement learning increases training throughput, but data from stale policies and numerical mismatch between training and inference can destabilize learning. To stabilize off-policy learning, score centering (SC) removes the effect of reward baselines on the expected update. Our gradient diagnostics show less extreme gradients with SC than with importance sampling (IS), but SC can still fail when the learner moves far from the behavior policy that generated the data. To limit this policy mismatch, we introduce Regularized Score Centering (RSC), which adds a reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) penalty to encourage the learner's next-token distribution to stay close to the behavior policy's next-token distribution. RSC works with or without truncated importance sampling (TIS), which caps token importance weights. Our theoretical analysis supports this approach, showing that KL regularization improves convergence guarantees. We evaluate dense and mixture-of-experts models on mathematical reasoning and agentic tasks, including online shopping, tool use, games, and fully asynchronous software engineering. RSC with TIS substantially improves sample efficiency across all agentic benchmarks, attaining higher training rewards with the same number of sampled responses. In final evaluations, it achieves top performance across all six agentic tasks, improving by 14.3% on AppWorld and reaching 9.9 times the strongest baseline's score on BabyAI.

title: Long-Term Spectral and Timing Variability of PKS 2155$-$304 from {\it Chandra} and {\it NuSTAR} Observations
abstract: Blazars exhibit strong variability across the electromagnetic spectrum, on timescales from minutes to decades. We present a study of the spectral and timing variability of the TeV blazar PKS~2155$-$304 using {\it Chandra} and {\it NuSTAR} observations spanning 25 years (1999$-$2024). Timing analysis reveals fractional variability amplitudes of up to $F_{\rm var}\approx 24\%$ in the hard X-ray band and $F_{\rm var}\lesssim 7.5\%$ in the soft X-ray band, along with variable power-spectral indices across observations. The minimum variability timescale, $τ_{\rm var} = 1.15\pm0.26$~ks, limits the size of the X-ray emitting region to $R \lesssim 7.7 \times 10^{14}$~cm, consistent with synchrotron emission from a compact region in the jet. We fitted the spectra using power-law (PL), broken power-law (BPL), log-parabola (LP), and bremsstrahlung plus power-law (BR+PL) models, the latter used only as a phenomenological description of the spectral curvature. The BPL model provides the best statistical description for most {\it Chandra} spectra. An F-test confirms a curved model over PL for all {\it Chandra} spectra, whereas most {\it NuSTAR} spectra are consistent with a single PL. Hardness ratio analysis shows a harder-when-brighter trend in the {\it Chandra} band. Joint fitting of the simultaneous 2013 {\it Chandra} and {\it NuSTAR} observations shows that the broadband 0.4$-$79~keV curvature is confined to the soft X-ray band, with the spectrum steepening above $\sim$2~keV and a steep hard X-ray power law ($Γ\simeq 2.7$). Our results reveal energy-dependent X-ray variability over more than two decades, and show that broadband X-ray coverage is needed to locate the curvature of the synchrotron tail in high-synchrotron-peaked blazars.

title: A 15-year K-band view of long-period variables in the central region of M33
abstract: Long-period variables (LPVs) on the asymptotic giant branch (AGB) trace the late stages of stellar evolution and the return of mass to the interstellar medium. Their periods range from about 100 to 2000 d, so a few-year near-infrared campaign covers too few cycles for the slowest pulsators. We combine four independent UKIRT $K$-band data sets obtained between 2003 and 2018 into a homogeneous catalogue of the central $\approx$12 arcmin$^2$ of M33: 847 stars with 21085 measurements over 15.11 yr. Using 82 calibration stars, we place all data on the 2MASS/Vega system and remove inter-dataset offsets of up to 0.22 mag. Of the 847 stars, 771 are variable ($σ_K>0.10$ mag), and 385 have peak-to-peak amplitudes $A_K\geq1.0$ mag, which makes them Mira candidates. Of the 156 stars with Spitzer/IRAC [3.6] photometry, 120 have $\langle K\rangle-[3.6]>0.5$ mag and are candidate dust-enshrouded AGB stars. The catalogue is the basis for a forthcoming period-luminosity and star-formation history analysis

title: A Single-Shot Method for the Absolute Polarization Angle Calibration of CMB Telescopes with Artificial Sky Sources via Stellar Diffraction Encoding
abstract: Absolute polarization angle calibration of cosmic microwave background (CMB) telescopes at the $\lesssim 0.1^\circ$ level is needed to prevent instrumental mixing of $E$ modes into $B$ modes from biasing constraints on primordial gravitational waves and cosmic birefringence. Artificial polarized sky sources like drones, balloons, or satellites can provide calibration references, but transferring their emitted polarization angle from the payload frame to the celestial frame remains a challenge. We propose a calibrator architecture, applicable to any such source, in which a single dual-use grid-optic sets the polarization axis of the emitted millimeter-wave signal and also diffracts starlight into a co-aligned star camera. The resulting diffraction spectra record the grid's orientation relative to the stars, so that it can be measured directly on the sky without fine alignment between the camera and grid-optic. We describe the geometry and physics of this concept and show that it significantly simplifies obtaining the calibration angle the observatory needs, because precise payload attitude is no longer needed and the received polarization is insensitive to small line-of-sight errors. In simulations of 1000 real star fields that include camera-grid misalignment, lens distortion, lateral chromatic aberration, atmospheric refraction, and stellar colors, a single exposure recovers the polarizing grid-optic's orientation in the celestial frame with an uncertainty of $\simeq 0.002^\circ$, fifty times below the $0.1^\circ$ goal. We also discuss the hardware tolerances a physical calibrator must meet, which future work will test. Our results establish the feasibility of this approach and motivate development of a dual-use grid-optic.

title: The Impact of Scenario Representation in Scenario-based Optimization Certification
abstract: Scenario-based optimization provides finite-sample guarantees for decisions constructed from sampled uncertainty, but its certification procedures can be sensitive to how those samples are represented. We investigate this sensitivity under lossless scenario regrouping, which preserves the sampled information, feasible region, optimizer, and primitive violation probability. For an equal-allocation support-subsample certificate, we derive the distortion factor \(k^2(1-ε)^{k-1}\), establish certification reversals between equivalent representations, and provide sufficient conditions for acceptance dominance under nested coarsening. We further apply nondegeneracy-free Wait-and-Judge theory to coordinatewise scenario envelopes, enabling stronger certification directly from the primitive observations. In paired scenario-MPC experiments, exact regrouping increases certification availability from 318 to 471 of 480 attempts without changing the samples, numerical proposals, or requiring any reduction in witness cardinality. Primitive Wait-and-Judge certification accepts the same 471 attempts without regrouping. These results demonstrate that apparent scenario sample-efficiency gains can arise from certificate accounting rather than additional information or reduced decision risk.

title: Bounded functions on the character variety for quadratic extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$
abstract: For any finite extension $L$ of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, Schneider--Teitelbaum defined and studied the character variety in $p$-adic Fourier theory. It is a rigid analytic curve over $L$ that parameterizes the set of locally $L$-analytic characters of $o_L$. It is conjectured that all bounded functions on the character variety of Schneider--Teitelbaum come from $p$-adic measures. We prove this conjecture for all quadratic extensions $L/\mathbb{Q}_p$.

title: Can Coding Agents Write and Transpile Unit Tests
abstract: Coding assistants built on Large Language Models (LLMs) have become a staple of modern software development, increasingly trusted to execute workflows and modernize code end-to-end. Much of this trust rests on passing tests, which are often written by the coding agents themselves. In this work, we examine the ability of these agents to both write reliable tests and translate them between programming languages. We benchmark three popular coding agents, each evaluated with a native frontier model and high reasoning effort. Verifying across a broad suite of metrics, we find that coding agents far exceed human written suites on traditional measures of coverage. This advantage, however, is uneven: agent test quality degrades sharply with project size, and much of the advantage lies in a greater number of written tests. We also show that agentic test translation---while seemingly strong in aggregate---remains inconsistent and unreliable.

title: Spectro-Spatial Survey Fusion
abstract: Imaging and spectroscopy constrain complementary information about the same sky but are usually processed separately. We introduce Spectro-Spatial Survey Fusion, a framework that unifies these measurements by fitting a continuous spectral surface-brightness field jointly through each instrument's response. Adapting from Gaussian splatting in computer vision, we represent the field as a sum of adaptive spatial Gaussians, each carrying a spectrum built from a shared, learned dictionary of templates. We demonstrate this on 400 Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) $ugriz$ exposures and 800 fiber spectra across an $84^{\prime}\times84^{\prime}$ region of COSMOS. The joint fit closely reproduces the spatial structure and broad spectral diversity of galaxies, stars, and quasars. For fitted SDSS observations, the summed predicted flux in source-selected pixels agrees with the data to within 2 percent in every band, and 96 percent of fitted spectra agree to within 10 percent in integrated flux. Sparse fiber spectra constrain a dictionary shared by every Gaussian component, so a model spectrum can be queried anywhere in the imaged area, including where no spectrum was fitted. Without refitting, the field predicts withheld SDSS images and spectra, and selected Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC) images and Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectra, which never enter the fit. The field predicts broad spiral-arm patterns in HSC images of two selected galaxies and DESI continuum shapes for galaxies without a fitted fiber. This framework provides a route to combining surveys so that spatial and spectral information from different observations and instruments can constrain a common representation of the sky.

title: Controllable Chains of Thought Can Reveal Less, Even Without Evasion Training
abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising tool for detecting hidden goals, off-task behavior, and other failures in AI agents. One risk is that models could deliberately shape their reasoning to make it opaque to monitors. We stress-test this risk through persona-control training: supervised fine-tuning on mathematical reasoning traces rewritten in the voices of diverse personas. This induces a broader ability to control CoT, even though training contains no monitor-evasion examples. In covert side-task evaluations, traces in which a gpt-oss-20b model organism completes the hidden side task contain less monitorable evidence than the base model's. Averaged across evaluations and CoT lengths, weighted by side-task-success counts, the CoT monitorability metric g-mean$^2$ falls from 0.94 for the base model to 0.68 for the model organism without a hiding instruction, and to 0.22 when explicitly instructed to hide. In intervention evaluations, explicit hiding often drives monitorability near zero. The effect extends to a Kimi-K2.6 model organism in agentic environments, though hidden objectives requiring extended reasoning or longer trajectories remain more monitorable than simple single-step side tasks. We further discover that targeted transparency prompts can substantially recover monitorability, sometimes surpassing the base model. These model organisms provide a testbed for studying monitorability failures and potential mitigations. Our code can be found on https://github.com/yongzx/cot-control-model-organism.

title: Brown dwarfs and stars are dynamically indistinguishable as companions in AU-separation binaries
abstract: Brown dwarfs occupy the mass range between stars and planets, populations whose dominant formation channels differ, which leave measurable differences in the orbital eccentricity and host-star metallicity distributions. We assemble a sample of astrometric binaries with main sequence primaries and brown dwarf companions at $\mathcal{O}$(AU) separations from $\textit{Gaia}$ DR3. The observable photocenter motions for such binaries are degenerate between a genuinely low-mass companion and a near-equal-mass binary. We break this degeneracy using $\textit{Gaia}$ XP spectrophotometry and follow-up FEROS spectroscopy, which removes removes ${\sim}70\%$ of initial low-mass-function candidates as likely near-twin binaries and leaves residual contamination of only a few percent. The resulting 368 systems, with masses and metallicities determined from the XP spectra and a selection function forward-modelled with $\texttt{Gaiamock}$, form the largest homogeneous sample of brown dwarf companions with astrometric orbits. We find the eccentricity distribution to be well described by a normal distribution. This is comparable to eccentricities of stellar companions at the same periods and higher than those of giant planets, with no significant dependence on companion mass ($α=-0.13\pm0.09$) or period ($β=0.10\pm0.05$). The host-star metallicity distribution is likewise stellar-like, extending to [M/H]$=-0.5$, in contrast to the predominantly super-solar metallicity hosts of giant planets. After accounting for selection, the companion-mass distribution over all brown dwarf masses is consistent with an extension of stellar-binary demographics. Brown dwarf companions at AU separations down to at least $20\,M_J$ therefore appear to form predominantly through a binary-star-like channel. A possible transition to planet-like formation at lower masses cannot be located with the present sample.

title: Symmetry-reduced k-point sampling and Wannier analysis with localized Gaussian orbitals
abstract: Brillouin-zone sampling with localized orbitals requires consistent transformations between sparse real-space matrices and complex Bloch states. Symmetry reduces the number of reciprocal-space problems, but scalar integration weights alone cannot reconstruct the matrices and wavefunctions needed for densities and orbital analysis. We develop a unified formulation of these transformations for nonorthogonal Gaussian bases and describe its implementation in CP2K. Atom permutations, local orbital rotations, and lattice phases connect irreducible-point solutions to full symmetry orbits while preserving the overlap metric. Direct and fast lattice transforms couple this construction to self-consistent calculations, including complex orbital optimization and finite-temperature occupations. Gauge-consistent full-mesh orbitals and directed inter-point overlaps support Wannier90 export, Wannier construction, and Hamiltonian interpolation. In silicon and aluminium tests, symmetry reduces a 64-point mesh to four representatives while retaining cell energies or electronic free energies within $1.5\times10^{-12}$ hartree of the unreduced calculation. Hybrid exchange and many-body applications illustrate the additional role of auxiliary bases and transfer momenta. The resulting framework connects symmetry-reduced integration to gauge-consistent analysis of periodic electronic states within a localized-orbital representation.

title: Data-Driven Variable-Length Compression of 3D Representations
abstract: Compressing 3D shapes is important for the efficiency of many applications, yet existing methods either cannot leverage dataset-level statistics or use a fixed compression ratio for all shapes. We propose a learned variable-length compression method that exploits structure across a training dataset while adapting compressed representation size to individual shape complexity using only fast feed-forward inference. Our method operates on general latent representations and improves rate-distortion for both meshes and signed distance fields. Code is available at https://github.com/voilalab/varlen-3D.

title: Mechanism Design and Active Systems Theory: 60 Years of Parallel Development
abstract: The survey compares two research traditions within the mathematical theory of designing the rules of interaction (mechanisms) for purposeful participants: mechanism design, together with contract theory and implementation theory, and the theory of active systems created by V.N. Burkov and developed into the theory of control in organizations (TCO) by D.A. Novikov's school; the main results of Yu.B. Germeier's school and of the domestic schools adjacent to active systems theory (AST) are covered as well. The problem statements and principal results of 2006-2026 are presented: for mechanism design (MD) - robust and dynamic mechanism design, multidimensional screening, information design, simplicity of mechanisms and credibility of the designer, market design, algorithmic and learning-based design, mechanisms for AI agents, and robust, relational, dynamic and algorithmic contracts; for AST and TCO - a general typology of control, strategy-proof and incentive-compatible planning mechanisms, decomposition of the agents' game, systems with distributed control and coalitional interaction, reflexive games and informational control, control of staff and structure, dynamic active systems, and project management. A correspondence between the classical results is established (the fair play principle and the revelation principle, the serial resource allocation mechanism and the uniform rule, active expertise mechanisms and generalized median schemes, quasi-compensatory incentive schemes and contracts under observable actions), and priorities are delineated by uniform rules; the areas where the two traditions diverge are identified, as are the dimensions of the problem (staff, structure, institutions, awareness, agents' beliefs) covered only by TCO.

title: Corrupting Ties: Investigating Robustness to Bias Injection Across Multi-Agent Network Topologies
abstract: AI systems are increasingly deployed in high-stakes decision-making contexts, where interactions among components can introduce fairness risks that remain undetected when auditing components or collective outcomes in isolation. As LLM-based multi-agent systems become more prevalent, understanding how biased information propagates through agent interactions is essential for assessing their fairness. We introduce a controlled bias injection framework that replaces selected agent responses with predefined biased ones, enabling an intervention-based analysis of how network topology and injection configurations shape system behavior. We propose decision divergence metrics that quantify the effects of these interventions at the agent, network, and system levels, and evaluate five topologies on three binary classification tasks using LLMs from the Qwen and Gemma families. Sequential networks show the greatest divergence, whereas fully connected and mesh networks show less. Injection position also matters: in star networks, injecting the central agent has larger effects than injecting peripheral agents. Models further differ in whether divergence follows the injected bias. These findings highlight the role of network structure in the propagation of biased information and motivate topology-aware auditing of fairness risks in multi-agent systems.

title: The Sharp Holder Constant in Mori's Theorem
abstract: Let $K\ge 1$ and let $f$ be a $K$-quasiconformal homeomorphism of the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ onto itself with $f(0)=0$. We prove that $\lvert f(a)-f(b)\rvert\le 16^{1-\frac{1}{K}}\lvert a-b\rvert^{\frac{1}{K}}$ for all $a,b\in\mathbb{D}$. The constant is sharp, confirming the conjectured value of the Mori constant. The proof reduces the estimate along a Beltrami path to an infinitesimal inequality, which follows from quasiconformal distortion bounds and a three-pole integral estimate.

title: A Probabilistic Lateral Motion Prediction Model with Improved Response Fidelity for Vehicle-in-the-Loop Simulation
abstract: Vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) simulation requires a lateral dynamics model that accurately reproduces vehicle responses and reliably generates horizontal lateral-position and heading commands through recursive integration. This paper presents a probabilistic lateral motion prediction model with improved response fidelity. A two-degree-of-freedom vehicle model provides the physical prior, while a recurrent neural network learns correlated residual corrections to lateral acceleration and yaw rate. To maintain prediction fidelity during recursive motion generation, multistep rollout training feeds corrected responses into subsequent states and histories and directly penalizes accumulated lateral-velocity error. A conditional Gaussian characterizes response uncertainty, which is propagated to lateral-response, position, and heading predictions through augmented-state linearization. Evaluation results demonstrate improved lateral-response and integrated-motion prediction. Compared with the Deep Dynamics lateral adaptation, the proposed model reduces mean lateral-position root-mean-square error (RMSE) from 0.596 m to 0.483 m, an improvement of 19.0%, while reducing mean lateral-velocity RMSE from 0.0469 m/s to 0.0441 m/s. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining physical priors, probabilistic residual learning, and multistep rollout training for response-faithful lateral motion prediction.

title: On the Structure of the Nuclear-Clock Isotope $^{229}$Th Beyond Quadratic Order
abstract: Precision measurements of the exceptionally low-energy nuclear transition of $^{229}$Th, offer an extraordinary sensitivity to a variety of new light fields. However, interpreting such measurements requires nuclear-structure information beyond what is currently constrained by spectroscopy. We develop a systematic description of the electric multipole interactions governing the hyperfine structure of ${}^{229}$Th, including the hexadecapole contribution, and perform a symmetry-based analysis of the resulting hyperfine splittings in crystalline environments. Hyperfine spectroscopy generally constrains combinations of nuclear moments and crystal-field gradients, leading to degeneracies when higher multipole interactions are allowed. We then combine experimental nuclear observables, particle-rotor relations, and a deformed-Fermi charge-density model to investigate the electromagnetic contribution to the nuclear clock's sensitivity to variations in the fine-structure constant. We find that higher-order nuclear deformation and state-dependent differences in the radial charge distribution of the clock states can substantially alter the predicted sensitivity, introducing large uncertainties that are not constrained by existing measurements. Our results highlight the importance of combining nuclear and solid-state theory with complementary measurements, including spectroscopy of higher-spin states, to constrain the nuclear structure and improve predictions of the clock's sensitivity to new physics. Our symmetry-based analysis also provides a framework for using hyperfine spectroscopy to investigate local defect symmetries in crystalline hosts.

title: SimAI: Mechanistic User Simulation through Psychological Network Models
abstract: Realistic user simulation enables the study of human interactions when direct experimentation is costly or potentially harmful. However, existing simulators largely overlook the psychological mechanisms that drive user behavior. We introduce SimAI, a framework for mechanistic user simulation that models how psychological factors interact to shape user responses. To overcome the challenge of supervising open-ended behavior, we propose a graph reconstruction objective that provides graph-level rewards based on how well simulated conversations reflect the underlying psychological relationships. To support this approach, we construct PSYCHE, a dataset of 18,576 profile-network pairs derived from 516 psychotherapy cases. Automatic evaluations show that SimAI achieves greater simulation and behavioral diversity than existing patient simulators while maintaining strong profile alignment. In an interactive study with 30 mental-health professionals and trainees, SimAI receives the highest average ratings for conversational authenticity, realistic help-seeking behavior, and clinical training utility. Beyond simulation quality, SimAI enables realistic clinical training and uncovers safety failures in prolonged AI interactions with vulnerable users. Code is available at https://github.com/behavioral-data/ANGEL-UserSim.

title: Evaluating the Evaluation of Music Generation Models with Generative Psychometrics
abstract: Subjective user studies are one of the major methods for evaluating music generation models. However, subjective evaluation protocols vary widely and are rarely specified in enough detail to be reproduced, hindering comparison across studies. In this paper, we map subjective evaluation methods in ISMIR music generation papers from 2020-2025 and apply generative psychometrics to assess the stability of their items. We extract 284 items from the papers' methodological descriptions, using an LLM and manual validation to standardize them. We represent these items as contextual embeddings and apply Unique Variable Analysis to remove redundant, locally dependent items and Bootstrap Exploratory Graph Analysis to estimate their latent dimensions. Results show the network converges onto a taxonomy of six stable quality dimensions: Rhythm, Melody, Audio, Composition, Structure, and Lyrics, pointing to a unified methodology for conducting user studies to evaluate music generation models.

title: Probing scalar-mediated Lorentz violation with hydrogen masers and spin-precession of molecules
abstract: We propose using hydrogen maser spectroscopy and molecular spin-precession experiments, traditionally employed in precision frequency measurements and searches for the electron electric dipole moment, as complementary probes of light scalar-mediated, spin-dependent fifth forces. We investigate their sensitivity to Lorentz-violating interactions mediated by scalars with masses ranging from $\mathcal{O}(10^{-4}~μ\mathrm{eV})$ to $\mathcal{O}(10~\mathrm{keV})$. While hydrogen maser spectroscopy and molecular spin-precession measurements probe different combinations of Lorentz-violating couplings, we find that the strongest projected sensitivities can be achieved using spin-precession of ultracold molecules, benefiting from their extended coherence times. These experimental approaches provide access to previously unexplored regions of parameter space, probing interaction ranges extending from centimeter to sub-angstrom scales. Our proposals highlight the potential of precision atomic and molecular experiments to search for new spin-dependent scalar-mediated interactions and violations of fundamental spacetime symmetries.

title: ARC-2: Continuous Compliance Through Delta Management
abstract: ARC 1 introduced a three-layer governance architecture for autonomous systems comprising model safety validation, cognitive certification (CRAB), and operational authorization (LEA). However, it did not address how compliance should be maintained after deployment. This paper introduces Delta Management, a continuous governance framework that measures deviations between a system's current operational state and its certified baseline, defined as a region rather than a fixed point. Compliance is assessed through continuous monitoring instead of static certification. Four extensions are proposed. First, CRAB evaluation incorporates the worst verified behavioral deviations, with isolated outliers quarantined pending confirmation to prevent unjustified restrictions. Second, a layered trigger taxonomy distinguishes hard safety violations, critical single-dimension failures, correlated multi-system degradation, and risk-weighted composite indicators, each triggering proportionate responses. Third, a graduated safe transition protocol separates withdrawal of operational authorization from physical shutdown, consistent with established safety standards and EU AI Act requirements. Fourth, environmental delta is introduced as a distinct baseline validity condition: environmental drift beyond the certified Operational Design Domain (ODD) triggers recertification or ODD revision rather than automatic authority contraction. Together, these extensions transform ARC from a deployment-time certification architecture into a continuous framework for monitoring, evaluating, and enforcing compliance throughout the operational lifecycle of autonomous systems. The framework addresses the continuous compliance obligations established by EU AI Act Article 72(2).

title: Sketch, Don't Paint: Allocating Test-Time Compute in Generative Visual Reasoning
abstract: Multimodal models increasingly reason by synthesizing pixels, sketching maze paths within interleaved chains of thought or rolling out video solutions frame by frame. Each visual thought runs the full diffusion schedule inherited from photorealistic synthesis, so iterative denoising dominates inference cost. We study how to allocate test-time compute along two axes: when to render visual thoughts rather than thinking in text or answering directly, and how many denoising steps each thought requires. Controlled interventions that vary only how the thought is rendered uncover three regimes. Causal thoughts carry the plan and become legible early: an 8-step sketch nearly matches a 50-step render in accuracy, commits to the same plan as often as two independent full renders agree, and in video models mostly fails by stalling short of the goal, so the rollout abstains. Decorative thoughts can be omitted without loss, whereas harmful thoughts lower accuracy. Because the regime depends on both model and task, always drawing is suboptimal. Across 14 model-benchmark pairs of three interleaved reasoners, answering directly, without any thinking, wins 9 pairs, and choosing among direct, text-only, and visual tiers from ten labeled examples per pair raises mean accuracy from 60.7% (always drawing) to 65.1%. Where drawing pays, we propose sketch-and-vote, which samples 8-step sketches (a step count chosen without labels) from independent noises until one answer reaches three votes. With this one setting, sketch-and-vote beats full rendering with fewer denoising steps on an image reasoner and two video reasoners, by 8.6 points on VSP spatial planning and by 9.6 and 22.1 points on mazes.

title: Probing $τ$ lepton dipole moments at multi-TeV muon colliders
abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of future multi-TeV muon colliders to the electromagnetic and weak dipole moments of the $τ$ lepton within the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory. We consider $τ^+τ^-$ production through $μ^+μ^-$ annihilation and vector-boson scattering, electroweak-boson-associated $τ$ production, and the radiative Higgs decay $H\toτ^+τ^-γ$. At high energies, the dipole-induced contributions quadratic in the Wilson coefficients become particularly important, with associated Higgs production, $μ^+μ^-\toτ^+τ^-H$, providing the strongest sensitivity through energy-enhanced contact interactions. The remaining channels offer complementary probes of the underlying dipole operators. For a $10$~TeV muon collider with an integrated luminosity of $10\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, we obtain combined sensitivities at the nominal $95\%$ confidence level of $|Δa_τ|<1.2\times10^{-5}$, $|d_τ|<6.6\times10^{-20}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$, $|Δa_τ^Z|<1.8\times10^{-5}$, and $|d_τ^Z|<1.0\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$. Compared with FCC-ee projections, the muon collider offers substantially stronger sensitivity to the electric dipole moments, while both facilities offer complementary probes of magnetic dipole moments. These results motivate further studies incorporating realistic detector effects and systematic uncertainties.

title: Newton's Method for CP Decomposition
abstract: We present an algorithm for computing the CP tensor decomposition using Newton's method. The problem of fitting a CP model to a data tensor with least squares loss can be solved by various gradient-based optimization techniques, including Gauss-Newton methods that exploit the tensor structure of the problem and iteratively solve the linear system involving the approximate Hessian matrix to determine the step direction at each iteration. Gauss-Newton methods exhibit superlinear convergence when the residual is small but can otherwise struggle to converge when the approximation to the Hessian is not accurate. We show that the Gauss-Newton approach can be extended to Newton's method, using the true Hessian to obtain fast convergence even in the case of large residuals. In particular, we derive efficient means of applying the true Hessian to vectors for use within an iterative solver, we employ globalization and regularization techniques to make the Newton model robust to ill-conditioned and/or indefinite Hessians, and we propose hybrid use of Gauss-Newton and Newton steps to balance convergence behavior both far and near local minima. Our numerical experiments use synthetic examples to show in which scenarios Gauss-Newton and other methods struggle to converge, and we demonstrate the superiority of the hybrid approach on two application data sets.

title: Adapted transport inequalities in continuous time
abstract: Given a strong solution $X$ to a stochastic differential equation (SDE), we establish sufficient conditions under which $\text{Law}(X)$ satisfies an adapted quadratic transport cost inequality (AQTCI) with respect to the semimartingale adapted Wasserstein distance. When the drift and diffusion coefficients are Markovian, we further show that the AQTCI tensorizes in a dimension-free manner. As a corollary, we show that various stochastic control problems, e.g. optimal stopping and mean-variance portfolio selection, are stable under bounded, measurable drift perturbations. Additionally, we derive concentration inequalities (with respect to certain dynamic risk measures) for stochastic integrals $\int H_s dX_s$ and deduce appropriate bounds on their tail behavior. Furthermore, using the functional Itô formula, we show that the AQTCI for $\text{Law}(X)$ allows one to deduce classical transport inequalities for $\text{Law}(F(X))$ even when $F$ is not Lipschitz on path space. Finally, we give sufficient conditions for $\text{Law}(X)$ to satisfy AQTCIs when $X$ is a solution to a scalar fractional SDE or stochastic Volterra equation.

title: Rethinking Perceptual Similarity for Remote Sensing: Multi-Layer Attention Scoring and Human Preference Benchmarking
abstract: Perceptual similarity metrics for natural images transfer poorly to remote sensing (RS), where severe geospatial and semantic failures can remain visually plausible while still being decisively wrong for downstream use. To address this, we develop a novel human-aligned perceptual quality metric for generated RS imagery and evaluate it across several generation tasks. We first conduct a controlled perturbation study where we progressively increase the severity of common synthetic perturbations. Using the layer-wise Aligned Attention Score (AAS) responses in RemoteCLIP, we find that different RS artifacts are best captured at different depths. Based on these findings, we introduce Remote Sensing Perceptual Distance (RSPD), a pairwise metric that averages seven independently calibrated layer distances without tuning on human-preference labels. To evaluate our metric on realistic RS generation tasks, we construct a blind, reference-conditioned two-alternative forced-choice (2AFC) benchmark with five 300-triplet subsets spanning synthetic artifacts, airborne and spaceborne super-resolution, SAR-to-optical translation, and timeseries controls. We also construct a 300-triplet ordered misregistration benchmark with deterministic labels. Using the same RemoteCLIP checkpoint, RSPD substantially outperforms simple cosine distance with the final global embedding and is competitive with the strongest generic baselines across the realistic RS generation tasks.

title: C*-algebras constructed using acyclic groups
abstract: We show that the free group on countably many generators is not $C^\ast$-superrigid. Furthermore, we realize each of $O_{\infty}$ and the Jiang-Su algebra as a crossed product of a commutative $C^\ast$-algebra. Finally, we construct non-trivial, outer actions on classifiable $C^\ast$-algebras whose crossed products exhaust all classifiable $C^\ast$-algebras. The common theme in the proofs is the use of torsion-free, acyclic groups.

title: Hill's Lunar Equation as a Leaf: Riccati Reduction and Frobenius Theory for Second-Order PDEs
abstract: The equations of Hill and Adams for the lunar perigee and node, Mathieu's equation and Lamé's equation arise as leafwise restrictions of one class of linear partial differential equations, the \emph{square-type foliated equations} $L^2u+A\,Lu+B\,u=0$, where $L$ is an analytic vector field and $A,B$ are analytic functions. Such an equation has a regular singularity exactly when the foliation defined by $L$ is analytically linearizable. At rational saddles, where every point of the indicial conic is resonant, we obtain convergent solutions whose exponents are holomorphic functions of a first integral; their variation describes the monodromy along the leaves and decides when classical Frobenius solutions exist. For a Hill equation, the characteristic exponent becomes the value of such a holomorphic function, given by a convergent series. This yields rigorous computer-assisted proofs of Hill's constant for the motion of the lunar perigee and of Adams' constant for the motion of the node: Hill's value is confirmed within his own error estimate and its fifteenth decimal is determined, his value of the motion of the perigee is shown to be correct in all its digits, and Adams' value is confirmed to twelve decimals. For Mathieu's equation, the curves of constant characteristic exponent that govern ion trapping appear as classical Frobenius loci. For Lamé's equation, we prove a product formula for the logarithmic obstructions, which coincide with the leading coefficients of the eigenvalue splittings computed by Volkmer and whose vanishing reflects the finite-gap property.

title: Comparative analysis of two delta Scuti stars approaching the TAMS using MESA-GYRE models
abstract: This study presents a comparative asteroseismic analysis of two late main-sequence \dss\ with slow to moderate rotation, TIC 274211446 and TIC 16053262. Both are also characterised by showing an intense emission in the H$_α$ line. Based on the first 35 extracted frequencies from short-cadence photometric data from the TESS mission, with no significant pulsations out of the [9, 40] \cd range, I estimated the large frequency separation. I calibrated evolutionary and adiabatic oscillation models using the \mesa\ and \gyre\ codes under the Traditional Approximation of Rotation (TAR). I used the observed large separation and spectroscopic temperature to constrain the models. Finally, I have used kernel curve fitting (KDE) to find the best profiles for both stars. With a hydrogen fraction of 21$\%$ in the convective core, TIC~274211446 is more evolved than TIC~16053262, which still retains 30$\%$ of its core fuel. The former has a large separation $Δν$ = (2.7$\pm$0.1) \cd, and points to a model with M = (1.84$\pm$0.07) M$_{\odot}$, a radius of R = (2.67$\pm$0.07) R$_{\odot}$, and an effective temperature of \teff = (7308$\pm$71) K. The latter, with $Δν$ = (3.25$\pm$0.1) \cd, points to a more compact model with M = (1.72$\pm$0.07)M$_{\odot}$, R = (2.28$\pm$0.05)R$_{\odot}$, and \teff = (7298$\pm$59) K. The equatorial rotation velocities are (28$\pm$1) \kms\ and (47$\pm$13) \kms, respectively. TIC~274211446 has an age of (1070$\pm$127) \myr, and TIC~16053262 is (1145$\pm$165) \myr\ old.

title: Direct Element-Level Mass Matrix Inversion
abstract: Explicit finite element methods for transient solid dynamics commonly use lumped mass matrices to avoid solving systems of equations for nodal accelerations at each time step. However, diagonal mass matrices may inadequately represent inertia, particularly for higher-order elements and coarse or distorted meshes. This has limited the use of higher-order elements in explicit dynamic analyses. This paper presents a systematic method for directly evaluating the inverse of non-diagonal element-level mass matrices for solid isoparametric elements of arbitrary interpolation order. The method applies to mixed mass matrices defined as linear combinations of lumped and consistent mass matrices, with a weighting parameter controlling the transition between diagonal, consistent, and intermediate formulations. It therefore provides a framework for incorporating non-diagonal mass formulations, including those for quadratic elements, into explicit finite element algorithms. The approach is demonstrated by deriving an explicit inverse formula for the mixed mass matrix of the eight-node hexahedral element. This formula enables efficient element-level inversion without solving a global system. The proposed method can improve inertial representation in transient dynamic analyses while retaining the computational advantages of explicit time integration and is suitable for element-by-element implementations.

title: A Forecast for Testing the Decreasing $H_0$ Trend in Time-Delay Cosmography
abstract: In 2019 the H0LiCOW/TDCOSMO collaboration reported a decreasing Hubble constant $H_0$ trend with lens redshift in the flat $Λ$CDM model at low statistical significance ($< 2 σ$). The signal is expected if physics is missing from the $Λ$CDM model in the late universe. In the wake of recent TDCOSMO 2026 results, we revisit the feature. Although the statistical significance of the trend has increased in a like-for-like comparison with earlier studies, propagating mass-sheet transformation (MST) uncertainties reduces the significance to $\sim 1 σ$. As a result, Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) currently favours a constant $H_0$ over a decreasing $H_0$ in the ratio 2.4:1. Nevertheless, we highlight good agreement on a negative slope with independent observables and forecast that approximately 40 and 90 lenses will be required to substantiate the trend at $\sim 2 σ$ and $\sim 3 σ$ significance, respectively, if the feature is physical and current uncertainties are representative. Even now, it is evident that the TDCOSMO 2026 $H_0$ constraint $H_0 \approx 71$ km/s/Mpc reflects an average over the lens redshift distribution and is naturally anchored at intermediate lens redshifts.

title: Threat Landscape of Vibe Coding and the Road to Secure Autonomy
abstract: Vibe coding is reshaping software development, enabling faster implementation and allowing individuals with limited programming experience to describe requirements in natural language while AI agents write, test, and deploy the code. As these agents evolve into autonomous systems that execute commands, manage dependencies, access cloud resources, and interact with other agents, their security risks extend beyond incorrect code to actions with direct consequences for software systems. Although research on these risks is expanding, it remains fragmented across areas including prompt injection, insecure code generation, supply-chain attacks, and human factors, with limited consensus on terminology, threat assumptions, and evaluation. This paper consolidates emerging research through the lens of the vibe coding workflow. We establish a reference architecture, characterise six levels of agent autonomy, and develop a threat model centred on five trust boundaries spanning developers, AI models, tools, cloud infrastructure, and the wider software ecosystem. Building on this foundation, we propose a taxonomy of twenty-one threats across nine classes. For each threat, we review the available evidence, assess proposed defences, and identify limitations. Our analysis highlights that risks increase with agents' operational authority, while most defences rely on model judgement and address isolated threats. Finally, we identify eleven research challenges, including enforceable limits on agent authority and shared benchmarks and methodologies for assessing vibe coding security.

title: TUSI: A Citation-Grounded Graph-Based Benchmark for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Persian Legal Question Answering
abstract: Evaluating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems in Persian law remains challenging because benchmarks lack realism, grounding, and coverage of legal reasoning. Existing resources are either synthetically generated from statutory texts, lacking natural information needs, or derived from informal legal question--answer sources without explicit linkage to authoritative legal documents, making them unsuitable for rigorous evaluation of grounded legal reasoning. To address this gap, we introduce TUSI-Bench, a structured Persian legal benchmark designed for the evaluation of RAG-based systems. TUSI-Bench is built upon a multi-layered legal knowledge framework containing 7,261 legal articles and integrating codified statutes, legal commentaries, doctrinal writings, and Supreme Court unification rulings. We also construct a legal knowledge graph linking articles and concepts for structure-aware retrieval. Based on this foundation, TUSI-Bench provides two complementary evaluation tasks: (i) TUSI-QA, an open-ended question answering benchmark containing 1,999 questions that requires grounded responses with explicit legal citations, and (ii) TUSI-Bar, a multiple-choice benchmark containing approximately 500 four-option questions derived from Iranian Bar examination questions. Furthermore, we propose a graph-based retrieval baseline that leverages relational structure within the legal knowledge graph. Experimental results demonstrate that incorporating graph-based relations improves retrieval recall by up to 8 percentage points compared to standard baselines, highlighting the importance of structured legal representations for RAG systems. The proposed benchmark provides a standardized resource for evaluating grounded legal reasoning in Persian and enables future research on structured legal intelligence.

title: ASCEND: Automated Shockproof Cost-Efficient Network Design
abstract: Designing resilient and cost-effective IP network topologies over an existing physical infrastructure is a challenging combinatorial optimization problem, particularly at large scale and under extensive failure modeling assumptions. Traditional deterministic approaches struggle to jointly address resiliency against shock (large customer-impact outages) and implementation cost objectives when the number of candidate circuits grows quadratically with the number of sites to be interconnected. In this paper, we propose Automated Shockproof Cost-Efficient Network Design (ASCEND), a systematic design pipeline for IP core network optimization based on a two-level optimization framework. At the outer level, ASCEND uses Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) to select core sites and core circuits. Given a core design, the inner-level integral Multi-Commodity Flow (MCF) formulation selects edge circuits and maps both core and edge circuits onto optical (fiber/transport) paths while prioritizing resource disjointness and latency. Network designs are evaluated using two competing objectives: a performance cost capturing resiliency under probabilistic failure scenarios and an implementation cost. The performance cost incorporates an exponentially weighted vulnerability metric that explicitly penalizes infeasible configurations. Experimental results on multiple real-world networks demonstrate that ASCEND consistently identifies designs that outperform a manually engineered baseline in both resiliency and implementation cost.

title: Urban Representation Learning for Identifying Potential Disparities in Crime Reporting
abstract: Open crime data support urban safety analysis but reflect reported incidents rather than the complete distribution of criminal activity, potentially introducing spatial distortions in downstream analysis. We propose a self-supervised urban representation learning framework for identifying unusual reporting patterns relative to representation-similar peers using only georeferenced crime records. The method constructs complementary hourly, weekly, and static reporting profiles, learns scale-specific representations under geographic self-supervision, and integrates them into a unified latent space. Neighbor Profile Divergence (NPD) is then used to quantify disagreement between each region's reporting profile and those of its retrieved peers. Experiments on more than 1.8 million crime records from Mexico City, aggregated into 1,058 H3 regions, show that the proposed representation achieves a mean Silhouette score of 0.4052, compared with 0.2863 for Hex2Vec. NPD rankings remain highly stable across neighborhood sizes, with Spearman correlations from 0.9720 to 0.9951, while most high-divergence candidates persist across configurations. The retrieved peers also extend substantially beyond immediate geographic neighborhoods, indicating that the learned representation captures structure beyond local spatial proximity. High-divergence regions exhibit spatially organized patterns and, in several cases, differences in incident volume relative to peer expectations. These results support NPD as an internal auditing and prioritization mechanism for identifying regions that warrant further investigation, rather than as direct evidence of underreporting.

title: Logical Relations on Display
abstract: The metatheory of programming languages suffers from a lack of reuse. Researchers develop individual calculi and prove standard properties, but very few results are truly reused across papers. The problem is worse in proof assistants, where developments routinely duplicate code from prior work or rebuild it from scratch. Category theory provides the most promising path toward reusable programming language semantics. Universal properties capture the type connectives---products, functions, sums---together with their $β$/$η$ laws. Free categorical structures identify syntactic calculi. \emph{Displayed} categories provide a uniform language for specifying logical relations, and general theorems about fibrations allow their structure to be assembled compositionally. In this work we develop a library of formalized category theory in the Cubical Agda proof assistant directly applicable to programming language metatheory. We develop theories of universal properties and free categorical structures, apply them to define denotational semantics and logical relations for simply typed calculi, and identify encodings of the categorical constructions that make typechecking them tractable. From the same categorical components, we construct several familiar results via a logical relations construction---canonicity,parametricity,conservativity---and provide a proof of coherence for monoidal categories.

title: How Much of SAR Vehicle Recognition Is the Vehicle? Background Shortcuts, Angle Gaps and Partial Libraries on MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR
abstract: Deep networks score near 99% on the MSTAR vehicle benchmark, and the newer ATRNet-STAR benchmark was built to be harder. We ask how much of these scores comes from the vehicle itself. With a modern network (ConvNeXt-Small, 3 seeds) we first reproduce the known MSTAR result: with the central 96x96 pixels zeroed out, accuracy is still 73.3% (chance 10%). The same shortcut is present in ATRNet-STAR, which was collected across several scenes: with the vehicle removed, accuracy is 63.3% on the 40-class SOC split (chance 2.5%). Under the official scene-change split, the background stops helping and starts hurting. Accuracy is 22.8% on full chips and 30.8% when only the vehicle is shown. A SAR foundation model, SARATR-X, leans on the background more than ConvNeXt does (+4 to +6 points with the vehicle removed, in every seed) and does not solve the scene change. We then hold the amount of training data fixed and vary the depression angles used for training. Accuracy is set mainly by the gap to the nearest training angle: 57% at 15 degrees, 39% at 30 degrees and 26% at 45 degrees. Adding more training angles does not help. Finally, when most classes have training images at the test angle and a few do not, the missing classes do worse than when no class has them: 9.0% instead of 22.4% at a 45-degree gap. Most of their images are assigned to known classes. We recommend reporting background-only and target-only controls, and the angle gap, next to any accuracy figure. Code is public.

title: Coordination of Heterogeneous Teams with Uncertain Task Requirements
abstract: Coordinating a team of heterogeneous agents to complete tasks with unknown requirements is a challenging multi-agent planning problem. Agents differ in their ability to discover task requirements and in their ability to engage tasks, so the planner must coordinate task discovery, execution, and staging. This paper introduces a hierarchical planner that uses a graph neural network policy to assign actions to agents, then finds a path to the action's location using a shortest-path algorithm. The central part of our approach is the CAAT graph, which is a graph representation of the planning context consisting of the agents, tasks, capabilities, and actions. We demonstrate that our learned planner can jointly coordinate a heterogeneous team to simultaneously discover task requirements and complete tasks in a shorter time compared to baselines that optimize task discovery and task engagement independently. Furthermore, we show that our policy can zero-shot plan on out-of-distribution settings by training only on an outdoor map then transferring without finetuning to an indoor map with more agents, tasks, and capabilities than seen during training.

title: Charge self-consistent DFT+QDMFT framework with a Krylov-based quantum impurity solver
abstract: We integrate a quantum impurity solver into a charge self-consistent density functional theory (DFT) plus quantum dynamical mean-field theory framework. The solver optimizes adaptive circuits to approximate the ground state of the impurity model and its particle and hole excitations, and reconstructs the impurity Green's function from their Hamiltonian moments. Higher-order moments are predicted from low-order ones using a machine-learning model, while regularized optimization mitigates violations of causality in the resulting self-energy. The latter is used to update the charge density until self-consistency is achieved. We demonstrate the framework through body-centered cubic lithium calculations and compare the results with a reference one using a continuous-time quantum Monte Carlo solver. These calculations converge with root-mean-square charge-density residuals below $\boldsymbol{2\times10^{-3}}$ and yield a nearly vanishing impurity self-energy, consistent with the noninteracting limit used for weakly correlated lithium.

title: Infrared fluctuations and collective entanglement modes in harmonic lattices
abstract: We investigate how infrared fluctuations and spatial separation shape vacuum entanglement between two finite regions in the relativistic harmonic chain and its Lifshitz generalizations. At fixed lattice spacing and finite geometry, we establish that logarithmic negativity remains uniformly bounded as the mass approaches zero, while mutual information diverges. Infrared-enhanced total correlations therefore do not provide an unbounded distillable-entanglement resource. Using local symplectic consolidation, we identify the collective canonical modes carrying the negativity and follow their evolution with separation. Their participation crosses over from localization near the facing boundaries to a collective distribution within each region. Expansion in the adjacent-state canonical basis connects this evolution to progressively weaker, more extended reference modes, including adjacent-halo directions. Building on the established concentration of long-distance logarithmic negativity into a single canonical pair, we show that its spatial participation is smooth and infrared-dominated despite its ultraviolet canonical structure, a distinction also present in pure-state entanglement modes. These results refine the ultraviolet mode picture by resolving the long-wavelength organization of the oscillators participating in the surviving entanglement. Across the massless dispersions studied, the normalized participation approaches a universal long-distance profile when separation is scaled by the negativity radius. Its detailed form and the entanglement range nevertheless remain sensitive to ultraviolet deformations. Together, these findings distinguish infrared-enhanced correlations from distillable entanglement and reveal the collective spatial organization underlying its persistence at large separation.

title: Asymptotic analysis of sample average approximations for optimal control problems with uncertain dynamics
abstract: We study sample average approximations (SAA) of optimal control problems with control-affine dynamics depending on an uncertain parameter. The objective is an expected terminal cost plus a Tikhonov regularization term, and the controls are square-integrable functions subject to pointwise convex constraints. We show that the reduced objective is twice continuously differentiable in the square-integrable topology, so that no two-norm discrepancy arises, and that its Hessian is a Hilbert--Schmidt perturbation of a multiple of the identity.
