abstract: Multi-modal image fusion combines complementary observations to improve scene visibility and perception. However, in real-world acquisition, differences in sensing principles and configurations introduce geometric discrepancies, while degradations further compromise source quality. Existing methods typically rely on explicit registration, yet large parallax complicates correspondence estimation, while mismatched fields of view leave some regions without cross-modal counterparts. Meanwhile, independent restoration underuses cross-modal information, whereas restoration-fusion methods assuming alignment remain vulnerable to misregistration. This study revisits misaligned and degraded image fusion in the era of generative foundation models, in which cross-attention enables position-agnostic complementary information aggregation, while generative priors support degradation recovery and inference in missing regions. Building on this perspective, we propose GenRF, which adapts pretrained FLUX through LoRA to jointly enhance degraded observations, infer missing cross-modal context, and fuse complementary information without explicitly estimating deformation fields. Extensive experiments on real-world infrared and visible captures show that GenRF delivers high-quality fusion directly from unregistered, degraded images without preprocessing, while improving downstream task performance under misalignment. Additional experiments demonstrate that GenRF can generalize to misaligned multi-exposure and multi-focus image fusion without task-specific fine-tuning.

title: 44 Tropen by Josef Matthias Hauer as orbits under the group of interval shifts
abstract: We generate a splitting of the 924 monotonically ascending twelve tone half series H=(H_1,..,H_6) in [0,..,11]^6 in 80 orbits H^G under the additive cyclic group G=Z/12Z of transpositions (interval shifts). By classification according to cardinality and forming the union of the orbits H^G and K^G of a half series H and its complement K, we obtain exactly the 44 Tropen by Josef Matthias Hauer, completely independent of symmetry properties, however, fundamentally due to so-called wider-gleiche orbits. This was not clear in previous literature.

title: Fast Bayesian Methods for Uncertainty Quantification in Sparse AI Evaluation
abstract: Estimating how an AI system will perform on a new benchmark need not require another large model. We use public evaluation counts to choose a weak Beta prior, then update it exactly from at most 31 revealed outcomes. The predictor uses no item semantics, pretrained weights, or inference API. Its single online evaluation in the AIMS competition returned a team-reported Brier ALC of 0.188477, a 24.6% reduction from the constant-0.5 reference. The complete submission is 7,754 bytes; a server microbenchmark measures 12.71 microseconds per prediction with 31 matching labels. We describe how source evaluations are compressed into 301 prior means and show why a concentration of two lets new evidence rapidly determine the prediction. The resulting posterior gives exact uncertainty about the modelled success rate without numerical integration or neural inference. A public evaluation covers 79 system-benchmark pairs and eight seeds, reaching Brier ALC 0.200250 for the submitted method. Accompanying code and sufficient statistics reconstruct the fitted prior byte for byte and replay all 632 evaluation trajectories. The result demonstrates how much predictive value a compact Bayesian model can extract from sparse target feedback at very low online cost.

title: Holomorphic Feynman diagrams in four dimensions and the quantum BPS ring
abstract: We compute at all loop orders the kernels of the holomorphic Feynman graphs governing loop corrections to supersymmetry transformations and regularized operator products in the holomorphic twist of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric gauge theories. Interpreting their current equations as those of an electrical network---with Schwinger parameters as resistances and holomorphic momenta as injected currents---we iterate series, parallel and star-triangle reductions on Schwinger space to obtain the fan, spider and cubic product-forest kernels at all loop orders. Assuming that twisting commutes with quantization for composite operators, we obtain every perturbative correction to the supersymmetry transformation in $\mathcal N=4$ Yang-Mills theory, acting on operators with arbitrary holomorphic derivatives. Using the marked higher operations of Gaiotto, Kulp and Wu, we construct the quantum product and prove that on cohomology of the quantum supercharge it is associative, graded commutative and unital, furnishing the multiplication of the quantum BPS ring; in $\mathcal N=4$ Yang-Mills theory every multi-graviton operator thus admits an explicit finite all-order completion. For the classical gauge groups, every perturbative differential image in the multi-trace ring vanishes upon Cartan restriction. In $\mathcal N=4$ Yang-Mills theory, we find new fortuitous classes and one-loop lifts across several gauge groups, no two-loop lift in the sectors tested, and rationally certified three-loop lifts in $SO(11)$, $SO(12)$ and $SO(13)$. The lowest example we find lies in the level-$34$ BMN sector of $SO(13)$. The glueball lifts in $SO(11)$ and $SO(13)$ remove the excess classical powers relative to their symplectic duals. Beyond $\mathcal N=4$, we find two-loop lifts in the Leigh-Strassler and $β$-deformations, and two- to four-loop lifts in abelian and $\mathcal N=2$ gauge theories.

title: AVTR: Adaptive Multimodal Reasoning with Visual Imagination
abstract: Vision-Language Models increasingly rely on textual reasoning to solve advanced multimodal tasks. Despite its effectiveness, this paradigm faces two fundamental limitations. First, relying on textual reasoning alone can limit perceptual ability in vision-centric questions, where accurate answers depend on interpreting task-relevant visual evidence. Second, applying textual reasoning uniformly across inputs overlooks question-dependent variation in both reasoning modality and depth, often producing verbose and unnecessary traces when little logical inference is required. To this end, we propose Adaptive Visual-Textual Reasoning (AVTR), which introduces visual imagination as a complementary reasoning modality to textual thinking, enabling the model to revisit its visual observations and distill the salient evidence through generative visual reflection. Furthermore, we formulate reasoning-modality selection as a learned routing problem, allowing a single policy to adaptively harness the complementary strengths of visual reflection and textual reasoning in response to the perceptual and inferential demands of the input. Across 16 benchmarks, AVTR improves the average score by 4.5 points over Qwen3.5 baseline, while reducing inference latency by 33\%. It also scales effectively into a smaller size backbone, outperforming the evaluated 2B-scale baselines.

title: Target-Clamped Contrastive Learning in Nonlinear Resistive Networks with Monotone Elements
abstract: In the pursuit of energy-efficient hardware for machine learning, nonlinear resistive networks trained via local learning rules are emerging as promising alternatives to digital neural networks. Learning in these physical systems is often achieved with Equilibrium Propagation (EP), which compares a "free" state to a "nudged" target-driven state to perform gradient descent on an objective defined by an explicit cost function. In contrast, Target-Clamped Contrastive Learning (TCCL) "clamps" output nodes directly to exact target values, performing gradient descent on an implicit contrastive function - an objective whose properties have long remained unknown. Focusing on nonlinear networks composed of resistors with monotonically increasing current-voltage characteristics (such as Ohmic resistors and diodes), our contribution is twofold. First, we establish rigorous convergence guarantees for TCCL. We prove that the contrastive function is convex for nonlinear resistive networks without hidden nodes, and demonstrate that this property does not hold in general for the objective function optimized by EP. For these networks, TCCL converges to a global minimum of the contrastive function under suitable assumptions on the learning rate. In the presence of hidden nodes, the contrastive function is not convex, but we show that TCCL still converges to a stationary point on a subsequence. We also reveal cases where such stationary points are global minimizers of the contrastive function. Second, we characterize the representational capacity of these circuits. We establish a novel function approximation theorem demonstrating that any continuous, monotonically non-decreasing, and shift-equivariant function can be approximated to arbitrary precision, proving that these properties are the sole limitations on the network's computational expressivity.

title: Stabilizing Neural-to-Image Retrieval with Frequency-Domain Priors and Adaptive Supervision
abstract: Visual neural decoding aims to infer perceived visual stimuli from brain activity, offering important insights into human visual cognition while enabling transformative applications in brain computer interfaces and artificial intelligence. Recent advances in pretrained vision-language models have provided a semantically rich representation space for this task. However, reliable alignment between EEG/MEG signals and visual embeddings remains challenging because neural responses are noisy, highly variable across trials, and subject dependent. To address this issue, we propose a unified neural-to-image retrieval framework that improves retrieval performance by aligning neural and image representations in a shared semantic space. The framework integrates dual-stream adaptation, frequency-domain calibration, and phase-guided temperature modulation to promote more robust cross-modal semantic alignment. Specifically, dual-stream adaptation models a low-dimensional shared subspace with correlation regularization to suppress redundant noise and enhance cross-modal consistency. Frequency-domain calibration conditionally modulates neural representations using amplitude and phase statistics. Phase-guided temperature modulation further adjusts the supervision strength in contrastive learning according to the stability of neural responses. Experiments on THINGS-EEG and THINGS-MEG under both intra-subject and inter-subject settings demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms strong baselines. These results suggest that robust neural-to-image retrieval under heterogeneous neural conditions benefits from a stable shared semantic space, frequency-informed representation calibration, and adaptive supervision. Code will be released at github.com/wanfkuabc/Geometry-Regularized-Brain-Embeddings.

title: Gaussian Primitive Fusion for Any-Resolution Multimodal Images
abstract: Multimodal image fusion integrates complementary observations from different modalities into a unified representation. Existing methods typically estimate modality contributions on a common discrete grid. When source modalities have different native resolutions, constructing such a grid generally involves resampling, which may introduce artifacts and affect subsequent fusion decisions. To address this problem, we propose Gaussian Primitive Fusion (GPF), which reformulates heterogeneous-resolution fusion in a shared continuous Gaussian space. Instead of first converting source images to a common resolution, GPF directly fits their native-resolution observations with shared Gaussian geometry and modality-specific content representations, and learns modality contributions within the resulting continuous representation. Once optimized, the fused representation is rendered at the finest native resolution without resampling the sources. With heterogeneous-resolution inputs, GPF produces clearer target contours and finer textures, with less blurring and blocking artifacts than resample-then-fuse pipelines. Quantitatively, it achieves the best results on multiple infrared-visible benchmarks against state-of-the-art fusion methods equipped with interpolation or super-resolution frontends.

title: MemoSync: Co-Managing Developer-Agent Metamemory Across Contexts
abstract: AI coding agents increasingly manage what context carries across sessions and projects, but developers have limited visibility into what these agents store, retrieve, and apply. This opacity creates a metamemory problem: the developer's meta-level judgments about what should be remembered are separated from the agent's object-level memory operations, disrupting the monitoring and control that keep the two levels aligned. We conducted a formative study with 12 developers and identified what they want to monitor and control across four dimensions of agent memory use. Based on these findings, we designed MemoSync, a co-management system that treats agent memory as a shared, operable representation: the agent proposes memory candidates and reports which items it uses, and the developer reviews, edits, and scopes them. In a between-subjects study (N=132) against two baselines, MemoSync participants achieved significantly higher task performance and the highest mean developer-agent memory alignment. In an exploratory mediation analysis, the alignment advantage was primarily driven by improved monitoring accuracy. Despite performing substantially more monitoring and control actions, participants reported no increase in perceived workload. A week-long deployment with nine developers showed that memory monitoring and control fit into everyday development work. MemoSync is open-sourced at https://github.com/SLEEPYBQ/MemoSync.

title: SoU-RHS: Bayesian Structured Sparsity for Compact Architecture Recovery in CNNs
abstract: Highly parameterized convolutional neural networks often achieve strong predictive performance, but their memory, computation, and deployment costs motivate the search for methods that recover compact architectures from large reference models. We propose SoU-RHS, a Bayesian structured-sparsity procedure that augments Regularized Horseshoe Shrinkage (RHS) with the so-called Sources of Uncertainty Sparse Global-Local mechanism (SoU-SGL). The resulting model sharpens the separation between active and inactive filters, providing an effective mechanism for architecture recovery. A key property of SoU-RHS is stability: across different overparameterized starting widths and under a reasonable range of pruning thresholds, it recovers compact architectures with similar total size and layer-wise allocation. This supports the interpretation that the procedure is identifying a compact structure adapted to the data, rather than merely compressing each initial model separately. Across standard image-classification benchmarks, SoU-RHS recovers substantially smaller architectures than deterministic structured-sparsity baselines, while maintaining competitive accuracy, achieving lower negative log-likelihood in every evaluated configuration and generally lower expected calibration error.

title: On the Complexity of Envy Cycle Elimination
abstract: The envy cycle elimination (ECE) algorithm is a fundamental algorithm for the fair allocation of indivisible goods, guaranteeing an allocation that is envy-free up to one good under arbitrary monotone utilities. We show that the ECE algorithm can be implemented in $O(nm)$ time for $n$ agents and $m$ goods, and establish the tightness of this bound.

title: CounselTraj: Synthesizing Process-Aware Psychological Counseling Dialogues via Dialogue-Act Trajectory Planning
abstract: The growing demand for psychological counseling has motivated the development of LLM-based systems that support human counselors, but training such systems requires large-scale, high-quality dialogue data. Authentic counseling transcripts are difficult to collect and share because of privacy concerns, making synthetic dialogues an important alternative. However, existing synthetic datasets, despite covering diverse scenarios and client profiles, often consist of brief exchanges and fail to capture session-level counseling processes. We propose CounselTraj, a dialogue-act trajectory planning framework for expanding brief synthetic dialogues into process-aware, session-level psychological counseling dialogues. CounselTraj learns dialogue-act patterns from role-play counseling dialogues produced by human counselors, plans coordinated trajectories for clients and counselors, and uses them as flexible guidance for long-form dialogue generation. Experiments across three Chinese synthetic counseling datasets show that CounselTraj produces more complete and coherent sessions with higher-quality counselor interventions than both direct expansion and expansion with randomly sampled trajectories. Based on CounselTraj, we construct CounselTrajD, a dataset containing over 10K process-guided Chinese psychological counseling dialogues, and use it to train CounselTrajLM for counseling response generation. Evaluations at both the response and session levels show that CounselTrajLM outperforms publicly available Chinese counseling models in response quality, therapeutic understanding and intervention, and counseling-process coherence and progress. Our code and model are publicly available at https://github.com/UEC-InabaLab/CounselTraj.

title: Matching-Logic-Based Understanding of Polynomial Functors and their Initial/Final Models Revisited
abstract: Many data types used in programming are initial algebras or final coalgebras of polynomial functors. We show how to specify them uniformly in matching logic, using the representation of polynomial functors as unary container functors $X\mapsto\sum_{a:A}X^{B[a]}$. For each container functor, we give a matching logic theory of its initial algebra and one of its final coalgebra. Besides the no-junk and no-confusion axioms and their duals, these theories include axioms about the elements that represent functions, for the initial algebra, and a bisimilarity axiom and a realisation axiom, for the final coalgebra; the existence axioms use free set variables to range over all subsets of a model. We prove that, in every model, the algebra extracted from the model is an initial algebra (a W-type) and the extracted coalgebra is a final coalgebra (an M-type) of the container extracted from the model, i.e., the one given by the model's interpretation of the shapes and positions, and that such models exist. So the data types are captured relative to the interpretation of the sorts of shapes and positions, and absolutely whenever these sorts are fixed by auxiliary specifications, which we show for finite sets, products, dependent sums, and (co)inductive sorts built from them. We derive the induction, coinduction, and bisimulation principles as theorems, and illustrate the approach on lists and on Moore machines. This paper revises and substantially extends a paper published in EPTCS 389 (FROM 2023): several axioms are corrected, and the adequacy and satisfiability proofs are new.

title: ViStep-RL: Stepwise Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Visual Agents
abstract: Long-horizon visual agents must do more than inspect images: they must turn observations into evidence that remains usable as a task unfolds. Existing active-perception methods teach agents where and how to look, while a final-answer reward gives little structure for deciding which observations satisfy dependent subgoals or should be retained for later use. We present ViStep-RL (Visual Stepwise Reinforcement Learning), which models execution as a dependency-linked graph of evidence-bearing subgoals. A verifier tracks which subgoals are supported by valid evidence, and changes in graph potential provide a net-progress learning signal; an active memory protocol preserves evidence across turns and links retrieval to downstream use. On ViInteract, ViStep-RL reaches 60.0% strict completion with Qwen2.5-VL-7B, compared with 10.0% for the base model and 46.5% after supervised fine-tuning. Controlled studies show that incremental task-state rewards outperform cumulative rewards by 3.2 points, while active evidence writing improves strict completion by 7.75 points over automatic writing. Under a common interaction framework, the task-trained ViStep-RL policy achieves 59.5% answer accuracy, 24.0 points above the strongest of six general-purpose reference models. Held-out episodes confirm the gain at both Qwen scales, and gains extend to three external visual reasoning benchmarks.

title: Efficient World-Model Planning via Physics-Guided Search Distillation
abstract: World models support autonomous driving by evaluating candidate trajectories through predicted future scene evolution. However, accurate future prediction does not ensure road-compliant execution; when all candidates violate road boundaries, re-ranking cannot select a feasible trajectory. We propose Physics-Guided Search Distillation (PGSD), a single-view planning framework that combines future representations and execution feedback for verified beyond-pool repair through three components: (1) Execution-Aware Selection checks ego-vehicle road compliance under simulated execution and selects the highest-scoring feasible trajectory; (2) a Clearance-Aware Search Teacher generates beyond-pool corrections and selects demonstrations with larger minimum road-boundary clearance during execution to buffer imitation errors; and (3) a Future-Conditioned Repair Student predicts one correction from rewarder features and execution feedback for single-rollout verification. The pretrained planner and rewarder remain frozen; no future scenes are generated online. On NAVSIM v1, single-view PGSD achieves 90.97 PDMS, exceeding all compared prior single-view planners and retaining 73.2% of the search teacher's PDMS gain over execution-aware selection. On NAVSIM v2 navhard, it reaches 38.96 EPDMS, improving on WorldDrive by 11.24 points (40.5%). The student replaces up to ten search rollouts with a single verification rollout per repair trigger. HUGSIM Hard examples provide qualitative evidence of zero-shot transfer.

title: A probabilistic analysis of the Brumadinho tailings dam-breach using uncertainty quantification and global sensitivity analysis
abstract: On 25th January 2019, Dam B1 in Brumadinho, Brazil, suddenly collapsed and produced a catastrophic tailings flow with severe human, environmental and infrastructural consequences. Previous numerical back-analyses of the tailings flow have relied on deterministic approaches, which provide useful reference results but do not explicitly incorporate uncertainty associated to rupture hydrograph and tailings' physical properties. This work presents a probabilistic approach to study the tailings dam-breach flow caused by the rupture of Dam B1, focusing on the quantification and interpretation of the effects of input uncertainty on hazard-related hydrodynamical outputs. Deterministic data was obtained through HEC-RAS v6.6 by considering tailings as an one-phase Bingham fluid. The probabilistic framework combines dimensionality reduction, metamodeling and flooding classification to perform fast prediction of unexplored input scenarios. It allows to obtain data distributions that reflect output uncertainty and to estimate variance-based sensitivity indices to quantify the influence of input uncertainty over output variability. Results show that uncertainty is strongly dependent on time and spatial location. Hydrograph-related parameters mainly control the timing and magnitude of the early flow, whereas yield stress becomes more influential in regions associated with flow attenuation, spreading and possible arrest. Overall, the framework provides probabilistic hazard estimates and insights into the physical mechanisms governing the dynamics of tailings flow.

title: Dual-Actuation Emulation of Scaled Relative Orbital Dynamics on a Free-Flyer
abstract: Ground-based free-flyer testbeds reproduce the planar motion of a free-floating spacecraft using air bearings, but not the relative dynamics of spacecraft in orbit. We present a dual-actuation architecture that physically emulates Clohessy-Wiltshire dynamics on an open-source free-flyer. Two model predictive controllers run in parallel: one drives the solenoid thrusters with an orbital dynamics model, representing the spacecraft under test; the other drives bidirectional propellers that physically apply the orbital accelerations, continuously updating its reference to account for thruster-induced velocity changes. A dynamic similitude maps the orbital scenario onto the limited floor area and actuation rates of the testbed, letting the spacecraft controller run directly at orbital scale. We validate the architecture on hardware and against a high-fidelity orbital simulation, where the orbital accelerations instead arise naturally, both driven by the identical spacecraft controller. Their agreement indicates that the testbed reproduces the relative orbital motion the controller would encounter in flight.

title: Gradient Blindness in Adaptive Architecture Search for IQP Born Machines
abstract: Instantaneous quantum polynomial (IQP) Born machines learn a probability distribution from data with a circuit of commuting gates that a classical computer trains at hundreds of qubits. Adaptive algorithms grow a sparse circuit from a small seed by adding in every round the candidate gates with the largest loss gradient. Such algorithms never add a candidate whose gradient vanishes, so the choice of seed decides which circuits they can reach. Here we show that a candidate gate has a nonzero gradient for some angles of the circuit exactly when its generator is the sum of an odd number of linearly independent generators already in the circuit. The common seed of one-qubit gates therefore never adds a gate on an even number of qubits, which exact gradients on 12 qubits confirm. A seed of one-qubit gates plus the edges of the Chow-Liu tree sees every candidate, and its circuits match the full circuits on 12 and 16 qubits with 10 to 13 percent of their parameters. At 484 qubits, a heredity pool keeps the search over higher-order gates feasible, and the circuits grown from this seed reach a lower test loss than the dense two-body circuit with 6 percent of its parameters, although the higher-order gates add no gain.

title: Rough vector fields with vanishing Lie brackets
abstract: We consider two vector fields $X, Y \in W^{1,p}_{loc}(\mathbb R^d) \cap \mathbf L^\infty$ with bounded divergence. If $p \geq 2$, this paper shows that $DX \,Y - DY \, X = 0$ almost everywhere if and only if their Regular Lagrangian Flows commute. If instead $1 \leq p < 2$, we present an example of two divergence free locally Sobolev vector fields in $\mathbb R^2$ with vanishing Lie brackets whose flows do not commute. In the regime $2 \leq p < \infty$ this paper also yields a quantitative commutation result not depending on the Lipschitz constant for vector fields with $[X, Y] \neq 0$, which is new even in the smooth setting.

title: Rotational Splitting of Reflectionless Matching and Virtual Absorption in a Semiopen BTZ Cavity
abstract: We study complex frequency reflection zeros of a scalar field in a finite rotating BTZ region. The region is bounded by a partially reflecting near horizon wall and connected to an exterior propagation channel. We use exact radial solutions to determine the conditions for zero reflection and test their finite time behavior through wave packet evolution. Rotation splits the reflection zeros in the $m=\pm1$ sectors. For a representative pair of branches, there is a range of reflection coefficients for a passive wall in which the co-rotating incident wave must grow in time, while the counter-rotating one must decay. In the near horizon limit, the magnitude of the wall reflection coefficient mainly controls the growth or decay rate, while its phase mainly controls the oscillation frequency. Exterior matching introduces corrections to these relations. We examine four truncated wave packets, including one tuned case and three reference cases. Tuning reduces the reflected energy fraction from $(3.5$--$7.6)\times10^{-4}$ to $1.8\times10^{-4}$, with little change in wall absorption or the peak energy stored in the cavity. We also find that two co-rotating branches merge at a second-order exceptional point (EP2). A near horizon expansion determines its location and the small wall reflectivity required for its formation. Under perturbations, the reflection zeros exhibit square-root splitting, while the poles of the local-source Green's function do not merge and its response remains linear. These results distinguish scattering zeros from the intrinsic resonances of the system.

title: Rigidity for the quadratic Riemann curvature functional in dimensions greater than four
abstract: We investigate rigidity properties of critical metrics for the quadratic Riemann curvature functional on Riemannian manifolds of dimension greater than four. This functional is the integral of the squared norm of the Riemann curvature tensor. On noncompact manifolds, criticality is understood with respect to compactly supported variations, without assuming finite total curvature energy. We prove that every complete noncompact critical metric with finite curvature energy is either flat or has strictly negative scalar curvature everywhere. We further show that every complete critical metric with concircular scalar curvature is flat. Here concircularity means that the Hessian of the scalar curvature is pointwise proportional to the metric. Consequently, every complete weakly Einstein critical metric with divergence-free Cotton tensor is flat. The latter two flatness results require neither noncompactness nor finite curvature energy. Finally, we construct a complete nonflat critical metric in dimension five with vanishing Cotton tensor, showing that the concircularity and weakly Einstein assumptions are essential in the respective flatness results.

title: Adaptive Action Horizon Selection via Flow-Field Uncertainty
abstract: Reliable uncertainty estimates are important for adaptive execution in vision-language-action (VLA) models. Existing approaches such as Adaptive Action Chunking (AAC) estimate action entropy from multiple sampled action chunks, introducing additional inference cost and capturing both uncertainty within an action trajectory and diversity across alternative strategies. We introduce Divergence-based Uncertainty-aware Adaptive Action Chunking (DUAC), a post-hoc method that extracts trajectory-conditioned predictive uncertainty from the vector field of a pretrained VLA. Building on a closed-form flow-posterior covariance formulation, DUAC derives action-level uncertainty scores from a single generated chunk using Jacobian-vector products, without retraining or multiple endpoint samples. DUAC strongly correlates with AAC, while capturing distinct information: AAC measures global dispersion across sampled chunks, whereas DUAC measures local uncertainty around the trajectory selected for execution. Consequently, DUAC is less sensitive to diversity among distinct but valid action strategies. Across LIBERO, LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboCasa, DUAC-based adaptive horizon selection performs favorably among the evaluated methods, combining strong task success with low uncertainty-estimation latency. These results establish the flow vector field as an efficient, trajectory-conditioned source of predictive uncertainty for robot decision making.

title: Linear Duality and Its Nonlinear Extension via Topological Covering Theorems
abstract: Linear programming duality and core existence theorems in cooperative game theory are closely related. For example, in the 1960s, Bondareva used linear duality to characterize when the core of a game with transferable utility is nonempty. Scarf later established a core existence theorem for balanced games with non-transferable utility. Shapley derived this result from his KKMS covering theorem, demonstrating how topological covering theorems yield core existence results. In this note we give a new KKM-type covering proof of linear duality. We then extend the argument to inequalities with continuous perturbations. Under some asymptotic growth assumptions on perturbations, we obtain a feasible point and balancing coefficients satisfying complementary slackness, a Lagrangian lower bound, and a Scarf-type feasibility criterion. The latter yields Scarf's theorem for normalized cooperative games with non-transferable utility. Using Musin's 2017 KKM-type theorems with boundary conditions and the author's 2026 results on cover degrees relative to point configurations, we also obtain a complementary slackness theorem for continuous functions on compact connected oriented manifolds with nonempty boundary.

title: Variational Estimates for the Hardy--Littlewood Maximal Operator on Finite Graphs
abstract: We study edge variation for the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator on finite connected graphs. We determine the optimal uniform coefficient controlling the oscillation of the maximal function by the edge variation of the original function and derive two-sided estimates for the variational constant of an individual graph. These estimates involve point-mass tests, the diameter, and the number of edges. On star graphs, we determine the sharp constant for exponents greater than one and characterize all nonconstant real-valued extremizers for every exponent.

title: Rare-Tail Statistics For Learning Biased Gaussian Halfspaces with Label Noise
abstract: We revisit the classical problem of learning general Gaussian halfspaces in the presence of label noise, with particular focus on the large-bias regime, where information-computation gaps are conjectured in several standard label-noise models. Concretely, we present and analyze the rare-tail mean estimator, an extremely simple one-shot statistic that averages only the observed minority class. In the large-bias regime, classical Averaging (Servedio, 1999) and related global first-moment statistics are provably suboptimal, while the rare-tail mean estimator recovers the target halfspace direction at the information-theoretic sample rate (modulo log factors) under a broad class of label noise models, including probit noise and margin-dependent noise with very slow decay away from the boundary. Notably, our guarantees allow labels arbitrarily close to the decision boundary to be nearly random, while still giving strong directional recovery from a small number of samples. The estimator also cleanly interpolates between the noiseless and noisy regimes: without noise, it attains the same sample rate as classical separability-based methods for realizable halfspaces, and under low noise, or noise that decays away from the boundary, it keeps this rate even after linear separability has been destroyed. As an application, we consider a two-stage curriculum in which source samples, whose noise may be arbitrarily close to $1/2$ near the boundary and decay very slowly away from it, precede target samples, whose noise flips every label at the same rate, i.e., random classification noise (RCN). Since both stages share the same Bayes optimal halfspace, our estimator supplies the directional warm start needed by existing refinement routines, and together they learn the RCN target at the information-theoretic sample rate in the large-bias regime, up to log factors.

title: ART: Bridging the Embodiment Gap in 3D Human-to-Robot Affordance Transfer
abstract: 3D affordance acts as a critical link between perception and action, providing priors for robotic manipulation. While existing approaches predominantly leverage human priors as direct references, they often overlook that affordance is not an object-intrinsic property but is inherently coupled with the agent's embodiment. Due to the structural and morphological disparities between human hands and robot end-effectors, directly applying human priors causes severe incompatibility for robotic execution. Motivated by this, we introduce a novel task setting, 3D Human-to-Robot Affordance Transfer, which addresses the affordance misalignment arising from distinct embodiment structures. To support this task, we construct the Human-Robot Paired Affordance Dataset (HPAD), the first large-scale 3D affordance benchmark in which every object is annotated with both human-prior and simulation-validated robot labels. HPAD covers 2,137 objects across 80 categories and 13 atomic action primitives, yielding over 27,000 object-action pairs. On top of HPAD, we propose the 3D Affordance tRansfer neTwork (ART). ART first filters geometric false positives in the human prior via a reliability gating stream, then reconstructs the prior into a robot-actionable distribution through hierarchical reconstruction and a graph-diffusion refinement that resolves the topological mismatch between human and robot affordances. Experiments on HPAD demonstrate the reliability of the proposed task and the superiority of ART. We further validate ART on a 6-DoF arm with a parallel-jaw gripper in a 2,400-execution benchmark across 12 objects and 4 action categories; ART attains the best success rate (86.5% over its 480 trials), confirming the practicality of the transfer paradigm. Project page: https://derek0907.github.io/ART/

title: On the slope stability of vector bundles on Sasakian manifolds
abstract: We study the variation problem of slope stability of $T$-linearized sheaves on a compact Sasakian manifold, or more generally, on an affine variety with a good $T$-action. In particular, we establish the wall-and-chamber structure for the slope stability of $T$-linearized torsion-free sheaves.

title: VideoACE: Benchmarking Agentic Video Understanding through High-Frame-Rate Actions
abstract: Agentic video understanding requires models to actively interact with video environments to gather evidence and form judgments. Evaluating this capability therefore requires assessing whether models can translate opportunities for interaction into better understanding. We introduce VideoACE, a benchmark for assessing video understanding under conditions that support sustained interaction. We focus on high-frame-rate action videos, where rapid, subtle changes make targeted observation especially valuable. The benchmark comprises 1,000 multiple-choice questions spanning six categories of fine-grained action understanding, accompanied by temporal evidence annotations and user hints screened for answer leakage. Its evaluation environment combines video inspection tools with a user simulator, allowing models to adjust temporal coverage, sampling density, and spatial detail, and to revisit evidence and revise their judgments under simulated user feedback. We evaluate single-pass observation, autonomous tool use, and tool use combined with user feedback to examine how effectively models exploit these opportunities. Evaluation of five models reveals distinct patterns in how they acquire evidence and respond to opportunities for further interaction. These findings establish VideoACE as a testbed for examining agentic video understanding beyond performance under a fixed observation setting.

title: Guarding the Kingdom of Skill-Based Agents in the AI Dynasty of Computation: Control-Flow Integrity for Agent Skills
abstract: Control-flow integrity (CFI) confines a program to a control-flow graph fixed ahead of time. Procedural agent skills move this control flow into prompt text, and a large language model (LLM) agent decides at runtime whether each step runs in its reasoning, a tool call, or a script. The procedure's control skeleton survives, but its enforceability depends on where each step runs. Many violations, such as overwriting a file before validation, use only operations the skill requires, so permission allowlists admit them. A deviating or prompt-injected model can also evade a monitor by regime migration, for example by claiming that a check passed. We present SkillCFI, which carries CFI over to skill-based agents. Its compiler confines LLM interpretation to compile time and derives the agent's instructions and an executable contract from one skill. By a formal enforceability criterion, it enforces obligations whose evidence crosses the tool boundary and rejects a skill whose mandatory obligation leaves nothing to check. A deterministic runtime enforcer admits a tool request only on trusted evidence and refuses unmediated channels such as inline scripts, so admitted traces follow the contract whatever the model proposes. On eight self-written skills, no compiled contract permits more than its source under 24 source mutations. In 770 agent sessions, SkillCFI blocks before dispatch all 240 such violations, which an allowlist admits, and normal tasks complete nearly as often as without it. Listing the next legal steps in a refusal raises recovery from 21% to 65%. Checking takes about 2% of task time, and a compact command form cuts session slowdown from 1.32 times to 1.08 times. None of 53 public skills is accepted as written. The compiler's diagnostics point to interfaces rather than workflows and guided seven into enforceable contracts.

title: Note on parallel transport of IHS manifolds of Kummer type
abstract: We give a characterization of parallel transport operators for irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds of Kummer type.

title: Worth Another Look:Constrained World-Model Planning for Visual Inspection
abstract: Visual inspection in field robotics and environmental monitoring must localize multiple targets under strict compute and sensing caps. Exhaustive sweeps waste calls on absent classes, while myopic and search-free policies stumble over heterogeneous tariff cliffs or discard viewport edits whose value emerges only after re-querying. We formulate inspection over frozen detectors as neuro-symbolic observation planning under partial observability, decoupling a compact recurrent world model (WM) from exact symbolic feasibility and tariff rules. Receding-horizon beam search with online replanning jointly schedules class queries, crops, enhancements, and termination (stop), paired with slack-aware shadow pricing and legal fallback at larger budgets. Across eight terrestrial, optical, and sonar benchmarks, multi-step lookahead outperforms static schedules and search-free offline RL under tight budgets -- gaining up to 28.4 AP percentage points over static priority on RUOD and 15.1 on ARIS -- while dynamic pricing lifts large-budget performance on all eight domains at 11 ms planning cost. Ultimately, pairing lightweight learned dynamics with exact symbolic constraints turns frozen detectors into adaptive, budget-aware inspection agents without retraining.

title: Electronically Rather Than Geometrically Driven Concerted Proton Transfer under Graphene Confinement
abstract: Proton transfer in water is a common yet mechanistically non-trivial phenomenon that underpins proton conduction and chemical reactivity. However, how confinement alters it, and whether the changes are driven by geometry or by electronic interaction, remains far from fully understood. Here, using a water hexamer confined between two graphene sheets as a model system, we combine coupled-cluster and first-principles calculations with energy decomposition to investigate how confinement alters its concerted proton transfer. We find that tightening the confinement lowers the electronic proton-transfer barrier. This reduction does not arise from the geometric distortion of the ring, which merely accompanies the confinement, but from the orbital stabilization of the transition state by the graphene walls. These results demonstrate that the proton-transfer barrier under confinement is governed by electronic rather than geometric factors, providing a mechanistic design principle for tailoring proton conduction and chemical reactivity through nanoscale confinement.

title: Variational Estimates for the Fractional Maximal Operator on Finite Graphs
abstract: We study edge variation estimates for the centered fractional maximal operator on finite connected graphs. For $0<α<1$, we determine the optimal coefficient in the uniform estimate of the oscillation of the maximal function by the edge $p$-variation of the original function. We also obtain two-sided variation bounds involving the number of vertices and the diameter. On complete graphs, we prove that the sharp $(p,q)$ constant is $(1-n^{α-1})(n-1)^{1/q-1/p}$ for all $0<p\leq q\leq\infty$. On star graphs with $n\geq4$, we determine the sharp infinite-exponent constant and show that the sharp constant for $p=2$ equals $1-n^{α-1}$ if and only if $n^{α-1}\geq1/2$. Combining this with the known estimate for $p=1$, we also obtain sharp mixed estimates. Extremizers and counterexamples are given.

title: Monitoring Unplanned Construction Using Satellite Change Detection
abstract: Cities need land for homes, shops, roads, and public services. New construction changes that land. It can harm natural areas and water bodies, add to waste, and strain public services. NITI Aayog's 2021 report stated that 65% of 7,933 urban settlements in India had no master plan. That number tells us about planning coverage at the time. It does not tell us whether any single building was authorised. Artificial intelligence, which lets computers learn patterns from data, can help find physical changes by comparing satellite images taken on different dates. We test simple methods on two public datasets from outside India. First, we turn each image into a set of numbers using a pretrained neural network, a model already trained to recognise patterns in images. We feed those numbers to standard machine-learning classifiers that predict land categories and physical changes. The methods reach about 95 percent accuracy at spotting built-up land and about 83 percent accuracy at saying whether a small pair of images shows change, where each pair gets one label. We also train a small neural network on a standard change-detection benchmark. Separately, we run a preliminary descriptive check on an Agra sample of 48 patches, 7 of them positive. The results show that satellite images carry information about physical change. They do not show whether construction was planned or permitted.

title: High-Precision Docking of Differential-Drive Mobile Robots Through LiDAR and Vision Collaboration
abstract: Precise docking requires a differential-drive robot to correct lateral offset through coupled rotation and translation within a short approach distance. We combine global navigation with terminal control using complementary LiDAR and visual observations. A line fitted to the cabinet front gives normal distance and heading. An AprilTag identifies the workstation; intersecting its center ray with the LiDAR plane determines tangential position. Taught observations define the docking reference and can cancel repeatable fixed biases under unchanged mounting and geometry. Lateral pre-alignment and continuous visual servoing coordinate the approach, with predictive stopping to account for low-speed actuation lag. Across two sessions using the same navigation and docking code at five workstations on Robot 2, all 111 tasks completed, including 101 on the first attempt. Relative to the taught observations, onboard longitudinal, lateral and heading residual root-mean-square values were 1.51 mm, 5.93 mm and 0.238 degrees, respectively. Joint acceptance within plus or minus 10 mm per position axis and plus or minus 1 degree heading was 96.4% (107/111), or 95.5% (106/111) with a plus or minus 0.5 degree heading limit.

title: TrajWAM: Trajectory-Conditioned Future Learning for Vision-Language Driving
abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) connect future scene prediction with action planning for autonomous driving. Each driving record pairs an executed ego trajectory with its observed future, providing a factual outcome for learning this connection. We present TrajWAM, a trajectory-conditioned WAM that improves vision-language driving through auxiliary bird's-eye-view (BEV) future learning. An ego-trajectory query conditions DINOv3-aligned BEV predictions from shared planner representations. Training combines factual reconstruction under the executed trajectory with one-sided feature separation under an unlabeled perturbed trajectory. Together, these objectives train the shared planner to generate driving waypoints. Native inference directly generates waypoints and bypasses the auxiliary future-prediction branch. On all 220 Bench2Drive routes, TrajWAM achieves 91.53 Driving Score and 75.45% Success Rate, exceeding a schedule-matched planning-only fine-tuning baseline by 5.31 Driving Score points and eight successful routes.

title: WM^MLLM: Turning MLLMs into World Models
abstract: Video world models keep the world in the context of a generator, so a revisit is synthesized again and earlier edits can drift or disappear. We present WM^MLLM, the first interactive world model built on multimodal large language models (MLLMs), for persistent, editable world generation from a single image. WM^MLLM keeps the world state outside every generator, as a panorama with a revision history, and lets the MLLMs write it: they turn each request into operations on this state, select where a local edit is written, and check every candidate before it becomes the next state. Image generators only propose views, and video only presents them. Users can walk to new places and return, edit objects through text or a box, place subjects, and change lighting, weather or season. By construction, a revisit at the same revision reproduces the earlier view exactly, a local edit leaves every panorama pixel outside its region unchanged, and each request starts from the result of the previous one. Against six world model baselines on MBench-A, WM^MLLM has the highest mean on all four environment-recovery metrics (Epipolar 91.5 versus 0.1 to 74.0) and completes the most camera round trips (85.3% versus at most 50.9%). It has the best value in all 15 CompBench columns against 15 baselines. On 112 local edits judged blind, selecting the region to write after generation raises completion from 34.8% to 83.0%. On 258 WBench and MBench-A items, all 46 revisits recover their earlier views, and all 97 local edits that pass the check leave panorama pixels outside their region unchanged.

title: Nonideal Absorbers in Hot-Carrier and Hot-Absorber Solar Cells: Losses and Heat Recycling
abstract: The hot carrier solar cell exhibits a photovoltaic conversion efficiency limit of 85.4%. Among the idealizations necessary to achieve this efficiency, it has traditionally been considered essential that the electrons absorbing sunlight do not end up transferring the captured energy to the crystal lattice. In this work, we argue that such a requirement is not necessary if the absorber is thermally insulated. In our analysis, we also consider the possibility of ohmic losses in the absorber due to finite electrical conductivity. We also demonstrate that such losses, delivered as heat, can be partially recycled into electrical work with an efficiency that is given by the Carnot factor. The high efficiencies reported here are thermodynamic limits obtained with ideal energy-selective contacts and negligible parasitic contact conductance, not projections of practical device efficiency. Our work includes a sensitivity analysis for finite contact-mediated heat leakage, and the results are presented as design targets.

title: Absence of uniform bounds for the boundary nodal count of Steklov eigenfunctions on Euclidean domains
abstract: We prove that for any $K,N\in\mathbb N$ there exist smooth bounded domains in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq 3$, homeomorphic to a ball, for which the first $N$ positive Steklov eigenvalues are simple and the boundary traces of the corresponding eigenfunctions have at least $K$ nodal domains. This provides a negative answer to the question of whether the number of nodal domains of Dirichlet-to-Neumann eigenfunctions satisfies a Courant-type bound in the Euclidean setting and complements the results of [6].

title: Large-Scale Tensor Trace-Ratio Problem: Randomized Algorithm and Sparse Multilinear Discriminant Analysis via Closed-Form Solution
abstract: Trace-ratio optimization problems from high-dimensional tensor data appear across numerous research domains including machine learning, signal processing, as well as pattern recognition. Up to now, analytical closed-form expressions remain unavailable for tensor trace-ratio tasks; prevailing techniques mostly adopt inner-outer iterative schemes to tackle such optimization tasks. However, when dealing with high-dimensional tensor data sets, existing multilinear discriminant analysis methods often encounter limitations such as heavy computational costs, insufficient memory space, and interference from redundant features. This paper yields two core contributions.First, we present a closed-form solution under the full row rank condition, and construct a randomized solver targeting large-scale tensor trace-ratio optimization. In contrast to prior approaches, the devised algorithm achieves substantial computational speedup.Its core mechanism is to reformulate the original large-scale tensor trace-ratio optimization into a tensor least-squares formulation, instead of the much more complicated (generalized) tensor eigenproblems. We derive theoretical error-bound results which verify the reliability of the newly developed algorithm. Second, we build a sparse multilinear discriminant analysis model leveraging the above closed-form result combined with tensor \ell_{2,0}-norm regularization, and propose a sparse multilinear discriminant method for tensor feature selection. The sparse method can identify key discriminative features from high-dimensional data and suppress redundant information. Comprehensive numerical evaluations are conducted over multiple publicly available real-world benchmarks.The proposed methods demonstrate significant advantages in computational efficiency and scalability for large-scale problems, while achieving competitive classification accuracy on some datasets.

title: From Neural Tokens to Language: Dual-View EEG Semantic Bridging for Brain-to-Text Generation
abstract: Visually evoked EEG-to-text generation aims to produce natural-language descriptions from neural responses elicited by visual stimuli. Existing approaches typically compress EEG signals into a single global representation and directly project it into the hidden space of a large language model (LLM), which may limit the preservation of complementary visual semantics under noisy and subject-dependent EEG signals. We propose a dual-view semantic token bridging framework that exploits raw images and sketch images as complementary visual supervision to learn raw-oriented and sketch-oriented EEG semantic token streams. To interface these structured neural representations with an LLM, we introduce a branch-specific semantic query bridge that aggregates each token stream into compact semantic slots and converts them into LLM-compatible soft prompts. A progressive adaptation strategy further transitions the learned visual-semantic interface from image-supported training to image-free EEG-conditioned generation. Experiments demonstrate strong subject-wise EEG classification performance and competitive EEG-to-text generation across multiple LLM backbones. Ablation, branch-level representation, and EEG-label disentanglement analyses further show that the two EEG streams learn complementary view-oriented representations and that EEG-derived prompts provide sample-specific information beyond category labels.

title: DOA Estimation in Antenna Arrays: Super-Resolution Methods in a Common Space
abstract: This paper introduces a unified framework for angular super-resolution in antenna arrays. By integrating linear prediction beyond the physical aperture, entropy variations, and harmonic spatial spectra averaging, we recast classical methods - including Capon, Pisarenko, Maximum Entropy, and MUSIC - into a single structure. We extend this framework to accommodate ESPRIT-type methods by treating the number of simultaneously predicted subarray channels as an additional dimension. Furthermore, we adapt this approach to non-Gaussian signals, establishing a parallel framework for Virtual-ESPRIT-type methods. As a practical application, we propose universal, J-orthogonalization-based algorithms that estimate spatial super- resolution spectra within a unified computational architecture. This architecture produces spatial spectrum estimates for multiple super-resolution methods and any intermediate variations.

title: Critical spectral weights on triangulated disk
abstract: We solve the common-positive-weight support problem at the local spectral threshold 1/2 for relative triangulated disks with interior degrees at most five and an empty or connected degree-five core. We characterize feasibility by a finite decomposition into three elementary pieces and a condition on the original boundary marking. The proof passes from spectral equality to a positive conjugate rectangle, then uses geometric reductions to obtain a serial presentation. The empty-face inequality holds for some common positive weights exactly when such a presentation has only old join endpoints. Whenever this condition holds, our construction yields weights with a positive definite empty-face matrix. Positive Schur responses establish sufficiency, and a uniform face-counting obstruction proves necessity. This gives a finite combinatorial criterion for critical spectral feasibility together with a constructive choice of common weights.

title: SpiderMark: Hybrid Watermarking for Generative AI via Algorithmic Injection and Learning-Based Verification
abstract: The proliferation of diffusion-based generative models has intensified the need for reliable methods to trace and verify the provenance of AI-generated images. Existing watermarking approaches for diffusion models typically rely on isotropic frequency patterns and handcrafted detection metrics, which are prone to directional vulnerability and threshold instability across diverse image transformations. We propose SpiderMark, a hybrid watermarking framework that combines algorithmic frequency-domain injection with learning-based probabilistic verification, requiring no modifications to pretrained diffusion model weights. SpiderMark embeds a structured spider-web pattern, comprising radial spokes and concentric polygonal rings, into the Fourier representation of the initial latent noise, and trains a lightweight ResNet-18 verifier augmented with auxiliary similarity cues (PSNR and L1) to produce a continuous watermark confidence score for watermark detection. Across nine evaluation conditions, SpiderMark achieves the highest fixed-threshold Accuracy in eight, while retaining strong detection on unseen COCO prompts without verifier retraining. CLIP similarity and FID measurements show that these detection gains are accompanied by small measured differences in prompt alignment and distributional image quality. SpiderMark establishes that structured watermark geometry and learned probabilistic verification can be unified into a single, practical framework, bridging the gap between imperceptibility, robustness, and real-world verifiability for generative AI content attribution.

title: A (12/11+eps)-Approximation for Nonpreemptive Throughput Maximization
abstract: We study unweighted nonpreemptive throughput maximization on an arbitrary number of identical machines: each job has a processing time and a release--deadline window, and the goal is to schedule as many jobs as possible. For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, we give a randomized $(12/11+\varepsilon)$-approximation. This improves the recent $(4/3+\varepsilon)$-approximation of Alexander Armbruster, Fabrizio Grandoni, Antoine Tinguely, and Andreas Wiese and the $(17/13+\varepsilon)$-approximation of Tong and Xu. For binary-encoded integral inputs, our algorithm runs in time $n^{O_\varepsilon(1)}\operatorname{poly}(N)$, where $N$ is the input length.

title: A Butterfly Collector's View of Fast Radio Bursts: Repeating Sources Go Quiet within a Few Years
abstract: How long repeating fast radio burst (FRB) sources stay active is key to their origins but poorly known as a population. We test this with unseen species estimation, a method first used to predict how many new butterfly species a further collecting trip would find. If each source keeps the same mean rate over time, the number of sources seen $k+1$ times in one window predicts how many bursts the sources seen $k$ times will emit in a later window. It assumes neither the burst rate distribution nor source distances. For the five years of CHIME/FRB Catalog 2, we measure the ratio $R$ of observed to predicted bursts against the gap $Δ$ between windows. A steady mean rate gives $R = 1$ at every $Δ$, so a change of $R$ with $Δ$ means that the sources change. $R$ is close to unity for $Δ\lesssim 60$ days and drops by half within one year. Neither steady nor randomly fluctuating sources reproduce this decline, unless the latter are mostly silent. Three models explain the data equally well: a lifetime of about three years, on/off activity with two-year active phases, or a mix of short- and long-lived sources. Fitted to the first three years alone, they correctly predict the further decline of $R$ in the last two years. Longer monitoring of $R$, and of whether silent sources come back to life, will distinguish them. Unlike butterfly species, FRB sources do not wait for the next collecting trip, so follow-up should start soon.

title: WFST0533buha (Bi'an): A Fast Blue Ultraluminous Transient Candidate with Unusual Blue/NUV Colors
abstract: We present WFST0533buha (Bi'an), a fast blue ultraluminous transient (FBUT) candidate discovered by the Wide Field Survey Telescope Deep High-cadence $ugr$-band Survey. The source brightened by approximately 2.5 mag in $u$ within 3 days and has a half-maximum timescale ($t_{1/2}$) shorter than 6 days. Two spectra show a blue, featureless continuum but do not provide a secure redshift. Einstein Probe observations yield only X-ray upper limits, while a faint radio counterpart was detected at 15 GHz with the VLA. The early $u$-band detection and intensive multiband coverage of Bi'an demonstrate the value of deep, high-cadence blue-band observations for discovering and characterizing FBUTs at early phases. Notably, Bi'an shows redder blue/NUV colors than AT 2018cow and AT 2024wpp, suggesting possible diversity in the short-wavelength properties of FBUTs.

title: SN 2025wiu: A Slowly Evolving Type Ib Supernova with an Extraordinary Post-maximum Bump
abstract: Stripped-envelope supernovae (SESNe) originate from massive progenitors that have lost most or all of their outer envelopes prior to core collapse. Recent advances in optical time-domain surveys have revealed a growing population of peculiar SESNe with unusual light-curve morphologies, pointing to energy sources beyond the standard radioactive-decay scenario. In this work, we present multi-band photometric and spectroscopic observations of SN 2025wiu, a peculiar Type Ib supernova discovered by the Wide Field Survey Telescope (WFST). SN 2025wiu is characterized by a high luminosity and exceptionally slow photometric evolution, with a prominent post-maximum bump peaking at $\sim50$ days after the primary maximum. Its early light curve also shows a weak excess consistent with shock-cooling emission from a compact progenitor with a radius of $\sim4\,R_\odot$. The spectra show only modest evolution, with persistently weak line features and no narrow emission lines detected even at $\sim110$ days after maximum. By modeling the primary peak and late-time tail with a combination of radioactive decay and additional energy sources, we isolate the post-maximum bump, which has a roughly symmetric profile with a peak luminosity of $\sim2.4 \times 10^{42}~\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and a characteristic duration of $\sim42$ days. We discuss circumstellar medium (CSM) interaction, accretion, magnetar activity, and a double $^{56}$Ni distribution as possible origins of the bump. The latter three scenarios face challenges in reproducing the post-maximum bump, while delayed CSM interaction remains a possible explanation.

title: Learning with Unlearning: Synaptic Role Partitioning for Simultaneous Continual Learning and Machine Unlearning
abstract: Continual Learning (CL) asks a model to acquire new knowledge without forgetting what it already knows. Machine Unlearning (MU) asks it to destroy specific knowledge without damaging the rest. The challenge is integrating them in the same system; the two objectives pull on the same weights, and an edit made for one harms the other. To address this, we propose Learning with Unlearning (LwU), a unified framework that resolves the conflict where it occurs: at the individual synapse. LwU scores every weight twice, once against the data to keep and once against the data to delete, and partitions the network into four zones with separate update rules. Weights that only require retention are frozen. Weights that only require deletion are cleared and returned to the network as free capacity. Contested weights take a gradient-ascent step projected orthogonally to the retention gradient. The remaining capacity learns the incoming task by a privileged teacher via self-distillation. Deletion is served post hoc, and no retraining is required. Across both CL and MU jobs, LwU outperforms or matches the strongest baseline. Its real-world practicality has been demonstrated on the Physical Artificial Intelligence (PAI) dataset we conducted. Additionally, in the image generation task and in removing dangerous content, it outperformed the closest baseline, as shown in Fig.1.

title: GALA: Gallery-Level Alignment for Real-Life Vision Decoding from EEG
abstract: Neural decoding of visual experience from electroencephalography (EEG) has achieved strong performance in intra-subject settings, but current methods fail to generalize across individuals: on the standard 200-way benchmark THINGS-EEG-2, top-1 accuracy drops from above 80% within subjects to about 32% for an unseen subject. Adapting a pre-trained encoder to new subjects and sessions typically requires labeled data, a bottleneck whose collection time severely limits practical device deployment. In a practical Brain-Computer Interface (BCI), however, the possible outcomes are known in advance and form a gallery of candidates, and the unlabeled EEG of the user accumulates as soon as the device is used. We propose a new setting, incremental transductive calibration, in which the decoder is calibrated regularly on all the unlabeled EEG received so far and on the known gallery, without any labels. This setting is closer to the conditions of a deployed BCI than the zero-shot and batch evaluations in current use. We evaluate it with a protocol in which queries arrive one at a time, with unknown and possibly unequal frequencies, and each query is decoded before it is used for calibration. In this setting, we introduce GALA : GAllery-Level Alignment, a label-free calibration method which registers the unlabeled EEG embeddings onto the gallery through shrinkage whitening, hubness correction and a Sinkhorn--Procrustes alignment with query frequencies estimated from the buffer, updated after every query. On THINGS-EEG-2, with a gallery of 200 images, it raises the top-1 accuracy on a new subject from 28% to 67% over 53 minutes of use. Across 60 evaluation settings that vary the gallery size, the query frequencies and the number of repetitions averaged per query, GALA is the most accurate label-free method in every setting, 6.6 points above the best competing method on average at the end of the stream.

title: TapTacTouch: Shape Completion from Sparse Tactile Contacts with Geometric Priors
abstract: 3D object reconstruction is essential for robotic perception and manipulation, yet conventional approaches predominantly rely on visual observations that can be limited by occlusion or unavailable in visually constrained environments. In this work, we propose a vision-free, training-free, and category-agnostic framework for reconstructing 3D object meshes from sparse tactile contacts without relying on pretrained shape models. A 6-DoF robotic arm equipped with a 20-DoF multi-finger robotic hand collects tactile observations using 3x3 pressure sensor arrays mounted on the finger pads. The acquired tactile measurements are transformed into 3D contact constraints through robot kinematics and integrated into a multi-scale Gaussian Process Implicit Surface (GPIS). To address sparse and incomplete surface observations, the proposed method incorporates contact confidence weighting, weak pseudo-surface constraints, and an observation-driven geometric prior to preserve local surface geometry and provide structural guidance in unobserved regions. Real-world experiments on six objects achieve a Chamfer Distance (CD) of 1.610, an Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) of 7.738, and an F-Score of 95.00, with reconstruction completed in an average of 49.99 s per object. These results demonstrate that sparse tactile sensing can provide sufficient geometric information for continuous 3D object reconstruction without visual or semantic information.

title: Conditional What-If Generation for Radio Access Network Energy under Rare and Unseen Contexts
abstract: Energy-saving mechanisms in RANs must balance energy reduction and network performance under varying traffic conditions. Conditional generative models support what-if analysis by generating plausible power-consumption trajectories for radio configurations and operating scenarios, helping operators evaluate energy-saving policies before deployment. However, representative measurements are costly and operationally constrained, so historical data cover only limited configurations and conditions, leaving some contexts poorly represented or unseen during training. In this paper, we study conditional generation of RAN power-consumption trajectories under decreasing training coverage, from well-represented to rare and unseen configurations. We first introduce a context-normalized conditional generator combining temporally aligned conditioning with configuration-dependent target normalization. It improves generation for well-represented configurations but becomes less reliable as training exposure decreases because target consumption is harder to estimate. We therefore introduce a prediction-based generative framework that decomposes power consumption into global prediction, residual level and scale correction, and temporal residual generation. Experiments on a commercial 5G RAN and a public dataset show that hardware metadata provides transferable information about residual scale, while limited target observations at inference improve generation through residual-level correction without retraining. An ablation study confirms that residual-level correction provides most of the gain. Both approaches outperform state-of-the-art methods for well-represented configurations, while the prediction-based approach also generalizes to rare and unseen contexts and, with one target observation, reduces median MAE by about 50% compared with TimeWeaver.

title: Two-Scale Calculus for Riesz Fractional Gradients: Compactness, Realization, and Periodic Homogenization
abstract: We develop a two-scale calculus for the Riesz fractional gradient $\grads$, $0<s<1$, acting on functions that vanish outside a bounded open set $Ω\subset\R^N$. For bounded families in $H_0^s(Ω)$ we characterize the interior two-scale limits of the fractional gradients and prove, by a Fourier-multiplier estimate, that every limit of this form is generated by such a family; a periodic fractional Helmholtz decomposition identifies the microscopic potentials, and $\eps^s$ is the natural amplitude of the oscillations. For periodic fractional divergence-form equations with bounded measurable, uniformly elliptic, not necessarily symmetric coefficients, we identify the two-scale limit of the fractional gradients and the homogenized problem, whose coefficient is the classical homogenized matrix in $Ω$ and the cell average outside $Ω$, and we construct correctors in $H_0^s(Ω)$ that give strong convergence in $H^s(\R^N)$. The identification extends to parabolic problems with dual-space forcing.

title: OmegaHyper: Explicit-State HyperLTL Model Checking on an omega-Automaton Diet
abstract: HyperLTL extends LTL with quantification over traces. AUtoHyper is the de facto explicit-state model checker for HyperLTL, complete for an arbitrary quantifier prefix: it eliminates quantifiers through products of the formula's omega-automaton with the systems, complementing on quantifier alternations. However, it suffers from state explosion, as it fully materializes input systems and intermediate automata. We present OmegaHyper, an overhaul of AutoHyper that keeps its algorithm but decomposes and reduces the size of the processed automata, and integrates the Kofola omega-automaton complementation tool. We compare OmegaHyper with existing explicit-state and symbolic HyperLTL model checkers, on 120 benchmarks from their published suites. OmegaHyper improves the performance of explicit-state HyperLTL model checking by up to orders of magnitude; bounded symbolic tools still reach further on violated instances with short counterexamples, as expected.

title: Expand & Reduce: a Framework Bridging Branch-and-Reduce and Dynamic Programming
abstract: We introduce expand-and-reduce, a framework that augments classical reduction rules with a new type of optimality-preserving operation, called an expansion rule. While a reduction rule in practice typically makes the instance smaller, an expansion rule may enlarge the instance yet still making progress towards a solution. We present a simple expansion rule called edge expansion for the Maximum Weighted Independent Set (MWIS) problem. It encodes the joint choice of two non-adjacent vertices by adding an edge between them and creating a new vertex representing their union. We prove that the number of edge expansions needed to transform a graph into a clique equals the number of independent sets in the graph minus the number of vertices. We demonstrate that expand-and-reduce, using edge expansion and just two well-known reduction rules, has greater reduction power than a set of 22 commonly used reduction rules for MWIS. Therefore, it can significantly simplify methods that depend on reduction rules. To highlight the practical potential of the expand-and-reduce framework further, we provide an implementation and preliminary results showing that a simple implementation outperforms a far more advanced method for MWIS preprocessing. Moreover, expand-and-reduce can simulate both branching and dynamic-programming-style state construction, yielding exact and fixed-parameter algorithms with matching asymptotic running times. By that, expand-and-reduce offers a unified and conceptually clean perspective on techniques that are usually considered incompatible.

title: DetailScale-SR: Decoupling Restoration and Continuous Detail Control for Real-World Super-Resolution
abstract: Real-world image super-resolution often seeks the most detailed plausible reconstruction, although more detail is not always desirable. The same degraded image may require restrained restoration, faithful reconstruction, or enhanced visual detail according to user intent. We present DetailScale-SR, a preference-conditioned framework that continuously controls reconstructed detail for a fixed low-resolution input without altering the scene being restored. Rather than relying on post-processing or repeatedly rewriting prompts, it learns a continuous family of reconstructions while separating content recovery from detail preference. This enables a smooth transition from conservative restoration to richly textured results under consistent input and semantic constraints. Its controllable range also extends beyond conventional restoration: DetailScale-SR can enhance high-frequency structures and generate perceptually richer textures than the paired high-resolution reference. Text restoration is another distinct strength. For text-rich scenes, especially Chinese posters and signs, it recovers more legible and character-faithful text than prior generative SR methods under matched textual guidance. DetailScale-SR therefore unifies continuous detail control, beyond-reference enhancement, and reliable recovery of semantically important content. Our model is available at https://modelscope.cn/models/DiffSynth-Studio/Qwen-Image-2.1-SR

title: Continuous Noisy-Loop Models
abstract: Efficient learning and inference need not imply a compact probabilistic circuit. We quantify this distinction for continuous noisy readings of agreement between adjacent latent spins on a known square grid with $d$ edges. With known margins and bounded Lipschitz channels, minimax squared Hellinger risk is $Θ(\min\{1,dN^{-2/3}\})$ from $N$ independent vectors, without a reliability lower bound. A spline estimator reaches this rate in polynomial arithmetic time given a fixed positive reliability bound; an exponential-size mixture removes that requirement. At fixed positive reliability, nonnegative decomposable circuits need $\exp(Θ(\sqrt d))$ nodes for fixed total-variation error below one, even when each leaf uses at most $αd$ coordinates, $0<α<1$. Optimal Kullback--Leibler (KL) approximation error is $Θ(d/\max\{\log d,\sqrt\ell\})$ in either direction with at most $d^r$ nodes and leaf scopes $\ell\leqαd$, for fixed $r>1$ and $0<α<2/3$. Node counts exclude leaf computation. For three fixed masks, optimal joint conditional KL has order $d/\log d$ when $\ell\leq(\log d)^2$. Local cycle identities relate joint divergence to identifiable channel products and separate weak-channel recovery from density estimation. Factorized evidence preserves a planar zero-field Ising model: given local integrals, exact queries cost $O(d^{3/2})$ arithmetic operations and one root extraction.

title: Towards Reliable Scaling Laws for Tabular Foundation Models
abstract: Scaling laws are widely used to predict foundation model performance and guide compute allocation. However, tabular foundation models (TFMs) differ from conventional foundation models in that they are pretrained on virtually unlimited synthetic data from configurable distributions, while ultimately being evaluated on real-world datasets. We investigate whether scaling laws for TabPFNv2-style models reliably extrapolate to larger compute budgets and generalize across evaluation settings. Our analysis reveals differences between synthetic and real-world scaling behavior and shows that accurately fitting a scaling law does not necessarily yield reliable prescriptions on unseen datasets. In particular, selecting configurations using too few evaluation datasets leads to systematically over-optimistic performance estimates. We further demonstrate that compute-optimal scaling requires expanding the range of synthetic pretraining dataset sizes alongside model size and training compute. Increasing the maximum numbers of rows and features sampled during pretraining improves performance and produces more predictable scaling trends.
