These insights guide the training of more efficient TabPFNv2-like models, using the open-source training pipeline of nanoTabPFN.

title: On Jacquet Modules of Principal Series in Families
abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over a $p$-adic field $F$. Let $Y$ be the diagonalizable affine group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}[p^{-1},p^{1/2}]$ parametrizing weakly unramified characters of a minimal Levi $M$. The relative Weyl group $W$ acts on $Y$. We define a coherent sheaf $\mathcal{J}$, called the universal Jacquet module, on the fiber product $Y\times_{Y/\!/W}Y$. The fibers of $\mathcal{J}$ can be identified with the duals of spaces of intertwining operators between weakly unramified principal series representations of $G$. We use the geometry of $Y\times_{Y/\!/W}Y$ to study the fundamental properties of $\mathcal{J}$. In particular, we determine the invertible locus of $\mathcal{J}$. Thus we show that for any field $k$ with $\operatorname{char}k\neq p, p^{1/2}\in k$ and any weakly unramified character $χ\in Y(k)$, the normalized Jacquet module $π_{χ,N}$ of the normalized parabolic induction $π_χ=\operatorname{ind}_P^Gχ$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal{O}(χ\times_{Y/\!/W}Y)$ as an $\mathcal{O}(Y)$-module if and only if $\operatorname{End}_G(π_χ)\cong k$. This addresses the precise non-semisimple structure of Jacquet modules in the scalar endomorphism case. Specializing to the case in which $G$ is split, $χ$ is trivial, and $k=\mathbb{C}$, this proves a conjecture of Dipendra Prasad. We also show that the isomorphism $π_{χ,N}\cong\mathcal{O}(χ\times_{Y/\!/W}Y)$ cannot be defined canonically over the family of characters $χ$ satisfying $\operatorname{End}_G(π_χ)\cong\mathbb{C}$, by showing that the restriction of $\mathcal{J}$ to its invertible locus is a nontrivial line bundle if the relative root system of $G$ contains an irreducible component of rank at least two.

title: The Comprehension Gap in LLM-Assisted Software Development: An Experiment
abstract: When LLM tools are pushed beyond their capabilities for software development tasks, developers must be able to step in. However, the comprehension that developers acquire during development might be negatively impacted due to excessive code generation. This could create a cognitive debt that needs to be resolved before tasks can be solved efficiently again. We explore how well developers understand code they generated by prompting in comparison to self-written and unseen code and how they reflect on their comprehension. We conduct a crossover experiment and interviews with 35 participants consisting of students, academic personnel, and software developers. After completing two programming tasks with or without LLM chat usage, respectively, participants are tasked with finding introduced mutations in the produced and additional unseen code. We use insights from interviews and screen recordings to supplement our results. Regarding the experiment, 36% of participants report a better understanding of self-written code compared to their generated code. On average, participants solved the comprehension task 20% faster for self-written code than for generated code and found 11% more mutations. Participants needed significantly less time to solve programming tasks when working with the LLM. However, participants with high reliance on the LLM chat and low task engagement showed significantly decreased comprehension. Our qualitative results show great variability in individual perspectives on comprehension differences and strategies to mitigate issues. Strategies for dealing with comprehension differences range from accepting comprehension differences to adapting their LLM interactions or avoiding the tools altogether. Our results warrant further investigation into cognitive debt in larger systems and developer practices to mitigate issues.

title: A Tight Broad-line Width-Luminosity Relation in Little Red Dots and Its Consequence for Virial Black Hole Masses
abstract: JWST has uncovered compact high-redshift sources with red, $\sim 5000$ K optical continua and broad Balmer lines, known as "little red dots" (LRDs). Whether these lines trace gas orbiting a massive black hole or electron scattering in a dense, Eddington-limited envelope around a lighter black hole leaves inferred masses spanning $10^{4}$-$10^{8}\,M_{\odot}$. We test both pictures by uniformly refitting public JWST/NIRSpec spectra of 29 LRDs, 15 other JWST broad-line sources, and luminosity-matched SDSS quasars. At fixed $\mathrm{H}α$ luminosity, LRD broad $\mathrm{H}α$ widths have an intrinsic scatter of 0.054 dex ($<0.075$ dex at 95%), less than half that of quasars (0.12 dex), clustering near $1760\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ outside the three brightest sources. Because single-epoch virial masses scale as width squared, they scatter intrinsically by $<0.16$ dex at fixed $\mathrm{H}α$ luminosity, making virial masses and mass functions nearly deterministic restatements of luminosity regardless of the underlying physics. Compared with the Keplerian speed $v_{\rm K}$ at the photosphere of an Eddington-limited envelope, from each source's measured continuum luminosity and temperature, observed widths are 2.5-3.0 $v_{\rm K}$ (2-3$\times$ standard expectations for virial factors $f_{\rm vir}\approx 0.5$-1), with a quarter of the flux above escape speed and no detected continuum-luminosity dependence at fixed $\mathrm{H}α$ luminosity. Bound orbits outside a spherical photosphere thus require sub-Eddington optical luminosities ($\leq 0.10$-0.30 $L_{\rm Edd}$, a requirement specific to spherical photospheres), whereas an Eddington or super-Eddington spherical envelope requires uniform 2-3$\times$ non-gravitational broadening within the $\mathrm{H}α$-emitting gas.

title: TableControl: Gesture Interaction Through Surface Vibrations
abstract: Integrating gesture sensing into furniture offers a way to interact with digital applications and physical devices through familiar surfaces. We present TableControl, an interactive demonstration of continuous surface-vibration-based gesture recognition with the complete processing pipeline running on a microcontroller. Using four concealed piezoelectric sensors, the system combines signal acquisition and preprocessing with neural event detection and gesture classification. The resulting labels for knock, swipe-up, and swipe-down gestures are transmitted to a host computer without streaming the underlying sensor signals. Visitors explore two example applications through hands-on interaction: an endless runner game and a physical table lamp with on/off and brightness control. A dashboard displays recognized gestures, class probabilities, and processing times.

title: The Partially Saturated Cells Method for Complex Moving Geometries in Turbulent Flow Conditions
abstract: We present four application cases to test and validate fluid-structure-interaction models based on the Lattice Boltzmann and the Partially Saturated Cells method (PSM) for turbulent flow conditions. For a flow around a stationary sphere we compare the PSM with direct mapping boundary conditions and achieve good agreement to reference data for Reynolds numbers up to one million. In particular, the model predicts the drag crisis for this case with good accuracy. For a three dimensional airfoil simulation at a Reynolds number of 150000, the PSM predicts the stall angle for a NACA0018 profile with excellent accuracy. For a geometry-resolved stirred tank simulation at a Reynolds number of 29000 the PSM produces the time averaged velocity profiles around the impeller with excellent fidelity. Finally, a wind turbine geometry is resolved with the PSM for a tip Reynolds number of 40000, where thrust and mean velocity in the turbine wake shows excellent agreement with reference data from literature.

title: Erased but Recoverable: On the Fragility of Concept Erasure Under Fine-Tuning
abstract: Existing concept erasure methods for text-to-image diffusion models primarily focus on suppressing target concepts while preserving non-target generation quality. However, in practical applications, open-source diffusion models are often further adapted through DreamBooth, LoRA, or Custom Diffusion. Such adaptations can reshape internal representations, thereby weakening or even reversing the erasure effects achieved by existing methods. We identify erasure persistence as a key yet underexplored dimension of concept erasure and analyze how downstream fine-tuning reshapes internal representations. Our analysis reveals that fine-tuning of the original model does not uniformly modify the model, but preserves certain high-contribution structures, particularly attention heads with stable output subspaces and response magnitudes. We also observe that, after downstream fine-tuning of concept-erased models, these heads' output representations more readily realign with their pretrained counterparts. Motivated by this observation, we propose Stable-Head-Aware Concept Erasure (SHACE), which improves erasure persistence by preserving stable attention structures during concept erasure. SHACE identifies stability-critical attention heads through Attention-Head Stability Profiling and keeps their corresponding parameter blocks unchanged during erasure via Stable-Head Gradient Preservation. Extensive experiments show that SHACE improves resistance to concept recovery across diverse fine-tuning settings while maintaining strong suppression and non-target generation quality.

title: Learning to Coordinate: LLM-Guided Workflow Evolution for Token-Efficient Red Teaming
abstract: Automated red teaming is essential for identifying safety failures in large language models (LLMs), but its practical scalability depends on the resources required to discover those failures. Multi-agent systems can combine complementary capabilities, yet repeated planning, redundant exchanges, and ineffective information routing can make their coordination expensive. Moreover, a target model's response indicates the outcome of a test without identifying which collaboration decision should change. We present Learning to Coordinate (L2C), an LLM-guided framework that evolves an executable multi-agent workflow for each red-teaming case. L2C represents agent responsibilities, execution dependencies, and input bindings in a versioned graph, and associates each graph with records of the information actually delivered and produced. A controller trained through supervised fine-tuning integrates these records with target responses, evaluator verdicts, and remaining budget to retain the workflow, refine instructions, restructure collaboration, or lock further editing. This design connects feedback to explicit changes in subsequent execution while allowing a useful organization to continue without repeated controller intervention. The evaluation protocol covers HarmBench with three execution backbones and two target models, together with component ablations, dataset transfer, and evaluator checks. Across the six executor-target configurations, L2C improves ASR over EvoSynth by 1.4 to 4.5 percentage points while reducing mean online tokens by 35.6% to 37.3%. L2C connects adaptive collaboration to the resource requirements of automated security evaluation.

title: Target-Consistent Action Guidance via Semi-Unbalanced Optimal Transport for Drifting World Models
abstract: Action-conditioned world models let robots imagine the outcomes of their actions for planning and offline policy evaluation, but these uses need many rollouts, which multi-step diffusion makes expensive. Drifting models move the iteration from inference to training and generate samples in one network pass. DriftWorld brought this paradigm to action-conditioned world models; to strengthen action following, it repels predictions from the current frame, a construction borrowed from classifier-free guidance. We show that this accentuation has a target bias: the push persists even when a prediction matches the recorded future, in kernel, balanced, and unbalanced Wasserstein drifting fields alike. We introduce Mass-Share Accentuation (MSA) to remove this bias. MSA treats the current frame as a counterfactual destination competing with the recorded future in a semi-relaxed optimal transport problem; subtracting the closed-form share of the correct future makes the guidance vanish at the target, and the remainder is shared by all predictions. We prove that the recorded future is the unique fixed point along the motion direction for collapsed predictions, and that the guidance fades with prediction error. On Push-T, Robomimic, and BridgeV2, where trained models under-react rather than overshoot, MSA improves action ranking, response slope, and moving-region error over latent-space baselines at no inference cost, though these benchmarks do not isolate bias removal as the cause.

title: Training Denoising Models of Any Architecture Without Stored Images
abstract: Can a pretrained denoising model replace the dataset used to train it? We investigate this question through teacher-supervised training, showing for the first time that continuous-time diffusion and flow models of any architecture and size can be trained from random initialization without stored images. Our students regress the teacher's velocity on a rolling pool of noisy samples, advanced along trajectories of random step counts to obtain independent, dense and approximately continuous noise levels. This saves considerable storage for large datasets and applies even when the data are unreleased or private. Our experiments include 12 teachers of 6 families and 6 datasets. Our method outperforms standard training of the same network on CIFAR-10 for students 4x smaller than the teacher, comes within 0.75 to 1.92 FID of it at the teacher's size and surpasses training on teacher-generated images and step reduction methods without teacher-based initialization. Our code is available at https://github.com/mever-team/ddm.

title: The Fujita equation with time-integrable forcing: effective mass, mass annihilation and sharp lifespan
abstract: We study the Cauchy problem $\partial_t u-Δu=|u|^p+ζ(t)w(x)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N\times(0,\infty)$, $p>1$, with sign-changing data and a forcing whose temporal profile $ζ$ is integrable on $(0,\infty)$, the model case being $ζ(t)=t^σe^{-t}$, $σ>-1$. For power-type profiles $ζ(t)=t^σ$ the forcing is known to raise the critical exponent above the Fujita exponent $p_F=1+2/N$ or to destroy global existence. We show that an integrable forcing leaves $p_F$ unchanged and acts only through the effective mass $M_{\rm eff}=\int u_0+(\int_0^\inftyζ)(\int w)$. Our central result is an exact mass-annihilation identity: if $1<p\le p_F$, every global weak solution lies in $L^p(\mathbb{R}^N\times(0,\infty))$ and satisfies $\iint|u|^p=-M_{\rm eff}$. Hence, for $p\le p_F$, no global solution exists when $M_{\rm eff}\ge0$ and the data are nontrivial, and every global mild solution vanishes in $L^1$ as $t\to\infty$; examples show that $M_{\rm eff}<0$ neither excludes nor implies global existence. For $p>p_F$, every solution is dominated by a multiple of the linear forced flow under a single integral condition; this gives small-data global existence without sign restrictions and, if $ζ$ decays mildly, convergence to $m_\infty G_t$ with asymptotic mass $m_\infty=M_{\rm eff}+\iint|u|^p$. We also give a localized necessary condition valid for all $p>1$, showing that large or slowly decaying data blow up regardless of the forcing and that non-integrable forcings shift the threshold, and sharp lifespan estimates for small data with positive effective mass: $T_\varepsilon\simeq\varepsilon^{-2(p-1)/(2-N(p-1))}$ for $p<p_F$ and $\log T_\varepsilon\simeq\varepsilon^{-(p-1)}$ for $p=p_F$.

title: Iterated socles and closure operations
abstract: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a $d$-dimensional Cohen--Macaulay local ring, $d\geq2$ containing a field, and let $J\subseteq\mathfrak m^s$ be a parameter ideal with $s\geq2$, also, in the mixed case via some mild assumptions. We prove for that $J:\mathfrak m^{(d-1)(s-1)}\subseteq\overline{J}$, and that $J:\mathfrak m^{(d-1)(s-1)+1}\subseteq\overline{J}$ when $R$ is not regular. We show that Cohen--Macaulayness cannot be removed. We also prove the characteristic-free exact formula $g(J)=(d-1)(s-1)+r$ for parameter ideals of order $s$ with a level tangent cone, giving singular mixed-characteristic Gorenstein and non-Gorenstein examples in which the singular bound is attained.

title: Neural Network-Based In-Contact Task Segmentation of Demonstrated Robot Motions via Hand Guiding
abstract: Intuitive robot programming approaches, such as Programming by Demonstration, enable non-experts to teach robots tasks through hand-guided demonstrations. However, for in-contact tasks requiring force control for parts of the motion, automated segmentation of motion types is crucial for improving usability. Considering the related work, this work proposes a neural network-based segmentation method categorizing motion into three fundamental types using input data of cartesian twists and wrenches at the end effector. We collect demonstration data using a 7-axis robot with a wrist-mounted force torque sensor and generate ground truth labeling by hand. While still in development, our research direction aims to enable non-experts to program in-contact tasks more intuitively.

title: A relativistic gravitisation of quantum theory?
abstract: We develop a model, that we call local semiclassical gravity, based on the distributional semiclassical Einstein field equations (EFEs) sourced by the local quantum state, i.e. the reduced density matrix of the local system updated by collapses (only) in its past light cone. We propose this as the basis of a relativistically causal generally covariant gravitisation of relativistic quantum theory in $1+3$ spacetime dimensions. We derive the weak-field limit which exhibits the explicitly causal dynamical structure of the theory, and recover the Schrödinger-Newton (SN) system in the nonrelativistic limit. This proposal can thus be understood as a causal completion of the SN equation, a nonlinear extension to quantum theory. We analyze relativistic quantum measurements in this nonlinear setup, showing that these do not lead to superluminal signalling if quantum states update (only) in the future light-cone of the measurement region. We give explicit examples of quantum measurements on a spatial superposition and on entangled subsystems showing how, in the weak field limit, discontinuities in the expectation value of the stress-energy tensor can be consistent with distributional solutions to the (linearised) semiclassical EFEs. We also highlight that the theory allows non-standard measurements via its nonlinearities. These effective ``readout devices'' can approximately determine a quantum state without affecting it through the state's influence on the classical gravitational field and hence can implement approximate quantum state cloning. Nonetheless, the theory does not allow superluminal signalling, although it does violate the quantum no-signalling principle. We further show that the classical gravitational field is generally not locally causal in the sense of Bell. We present several paths to test the model against low-energy quantum gravity in tabletop experiments.

title: Functional Principal Component Analysis: Minimax Optimality from Sparse to Dense Designs and Beyond
abstract: Functional principal component analysis (FPCA) plays a central role as a dimension-reduction and representation tool in functional data analysis, but its minimax theory for diverging spectral indices under noisy discrete observation has remained open for over two decades. To fill this gap, we consider a sieve-based FPCA framework that pools discrete measurements across subjects and accommodates sampling frequencies ranging from sparse to dense under random designs. We begin by establishing new minimax rates for covariance estimation over general bivariate function classes beyond tensor-product low-complexity structures, thereby identifying the intrinsically two-dimensional optimal rate. Our central theoretical contribution is to establish minimax optimal rates for both individually labelled eigenfunctions with diverging indices and leading principal subspaces of increasing dimensions, under explicit growth and regularity conditions. To establish these results, we develop a general framework for sharp minimax analysis of FPCA under discrete observation, separating spectral approximation from stochastic perturbations and exploiting their distinct structures, thereby offering a new approach to a broad class of nonparametric spectral estimation problems. For both spectral targets, the optimal rates reveal two distinct statistical mechanisms, spectral identification and nonparametric reconstruction, whose interplay gives rise to either four or two sampling regimes. This yields, for the first time, a precise characterization of the impact of discrete sampling across the full range from sparse to dense designs. Finally, as a downstream application, we analyze FPCA-based functional linear regression and show that the FPCA-based estimator attains the minimax-optimal rates.

title: ProbeShare: Probing a Few, Sharing Across Many for Fast World-Model Planning
abstract: Visual planning with a frozen joint-embedding world model supports robotic reaching and object manipulation by evaluating candidate action sequences against an image goal before execution. Standard cross-entropy method (CEM) planners roll out every candidate independently through a billion-parameter predictor, even when nearby actions induce similar scene changes. This redundant computation grows with population size and search rounds, slowing closed-loop replanning. We observe that candidates within a planning step share an observation history and thus a common action-to-feature map. Based on this insight, we propose ProbeShare, which measures local responses with a few representative probes and reconstructs each candidate's feature grid through scene-conditioned, geometry-aware weighting. When promising candidates move beyond existing probe coverage, ProbeShare evaluates a new probe to rescore nearby candidates. Across four RoboCasa tasks, ProbeShare accelerates episode planning by 43.8--128.9 times over dense RoboJEPA and at least $14.2\times$ over competitive baselines, with greater mean goal progress in a matched-time comparison.

title: Large Single Crystal Growth and Transport Properties of KCd$_4$As$_3$ and RbCd$_4$As$_3$
abstract: Large-size KCd$_4$As$_3$ and RbCd$_4$As$_3$ single crystals were grown using the flux method. Appropriate flux for growing single crystals was determined to be Cd$_2$As, resulting in the increase in their size to be a centimeter for KCd$_4$As$_3$. The KCd$_4$As$_3$ and RbCd$_4$As$_3$ crystals exhibited metal-like temperature dependences of their electrical resistivities with negative Seebeck coefficients, characterizing them as n-type thermoelectric materials.

title: What Survives the Shift from Text to Pixels? Conditional Protection against Prompt Injection in Image-Rendered Documents
abstract: Multimodal language models increasingly answer questions over external documents, exposing them to indirect prompt injection: commands planted in untrusted content to hijack the response. Rendering untrusted content as page images lowers attack success on average, leaving open which injected operations survive rendering, at what utility cost, and whether failed image attacks reflect unread commands or commands read but not followed. We pair text and page-image versions of 191 English question-answering sources across six models, measuring marker appending, answer formatting, and answer replacement alongside clean Question-Answering utility. Rendering reduces append and format execution for every model, yet Qwen3-VL-8B still executes image-borne replacement at 77.96\%. Protection also depends on target type, rendering settings, wording, and repetition, and a search over eight fixed attack candidates largely closes the image deficit in appending and formatting for Qwen and Gemini, though not for GPT-5-nano. Utility ratios on original questions range from 93.31\% to 101.61\%, but Qwen falls to 61.99\% when answers combine two evidence spans. Illegibility cannot explain all failed attacks: models often transcribe and identify image-borne commands they do not execute, and trusted user authorization raises execution on unchanged pages. Inside Qwen, patching early attack-region states induces all three operations, more weakly in images. Attention blocking suggests why: a text command acts through its own positions, whereas visual encoding spreads an image command and its target across the instruction page. Rendering thus offers conditional protection, motivating evaluations that report security by model, operation, and attack budget alongside utility.

title: Stochastic Optimisation for Scalable Ptychographic Image Reconstruction
abstract: X-ray ptychography is a lensless coherent diffraction imaging technique capable of high spatial resolution, in which an image is reconstructed by solving a large-scale inverse problem from highly redundant far-field diffraction measurements acquired under overlapping illumination. Whilst the measurement redundancy created by overlapping illumination is essential for reconstruction fidelity, it leads to computational and memory demands that scale poorly with object size and target resolution when using conventional reconstruction algorithms. This work proposes a ptychographic reconstruction framework that reduces peak memory usage and time to convergence by leveraging stochastic optimisation techniques developed for large-scale machine learning. Specifically, the framework employs stochastic gradient descent with a decaying step size that progressively reduces the effect of gradient noise, referred to here as variance reduction (VR), with gradients that agree with automatic differentiation, to optimise the ptychographic forward model using randomly sampled subsets of diffraction measurements. For an experimental dataset of 200,000 diffraction patterns of $128\times128$ pixels, VR is demonstrated to require $65\%$ of the peak GPU memory and $22\%$ of the reconstruction time of the established maximum-likelihood (ML) algorithm. The VR framework incorporates the Poisson maximum-likelihood formulation and partial coherence within a unified and extensible optimisation setting. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the framework achieves reconstruction quality visually comparable to established methods, with lower peak GPU memory and a shorter time

title: Psychometrics-Inspired Coreset Selection for Image Quality Assessment
abstract: Collecting large-scale subjective annotations remains a critical bottleneck in training accurate image quality assessment (IQA) models. Coreset selection reduces this burden by selecting representative images before annotation. However, diversity in a visual feature space does not necessarily reflect diversity in perceptual quality, raising a fundamental question about which quality-related factors the representation should encode. We propose GRAM, a quality-aware representation learning framework inspired by the graded response model (GRM) from psychometrics. GRM describes how an individual's latent ability determines the probabilities of reaching successive assessment grades, with response sensitivity and grade thresholds governing this relationship. In this paper, we find that this principle naturally aligns with perceptual quality assessment, where the impact of image degradation depends on image content and distortion characteristics. Building on this connection, GRAM models quality judgments through three complementary factors: latent quality, content-dependent response sensitivity, and distortion-dependent grade thresholds. These factors jointly determine the probabilities of attaining different quality grades and the resulting expected quality score. The learned parameters provide a structured quality-aware representation that complements general visual features for coreset selection. Experiments on nine datasets demonstrate improvements across different selection strategies, downstream IQA models, and annotation budgets. The code will be made publicly available.

title: Hardware Acceleration of Vision-Language-Action Models with Weight Precision Rising over the Flow Steps
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models such as GR00T control robots through an action head: a diffusion transformer that turns noise into a chunk of actions in a few flow-matching steps. Every step re-reads all of the head's weights from DRAM but applies each weight to only about fifty tokens. Inference is therefore memory-bound, and its latency and energy are largely determined by the total number of transferred weight bits. We show that later flow steps attenuate the quantization errors of earlier steps, so the weight precision of an action head should rise over the steps. With plain per-channel rounding and without calibration or training, widths rising over the steps from 2 to 4 bits preserve the closed-loop success of robot policies. These widths transfer 25% fewer bits than 4-bit weights at every step. However, we show that on Jetson AGX Thor, current GPU kernels cannot exploit this per-step precision due to fixed overheads. We therefore present a programmable accelerator whose latency and energy both scale with the transferred weight bits. It decodes entropy-coded weights for bit-serial sub-arrays at the DRAM rate. Because the width changes per step, a run-time allocator divides these sub-arrays between the linear layers and the attention to balance their workloads. The same sub-arrays are thus capable of running action heads of different families and sizes, as well as a vision-language model. On the DRAM side, a requantizer and an entropy encoder at each bank let one stored 8-bit copy replace the copies of all widths. Simulated with LPDDR5X timing, our RTL implementation runs the GR00T N1.6 action head in 8.02 ms per inference with 2, 3, 3 and 4 bits in its four flow steps. With a copy per width and 50% of Thor's memory bandwidth, the accelerator runs this schedule 1.7x faster than Thor in NVFP4, at 9.1x less energy and equal closed-loop success.

title: Canonical Proof Nets for Intuitionistic Multiplicative Linear Logic
abstract: We study the problem of finding canonical representations of proofs in the multiplicative fragment of intuitionistic linear logic with units. We show that, contrary to the classical case, it is possible to define a notion of proof nets for this fragment which is provided with a polynomial-time sequentialization procedure and is both canonical and efficient. In particular, we show that sequent calculus derivations differing only by a permutation of independent rule applications are translated to the same proof net, and that the translations between sequent calculus and proof nets are inverse to each other.

title: From a finite subgroup of $SO(3)$:$C_2$ leads to a Holant dichotomy
abstract: Counting complexity within the Holant framework has been extensively studied through complexity dichotomy theorems. While substantial progress has been achieved for various restricted settings, the general complex-valued even-arity case without auxiliary unary signatures remains largely open. This paper studies a fundamental case in this program where the binary signatures induce a group structure satisfying \(M(B(\mathcal{F}))\cong C_2\). It is observed that projective equivalence classes of binary signature matrices naturally embed into finite subgroups of \(SO(3)\), providing an algebraic viewpoint for structural classification. This paper further identifies two fundamentally different regimes for the \(C_2\) case, namely the normal and isotropic cases, and analyzes their complexity behavior separately. Combining gadget constructions, decomposition techniques, interpolation arguments, and a realnumberization approach that transforms the complex-valued setting into an equivalent real-structured framework, this paper establishes a complete dichotomy theorem: for every even-arity signature set \(\mathcal{F}\) satisfying \(M(\B(\mathcal{F}))\cong C_2\), the problem \(\mathrm{Holant}(\mathcal{F})\) is either polynomial-time computable or \#P-hard. A Pauli-basis representation for signatures is further introduced as an algebraically natural language for organizing realizable signatures and revealing structural relations that are less transparent in the standard basis.

title: A semialgebraic description of matrices of positive semidefinite rank at most 2
abstract: The main result of this paper is a semialgebraic description of the set of matrices of rank at most 3 and psd rank at most 2. Such a semialgebraic description allows one to check whether a matrix has rank at most 3 and psd rank at most 2. This description builds on the geometric characterization of matrices of rank 3 and psd rank 2 using the existence of an ellipse nested between two polygons. The main step towards deriving the semialgebraic description is the observation that we need to consider only finitely many ellipses that go through some of the vertices of the inner polygon and are tangent to some of the edges of the outer polygon. Although the description is not completely quantifier-free, for a general matrix, the quantified variables satisfy a system of polynomial equations that has at most four solutions corresponding to reduced conics.

title: Counting shorter even cycles in graphs forbidding an even cycle
abstract: For graphs $H$ and $F$, the generalized Turán number $\operatorname{ex}(n,H,F)$ is the maximum number of copies of $H$ in an $n$-vertex $F$-free graph. Let $C_m$ be a cycle on $m$ vertices. Liu and Wu (2026) proved that, for fixed integers $k>\ell\ge 2$, $\operatorname{ex}(n,C_{2\ell},C_{2k})=\left(\frac{(k-1)_\ell}{2\ell}+o(1)\right)n^\ell$, where $(k-1)_\ell=(k-1)\cdots(k-\ell)$. In this paper, we determine the exact value of $\operatorname{ex}(n,C_{2\ell},C_{2k})$ for all sufficiently large $n$ and characterize the unique extremal graph.

title: Approximation Algorithms for Product Query Optimization
abstract: We study database query optimization for Cartesian products. This problem is equivalent to finding an optimal plan for multiplying non-negative integers. We call this problem multiplication ordering. We show that the problem has an FPTAS when the cost of a plan is the sum of all intermediate products; both in the case when the overall final product is counted and when it is not. We show that using the optimal solution to the well-known product partition problem does not always lead to an optimal plan, but we establish connections between the product partition and multiplication ordering problems. Finally, we prove that multiplication ordering is in PTIME (resp. \NP-complete) when integers are powers of a same base where the exponents are written in unary (resp. in binary).

title: ViLFlow: Parallel Vision-Language Generation with Continuous Latent Flows
abstract: Vision-language generation has predominantly relied on autoregressive and discrete diffusion models. Autoregressive models generate tokens sequentially, while discrete diffusion models typically predict tokens independently within each denoising step. We propose ViLFlow (Vision-Language Flow), a continuous-flow vision-language model that combines joint modeling of output embeddings with parallel token decoding. ViLFlow adapts pretrained continuous language generation to visual question answering and image captioning through learned image guidance and prediction-aware token decoding. A visually adapted teacher provides image-guided predictions as additional denoising supervision. The denoiser learns to reproduce these predictions directly, retaining one image-conditioned prediction per generation step. We train the token decoder on denoiser predictions and paired reference text to improve the conversion of continuous outputs into words. The decoder can be adapted independently, improving answering and captioning without further denoiser training. For captioning, it also supplies text feedback during late denoising, allowing decoded words to inform subsequent refinement. ViLFlow outperforms autoregressive and masked-diffusion baselines by up to 8.46 percentage points on VQAv2 and 4.50 points on GQA without GQA training. On COCO Karpathy test, it improves CIDEr by 16.25 over masked diffusion and 17.81 over sampled autoregression.

title: Search for Heavy Charged Higgs Bosons in Boosted Top and Bottom Quark Final States at a 1.4 TeV Future Lepton Collider
abstract: The discovery potential for heavy charged Higgs bosons $H^\pm$ decaying into a top-bottom quark pair is investigated at a future $e^+e^-$ collider operating at $\sqrt{s}=1.4~\mathrm{TeV}$. The study considers charged Higgs masses between 200 and 600 GeV within all four Yukawa types of the two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM). The boosted $tb$ final state is explored using complementary cut-based and machine-learning analyses based on boosted decision trees (BDT). The expected signal significance and sensitivity contours in the $(m_{H^\pm},\tanβ)$ plane are obtained for each Yukawa type. The resulting sensitivity extends to regions of the 2HDM parameter space beyond the projected reach of the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC), demonstrating the complementary potential of a future high-energy lepton collider to probe heavy charged Higgs bosons.

title: Joint Image Denoising and Interpolation via Mixed Graph Filtering
abstract: Images often require both denoising and interpolation, yet treating the two tasks separately is suboptimal: interpolation introduces correlated noise that complicates subsequent denoising, while denoising may remove image details useful for interpolation. In this paper, we study joint image denoising and interpolation from a mixed graph filtering perspective, where denoising is modeled using undirected graph filters and interpolation using directed graph filters. We first establish that, under mild conditions, any (pseudo-)linear denoiser and interpolator can be interpreted as solution filters of maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation problems regularized by undirected and directed graph smoothness priors, respectively. Guided by these results, we formulate graph-based joint denoising and interpolation problems using both directed and undirected graph structures. We characterize when joint denoising/interpolation reduces to a separable pipeline and when a genuinely coupled optimization is required. For the non-separable case, we recover sparse graph operators from given denoisers and interpolators, yielding an efficient linear-system formulation solvable via conjugate gradient. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed joint framework consistently outperforms separate denoising and interpolation pipelines across multiple denoiser-interpolator combinations.

title: End-to-End Landsat Land Surface Temperature Reconstruction with AlphaEarth Embeddings
abstract: Land surface temperature (LST) data at Landsat's 30 m resolution is important for many applications, but cloud contamination prevents its spatially continuous observations. Here, we propose A$^2$E$^2$, an end-to-end U-Net that integrates annual temperature cycle (ATC), coarse LST from Earth system modeling, and AlphaEarth embeddings for Landsat LST reconstruction. The ATC supplies a physics-guided thermal prior, the coarse LST provides a temporal background, and the U-Net converts the embedding field into day-specific fine-scale correction using observed pixels. Experimental results on four seasonally distributed Landsat 8/9 scenes over New York City in 2022 show that A$^2$E$^2$ achieves 0.78 K mean absolute error and 1.01 K root mean squared error, reducing error by 60.1% relative to baseline method without spatial correction and by 3.7% relative to the same U-Net guided by annual mean spectral reflectance. Sensitivity analysis shows stable performance regardless of distance to clear pixels and percentage of blocked pixels. Independent validation with ECOSTRESS LST shows that Earth foundation model embeddings have better performance than annual mean spectral bands for LST reconstruction.

title: CommDreamer: Radio-Geometric World Models for Mapless Cellular-Connected UAV Trajectory Planning
abstract: Reliable cellular connectivity and collision-free flight are essential for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) operations in low-altitude urban canyons, where dense 3D buildings obstruct flight clearance, shadow serving base stations, and create strong co-channel interference at street intersections. Existing planners either require prior 3D city meshes and channel knowledge maps unavailable onboard, or rely on model-free reinforcement learning with low sample efficiency and poor cross-city generalization. We propose CommDreamer, a mapless radio-geometric world model that fuses raw onboard 3D LiDAR scans, multicell cellular reports, and shift-invariant relative kinematics to jointly infer local obstacle clearance and directional signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) dynamics. Using a categorical recurrent state-space model, CommDreamer compresses multimodal measurement histories into a coordinate-invariant latent belief, enabling the UAV to foresee deep shadow zones and train a lightweight online policy purely via multi-step latent imagination without prior maps or antenna patterns. Zero-shot evaluations across unseen urban morphologies in our open-source ray-tracing simulator, AeroCity-RT, show that CommDreamer converges within 150 episodes where model-free reinforcement learning fails to complete flights, achieving 100.0% mission success with zero collisions while lifting median route SINR to 8.02 dB and cutting effective SINR outage by over 50% relative to radio-blind world-model and reactive LiDAR baselines.

title: Mixed-integer programming formulations for the quadratic bin packing problem: linearization, hybridization, and enhancements
abstract: The quadratic bin packing problem (QBPP) extends the classical bin packing problem by incorporating pairwise dissimilarity values between items assigned to the same bin. The objective is to minimize the total cost, composed of the cost associated with the number of bins used and the sum of pairwise dissimilarity values for items assigned to the same bin, subject to the bin-capacity constraints. We study the quadratic programming formulation together with a broad family of equivalent mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulations for the QBPP based on classical linearization techniques. We analyze the relationships among the linear programming relaxations of the MILP formulations and strengthen several of these relaxations by exploiting the structure of the QBPP. We further introduce the first hybrid exact formulation for the QBPP that combines elements of two distinct modeling approaches. In particular, we show that the combination of explicit bin patterns and assignment-based representation performs particularly well. For the hybrid formulation, we investigate the effect of item selection, and for both the hybrid and non-hybrid formulations, we study the impact of item ordering on formulation size, relaxation strength and computational performance. Although a recently introduced tailored branch-and-price algorithm remains the state-of-the-art for the QBPP, we show that the proposed ordering-based non-hybrid and hybrid formulations substantially improve computational performance over the best MILP formulation known to the literature, in addition of solving 33 new benchmark instances to optimality.

title: Quadratic Convexity for Closed and Free Boundary High Codimension Mean Curvature Flow
abstract: We introduce quadratic convexity for mean curvature flow in high codimension. It combines quantitative convexity in the mean curvature direction with control of the full second fundamental form. Strict Andrews-Baker quadratic pinching implies quadratic convexity, while the new inequality also admits curvature tensors beyond the critical quadratic ratio. For compact connected closed submanifolds of dimension $n\geq5$, we prove preservation of quadratic convexity and convergence in finite time to a round point. For compact connected submanifolds of dimension $n\geq4$ with spherical free boundary, we prove preservation and convergence to a round hemisphere in a uniquely determined $(n+1)$-plane. To our knowledge, this is the first such convergence theorem for spherical free boundary MCF in arbitrary codimension. The closed theorem requires additional quadratic pinching for $5\leq n\leq7$, and the free boundary theorem for $4\leq n\leq7$. For $n\geq8$, the necessary quadratic bound follows from quadratic convexity. We also establish preservation of ordinary quadratic pinching $|A|^2\leq c|H|^2$ under spherical free boundary flow for $n\ge2$ and $\frac{9}{8n}\leq c\leq\frac{4}{3n}$, including both endpoints.

title: Allocentric Memory, Egocentric Acting: A Dual-Frame VLA for Urban Aerial Navigation
abstract: Language-goal aerial navigation requires a UAV to reach a destination specified in natural language using observations collected during flight. A key challenge is linking changing egocentric perception with spatial evidence anchored to stable locations for long-range navigation. We propose CityNav-VLA, a dual-frame vision-language-action model for urban navigation integrating dynamic egocentric context with persistent allocentric spatial memory. The UAV incrementally accumulates visual observations on a fixed north-up map initialized with geographic and landmark priors, preserving evidence across viewpoint changes. A dynamic query conditioned on the instruction, current observations, UAV state, and motion history retrieves relevant memory evidence to predict a map-frame target. A deterministic controller converts this target into body-frame commands using the UAV's current pose, connecting global reasoning with egocentric execution. To reduce target fluctuations over long horizons, early goal commitment (EGC) fixes the execution target to the coordinate-wise median of the first $K$ predictions without extra trainable parameters. On Test Unseen, CityNav-VLA reduces NE by 21.2% and improves SR and SPL by 15.8% and 30.9%, respectively. It also reduces NE by 6.2% and improves SR and SPL by 5.6% and 23.2%, respectively, relative to the former SOTA after dataset refinement. Cumulative ablations show that navigation-map features yield the largest gains, while metric coordinates further improve endpoint accuracy. With a 4B-scale backbone, inference averages 0.68 s per decision with 8.6 GB peak memory on a single A100, presenting remarkable model efficiency.

title: PMKPIR: Parallel Multi-Keyword PIR with Interleaved Batching for Private Boolean Retrieval
abstract: Keyword Private Information Retrieval (Keyword PIR) allows users to retrieve data associated with specific keywords from a database while protecting query privacy. However, existing Keyword PIR schemes supporting boolean retrieval either incur high computational overhead due to multiple database traversals, or fail to support universal boolean computation. We propose PMKPIR, a novel keyword PIR scheme supporting both parallel multi-keyword queries and universal boolean computation. We utilize the single instruction multiple data (SIMD) capability of BFV homomorphic encryption to propose an interleaved batching method, and design IBPIR based on this method, achieving the private matching of multiple keywords in a single database traversal. Furthermore, we design a boolean query processing method, extending the parallel capability of interleaved batching from keyword querying to boolean query computation, to support universal boolean computation and accelerate boolean operations. Building upon IBPIR, we integrate this method to further design PMKPIR. To the best of our knowledge, PMKPIR is the first Keyword PIR scheme to support multi-keyword batch matching within boolean queries. Security analysis demonstrates that, consistent with existing PIR schemes supporting boolean retrieval, PMKPIR preserves the core security guarantees of classic PIR. Compared with state-of-the-art schemes, PMKPIR reduces query time, communication overhead, storage overhead, and peak memory by up to 79.06%, 75.00%, 97.92%, and 80.26%, respectively.

title: From Points to Trajectories: Rethinking Multimodal Alignment for Physical Events
abstract: Advancing physical artificial intelligence (Physical AI) requires moving beyond static object recognition to ground how real-world mechanics (e.g., impact, friction, and force transfer) unfold over time. While multimodal aligners seek to capture these interactions by matching multi-sensor streams, prevailing architectures compress each temporal sequence into a single pooled embedding. We show that this paradigm fails on twin events: distinct physical executions recorded under identical task conditions. Collapsing the temporal dimension averages out transient cross-modal dynamics, effectively reducing physical event alignment to static scene recognition. Formally, we prove that as sequence length increases, any temporally pooled representation converges to the stationary recording condition. Consequently, as windows grow, no choice of loss function or embedding geometry can disambiguate twin events from pooled features alone. Instead, we show that physical events are uniquely identified by the event gap, namely the instantaneous, synchronous co-fluctuations across modalities that are erased by pooling and accumulate only along unpooled trajectories. To recover this signal, we introduce CounterPoint, a lightweight plug-in module that strips out each modality's temporal mean to score frame-level cross-modal agreement. Integrated across four state-of-the-art (SOTA) multimodal aligners, CounterPoint shifts representations from coarse condition matching to fine-grained physical event alignment, consistently outperforming existing temporal alignment methods.

title: Grade Restriction Rule For D-Brane Transport In Non-Abelian Gauged Linear Sigma Models
abstract: We study the low energy behaviour of B-type D-branes in non-Abelian gauged linear sigma models. The main problem is to determine the grade restriction rule for D-brane transport from one phase to another along paths. We analyze the convergence condition of the integral for the hemisphere partition function. We perform a thorough analysis in a particular model with two phases, one weakly coupled and one strongly coupled, both corresponding to Calabi-Yau threefolds. General methods are developed in this study and are applied to other models successfully. The integrals for a set of special Chan-Paton representations exhibit critical behaviour around each singular point on the phase boundary. From each of these points emanate ``no entry zones'' where a convergent contour is lost or is forced to traverse Gamma function poles. Knowledge of the special representations and no entry zones is strong enough to uniquely determine the grade restriction rule. In the course of this study, we encounter a problem in Weyl invariance of convergent contours, which forces us to modify the grade restriction criterion. The special representations play an important rôle in the monodromy around the singular point. We also obtain exact results on boundary conditions in supersymmetric QCDs and apply them to understand the low energy behaviour of D-branes in the strong coupling phase.

title: Analysis of the (1+1)-EA-ES-Bilevel on Mixed Discrete-Continuous Optimization Problems with Interactions
abstract: Mixed discrete-continuous optimization problems can pose challenges -- especially for previous integrated approaches -- when interactions cause beneficial discrete changes to be rejected before sufficient continuous adjustment. We introduce ProximityOneMax as a simple benchmark with pairwise discrete-continuous interactions. On this function, we prove an exponential lower bound on the expected time for the (1+1)-EA-ES-Integrated to reach the target accuracy when initialized near a continuous optimum for a suboptimal discrete configuration with a sufficiently small step size. Experiments show frequent entries into such states from random initialization. We introduce the (1+1)-EA-ES-Bilevel, which uses an upper-level (1+1)-EA to optimize discrete variables and a lower-level (1+1)-ES to optimize continuous variables for each fixed discrete offspring before selection. For several interaction benchmarks and sufficiently small target values $ε> 0$ that require an optimal discrete configuration, using fixed continuous initialization and a suitable fixed budget per lower-level call, we prove that the expected number of fitness evaluations to reach objective value at most $ε$ is $Θ(n_d \cdot \log n_d \cdot n_c \cdot \log(R/\sqrtε))$, where $n_d$ is the number of discrete variables, $n_c$ is the number of continuous variables, and $R$ bounds the distances from the fixed continuous starting point to all relevant continuous optima for fixed discrete configurations.

title: Neither graphs nor hypergraphs: structural moments of higher-order interactions determine stochastic social-impact dynamics
abstract: Whether higher-order interactions can be reduced to simpler representations is a question about the dynamics they drive, not only about their structure: what can be discarded is whatever the dynamics does not see. We make this precise for binary-state stochastic dynamics in which each agent, when updated, interacts with a randomly selected group and changes state according to the fraction of disagreeing members, as in generalized voter and social-impact models on hypergraphs. We ask which statistics of the group-interaction process determine the resulting Markov dynamics. For response functions that are polynomials of degree $q$, the answer is a hierarchy of size-weighted inclusion moments, which we call structural moments, involving at most $q$ neighbors at a time, regardless of how large the groups are. These moments are not only sufficient but also necessary: two interaction structures produce identical dynamics for all such rules if and only if their moments coincide. More generally, each class of rules selects its own minimal structural description, ranging from weighted pairwise links for linear rules to the full distribution of co-membership by group size for arbitrary rules. For voter-type rules, the same moments also reconstruct exact pairwise copying representations of these dynamics.

title: One Shot, Any View: High-Fidelity Video Reshooting with Geometry Guidance and Visual References
abstract: Filming a scene from an additional angle after production usually requires a costly reshoot. We present One Shot Any View, a system that takes a recorded clip and generates a reshot video of the same performance along a user-specified camera trajectory. As in recent geometry-grounded methods, the system conditions generation on the source video and an explicit 3D prior, namely a point video rendered along the requested trajectory from a feed-forward reconstruction of the source video. We target human-centric cinematic videos, which are often shot with long lenses, shallow depth of field, and low-key lighting, all of which degrade feed-forward reconstruction. Existing geometry-grounded methods tend to inherit the degraded point video, and their output quality drops visibly. Two designs make such point videos usable. First, in addition to rendered videos of 3D assets, we train on real-world multi-camera videos, whose point videos are produced by the same reconstruction pipeline as at inference. This training-inference consistency enables the generator to take only the composition of people and scene elements from the point video, and their appearance from the source video. Second, a geometry-anchored RoPE offset keeps the generated video temporally synchronized with the source while largely preventing the output from copying the degraded appearance of the point video. Meanwhile, since the generator is a pretrained reference-to-video (R2V) model, the system also accepts optional character and scene reference images, which supply the appearance of regions that the source never shows. In both objective and human evaluations, One Shot Any View outperforms existing reshooting methods.

title: FedE2E: One-Shot Federated Learning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving with Closed-Loop Evaluation
abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative model training without sharing datasets. However, existing federated learning methods for autonomous driving typically require multi-round communication and lack closed-loop evaluation, while one-shot methods mainly focus on perception tasks. To address these limitations, we propose \method, a one-shot federated learning method for end-to-end autonomous driving. It comprises multi-client calibration, anchor-based feature alignment, and token-wise consensus distillation to distill knowledge from heterogeneous models. Closed-loop evaluation on Bench2Drive demonstrates the effectiveness of \method in both one-shot and multi-round federated learning. In the one-shot setting, it achieves a Driving Score of 55.85, which is 4.07 points higher than prior work. In the multi-round setting, it reaches 60.35 after five communication rounds, the best performance among all compared methods under the same number of communication rounds.

title: In-memory measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution
abstract: Quantum memories offer to significantly extend the performance of quantum networks, but their complexity and limited performance at telecommunication wavelengths have so far hindered practical deployment. We propose a new memory-assisted measurement device independent quantum key distribution (MDI-QKD) protocol based on in-memory interference. Our approach leverages progress in atomic ensemble memories that enable the interference of a stationary matter qubit and a travelling photonic qubit inside a single quantum memory. We quantitatively evaluate the performance of this scheme against memoryless MDI-QKD and existing two-memory architectures, showing that it not only achieves superior secret key rates and surpasses the memoryless bound at substantially shorter distances, but also reduces hardware requirements by halving the number of memories and detectors. Our results further indicate that off resonant cascaded absorption (ORCA) memories are a particularly promising platform for implementing this protocol, and we outline a concrete design compatible with their capabilities. These findings demonstrate that in-memory interference provides a higher performance, and resource efficient route toward near term memory enhanced quantum secure communications.

title: Spark-H3: Adaptive Block Sparse Attention for Video Diffusion Models
abstract: Long video sequences make attention a substantial cost in video diffusion models. Block sparse attention (BSA) reduces this cost by computing selected blocks exactly while compressing the remaining blocks. However, fixed token grouping can place tokens with dissimilar attention preferences in the same group, while uniform key averaging can underestimate the attention mass of compressed blocks. We introduce Spark-Attn, a training-free BSA method comprising Spark-Reblock and Spark-Reweight. Spark-Reblock recursively groups tokens by attention preference while preserving regular block shapes for efficient GPU execution. Spark-Reweight uses the global mean query as an anchor to construct attention-weighted key-value representations and logit biases for the compressed blocks, calibrating their attention mass. We instantiate Spark-Attn in MiniMax-H3 as Spark-H3. At 10% exact-block density, Spark-H3 delivers a 2.49$\times$ DiT speedup and reaches 24.81 dB PSNR against the corresponding dense outputs on MiniMax-H3 (20 denoising steps, 345 frames, 1344$\times$768). Increasing the density to 20% further improves PSNR to 26.76 dB while still achieving a 2.26$\times$ DiT speedup. These results demonstrate that Spark-H3 achieves a state-of-the-art quality-efficiency trade-off for training-free BSA on video diffusion models.

title: TRESS: A Fixed-Size History Representation for Irregular Time Series Forecasting
abstract: A fixed number of recent observations may span minutes for one variable and days for another. Earlier measurements can still reveal whether the latest value is unusual for that variable. We propose TRESS (Timestamped Recent Events and Statistical Summaries), a forecasting model that retains the latest observations at their original times and summarises the full history of each variable. For a given set of variables and event budget, this representation stays the same size as the record grows. Its query-conditioned event lifting module weights deviations from the latest value according to the age of each observation and the forecast horizon. A channel-specific decoder combines the resulting features with historical statistics and a summary shared across variables to predict a correction to the latest value. Retaining 8 to 16 observations per variable, TRESS records the lowest mean test MSE and MAE among the methods compared on all four benchmarks. Serving 32 successive query times from one encoded history reduces CPU inference time by a factor of 2.12--2.60 across the four datasets. The code is at https://github.com/SSMa913/NICLab-TRESS.

title: Towards Vacuum-Assisted Robotic Needle Interventions: From Fluid Aspiration to Tissue Biopsy
abstract: Robotic ultrasound-guided needle interventions have primarily focused on target localization and accurate needle placement, while the subsequent acquisition of diagnostic material remains comparatively underexplored. Moreover, pleural fluid aspiration and tissue biopsy are typically addressed as separate procedures, despite sharing common requirements for ultrasound guidance, safe access, and sample transport. This work presents a unified robotic framework for ultrasound-guided fluid and tissue extraction using a single vacuum-assisted end effector. The proposed system combines force controlled ultrasound scanning, semantic target identification, automated needle deployment, and procedure specific material acquisition. A coaxial needle assembly and shared pump assisted pathway enable direct pleural fluid aspiration, while controlled cannula actuation provides the additional cutting action required for solid-tissue acquisition. End-to-end evaluation using a Franka Emika Panda robot over 50 phantom trials achieved successful extraction in 23/25 pleural fluid aspiration trials (92\%) and 22/25 tissue acquisition trials (88\%). Following successful tissue-target access, acquisition and transport were completed in all 22 trials.

title: Do VLMs Need to Keep Looking at Long Videos? Write It Down, Then Look Away
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) reason about long videos over hundreds to thousands of tokens. Every decoding step re-reads the key-value (KV) cache of the entire video. Must the model keep looking while it reasons? In LookAway, the model first writes timestamped notes on what the question needs and then puts the video away. Once the notes close, the inference engine hides the video's KV cache for the rest of the response. Across both hybrid and pure-attention VLMs, dependence on the video is concentrated early in the response. On Qwen3.6-27B, writing notes preserves accuracy better than free reasoning at the same withdrawal step. Replacing them with another video's notes harms accuracy, whereas keeping the video visible alongside the model's own notes adds no significant benefit. Without additional training, LookAway nearly matches full-video thinking accuracy at 0.12-0.13 times its modeled decode cost. To shorten this initial look, we fine-tune the model on its own correct LookAway responses. Reinforcement learning then rewards correct answers while penalizing KV reads. The trained model puts the video away after a median of 66-68 tokens. Across three held-out benchmarks, it writes more tokens than an identically trained full-video model yet reads only 27-35% as many KV positions at matched accuracy.

title: Vertical Structure-Based Composites for Analyzing Atmospheric Front Environments
abstract: In many mid-latitude regions, a substantial fraction of extreme precipitation events occur in the vicinity of atmospheric fronts. To understand the processes that lead to such extreme precipitation, it is important to study the environment of the front. In this paper, we introduce a new method for computing vertical composites of frontal environments. Existing approaches construct such composites relative to front lines that represent the front at a single pressure level. However, fronts are vertically tilted and can exhibit substantial geometric variability, both within an individual front and between distinct events. Therefore, at levels away from the reference front line, the alignment of front environments based on a single front line commonly blurs the signals in the analyzed atmospheric variables. Our method accounts for the vertical structure of the front by computing composites relative to the actual front position at all height levels. We showcase the method using ERA5 reanalysis data for 50 cold fronts over Europe and apply it to thermodynamic and kinematic fields. Compared with conventional line-based composites, the new approach yields signals that are sharper and spatially more coherent. It also provides a visualization in which front-relative distances can be interpreted directly throughout the vertical column. Our method offers a general framework to study atmospheric processes in frontal environments and can be applied to different types and definitions of fronts.

title: Calibration of LHAASO-WCDA Energy Scale using Cosmic Ray Moon Shadow
abstract: Cosmic-ray particles in the TeV range, originating outside the solar system, are partially blocked on their way to Earth by the Moon, producing a deficit in their flux known as the Moon shadow. This work presents a precision measurement of the westward shift of the Moon's shadow using 3.4 years of data from LHAASO's Water Cherenkov Detector Array (WCDA). We use this direct physical measurement, combined with four cosmic-ray composition models, each divided into five mass groups, to calibrate the detector's absolute energy response in the range of 4 - 37 TeV. We quantify the fractional deviation between the calibrated and simulated energy scales by determining a best-fit scale shift parameter of $ε$ =-0.04 $\pm$ 0.03. This yields a 95% confidence interval of -9% to +0.2% for the systematic energy scale deviation. Complementing the simulation based on hadronic interaction model, this geomagnetic calibration provides a data-driven physical validation of the simulated WCDA energy response, effectively bounding systematic uncertainties and refining the overall energy scale.

title: Study of the intra-pixel timing resolution of planar silicon sensors using the TDCpix ASIC
abstract: A study of the intra-pixel timing resolution in planar silicon detectors, bonded to the TDCpix Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC), is performed using the TimePix4 telescope. Spatial non-uniformities in the timing resolution, arising from the weighting field, are measured for the first time in an experimental environment. The results are validated using simulation and discussed in the context of future Research and Development (R&D) goals.

title: Design and performance of the front-end readout electronics for LACT
abstract: The Large Array of Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescope (LACT) will complement the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) with a target angular resolution of 0.05 degrees to resolve the morphology of Very-High-Energy gamma-ray sources. The array is designed to comprise 32 telescopes with 6-meter apertures within LHAASO at an altitude of approximately 4410 meters. Each camera contains 1616 silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs). We developed a front-end readout electronics (FEE) board integrating 16 channels of SiPM gain compensation and high-speed waveform sampling for operation at high altitude and over a wide temperature range. The gain compensation circuit independently adjusts the operating voltage of each SiPM according to its temperature and monitors the actual operating voltage. Previous tests of the adopted compensation scheme showed SiPM gain drift below 2% from -20 to 30 degrees Celsius. The waveform sampling circuit uses two 14-bit AC9628 analog-to-digital converters, each operating in eight-channel mode, to digitize the SiPM pulse waveform at 250 million samples per second. The integral nonlinearity of the DC response is 0.0709% over a differential DC voltage range of -950 mV to +950 mV at the AC9628 input. Equivalent electrical pulses with a full width at half maximum of 37.42 ns are used to simulate the SiPM output signals. At a differential pulse amplitude of approximately 237 mV at the AC9628 input, the pulse integral area resolution is 0.2725%. This paper presents the circuit design and performance tests of the FEE for the LACT camera.

title: Multilevel Graph Partitioning on GPU Supercomputers
abstract: Graph partitioning is a key enabler in computational science, with applications to sparse linear algebra, load-balanced parallel computation, and graph computations. In recent years, graphics processing units (GPUs) have become the preferred accelerator on the world's top supercomputers. Despite this, most existing distributed graph partitioners do not utilize GPUs. In this work, we develop a new multi-GPU distributed partitioner based on Jet, a prior single-GPU partitioner. We seek to optimize scalability without sacrificing quality. Our partitioner utilizes CUDA-aware MPI, one-sided communication routines, and an overall bulk-synchronous parallel structure. We demonstrate solution quality comparable to Jet. Our experiments show excellent weak scaling up to 256 GPUs, enabling partitioning of instances significantly larger than a single-GPU partitioner can handle.

title: Retained Encrypted Search with Certified Split Joins
abstract: Retaining encrypted search across data edits and worker replacement requires separating computational validity from current release authority. We give exact Hamming search with at most one authorized decryption and decoding attempt per query preparation. Under authenticated prescribed execution, exclusive nonrollback owner state, an ideal public seed-expansion interface and a stated observation model, we reduce bounded adaptive privacy to ordinary ring learning with errors (Ring-LWE). Expanded second components depend only on public masks and fixed maps, independently of queries and the fresh database key. This compiler invariant permits a retained split join against a smaller-modulus encrypted database. A simultaneous bound on the completed circuit covers a finite honest reservation family, including adaptive queries and slot selection, with explicit statistical correctness and privacy losses. In three post-calibration local CPU comparisons on 32,768 vectors of 512 bits, the 60-bit-join construction takes a median 9.825 s for an end-to-end two-query workload, versus 12.159 s for the optimized full-source-modulus baseline. These times include setup, transfers, preparation and private completion. They are local implementation results, not deployment or concrete-security claims.

title: Sensitivity analysis in real options studies: systematic review and recommendations
abstract: Real options (RO) modeling provides a powerful framework for valuing managerial flexibility under uncertainty in capital-intensive investments across various industries, including climate, energy, and transportation. However, the transparency and usefulness of such models depends heavily on sensitivity analysis (SA). This study reviews over 100 peer-reviewed RO journal articles to examine the extent and quality of SA practices. The review focuses particularly on the extent of model scrutiny: how many input variables are subjected to sensitivity analysis; whether local or global approaches are applied; and whether the shape of the input-output relationships is examined. Our findings reveal a strong overreliance on one-at-a-time (OAT) techniques and a corresponding minimal adoption of global sensitivity analysis (GSA). This methodological gap limits the ability of the RO field to critically examine its own models and to support its decision-making. The paper concludes by outlining concrete recommendations for how to effectively incorporate GSA into future RO studies in order to enhance model transparency, relevance, and credibility.

title: Look Closer, Look Back, or Wait for Agentic Streaming Video Understanding
abstract: Streaming video models must answer questions about a live video under strict memory and latency limits. Feeding only the latest few frames keeps present perception sharp, whereas adding past frames dilutes attention on the current scene and triggers hallucinations. Recent cascade methods retrieve past frames when uncertain, but they still fail when current frames are blurry or when decisive future clues have not appeared yet. We introduce ActiveForager, a streaming video agent that maintains a clean short working window and gathers extra evidence only on demand. For each query, the agent either answers directly, zooms into high-resolution recent frames, recalls past events from memory, or waits for upcoming frames. When recalling history, a shared-weight sub-agent verifies candidate clips in isolation and returns a compact evidence summary. A stream-decoupled attention mask then keeps historical evidence from interfering with present visual tokens. We train this policy using counterfactual information gain, which rewards a tool call only when the gathered evidence makes the true answer more likely and prevents tool collapse across all actions. Across Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B on OVO-Bench, ActiveForager improves real-time perception, historical recall, and proactive response at once, lifting overall accuracy on Qwen3-VL-8B from 47.6% to 65.9%. It also doubles zero-shot accuracy on the multi-hop Video-Holmes benchmark while adding minimal visual tokens per query.

title: Amplifying or Redistributing Coupling: Synchronization in Sparse Adaptive Oscillator Networks
abstract: Synchronization -- different units falling into a common rhythm -- matters in systems ranging from electrical generators to populations of neurons. But what happens when the connections that coordinate their timing can also change? If two units become more closely aligned and their connection strengthens, that extra influence can either increase the total coupling received by a unit or take a larger share of a fixed total. We examine these alternatives in a mathematical network of oscillators, each representing a repeating cycle, connected by sparse directed links. We compare constant connections with two adaptive rules that favor phase-aligned neighbors: unconstrained Hebbian coupling and homeostatic normalization, which keeps the total incoming effective coupling of each oscillator constant. Exact relationships establish this conservation and show that the mean Hebbian weight relaxes toward a value set by alignment along the network links. In matched numerical experiments, unconstrained adaptation reaches a given level of collective synchrony at weaker imposed coupling than fixed connections, whereas the normalized network requires stronger coupling within the same observation window. Longer observations reveal distinct individual trajectories, including increasing, sustained, and declining coherence. The central lesson is that the collective consequences of adaptation depend not only on which links are strengthened, but also on whether their strengthening adds influence or redistributes it.

title: Keeping Up with the Kernel: Can LLMs Adapt Linux Drivers to Interface Changes?
abstract: We analyze collateral evolution in Linux, the coordinated updates that drivers require when the kernel interfaces they depend on change, over the 20 years since it was first studied, covering releases from v3.0 to v7.2. Since v2.6.13, the number of driver files and support libraries has grown about eightfold, a single change to the most widely used library can now reach about 5.3k driver files, and such changes arrive either in bursts or spread over many releases. We introduce CoEvoBench, a benchmark that asks models to adapt an old driver module to a target kernel and evaluates the result against the developer's reference patch. The benchmark contains 316 manually confirmed tasks from 202 mainline commits and 268 modules, spanning kernel releases v6.19 to v7.2. It distinguishes 134 build-breaking tasks, where the old driver fails to compile, from 182 build-compatible tasks, where the old usage still builds. Using CoEvoAgent, we evaluate Direct, SmPL, and mini-SWE-agent with DeepSeek Flash, and compare Direct with Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol. With DeepSeek, default Direct generation achieves strict reference agreement on 41.0% of build-breaking tasks but only 3.3% of build-compatible tasks.

title: A fully differential charged-particle phase-space measurement of $Z$+jets production in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV with the ATLAS detector
abstract: The production of a $Z$~boson decaying to muons in association with hadronic jets is a benchmark process in proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider. It provides a clean experimental signature with high selection efficiency and purity while probing a wide range of Standard Model dynamics. Measurements of this process are typically reported as binned differential cross sections in a limited set of predefined observables, which reduces the information retained and hinders reinterpretation. In this paper, the OmniFold method is used to produce an unbinned and highly differential measurement of the $Z$+jets cross section using 140 $\text{fb}^{-1}$ of $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV proton-proton collision data collected by the ATLAS detector. This constitutes the first published unbinned, fully differential measurement of a collider cross section, describing the kinematics of individual charged particles within a well-defined region of phase space. This unbinned event representation is used to construct measurements in four example applications that illustrate the broad range of observables constrained with a single measurement, including several that would be difficult or impossible to access using traditional unfolding methods. The measurement is published as particle-level Monte Carlo events together with unfolded event weights, allowing arbitrary observables to be constructed after publication and enabling a broad range of future applications and reinterpretations.

title: Constellation Shaping for OFDM-ISAC Systems: A Systematic and Experimental Comparison
abstract: Emerging integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) systems reuse the communications signal for radar-like sensing to provide environmental awareness. However, this integrated design imposes conflicting constraints on the modulation format, as communications systems use higher-order modulation formats while sensing systems use unit-modulus signals, making constellation shaping a key performance driver in ISAC systems.
