The result is used to test theoretical models of two-body hadronic decays of $B^+_c$ mesons and agrees with several predictions in the literature.

title: A Monte Carlo study of closely packed two-patch particles with frustrated interactions
abstract: Recently it was found that closely packed two-patch particles exhibit rich orientational ordering behaviors, e.g., nonmonotonic changes of the nematic order parameter and double BKT phase transitions [arXiv:2509.03981]. In this work, we show that, with repulsive patch-patch, attractive patch-nonpatch and intermediate nonpatch-nonpatch interactions, there exist frustrations in the system of closely packed two-patch particles. To investigate the ground states of the system, we design a Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm with single-defect propagation. The simulation results show that the ground states are disordered and the correlation functions decay exponentially with the distance. These results demonstrate that in 2D close packing one could design patchy particles to explore orientationally disordered systems.

title: Gaia Science Alerts microlensing events with mass estimates verifiable in Gaia Data Release 4
abstract: Gaia Science Alerts provide an all-sky stream of photometric transients, including events consistent with gravitational microlensing. For such events, forthcoming epoch astrometry from the Gaia mission offers the possibility of testing photometric lens mass predictions. While microlensing parallax inferred from the photometric light curve can constrain the event geometry, a direct lens mass measurement additionally requires the angular Einstein radius, which may be accessible through astrometric microlensing. We aim to construct a pre-Data-Release-4 (DR4) sample of Gaia microlensing events for which the available photometry provides a measurable microlensing-parallax signal. This allows us to derive statistical predictions for the lens mass and distance. We forward-modelled these events to predict the detectability of the astrometric microlensing signal in Gaia DR4. We identify 56 Gaia Science Alerts microlensing events with 71 point-source point-lens solutions with annual parallaxes that satisfy our fit-quality, posterior-boundedness, and parallax-significance criteria. Lens masses and distances were inferred using two prior-based frameworks, pyLIMASS and the Besançon Galaxy Model, which combine the measured microlensing parameters and Gaia source information with stellar-population and Galactic models. These inferred parameters were used to simulate Gaia DR4-like along-scan astrometry and estimate the detectability of the astrometric microlensing signal. The inferred lens masses and distances remain strongly prior-dependent without a direct angular Einstein radius measurement. Among the 284 event-solution-prior branches, 47 are classified as high-confidence astrometric detections using Gaia DR4-like simulations. These predictions can be tested once epoch astrometry is released in Gaia DR4.

title: Taming the Tails of Stochastic Gradient Descent in the Interpolation Regime
abstract: In this paper, we study stochastic gradient descent in the smooth interpolation regime, where the population objective shares a common minimizer with the sample losses. In contrast to prior work, which has largely focused on in-expectation analysis, we obtain high-probability convergence guarantees under the same assumptions. In the convex case, we prove a fast rate of order $\log(β^{-1}) \cdot n^{-1}$ after $n$ iterations, with failure probability at most $β$. In the strongly convex case, we derive a family of moment-based bounds of order $β^{-p} \cdot \exp(-\mathcal{O}(p \cdot n))$ for $p \in (0,1]$, and complement them with a matching lower bound showing that the corresponding deterioration in the exponential rate is essentially unavoidable. In both settings, our theoretical results are unified across a broad class of step-size schedules. Building on this analysis, we extend our results to a low-noise regime and to nonconvex objectives satisfying the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition.

title: Positivity and uniform log-concavity for rank-two Chern coefficients
abstract: We study the binomial-basis coefficients in the Schur expansion of the Chern classes of symmetric powers of a rank-two bundle. Bérczi and Fehér conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative and log-concave in the Newton index. An inverse-series formula yields an integral gamma-positive refinement with exact support and a positive expression for the derivatives of the shifted Chern quotient. We prove that generalized Bernoulli polynomials of real order at least their degree have simple real zeros. Applied to the shifted quotient, this gives strict ultra-log-concavity in the Schur index at every positive shift. For the original Newton coefficients, we establish strict log-concavity with an explicit multiplicative margin in two uniform regions. A Hahn projection gives a square-root band about the balanced Schur index; a complex saddle estimate extends this to a band of linear width. Uniform estimates for the cumulants of a normalized Schur functional give a terminal Newton region of linear width. Polynomial coefficient identities also establish every row with Schur index at most six or imbalance at most nine. The argument separates log-concavity in the Schur, derivative and Newton indices and identifies the factorial factors in the transfer between the latter two. The unrestricted Newton log-concavity conjecture remains open.

title: Asymptotic probabilities in random Latin squares
abstract: We introduce some new general techniques for studying asymptotic probabilities in random Latin squares. Using these techniques, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the probability that a given 'small' partial Latin square $H$ is present in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square (as conjectured by Divoux-Kelly-Kennedy-Sidhu). As applications, we determine which configurations are likely to appear in random Latin squares (resolving a conjecture of Allsop-Morris), we determine the asymptotic distribution of the number of $3\times 3$ Latin subsquares in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square (resolving conjectures of McKay-Wanless and Kwan-Sah-Sawhney), and we show that the first two rows of a random $n\times n$ Latin square are statistically indistinguishable from a random derangement (answering a conjecture of Cameron and Cavenagh-Greenhill-Wanless).

title: Beyond Appearance: Evidence-Guided Programmatic 3D Scene Reconstruction with Agentic Lighting Reasoning
abstract: Image-to-code methods for 3D scene reconstruction produce executable code that generates editable digital content and supports visual simulation. However, existing methods primarily rely on appearance similarity, which provides limited guidance for distinguishing errors in geometry, materials, and illumination. Light shapes scene appearance through its interactions with geometry and materials, influencing shading, cast shadows, and reflections. We therefore present LightHarness, a VLM-based agentic framework that incorporates explicit lighting reasoning into iterative scene reconstruction. To be specific, we leverage complementary geometric, intrinsic, and illumination cues to jointly refine scene structure and appearance, and propose Lighting Reasoning Memory to maintain light-source hypotheses, which supports evidence, and revision history throughout iterations. Together, they support reasoning about partially visible and unseen sources, with evidence-guided verification directing subsequent revisions. Our framework reconstructs explicit scenes through coherent reasoning about geometry, materials, and illumination without additional training or differentiable rendering. Extensive experiments demonstrate superior image-to-code reconstruction accuracy under challenging shadows and complex illumination, further supporting downstream scene editing, object insertion, and versatile relighting.

title: Quaternionic Torus Actions on Manifolds
abstract: We study smooth actions of quaternionic tori $\operatorname{SU}(2)^r$ on closed, connected smooth manifolds, establishing sharp bounds for $r$ in terms of the dimension of the manifold when the action is either effective, effective almost-free, or almost-effective. In particular, we prove that an almost-effective $\operatorname{SU}(2)^r$-action on an $n$-dimensional manifold satisfies $r\leq \lfloor2n/3\rfloor$, and we classify up to diffeomorphism all simply connected manifolds attaining the maximal possible rank. This gives a quaternionic counterpart of the maximal symmetry rank conjecture without any curvature assumption. We also establish the bounds $r\leq n/3$ for effective and effective almost-free quaternionic torus actions, and we compute the exact value for spheres, quoric manifolds, or manifolds of the form $(S^3)^a\times (S^1)^b$.

title: Objective-Specialized Residual Streams in Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections
abstract: Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) extend a Transformer's residual stream into multiple parallel streams with learned cross-stream connections. Prior work trains all streams toward a shared objective. We instead study whether assigning distinct learning objectives to different streams can improve task performance and induce objective-specific specialization. Using complementary lexical (sparse) and semantic (dense) retrieval objectives as a test case, we find that objective-specialized mHC consistently outperforms a non-specialized mHC model across the full sparse--dense fusion range, for both two- and four-stream models and at two model scales. We then examine how specialization changes the model internally using probes of stream representations, residual mixing, objective-specific gradient flow, and read/write gates. The specialized and non-specialized models behave similarly through most of the network but diverge in the final layers: the specialized model develops increasingly objective-specific gradient flow, distinct read/write routing patterns, and reduced cross-stream mixing, and streams assigned to different objectives become increasingly dissimilar while those trained toward the same objective remain highly similar. Fixing the residual mixing to the identity leaves the specialization benefit intact, indicating that the benefit stems from objective-specific read/write routing rather than learned cross-stream mixing. These results show that assigning distinct objectives to mHC streams can improve multi-objective retrieval while inducing structured, depth-dependent specialization in the residual computation.

title: AGAMOTTO: An AI-Enabled Framework for Time-Critical Tactical Course-of-Action Evaluation and Generation
abstract: Current command and control (C2) platforms lack integrated simulation capabilities that would allow commanders to dynamically explore courses of action (COAs) during live operations. This paper presents ongoing research and contributions to the development of AGAMOTTO (Advanced Guidance and Analytics for Military Operations, Tactical Threats, and Outcomes) as part of the overarching NGC2 program, which advances the Army's efforts to modernize C2 systems, such as the Tactical Assault Kit (TAK). The paper outlines the current design, preliminary findings, and the remaining research tasks, with an emphasis on how the completed work will support tactical decision-making in future time-constrained environments. While the full system is still under development, initial development and results demonstrate the feasibility of AGAMOTTO. Early experiments highlight both the potential benefits and practical constraints of deploying AI-enabled tools in operational settings, and introduce lessons learned and a viable training strategy to make AI-generated COAs feasible in tactical scenarios.

title: A high-resolution search for axion dark-matter flows with ORGAN-Q
abstract: We search for narrow axion dark-matter flows using the high-resolution data acquired during the ORGAN-Q experiment. The analysis covers nine potential axion linewidths from 0.466$~$Hz to 119.209$~$Hz, equivalent to axion effective quality factors $1.3\times 10^{10}$ to $5.2\times 10^7$, over the range 6.1550$~$GHz to 6.3496$~$GHz, corresponding to axion masses of approximately 25.455$~μ\mathrm{eV}$ to 26.260$~μ\mathrm{eV}$. Once contributions from native-bin correlations, data-quality and interference vetoes, frequency-dependent system noise, the cavity response, and filter attenuation are accounted for, no candidate satisfies the required persistence ratio in any search bandwidth. Across the nine assumed linewidths, the strongest $95\%$ KSVZ axion-flow density limits range from 22.8$~\mathrm{GeVcm^{-3}}$ for a $0.466~\mathrm{Hz}$ signal to $153.7~\mathrm{GeVcm}^{-3}$ for a $119.209~\mathrm{Hz}$ signal, with both attained near $m_a=25.857~μ\mathrm{eV}$.

title: Cox rings of Jacobian elliptic surfaces of Kodaira dimension one
abstract: We study Cox rings of relatively minimal semistable Jacobian elliptic surfaces over $\mathbb P^1$ with $χ=χ(\mathcal O_X)\ge3$ and finite Mordell--Weil group. When the Mori cone is generated by the zero section and the reducible-fiber components, we give a finite criterion for Cox-ring generation: a numerically determined set of nef classes must admit sections nonvanishing along the zero section. The criterion supplies a minimal homogeneous generating set without assuming finite generation in advance. We prove that its nonvanishing condition holds whenever $\sum_i n_i\le2χ+4$, where $I_{n_i}$ are the reducible fibers; hence every such surface is a Mori dream surface. Independently of this condition, we exclude ample generator degrees throughout the stated cone range. We also determine the section--fiber subring and give minimal complete-intersection presentations when all $s$ reducible fibers have type $I_2$ and $s\le2χ+1$, including the endpoint beyond that cone range.

title: An asymptotic ball algebra with countably determined spectra and a nonseparable character space
abstract: Let $X=\partial\mathbb B_2\subset\mathbb C^2$ and let $\mathcal R$ be the restrictions to $X$ of functions in the ball algebra $A(\overline{\mathbb B_2})$. The unital uniform Banach algebra \[ \mathcal A=\{(f_n)\in\ell^\infty(\mathbb N,C(X)):\mathrm{dist}_{C(X)}(f_n,\mathcal R)\longrightarrow0\} \] is inverse-closed in $\ell^\infty(\mathbb N,C(X))$. Consequently one countable family of evaluation characters generates the spectrum of every element of $\mathcal A$. Nevertheless $Δ(\mathcal A)$ contains continuum many pairwise disjoint nonempty open subsets and is therefore nonseparable. This gives a negative answer to a problem posed by Ohrysko, Wojciechowski and Graham.

title: Radii of Sn Isotopes near the Proton Dripline from Nuclear Lattice Effective Field Theory
abstract: We present the first $\textit{ab initio}$ lattice calculations of charge and matter radii of tin isotopes $^{96}$Sn, $^{98}$Sn, $^{100}$Sn, $^{102}$Sn and $^{104}$Sn near the proton dripline using nuclear lattice effective field theory with high-fidelity two- and three-nucleon forces combined with the partial-pinhole algorithm. The resulting radii are larger then predicted from other ab-initio methods. We find that variations of the three-nucleon interaction reveal substantial radius differences even among interactions with similar binding energies. We intensively discuss of the role of different choices of the three-body forces.

title: Proof of the polygonal Saint-Venant inequality conjectured by Pólya--Szegö
abstract: We prove the polygonal Saint--Venant inequality conjectured by Pólya and Szegö: for every $n\geq 3$, among (possibly non--convex) polygons of prescribed area with at most $n$ sides, the regular $n$-gon uniquely maximizes torsional rigidity. The proof is purely analytic and stems from the local version of the result given in our previous paper: it combines an area--angle proportional partition of a polygon, inspired by Solynin and Zalgaller, with a sharp comparison for the mixed torsional rigidity of the partition cells, and with an angular concavity property of this functional on the class of isosceles triangles.

title: The number of cycles in a random 2-factor of a random regular graph
abstract: We study the number of cycles $X$ in a uniformly random 2-factor $F$ of a random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices (in the pairing model) for any fixed $d\ge 3$. When the pairing $P$ and the 2-factor $F\subseteq P$ are chosen uniformly at random together, the probability generating function of $X$ is $Γ(n+\tfrac u2)Γ(\tfrac12)/\bigl(Γ(n+\tfrac12)Γ(\tfrac u2)\bigr)$, which does not depend on $d$. Consequently, $X$ has mean $\tfrac12\log n+O(1)$ and variance $\tfrac12\log n+O(1)$, satisfies a central limit theorem, and equals $1$ (so that $F$ is a Hamilton cycle) with probability $Θ(n^{-1/2})$. Using an exact formula for the second moment of the cycle generating polynomial together with small subgraph conditioning, we transfer these results to a uniformly random 2-factor of a fixed random regular graph.

title: Volume growth and gap Theorem for manifolds with non-negative complex sectional curvature
abstract: The combined work of Liu, Ni, and Ni-Tam established that a complete Kähler manifold with positive bisectional curvature has Euclidean volume growth if and only if its curvature decays quadratically on average. In this work, we use the approximation scheme developed by Cabezas-Rivas and Wilking to establish the Riemannian analogue under the assumption of nonnegative complex sectional curvature. As an application, we prove an optimal gap theorem for manifolds with nonnegative complex sectional curvature. These results generalize the authors' earlier work.

title: Late Entry in Looped Language Models
abstract: Looped language models deepen reasoning at a compact parameter count by iterating a shared layer stack T times per token, turning recurrence depth directly into sequential decoding latency. Conventional early-exit decoding halts after initial passes without cache completion, truncating cached key-value states of past tokens to shallow depth. We study the opposite strategy, late entry, where new tokens skip initial passes and enter directly into the final K < T passes over a deep context cache. Once lightweight fine-tuning resolves hidden-state norm mismatch at the entry boundary, deep cached context substitutes for skipped token-local passes, allowing late entry to outperform matched early exit across model families and pass budgets. To turn this asymmetry into wall-clock speedups without stalling to build deep caches, candidate blocks verify through only the final K passes on the critical path while previously committed tokens complete passes 1 -> T alongside subsequent steps at zero extra serial calls. Projecting these finished T-pass wake states inside the existing output GEMM (Wake verification, governed by logit-margin tolerance tau in [0, inf]) unifies greedy-exact T-pass decoding (tau = 0, matching K = T block decoding within bf16 reduction order), margin-gated verification (tau > 0), and non-rollback lossy late entry (tau = inf) inside a single static CUDA graph. On Ouro-2.6B (T = 4), K = 2 Wake reaches 5.2x greedy-exact speedup at tau = 0 (+26% over K = 4 block decoding on GSM8K) and 6.8x at tau = inf (+16.9 points over trained early exit at matched speed). Scaling test-time recurrence across T in {8, 16, 32, 64} on Huginn-3.5B cuts K = T/4 rollbacks 21.5x with depth, driving greedy-exact (tau = 0) speedups to 6.1x (T = 32) and 8.4x (T = 64, +153% over K = 64 block) and tau = inf speedups to 10.6 to 12.5x.

title: Stafford's conjecture on cyclicity of torsion modules
abstract: We prove that over a Weyl algebra over a field of characteristic zero $A_n(k)$, every nonzero $d\in A_n(k)$ admits $F,R,S\in A_n(k)$ such that $1=dR+FdS$, a conjecture Stafford proposed in 1978. As a consequence, every finitely generated torsion right $A_n(k)$-module is cyclic. The proof maps $d$, by a symplectic change of variables, to a normal form $\tilde d$ and shows that the cyclic module $Q=A_n(k)/(\tilde dA_n(k)+x_1^N\tilde dA_n(k))$ vanishes. We first show that right multiplication by $x_1$ is surjective on $Q$. A comparison of lengths of localized modules over the associated graded ring then gives $\operatorname{gr}Q=x_1\operatorname{gr}Q$, so that the characteristic variety of $Q$ is disjoint from the hyperplane $\{x_1=0\}$. Finally, Gabber's involutivity theorem together with an argument about conormal directions at infinity from algebraic geometry shows that such a characteristic variety must be empty and therefore, $Q = 0$.

title: BaseRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of a Base Vision-Language Model via Training-Free Harness Internalization
abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) is moving from the harness of prompts and tools around a base model toward the model itself. However, existing RSI still faces key challenges, including harness-bound gains that stay outside the base model, black-box supervision that reads only the model's outputs, and imprecise edits whose site and strength are fixed in advance. To address these challenges, we propose BaseRSI, a new paradigm of Recursive Harness Internalization: the base model improves its harness, then writes what the harness adds into its own weights through training-free edits, round after round on its own responses. To support this paradigm, we introduce ReGap, a mechanism that supervises every transformer block with the high-dimensional activation difference that the harness makes at that block alone, and updates the block's weights along this signal in a low-dimensional subspace. Building on this mechanism, we further propose ReKey, an algorithm that writes this signal by regression into a few key-value neurons of every block, and measures the site and strength of each edit on the model's own responses. Moreover, the base model fills every role of this recursion with forward passes alone, and its edits, written at different sites, compose in one checkpoint without refitting. Experimental results on ten visual reasoning benchmarks show that BaseRSI consistently improves a base vision-language model both in distribution and on held-out benchmarks. Our code is available at https://github.com/beita6969/BaseRSI.

title: ALIVE: Bring Foundation Features to Life with Events
abstract: Visual foundation models provide powerful representations for diverse tasks, but their features become stale as visual content changes between image observations. Refreshing them requires new frames and repeated runs of a computationally expensive image encoder. We introduce ALIVE, an event-based method that incrementally updates native foundation model features between image observations. Given an anchor image, ALIVE uses subsequent events to transport and correct existing multi-layer features extracted by a frozen DINOv3 encoder. Its lightweight updater is trained end-to-end using only synthetic data, without downstream task supervision, and transfers directly to real-world event streams without any adaptation. Across three real-world datasets and five task-dataset settings spanning object detection, semantic segmentation, and depth estimation, ALIVE outperforms all evaluated event-based methods in every metric. On DSEC, when the anchor frame is 200,ms old, ALIVE improves over anchor-image predictions by 30.9,mAP in detection, 11.6,mIoU in segmentation, and 15.9% in depth AbsRel. Compared with image re-encoding, ALIVE reduces FLOPs by 82.4% and latency by a factor of 2.5.

title: Trickle groups on a complete graph are linear
abstract: Trickle groups were recently introduced by Bellingeri, Godelle and Paris, as generalizations of both cactus groups and right-angled Coxeter and Artin groups. We construct a representation of any trickle group $\mathrm{Tr}(Γ)$ with complete graph $Γ$ on a space having a basis in bijection with the vertex set $V(Γ)$, and show that it is faithful. This in particular shows that trickle Garside groups are linear. It also allows one to realize every finite trickle group as a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_{|V(Γ)|}(\mathbb{C})$. We do not use the results of Bellingeri, Godelle and Paris; instead we rather show that several properties of trickle groups that they obtained (and also some new ones) can easily be proven in the particular case of a complete graph using our representation. This includes the normal forms, the embedding of the trickle monoid inside the group in the case where $μ(x)=\infty$ for all $x\in V(Γ)$, and the absence of torsion of the latter. In this last case we give a second proof of faithfulness in the spirit of Krammer-Hée, which explains how to read Garside-theoretic information from the representation.

title: Cosmological First-Order Phase Transitions with Full Nonlinear Gravity
abstract: Cosmological first-order phase transitions can contribute to the stochastic gravitational wave background. For decades, these first-order phase transitions have been studied using a Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker background where the gravitational waves are treated as linear perturbations. Here, we present simulations of a first-order phase transition in the presence of fully nonlinear general relativity, using the BSSN formalism. We simulate a universe that contains a scalar field alongside a relativistic radiation fluid. We focus on GUT-scale transitions in which bubbles nucleate near the horizon size. We describe a method to construct initial data that satisfies the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints, starting from a Coleman--de~Luccia-like bubble profile and adjusting the bubble radius. We compute the gravitational wave spectrum directly from the trace-free extrinsic curvature and find a present-day peak amplitude of $Ω_{\rm GW,0}h^2 \sim 5\times 10^{-11}$, consistent with earlier results that do not include nonlinear gravity. The peak frequency depends on the symmetry-breaking scale and could fall anywhere from the LISA band to GHz frequencies. At late times, the field fragments into long-lived oscillons, which push its effective equation of state toward that of matter.

title: On metric multiplicative Diophantine approximation
abstract: Gallagher's theorem (1962) gives a Khintchine-type dichotomy for the Lebesgue measure of the set of multiplicatively $ψ$-approximable points in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \geq 2$, for monotonic functions $ψ$. We establish this dichotomy for arbitrary functions $ψ$, proving a conjecture of Beresnevich, Haynes, and Velani (2013).

title: Cwikel and Kato-Seiler-Simon estimates for commutators
abstract:
We prove that the commutator $[a(X),b(-\mathrm{i}
abla)]$ belongs to the weak Schatten class $\mathcal{S}^p_{m weak}$ provided $
abla a\in L^p$ and $
abla b\in L^p_{m weak}$ for $\max\{1,2d/(d+2)\}<p<\infty$. This is an analogue of Cwikel's estimate, with a larger range of exponents. We also prove analogues of the Kato-Seiler-Simon and Birman-Solomyak-Simon estimates. Counterexamples show the necessity of the lower thresholds and the failure of the Lipschitz endpoint estimate.

title: JCMT POL-2 observations of NGC 253: evidence for large-scale reordering of magnetic fields in giant molecular cloud complexes
abstract: In this paper we present observations of the magnetic field of the starburst galaxy NGC 253 made in polarized 850 $μ$m dust emission using the POL-2 polarimeter on the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope (JCMT). While the magnetic field typically traces the galactic spiral structure, we see significant deviations in field direction associated with the presence of stellar and/or supernova feedback, with the mean plane-of-sky magnetic field direction offset 24$^{\circ}$ from the galactic plane. Polarization fraction is anticorrelated with total 850 $μ$m intensity, with a power-law index of 0.72$\pm$0.03. Using the Fasano-Franceschini test, we find that the positions of POL-2 detections and radio sources in the spiral arms are inconsistent with one another, indicative of depolarization resulting from magnetic fields being tangled on scales smaller than the 240 pc JCMT 850 $μ$m beam in sites of star formation and feedback. Moreover, in both the starburst superwind and in one star-forming clump in the spiral arms, we observe a magnetic field direction consistent with being directed out of the plane of the galaxy. We thus hypothesise that magnetic fields in the giant molecular clouds (GMCs) of NGC 253 are undergoing an evolutionary sequence from a relatively ordered field parallel to the spiral arms in the pre-star-formation gas, to a complex field caused by the interplay of turbulence, gravity and small-scale feedback in relatively young GMCs, to a field that is reordered out of the plane of the galaxy as large-scale HII region expansion reshapes the gas and dust of galactic spiral arms.

title: SHAPE: Discrete Supervision and Parallel Continuous Streams for Learning Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Human Data
abstract: Egocentric human recordings are far cheaper than dexterous robot demonstrations, promising stronger pretraining and direct skill learning without task-specific robot data. Yet humans and robots differ in morphology and kinematics, so human recordings lack the joint positions and actuator commands that supervise robot policies, providing only retargeted end-effector (EEF) actions. This raises two questions: how human data should supervise the policy, and how a dexterous robot should read out actions at deployment. We address both in SHAPE (Supervision from Human Action tokens with Parallel Executable streams), a vision-language-action (VLA) model whose backbone predicts discrete action tokens of EEF chunks as an auxiliary task, while a shared flow-matching expert outputs two executable streams, EEF and joint. On a bimanual robot with 22-DoF hands, a matched study shows that discrete supervision helps learn from human data, driving backbone gradients and shaping action-informative representations across domains. Under standard control pipelines at deployment, direct joint readout excels at fine-grained control with robot demonstrations, scoring 0.80 across six tasks against 0.63 for π0.5, whereas IK-based EEF readout excels at human-to-robot transfer. Pretrained with human data and discrete tokens, SHAPE learns new tasks from human demonstrations without task-specific robot data.

title: Playing the SMR Game with Existential Honesty
abstract: State machine replication protocols are usually proven secure in the honest-Byzantine setting, which requires an honest supermajority of validators. Deployed systems offer no such guarantee: validators participate for profit and may deviate from the protocol whenever doing so increases their gains. In our work, every validator is rational or Byzantine, and none is honest. Rational validators may collude with each other and with the Byzantine ones, who may also bribe them to deviate. Known impossibility results show that, without honest validators, clients that decide whether to accept a transaction based on a non-interactive certificate and without further communication cannot be kept safe. To bypass these results, we let clients relay the certificates they receive to full nodes and wait before confirming transactions. We also assume that one full node, whose identity is unknown, is honest and always online. Under this assumption, we build a finalization layer over any certifiable quorum-based protocol in a synchronous network. Clients run an existing freezing gadget and fetch past certificates from the honest full node, which makes the protocol \emph{always-safe}: no two honest clients confirm conflicting ledgers, for any strategy of the validators. We incentivize participation through rewards, which the adversary may use to bribe rational validators into censoring transactions. In this setting, we formalize censorship and characterize it tightly: paying only with his rewards, the adversary censors less than a $\bw$ fraction of the available fees at each height, where $\bw$ is the fraction of the quorum he signs, and every coin of censorship beyond that comes from his own funds.

title: A limit theorem for deviation of ergodic integrals on a class of flows on the two-torus
abstract: We study the fluctuations of ergodic integrals for locally Hamiltonian flows on the two-torus with a single non-degenerate saddle (Arnol'd flows). We sample a flow from a suitably random family, together with a base point $p$ chosen uniformly at random on that flow's domain. For a smooth observable $f$, we show that the centered Birkhoff integral $\int_{0}^t f(ϕ_s p)\,ds-t\bar f$, where $\bar f$ is the spatial mean of $f$, normalized by $(\log t)^2$, converges in distribution to the product of two independent random variables. Using special representation of locally Hamiltonian flows, we reduce the problem to studying ergodic sums of functions with logarithmic singularities over circle rotations. Then, we prove a Cauchy limit theorem for such ergodic sums, which is a result of independent interest.

title: Large Language Models or AI Agents for English to Arabic Translation? An assessment on WikiEn-Ar190
abstract: This research investigates whether a large language model or an autonomous AI Agent performs better at translating from English to Arabic, which is considered a low-resource language. The authors introduce WikiEn-Ar190, a new dataset of 190 carefully selected Wikipedia articles from 18 different areas, which were created and verified by two native Arabic speakers to ensure that they accurately reflect both meaning and style. Using this dataset, the study evaluates the translation quality of GPT-5-mini both as an independent neural translator and when used within a more complex process that includes self-assessment and improvement. As a standalone model, GPT-5-mini produced very fluent translations , achieving a COMET score of 0.8649 and receiving high human scores for adequacy, fluency, and style (averaging 4.53 out of 5). When used in a system that combined translation with self-assessment, it improved lexical accuracy by 28.76% (BLEU score of 22.83) while maintaining a similar level of semantic quality. These findings show that methods involving autonomous reasoning can improve translation consistency for language pairs with limited resources. Beyond the results, the approach offers a framework for evaluating and improving translations, potentially using them as assisting tools to expand the representation of low resource languages, such as Arabic, on the web.

title: Quasimonomial Monge--Ampère equations for big classes
abstract: Let X be a normal projective variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We describe an alternative approach to a differentiability result of volumes of norms defined by finitely many quasimonomial valuations. As a consequence, we prove the non-Archimedean Calabi--Yau theorem for quasimonomial measures on $X$ with respect to big classes, in the trivially valued case. We also obtain continuity of solutions as numerical classes vary in the big cone. This extends previous results of Boucksom--Jonsson and Dervan--Reboulet, and gives the first uniqueness results in the big case. Our approach relies on convex geometry and Okounkov bodies, without involving non-Archimedean pluripotential theory or test configurations.

title: Think Offline, Act in Real Time: Self-Improving Visual Game Agents through Code
abstract: Pre-trained models can read screens and reason about games, yet on an unfamiliar game, an agent still has to learn to play. We ask how an agent can self-improve on such a game from a few of its own attempts, in real-time visual games where the agent sees only the screen and the game keeps running while the agent thinks. We study two kinds of policy that can carry this improvement. In model as policy, a model selects actions during play; we adapt real-time chunking so that committed actions keep executing while the model reasons, and train a 2B controller for this interface. In code as policy, a model writes, tests, and revises a program between attempts, and the program acts during play. Across 170 GameWorld tasks, with at most eight one-minute executions per run, code as policy reaches 47.80% mean progress, against 30.90% for our trained controller, and leads in all five game categories. Improving the controller's weights on a single game, by contrast, yields only modest gains. These results favor letting a model think offline and storing what it learns in a program that acts in real time. Project repository: https://github.com/TabibitoQZP/SIGame

title: Reliable arithmetic circuits using less reliable (sub-digital) logic
abstract: The frequent static failure of CMOS logic gates at ultra-low voltages has historically been perceived as a strict barrier to extreme voltage scaling: this paper introduces a statistical circuit law proving this intuition wrong. We discovered a universal power law connecting gate and circuit static failure probabilities, revealing that circuit failure requires the simultaneous breakdown of an entire gate cluster rather than a single component. Because the required cluster size increases rapidly as voltage drops, low-voltage \textit{sub-digital} logic exhibits surprising inherent resilience to static failure. This insight stems from new theoretical tools we developed to quantify static failure, extending well beyond conventional voltage-margin analysis. Consequently, sub-digital processors could potentially offer a viable, near-term solution to drastically reduce the energy demands of AI.

title: Gutzwiller Quantum-Classical Embedding for Dynamics Simulations of Correlated Electron Systems
abstract: Simulating the real-time dynamics of correlated electron systems requires a nonperturbative treatment of local correlations over long times, a challenge for classical methods. We present the time-dependent Gutzwiller quantum-classical embedding framework, t-GQCE, for generic multi-orbital lattice models with time-dependent Hamiltonians. Within the time-dependent ghost Gutzwiller approximation, the lattice dynamics is mapped onto a noninteracting quasiparticle lattice, propagated classically, coupled to finite interacting embedding models propagated on quantum processors. The two parts exchange only embedding Hamiltonian parameters and single-particle density matrices, and the framework is agnostic to the quantum dynamics solver. We demonstrate it with adaptive variational quantum dynamics simulations of interaction quenches in the Hubbard model on the Bethe lattice. Without ghost orbitals, the embedding problem reduces to a single qubit, simulated on IBM quantum hardware with two qubits, including an ancilla. With more ghost orbitals, t-GQCE suppresses the artificial undamped oscillations of the conventional Gutzwiller approximation and approaches nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory results for weak and strong quenches. Statevector simulations with 2, 4 and 6 ghost orbitals per spin, or 8, 12 and 16 qubits, give adaptive circuits that follow the embedding states with infidelities below $5\times10^{-4}$. Under trapped-ion noise models, circuit compression, measurements in rotated orbital bases with post-selection, and noise mitigation reduce the measurement errors severalfold. At one third of the error rates of a hardware-benchmarked noise model, they reach an accuracy of $0.01$ for the single-particle density matrix and the double occupancy with $10^5$ shots per time step, and the Quantinuum H2-Emulator gives similar accuracy.

title: The number of $k$-factors of a random regular graph
abstract: Let $Z_k(G)$ be the number of $k$-factors ($k$-regular spanning subgraphs) of a uniformly random simple $d$-regular graph $G\sim G(n,d)$, where $d\ge 3$ and $1\le k\le d-1$ are fixed integers such that $dn$ and $kn$ are even. We determine the asymptotic second moment of $Z_k(G)$ and show that $Z_k(G)/\mathbb{E} Z_k(G)$ converges in distribution to an explicit random variable $W$ that depends on the short-cycle counts of $G$ but not on $k$. Moreover, for any $1\le k,\ell\le d-1$, the normalised counts on the same graph satisfy $Z_k(G)/\mathbb{E} Z_k(G) - Z_\ell(G)/\mathbb{E} Z_\ell(G) \to 0$ in probability, and, since $W>0$ almost surely, their ratio converges to $1$ in probability. This extends results of Bollobás--McKay and Janson for $k=1$ and Robalewska for $k=2$ to all $1\le k\le d-1$. In the pairing model, the second moment reduces to a one-dimensional lattice sum over the overlap of two $k$-factors. We evaluate this sum using the Poisson-binomial representation of the hypergeometric distribution, exponential tilting, and a uniform local limit theorem.

title: A Cubic Obstruction to Sums of Tripotent and Square-Zero Matrices
abstract: Let $R$ be a nonzero unital ring of characteristic $2$, and let $λ$ be a central unit of $R$. We prove that an element $a\in R$ satisfying $a^3+a^2+λ=0$ cannot be expressed as the sum of a tripotent element and a square-zero element. The proof does not require the summands to commute. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$, this gives counterexamples in every order divisible by three, including order twelve, and proves the optimality of the known uniform exponent four in those orders. We also give constructive proofs that every matrix of order four or five over $\mathbb{F}_2$ is a sum of a tripotent and a square-zero matrix, and deduce a complete criterion in order three. Combining the cubic obstruction with the quartic obstruction for idempotent-plus-cube-zero decompositions, we obtain two-way incomparability of the corresponding decomposition classes in every positive order divisible by twelve.

title: Asymptotics for generalized integer partitions
abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of weighted partition functions $p_f(n)$, defined by the generating function $\prod_{n \geq 1} (1 - q^{n})^{-f(n)}$ with non-negative real weights $f(n)$. We assume that the associated Dirichlet series $D(s) = \sum_{n \geq 1} f(n) n^{-s}$ admits a meromorphic continuation to a half-plane $\Re(s) \geq -\varepsilon$, with finitely many real poles of arbitrary orders, the largest of which is a positive pole $α$ of order $k$, and a possibly infinite collection of complex poles lying strictly to the left of $α$, with some additional conditions. We extend the saddle-point method of Debruyne and Tenenbaum, and show that the pole $α$ dominates the contribution of all other poles. As a result, we give an explicit asymptotic formula for $p_f(n)$ described via generalized Lambert functions. Furthermore, we show that for $k \geq 2$ no finite combination of powers of $n$, $\log n$, $\log \log n, \ldots$ approximates the saddle point well enough to give an asymptotic formula for $p_f(n)$. We also discuss a number of applications related to algebra, number theory, and combinatorics.

title: From Activity Recognition to Shift Detection: Variational Wi-Fi Sensing with Evidential Uncertainty
abstract: Human motion perturbs wireless channels, making commodity Wi-Fi devices a practical platform for device-free activity recognition. Yet Channel State Information (CSI) also depends strongly on the person, receiver position, recording session, and surrounding environment, so a classifier can continue producing activity labels after its deployment conditions have moved away from those seen during training. We propose Wi-HAR, a multi-antenna architecture in which four Variational Auto-Encoders learn compact distributions from raw Wi-Fi 6 CSI magnitudes and a delayed-fusion classifier combines their means and log-variances. On twelve activities from a public benchmark, Wi-HAR reaches 96.6% median recognition accuracy, compared with 70.8-81.5% for independently optimized single-antenna models, showing that the antennas provide complementary views of the same activity. We then use the same latent backbone to detect deployment shifts without using shifted samples for model selection or calibration. A class-conditional uncertainty score derived from Evidential Deep Learning achieves a macro-average ROC-AUC of 0.897 across eleven datasets that change receiver position, participant, recording session, or room, and detects 82.5% of shifted samples at a realized 5.2% in-distribution rejection rate. Detection performance nevertheless varies substantially across receiver positions, showing that the same physical change does not induce a uniform uncertainty response. The compact representation also supports shallow decision-tree analysis using variables from several antennas.

title: DAL: Dynamic Angular Loss for Imbalanced Medical Image Classification
abstract: Class imbalance remains a major obstacle in medical image classification, where rare but clinically important classes are often overshadowed by majority categories. Although current strategies for reducing bias, including angle-based softmax (ABS) losses, offer strong discriminative features, their behavior in settings with a small number of severely imbalanced classes remains insufficiently understood. Previous approaches that estimate the intrinsic parameters of ABS rely on the assumption of many classes, which does not hold in medical settings. We derive data-driven upper and lower bounds for the scale parameter and an upper bound for the angular margin using negative-angle statistics, and use these to drive a batch-adaptive angular margin (BAAM), which we combine with dynamically-weighted cross entropy (DWCE) to define our dynamic angular loss (DAL). Across four highly imbalanced medical image classification benchmarks spanning dermatology, ophthalmology, and gastrointestinal endoscopy, our method consistently achieves superior balanced accuracy and the lowest coefficient of variation of per-class recall. Although this entails a small performance reduction on majority classes, the gains on minority categories are substantial, yielding a reliable and equitable overall classifier. Our source code is available at: https://github.com/msalman95/DAL.

title: Chain-of-Thought Hidden States Reveal Task-Solving Directions for Direct Answers
abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting improves the performance of Large Language Models by eliciting intermediate reasoning steps. However, CoT is far from perfect: on some tasks, models perform worse than with direct-answer prompting, and on others they generate a few hundred tokens to reach the correct answer. We start by labelling each CoT hidden state as recovering if patching it into the direct prompt yields the correct answer, and failed otherwise. A linear probe shows that the model encodes these two classes differently. We then show that the representation space of the direct prompt holds a direction for each question that leads the model, in a short generation, to the correct answer more often than CoT does. Specifically, we rotate the direct prompt's last hidden state once, before generation, towards a direction built for each question from its own recovering and failed states. Across 25 tasks, these directions raise the direct prompt's mean accuracy from $46\%$ to $85\%$ on LLaMA 3.1 8B (CoT: $69\%$) and from $52\%$ to $86\%$ on Qwen 2.5 7B (CoT: $77\%$), with a tenth of CoT's tokens. CoT is thus not the shortest route to this accuracy, and these directions can be used in future work to train models to align their states with them.

title: Morpho-Spectral Projection Analysis (MSPA) for Plant Spectroscopy
abstract: Plant reflectance spectroscopy across the visible, near-infrared, and shortwave infrared domain encodes foliar biochemical and anatomical traits into contiguous spectral signatures with locally differentiable structure; however, extreme inter-band collinearity and unfavorable sample-to-feature ratios challenge predictive modeling. Conventional dimensionality reduction methods routinely adopted in spectroscopy, are column-permutation invariant: they treat adjacent wavelengths as unordered tabular columns and discard the sequential differential geometry of absorption features. Here, we propose Morpho-Spectral Projection Analysis (MSPA), a supervised dimensionality reduction operator that projects contiguous spectra into a compact morpho-spectral subspace through three complementary blocks: (i) additive continuum-removed absorption depth, area, and red-edge inflection kinematics; (ii) local multi-order singular eigenmodes (0th, 1st, and 2nd derivatives) partitioned across contiguous radiative sub-windows; and (iii) global Fisher-weighted canonical subspaces regularized via trace-normalized isotropic covariance shrinkage. We validated MSPA across 8,963 spectra spanning five plant systems, coupled with six classical machine learning classifiers and four Tabular Foundation Models (TabPFN v3, TabICL v2, TabDPT v1.2, and TabFM). Despite compressing the 1,580-band spectrum by 96%, MSPA outperformed the full spectrum in 92.0% of all benchmarks and conventional reducers in 90.0% of all model-crop evaluations, raising the global mean macro-F1 from 0.7756 (full spectrum) to 0.8520, accelerating in-context inference by up to 126.5x. Designed as a self-contained spectral projection operator, the MSPA method can be directly integrated into spectroscopy workflows via the open-source code available at GitHub: https://github.com/Lucas-Osco/mspa.

title: Data-driven control of polynomial systems using implicit methods
abstract: While conventional behavioral data-driven control represents linear time-invariant (LTI) systems directly from data, extending these data representations to nonlinear systems remains an open challenge. We address this gap for general polynomial systems, characterizing their finite-length trajectories as a real algebraic variety defined by implicit polynomial relations rather than explicit equations. First, we provide conditions on measured data under which these data can be used to represent the system. Building on this representation, we formulate data-driven simulation and predictive control problems that are equivalent to their model-based counterparts, and solve the resulting polynomial systems globally using homotopy continuation. Numerical case studies confirm the effectiveness of this approach by successfully simulating a stiff Van der Pol oscillator in situations where explicit models fail. Furthermore, these data-driven simulation and control methods are illustrated on a Duffing oscillator, demonstrating that our method outperforms Koopman-based approaches in predicting long trajectories.

title: Boundedness of the Riesz potential associated to diffusion operators in Lebesgue spaces
abstract: We revisit boundedness of the Riesz potential associated to a diffusion operator both in fixed and variable exponent Lebesgue spaces. We obtain optimal asymptotics in the former setting and we provide new tools to establish boundedness in the latter.

title: Diffusion Models are Provably Efficient Priors for Sparse Recovery
abstract: Diffusion models have transformed generative modeling through their ability to capture and generate samples from complex data distributions. This success has spurred substantial interest in using pretrained diffusion models as expressive priors for highly ill-posed inverse problems in imaging and sensing. Despite strong empirical performance, theoretical understanding of this approach remains limited: existing guarantees are often asymptotic or entail prohibitive computational costs in the worst case. In this paper, we address this gap by studying sparse recovery from a small number of linear measurements, a classical problem in compressed sensing. We show that, given an accurate diffusion model capturing a sparsity-promoting Bernoulli-Gaussian prior, a likelihood-guided annealed Langevin sampler provably recovers the sparse signal in polynomial time with near-optimal sample complexity for a broad family of random and deterministic sensing matrices. When the signal is indeed drawn from the postulated prior, we further establish total variation guarantees for posterior sampling after a final denoising step. These results lay a theoretical foundation for statistically and computationally efficient inverse solvers with diffusion priors.

title: No-Go Theorems for Ordered Universal Entanglement Purification
abstract: Entanglement purification is a fundamental tool for obtaining high-fidelity entangled states used in various quantum technologies. It aims to increase the fidelity of noisy shared entangled states with a fixed maximally entangled state through LOCC. In distributed quantum systems, such as networks employing quantum repeaters, limited memory, probabilistic entanglement generation, and unequal storage times can leave a finite collection of nonidentical pairs. Their states may remain incompletely characterized even when calibrated preparation and storage records establish their fidelity ordering. Recent work has investigated whether fidelity ordering permits nontrivial universal purification. A nontrivial universal $n$-to-1 protocol must, conditioned on success, never lower the highest input fidelity and strictly increase it for at least one allowed joint input. Although no-go results have been established for a restricted class of LOCC protocols, the corresponding question for general LOCC has remained unresolved. Here, we study ordered universal purification under separable operations. Specifically, for every fixed finite $n\ge2$, we prove that when independently prepared two-qubit pairs range over the full family of states above a fixed fidelity threshold $0\le F_*<1$, any separable success map that never lowers the highest input fidelity on the allowed ordered inputs must preserve that fidelity exactly whenever it succeeds. This excludes nontrivial universal LOCC purification even for arbitrarily high input fidelities, without imposing a positive lower bound on success probability. ...

title: Measurement-order dependence bounds uncertainty, contextuality, steering, and Bell nonlocality
abstract: Two quantum measurements applied to the same input in opposite orders give two joint distributions of the same outcomes. For Lüders instruments we measure how far apart these order records can be, over all inputs, by their total-variation distance $\mathcal{T}$, their Jensen-Shannon divergence $\mathcal{J}$ (in bits), and their squared Hellinger distance. These order scores vanish exactly when the measurements commute, and $\mathcal{T}=\|[A,B]\|/4$ for two binary sharp observables. Some pairs of bases exceed mutually unbiased bases in squared Hellinger score, and in odd dimensions in $\mathcal{J}$, although their minimal entropy sum is smaller. For projective measurements, a Maassen-Uffink bound $q>0$ implies $\mathcal{T}\ge1-2^{-q}$ and a positive lower bound on $\mathcal{J}$. Measuring all observables of a scenario in sequence defines a joint distribution, so violations of noncontextuality, steering, and Bell inequalities are bounded by distances between order records. For correlation Bell inequalities with binary sharp observables, the squared Bell operator is a symmetrized (Jordan) part minus tensor products of local commutators. If one party has two settings, the violation is bounded bilinearly in the two parties' order scores; we conjecture this bound in general. On Clifford realizations it would follow from a Hilbert-Schmidt variant of Grothendieck's inequality, which we prove when one party has at most three settings. For three binary sharp measurements, the violation of Bell's original inequality by a maximally entangled state equals an order effect in three-measurement records of the maximally mixed state minus four times an alternation probability. For the rank-one Klyachko-Can-Binicioğlu-Shumovsky pentagon on a qutrit, the violation is at most the largest product of the order scores of two crossing diagonals, with equality at the maximal violation.

title: Number-correlated photon entanglement with a quantum memory interferometer
abstract: Strong photon-photon interactions are central to quantum optical technologies yet remain challenging to realise at the single-photon level. Here, we show how embedding a quantum memory within a Mach-Zehnder interferometer enables a coherent transformation that converts single-mode photon states into number-correlated entangled states. Using an off-resonant ladder-type atomic interaction, storage and retrieval within a quantum memory maps a single-photon excitation onto a pair of photons across distinct optical modes via a driving control field. Embedding this within an interferometer deterministically produces an effective transformation in the photon number basis: $\sum_n a_n |n\rangle \to \sum_n a_n |n\rangle |n\rangle$ without relying on conventional optical nonlinearities. Measurement of one mode enables photonic non-demolition detection, state preparation, and frequency conversion as applications of the same underlying transformation. These results establish quantum memories embedded within an interferometric architecture as a platform for measurement-induced photon-photon interactions and the generation of Gaussian and non-Gaussian entangled states.

title: Combinatorial Properties of The Giant Under Supercritical Percolation
abstract: We study combinatorial properties, such as diameter and long paths and cycles, of the giant component of percolated graphs. Such combinatorial properties are well studied for classical graphs such as pseudo-random graphs and the hypercube. We aim to obtain similar results for extensive families of $d$-regular $n$-vertex graphs. Specifically, assuming expansion properties of the host graph, we show a typical vertex expansion by a factor of $1/d\log d$ in the giant component of the percolated subgraph. As a consequence, we obtain bounds on various combinatorial properties of the giant component. For example, a bound of $O\left(d\log^2 d+\log n\right)$ on the typical diameter of the giant component of the percolated subgraph. In addition, we construct graphs with very good vertex and edge expansion, but having large diameter, showing that the diameter of the percolated subgraph is not necessarily typically logarithmic in the number of the vertices of the graph. We also present good expanders such that their percolated subgraph typically contains a bad expanding set.

title: Relative Entropy under Ordered Chi-Squared Constraints: Exact Bounds and Extremizers
abstract: We derive a sharp upper bound on the relative entropy $D(P\|Q)$ in terms of the two ordered chi-squared divergences $χ^2(P\|Q)$ and $χ^2(Q\|P)$. For any $A,B>0$, the constraints $χ^2(P\|Q)\leq A$ and $χ^2(Q\|P)\leq B$ yield upper bounds on $D(P\|Q)$ and $D(Q\|P)$. Two pairs of Bernoulli distributions each attain both bounds simultaneously. As a consequence, for sequences of probability mass functions $\{P_n\}$ and $\{Q_n\}$ on a common finite or countably infinite alphabet, both $D(P_n\|Q_n)$ and $D(Q_n\|P_n)$ tend to zero whenever one of the two ordered chi-squared divergences tends to zero and the other remains uniformly bounded. Without this boundedness assumption, $D(P_n\|Q_n)$ can fail to converge to zero even when $χ^2(Q_n\|P_n)\to 0$. Finally, in contrast to the attainable upper bounds, on any finite or countably infinite alphabet containing at least three elements, the infimum of $D(P\|Q)$ under the exact constraints $χ^2(P\|Q)=A$ and $χ^2(Q\|P)=B$ is zero and is not attained.

title: A $10^5\,M_\odot$ Black Hole in the Bulgeless Spiral Galaxy IC 342: First Stellar-Dynamical $M_{\rm BH}$ Measurement with Keck/OSIRIS LGS-AO
abstract: We present the first direct stellar-dynamical measurement of an intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) in IC 342, a nearby nearly face-on ($i\approx31^\circ$) bulgeless spiral at $D=3.45\pm0.13$ Mpc, using near-infrared integral-field spectroscopy with Keck/OSIRIS LGS-AO. The heavy foreground extinction ($A_{\mathrm{F814W}}\approx0.74$ mag) renders the nucleus inaccessible to optical spectroscopy, making $K$-band observations at $\sim$2.3 $μ$m the only viable path to high-resolution nuclear kinematics. Two-dimensional stellar kinematics extracted from the CO bandheads via pPXF at $0.062''$ resolution reveal a central velocity dispersion rising from $\sim$42 km s$^{-1}$ at $r\gtrsim0.2''$ to a peak of $\sim$49 km s$^{-1}$, providing kinematic evidence for a central dark mass within the nuclear star cluster (NSC; $M_\mathrm{NSC}\approx1.17\times10^7~M_\odot$). Modeling these kinematics with an ensemble of four JAM models, spanning cylindrical and spherical velocity-ellipsoid alignments and two PSF representations, combined with an MGE mass model constructed from a three-Sérsic plus exponential-disk decomposition of archival HST/WFC3 F814W imaging and incorporating a physically motivated stellar mass-to-light ratio gradient, driven by the young central NSC population, yields $M_\mathrm{BH}=(1.95\pm0.61)\times10^5~M_\odot$. Accounting for this stellar population gradient is essential for the detection: standard constant-$M/L$ models systematically overestimate the central stellar mass, hiding the BH signature and yielding only an upper limit. The stellar orbits are near-isotropic ($β\approx0$), typical of fast-rotating late-type spirals. This measurement places IC 342 among the rare bulgeless spirals with a direct dynamical $M_{\rm BH}$ at the IMBH mass scale, where both the NSC and BH are directly characterized, providing a new anchor for compact massive object co-evolution models.

title: Negotiating Control and Accountability among Stakeholders in High-Risk AI Use Cases: Development and Evaluation of the Method ALIGN
abstract: Characteristics of Artificial Intelligence (AI) severely restrict human control. This creates new challenges for socio-technical systems design especially in safety-critical domains, where control over risks is essential along with the accountability for any harm caused. Drawing from human factors and AI governance literature, expert interviews and participant observation in a complex high-risk AI use case from the railways, we developed ALIGN, a scenario-based method that supports the governance of and stakeholder involvement in AI development and implementation in three ways: raising awareness for potential accountability-control misalignments in socio-technical systems and their negative consequences, offering a structured approach to assessing the alignment between accountability and control for stakeholders in a given use case, and supporting effective design decisions to mitigate AI risks. We describe the iterative development and evaluation of ALIGN and discuss how this method promotes AI governance by highlighting the relevance of control-accountability alignment throughout the AI life cycle.

title: Recent developments in stochastic systems with singular dynamics -- a brief survey --
abstract: Diffusions with singular drifts appear naturally in the study of certain classes of interesting particle systems. Due to the singularities involved in the equations describing them, studying their dynamics is both interesting and challenging as they fall outside of the usual regularity assumptions on the vector fields in the literature. One needs to introduce and study them with different methods, with the use of symmetric polynomials being a particularly promising approach. In this expository work, we give an overview of some models and methods, and we further explore their interactions with the areas of Multiple Loewner chains (in particular, multiple Schramm-Loewner Evolutions), the new links with Random Matrices, and the novel area of Machine Learning for Singular Dynamics.

title: Inapproximability of Euclidean Steiner Tree
abstract: We consider the Euclidean Steiner Tree problem of connecting $n$ given points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ by a shortest network allowing the addition of Steiner points anywhere in the space. Arora [FOCS'96/'97, J. ACM'98] gave a polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS) for Euclidean Steiner Tree and TSP in every fixed dimension, and Trevisan [STOC'97, SICOMP'00] proved that Euclidean TSP is APX-hard in $O(\log n)$ dimensions. They left open whether Euclidean Steiner Tree admits a PTAS in high dimension. Our first contribution settles this thirty-year-old question by proving APX-hardness in $O(\log n)$ dimensions. Assuming that not all problems in NP can be solved in subexponential time (NP $\not\subseteq $SUBEXP), we also rule out a PTAS for Euclidean Steiner Tree in $O(\log\log n)$ dimensions. This dimension bound is tight up to a factor of $O(\log\log\log n)$, since Arora's scheme is a PTAS in up to $\log\log n/\log\log\log n$ dimensions. In fixed dimension, Kisfaludi-Bak, Nederlof, and Węgrzycki [FOCS'21, J. ACM'25] obtained approximation schemes running in time $2^{O_d(\varepsilon^{-(d-1)})}n\log n$ and proved matching Gap-ETH lower bounds for Euclidean TSP and Rectilinear Steiner Tree, but left a corresponding lower bound for Euclidean Steiner Tree as an open question. Our second contribution answers this question with a nearly tight lower bound on the dependence on accuracy for Euclidean Steiner Tree. However, given the recent claimed refutations of ETH and hence Gap-ETH by OpenAI and Anthropic, we use the weaker assumption that 3SAT has no truly subexponential-time algorithm, that is, no $2^{n^γ}$-time algorithm on formulas of size $n$ for any constant $γ<1$ (a hypothesis one might call weak ETH). Under this assumption, we prove that no $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm runs in time $2^{O(\varepsilon^{-γ(d-1)})} poly(n)$ for any such $γ$.

title: The infrared arc around $α$ Crucis: a weak interaction with a structured interstellar medium
abstract: Infrared arc-shaped structures around early-type stars are commonly interpreted as stellar wind bow shocks, although their morphology may also be shaped by gas motions and density variations in the surrounding interstellar medium. We present a multiwavelength study of the infrared arc associated with the nearby $α$ Crucis system, comprising HD 108248 (B0.5 IV), HD 108249 (B1 V), and HD 108250 (B4 V). We combine WISE, Herschel, Planck, stellar astrometry, and eROSITA X-ray data to investigate the structure and its relation to the stellar components. The WISE W4 ridge extends over $\sim$0.65 pc and has a median PSF-corrected width of $\sim$0.037 pc. The HD 108248/HD 108249 pair lies $\sim$0.13 pc from the ridge, compared with $\sim$0.17 pc for HD 108250. Relative to the mean motion of the Lower Centaurus-Crux (LCC) subgroup of the Scorpius-Centaurus association, the close pair is consistent with LCC, whereas HD 108250 has a transverse peculiar velocity of only $\sim$1.8 km s$^{-1}$. Its motion lies within $\sim$23$^\circ$ of the geometrical symmetry axis of the infrared arc, but points in the opposite sense from the arc. Herschel maps show slightly higher median dust temperature ($ΔT_d\sim$0.8 K) and molecular-hydrogen column density ($ΔN_{\rm H2}\sim$7$\times$10$^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$) toward the W4-defined region than in the nearby background. On larger scales, Planck maps reveal a strongly structured microwave environment around the system. Both the HD 108248/HD 108249 pair and HD 108250 are detected by eROSITA, with the former approximately 60 times more luminous in X-rays. The combined morphology, kinematics, and dust properties do not support an unambiguous classical high-velocity bow-shock interpretation. Instead, the arc likely traces a weak interaction between the multiple stellar system and an inhomogeneous ambient medium.

title: Dessins d'Enfants as a Topological Lens on Temporal Hypergraphs
abstract: Hypergraphs are the natural language for group interactions, and topological data analysis has given us several ways to look at them: simplicial and cell complexes, persistent homology, and sheaves. All of these treat a hyperedge as an unordered set. In this paper, we introduce a different and, to our knowledge, new viewpoint that comes from Grothendieck's theory of dessins d'enfants and, unlike these approaches, takes into account the order in which vertices appear in each hyperedge and hyperedges appear around each vertex. A dessin is a bipartite graph drawn on a closed orientable surface. Through Walsh's classical correspondence between hypermaps and bipartite maps, every hypergraph equipped with a cyclic order of incidences at each vertex and inside each hyperedge is a dessin, and therefore determines a surface with faces and a genus. We develop this idea for temporal hypergraphs and build the surface by replaying history: incidences are added in the order in which they occurred, and each new incidence is inserted into the cyclic orders built so far, next to the earlier incidence to which it is related. We prove that every insertion either grows the hypergraph without creating a cycle, closes a cycle locally by splitting a face, or closes it globally by adding a handle; the number of independent cycles equals the number of local plus handle events, and the genus equals the number of handle events. These counts give interpretable, size-controlled measures of how a temporal hypergraph's cycles organize on a surface as it grows. We apply our method to five Stack Exchange communities and show that it separates communities that standard statistics cannot tell apart and quantifies how much the real order of interactions matters. We further discuss what the surface viewpoint adds to existing higher-order network analysis and how it opens a path toward dessin-based learning on hypergraphs.

title: On the equilibrium lattice of supermodular games
abstract: This paper shows how the meet and join of any pair of equilibria in a super- modular game can be constructed. The method relies on two one-directional best-response processes that I call contagion up and contagion down. Starting from any action profile, applying this pair of processes in opposite orders produces two equilibria that define its equilibrium envelope. The endpoints of the envelope are precisely the least and greatest equilibria reachable through arbitrary asynchronous best-response dynamics, and can only move closer together as players revise their actions. These and other results show how appending one-directional adjustment processes to the familiar equilibrium lattice structure allows us to explore the relationships between equilibria further.

title: Thermodynamics of gas giants accreting via shocks: the role of molecular hydrogen dissociation
abstract: Within the core-accretion framework, gas giants acquire the bulk of their mass through accretion shocks during runaway gas accretion. The shock thermodynamics---governed by radiative cooling efficiency, accretion history, and equation of state (EoS)---sets the post-shock entropy and initial thermal state, strongly influencing both observables and subsequent evolution. We construct a coupled evolutionary model predicting the initial thermodynamic states, intrinsic luminosities, and upper limits on the magnetic field strengths of gas giants across diverse accretion histories. We couple radiation hydrodynamics and $\mathrm{H_2}$ dissociation to long-term interior evolution by training a fast physics-informed neural network (PINN) surrogate model on 1000 first-principles simulations resolving the shock physics. This surrogate model supplies post-shock outer boundary conditions for MESA to evolve the planetary envelope beyond runaway accretion. It yields higher post-shock temperatures than the canonical cold-start model, with the discrepancy widening with planetary mass, while the post-shock entropy jumps sharply when $\mathrm{H_2}$ dissociates at $\sim 2000$ K. Gas giants evolved with these boundary conditions attain intrinsic luminosities 4--10 times higher than cold-start models. Under optimistic assumptions, the maximum magnetic field strength at $2\,\mathrm{R_J}$ reaches a few gauss for a $0.3\,\mathrm{M_J}$ planet, $\sim 100$ G for $1\,\mathrm{M_J}$, and $\sim 500$ G for $3\,\mathrm{M_J}$. Incorporating detailed radiation hydrodynamics and realistic thermodynamics into accretion shock models yields higher initial entropies, brighter intrinsic luminosities, and stronger magnetic fields, providing improved constraints on the masses and accretion rates of directly imaged exoplanets.

title: EgoJev: Finding Evidence in Egocentric Video by Reading VLM Decisions
abstract: Questions about long egocentric video often depend on one brief moment, such as the second a hand puts an object down. A vision-language model (VLM) that sees a few evenly spaced frames usually misses it. Training-free methods rank frames with a separate image-text model or ask the VLM to write a time. In a controlled test, the VLM itself locates the moment better when it chooses among labeled frames, and we read this choice from its output distribution. With the same candidates, this choice lands on the evidence more often than image-text scores or a written time span, and it compares all candidates in one decision. Based on this finding, we propose EgoJev, a training-free frame selector for wearable assistants. EgoJev reads where the evidence is from labeled thumbnails and looks again at the windows it points to. It places its few answer frames at the quantiles of the resulting distribution. One frozen VLM selects, answers and returns the evidence time, with no second model. A wearable device can encode its coarse thumbnails while it records. With Qwen3.5-4B and 8 answer frames, EgoJev raises QAEgo4D accuracy from 51.2% with uniform sampling to 62.0%, and it outperforms recent training-free frame selectors on QAEgo4D and MyEgo. A single-level version runs on a Mac and an iPhone.

title: On the Principle of Localization on Quasi-Orbits in Crossed Products
abstract: Quasi-regular $C^*$-dynamical systems with locally closed quasi-orbits are considered. For the corresponding crossed products, a localization principle on quasi-orbits is proven. This principle reduces the study of the primitive spectrum of the original crossed product to the study of the primitive spectra of crossed products, each corresponding to its own $C^*$-dynamical system with a single quasi-orbit. Assuming that the group action on the primitive spectrum of the $C^*$-algebra in the crossed product is free, except for some fixed subset, a characterization of the spectrum of the crossed product is provided, which allows for a description of the Jacobson topology on it.

title: Gravitational Illumination Bodies
abstract: For a given convex body $K$ in $\mathbb R ^n$ and $δ>0$, we introduce a new class of bodies, the {\em gravitational illumination bodies} $I^δ(K)$. We show some of their properties and explore their relation to floating bodies, illumination bodies and Ulam floating bodies. Unexpected phenomena happen and the gravitational illumination bodies exhibit very different behavior than the floating bodies, illumination bodies and Ulam floating bodies. While the classical bodies are all convex and either contained in $K$ or containing $K$, this is no longer the case for the new bodies. They need not be convex, but they are star shaped and it may happen that $I^δ(K)$ has non-empty intersection with both, $K$ and its complement. Moreover, the containment behavior may change with the dimension. Most surprising is the behavior of a volume derivative, $$ \lim_{δ\to 0} \frac{ |\vol_n(K)-\vol_n(I^δ(K)) |}{δ^\frac{2}{n+1}}. $$ In all dimensions the corresponding volume derivative for the classical bodies results in the equi-affine invariant affine surface area of the body $K$. In the case of the gravitational illumination body, this is also the case in all dimensions, except in dimension $3$. In dimension $3$ the limit is equal to $0$ for all convex bodies. A non-zero derivative is obtained in dimension $3$ if one normalizes by $δ$ instead of $δ^\frac{1}{2}$. The non-zero limit is a new affine invariant involving the {\em affine mean curvature } and the {\em Pick invariant} of the convex body.

title: GateWatch: Low-Overhead LLM Monitoring with Boolean Circuits
abstract: As large language models (LLMs) and LLM-based agents are increasingly deployed, monitoring their behavior becomes important for detecting unsafe or unintended actions. Activation probes offer an efficient approach, but existing methods face trade-offs between accuracy, interpretability, and computational overhead. Probes on raw activations lack interpretable inputs, whereas sparse autoencoder (SAE) probes use interpretable features but often rely on additive classifiers and large SAE encoders, limiting interpretability and increasing memory overhead. We introduce GateWatch, a compact, interpretable classifier that expresses its entire decision rule as an explicit Boolean logic over a small number of binarized SAE features. We explore three approaches to constructing these circuits under a specified gate budget. For efficient deployment, GateWatchServe computes only selected SAE features, enables streaming of their binary values across layers during inference, and evaluates multiple GateWatch classifiers in parallel using compact lookup tables. Across 24 tasks on Gemma-2-9B, GateWatch achieves 80.49% mean test accuracy using only 3.8 SAE features and 3.5 logic gates per probe on average, just 1.17 percentage points below full 16K-feature SAE probes, while matching or outperforming them on 10 tasks and reducing probe memory by 99.98%. Inside vLLM, 1,000 concurrent multi-layer, multi-token GateWatch classifiers retain 97-98% of baseline throughput and 99.8% of KV-cache capacity.

title: A multilayer network-based modelling framework for epizootic haemorrhagic disease virus transmission in France
abstract: Epizootic haemorrhagic disease virus serotype 8 (EHDV-8) emerged in France in September 2023 but its transmission dynamics remain poorly characterised. We adapted a stochastic, spatially explicit compartmental model developed for bluetongue to reconstruct the 2023-24 EHDV-8 epidemic in cattle in mainland France. The model represented transmission across cantons, incorporating cattle demography, pasture cover, relative Culicoides abundance and temperature-dependent vector processes. Three networks represented between-canton spread through short-range vector dispersal (pasture network), non-commercial cattle movements between pastures of the same farm (farm network), and cattle trade (trade network). Using approximate Bayesian computation with sequential Monte Carlo (ABC-SMC), we calibrated the model to canton-week seroprevalence estimates derived from bulk-tank milk measurements. Calibration narrowed the plausible range of the baseline vector-mediated transmission parameter and favoured higher movement intensities through the farm network, although movement intensity remained uncertain. Simulation-based parameter recovery showed that calibration generally identified parameter regions capable of reproducing epidemic patterns comparable to the pseudo-observed data, although predictive performance varied among datasets and was typically lower than that obtained with the generating parameters. When applied to observed data, the calibrated model captured several features of the observed weekly median seroprevalence across sampled cantons, although discrepancies remained at some sampling times and predictive uncertainty was substantial. These results demonstrate how bulk-tank milk surveillance can inform the reconstruction of EHDV-8 epidemic patterns within a national-scale transmission framework. This framework provides a basis for future evaluation and optimisation of vaccination strategies.
