Here, we evaluate whether simple electrochemical tests can reveal which electrode (cathode, anode or both) is targeted by specific additives. Our experiments quantified the rates of reductive and oxidative side-reactions in NMC532 vs. graphite cells containing 12 different electrolyte formulations. We found that gains in interphasial stability were highly correlated, with successful additives decreasing both types of side-reactions by similar magnitude. This dual action could be indicative of the role of crosstalk on cell degradation, as soluble species formed on one electrode can decompose at the other end of the cell. Although electrochemical tests are insufficient for understanding mechanisms of improvement, they can reveal interesting effects that complement other characterization tools.

title: SpatialScout-V2: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore Real-World 3D Scenes and Localize Objects?
abstract: Spatial intelligence requires agents to acquire visual evidence and integrate partial observations into coherent three-dimensional representations. We introduce SpatialScout-V2, which extends SpatialScout's active mapping task from simulation to real residential scenes through three advances: real visual observations, preservation of original scene content, and interactive exploration of recorded views. Built from 100 homes in Realsee3D, the benchmark covers 3,171 target objects across 29 categories. Given a fixed target inventory, agents autonomously select recorded viewpoints and viewing directions, integrate calibrated RGB observations, and iteratively estimate and revise object centers within a fixed interaction budget. We evaluate the localization accuracy and completeness of object-center maps using mean IoU, IoU-threshold hit rates, and target coverage. Evaluating seven frontier vision-language models (VLMs), we find that six achieve an all-target mean IoU below 20\%. Even the best-performing model, Claude Opus 5.5, reaches only 22.52\%, with just 18.36\% of targets exceeding an IoU of 0.5. Further analysis shows that broad submission coverage can coexist with limited localization accuracy, while target omissions further reduce overall scores. These results highlight substantial challenges in constructing accurate and complete object-center maps through active exploration of real scenes.

title: FlexVSR: Continuous-Scale Super-Resolution for Streaming Video Generation
abstract: Real-time streaming video generation has gained rapid momentum in live content creation and interactive media. Deploying such systems in practice requires flexible scaling factors to accommodate diverse source resolutions, target displays, and computational budgets. However, extending fixed-scale generative video super-resolution (VSR) to varying target scales poses two challenges: downsampling from a larger fixed scale incurs redundant cost, while re-optimizing the diffusion transformer (DiT) is costly and alters the shared generative prior. To address both, we propose FlexVSR, a decoupled framework for continuous-scale streaming generative VSR with supervision at only a few scales. Our key insight is that naively resampling fixed-scale latents onto a new target grid induces scale-dependent input mismatch, which can be effectively addressed through parameter-efficient, scale-aware adaptation of the latent interface without updating the DiT. To this end, FlexVSR introduces ReLSA (Refined Latent Scale Adaptation), a lightweight latent adapter that constructs and refines target-grid latents before they enter the DiT, enabling a shared frozen VSR prior to generalize across continuous scales with only 0.274M trainable parameters and an adaptation cost of 7.3 H100 GPU-hours, while introducing no additional temporal dependencies and preserving the native causal streaming protocol. Extensive experiments demonstrate competitive or superior reconstruction and temporal quality, lower latency than most native-scale streaming baselines and offline methods, and effective generalization to unseen continuous scales, filling the continuous-scale gap in real-time streaming generative VSR.

title: RegionAgent: Two-Stage Preference Optimization for Regional Image Restoration
abstract: Images under non-uniform coupled degradations require diverse restoration capabilities for different degraded regions. Existing methods employ globally uniform operations, potentially overlooking regional differences and causing incomplete restoration or even damage to image content. Moreover, a degraded region may require successive restoration actions, and earlier actions may alter residual degradation characteristics or introduce artifacts, potentially hindering subsequent restoration. To address these challenges, we propose RegionAgent, an adaptive restoration framework that trains a Vision-Language Model (VLM) through two-stage preference learning to generate a region-specific restoration action at each iteration. Specifically, we first train the VLM to select an action suited to the current region through step-level Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), using preferences derived from immediate restoration feedback to supervise only the differing component in each action pair. To account for the effects of current actions on subsequent restoration, we then apply trajectory-level DPO, using preferences derived from complete trajectory scores to supervise the sole differing action in each trajectory pair. Furthermore, as conventional image-pair datasets do not directly provide preferences over regional restoration decisions, we construct a regional restoration preference dataset comprising 10K action pairs and 20K trajectory pairs for two-stage VLM training. Experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate strong restoration performance under both mixed and single degradations. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of two-stage preference learning in improving restoration quality.

title: Stablecoin Runs as Safe-Asset Stress Signals: Episode-Level Evidence for Central Bank Surveillance
abstract: This paper asks whether stablecoin runs carry information about U.S. Treasury yields. Using daily data on USDT, USDC and BUSD from 2021 to 2025 and five stress episodes, it measures flows from changes in token units rather than market capitalisation, which removes the phantom inflows the standard measure records when tokens lose their peg. Flows have no stable relationship with yields in normal periods. During the three panic-driven runs, a one-billion-dollar five-day redemption is associated with an 8.5 basis point fall in the three-month bill yield within ten trading days, while two regulatory episodes carry no such signal. The response is broad across maturities and has the opposite sign to what reserve liquidation predicts, which points to flight to quality. The effect is led by the TerraUSD collapse and corroborated by the USDC/SVB run. Five-day redemptions of roughly USD 2 to 3 billion during a panic mark the scale at which stablecoin stress becomes informative for surveillance.

title: DUV (257 nm) LIDT of Anti-Reflective Coatings
abstract: Laser-induced damage threshold in the deep ultraviolet (DUV) was used to perform tests on AR coated windows intended for industrial processes. The 257 nm wavelength was generated from Yb:YAG fundamental (1030 nm) and the long-term LIDT stability (up to 100000 shots) was selected as representative for minimal industrial qualification. Selected setup for the fourth harmonics generation consists of two stages, generation of second harmonic and subsequently the fourth harmonic with 13,4% conversation efficiency. In both 1-on-1 and S-on-1 experiments, the optics coated with Al2O3/SiO2 by ion beam sputtering technique demonstrated the highest LIDT value of 0.73 and 0.5 J/cm2 respectively. Various damage morphologies, color centers, ballistic damage, delamination, and blistering were observed across the samples with respect to the 1-on-1 and S-on-1.

title: The long-term divergence exponent and the temporal structure of step-to-step perturbations: a simulation study in two passive walking models
abstract: Purpose. Divergence exponents are used to assess the local dynamic stability of gait. Human experiments have related the long-term exponent ($λ_L$) to the complexity of gait fluctuations. Model studies used perturbations without controlled temporal structure. The question was whether $λ_L$ responds to the temporal structure of perturbations in walkers without neuromuscular control. Methods. Two passive walkers, M1 (pilot) and M2 (exploratory), received step-to-step perturbations of five amplitudes ($σ$) and nine temporal structures (ARFIMA parameter $d$), and human stride series of free and metronome walking. Results. At constant amplitude, $λ_L$ increased with $d$ in both models. It was higher with free series than with metronome series or with surrogates. It did not follow $σ$ in M1 and followed $σ$ in M2. Its double dissociation from the short-term exponent was supported in M1 only. In a descriptive analysis, the condition means of $λ_L$ correlated with the scaling exponent of the step durations ($r = 0.980$ in M1 and 0.906 in M2). Conclusion. In two passive walkers with fixed mechanics, $λ_L$ followed the temporal structure of the perturbations; its specificity depended on the model. This response supports the name attractor complexity index (ACI), proposed for $λ_L$ from human experiments.

title: Thermodynamically Consistent Neural Networks for a Universal Fluid Gibbs Free Energy Equation of State
abstract: Over the past three centuries, many thermodynamics researchers have worked to develop fluid equations of state with both high accuracy and broad applicability, proposing various theoretical frameworks and models. Building on these efforts, this study uses Gibbs free energy as the starting point and introduces thermodynamically consistent neural networks to construct a fluid equation of state based on Gibbs free energy (GEoS). This approach establishes a novel machine learning framework that provides a unified representation of fluid states. GEoS performs well on the vapor- and liquid-phase density test sets, with average absolute relative deviations (AARDs) of 5.25% and 3.96%, respectively. It outperforms conventional volume-translated cubic equations of state and existing machine learning models, demonstrating its effectiveness. Further analysis using the UMAP dimensionality reduction method shows that most molecules in the test set belong to extrapolation systems, confirming the strong generalization ability of the model. Finally, the test results show that the PC-SAFT equation fitted using GEoS maintains high predictive accuracy, providing a reliable basis for its practical application in industry.

title: Invariant real curves arising from semiconjugacies of rational maps
abstract: In this paper, we study real analytic invariant curves arising from semiconjugacies of real rational maps. Such semiconjugacies arise naturally in Eremenko's work on invariant Jordan analytic curves. While invariant generalized circles are easy to obtain from real rational maps, we are interested in curves not contained in any generalized circle. First, for a non-exceptional polynomial of degree at least two, we prove that every invariant curve arising from such a semiconjugacy is contained in a generalized circle. Second, in the rational map case, we construct invariant curves arising in this way that are not contained in any generalized circle and have arbitrarily many self-intersections, counted with multiplicity. Moreover, the rational maps can be chosen so that their restrictions to these curves have positive topological entropy.

title: Euler up-down numbers and quiver representations
abstract: We show that Euler up-down numbers enumerate isoclasses of representations arising from quiver Grassmannians which provide an explicit realization of PBW degenerate flag varieties. Using this geometric realization, we derive several formulas connecting Euler up-down numbers, median Genocchi numbers, and Motzkin numbers. We also define a new $q$-analogue of Euler up-down numbers and derive several formulas for these polynomials. We describe a natural poset structure on the set of isoclasses of subrepresentations and describe it in terms of the classical degeneration order. Finally, we prove that the finer strata defined by fixing isotypes of sub- and quotient representations are the orbits under the automorphism group of the ambient quiver representation.

title: Reward misalignment as an opportunity for materials discovery
abstract: Reward misalignment is usually regarded as a failure of artificial intelligence. In materials discovery with generative AI models, however, disagreement between predefined rewards and expert judgment may reveal materials that the rewards overlook. We investigate this possibility using electronic flat bands as a prime example. Experts mostly agree with a numerical bandwidth score, but their disagreements are systematic and cannot be explained by an estimated 5% rate of mistaken labels. We learn the experts' preferences from pairwise comparisons and use them to guide a crystal diffusion model. The learned preferences and numerical score agree on the flattest bands but diverge elsewhere. For example, the preferences favor KCo2As2 and CoGa, reported compounds with partially flat bands that the score would discard. The framework also extends to synthesizability and phonon properties. Our findings suggest that reward misalignment can expose opportunities for materials discovery beyond what fixed rewards are designed to find.

title: Invertible Transport Between Sample-Only Distributions via Projected Characteristic Functions
abstract: Many useful latent distributions can be sampled but do not have a tractable density. Such distributions may be represented by empirical collections of real-world observations or generated by scientific simulators and black-box generative models. These sample-only priors cannot be used directly in likelihood-based normalizing flows, which require evaluating the prior density. We propose Projected Characteristic-Function matching (PCF), a density-free framework for learning an invertible map between a data distribution and a prior specified only through samples. Our method aligns distributions using projected empirical characteristic functions, eliminating the need for density estimation, adversarial training, or paired observations. To address the non-uniqueness of the transport map, we introduce an optional transport regularizer that selects lower-displacement transformations while preserving endpoint alignment. We benchmark PCF on controlled transports, sample-efficiency studies, and high-dimensional alignment tasks. PCF matches the accuracy of kernel MMD on the controlled benchmark and on raw-pixel MNIST--USPS at a cost linear in the batch size, and it is more sample-efficient, achieving lower endpoint error than MMD in 13 of 15 paired runs across library sizes. By avoiding pairwise kernel evaluation, it reduces discrepancy memory by 29.8% and trains at batch sizes where kernel MMD exceeds GPU memory. These results show that PCF provides accurate and efficient invertible transport, particularly in sample- and memory-limited settings.

title: Approximation Algorithms for Asymmetric Multi-Path TSP
abstract: Asymmetric Multi-Path TSP is the generalization of the Asymmetric Traveling Salesperson Problem where we are looking for $k$ walks, each with prescribed start $s_i$ and prescribed end $t_i$, such that every vertex is visited by at least one of the walks. The objective is to minimize the total length of all walks. In general, it is NP-hard to find any approximation for this problem in polynomial time (even if the approximation factor is allowed to depend on the number of vertices). We show that one can obtain an $O(k)$-approximation in time $n^{O(k)}$, answering an open question by Friggstad [2013]. For the special case where all tour start vertices $s_i$ are identical and all end vertices $t_i$ are identical, we obtain an $O(k)$-approximation in polynomial time, as well as an $(O(\frac{1}ε), 1+ε)$-bicriteria approximation. For the multi-depot setting, where $s_i =t_i$ for all $i$, we obtain a constant-factor approximation in polynomial time. Finally, our results imply improved constant-factor approximation algorithms for Asymmetric Regret-Bounded Vehicle Routing and unit-weight Path ATSP.

title: Optimal Radius Ratio of Compact Nonuniform Packings
abstract: We study the ratio of the smallest to the largest radius in a nonuniform disk packing whose tangency graph triangulates the plane. We give a computer-assisted proof that the largest possible ratio is $s=0.651050185882609\ldots$, attained uniquely up to similarity by packing~53 of Fernique, Hashemi, and Sizova. In fact, every nonuniform packing with radius ratio at least $0.65105$ is similar to this packing. No periodicity or restriction on the number of radii is assumed; the radii are required only to have a positive infimum and a finite supremum. Following the finite-subgraph exclusion program of Connelly and Zhang, we first restrict the degree-five flowers and their pairings. The remaining exceptional degree-seven corona forces seventeen complete flowers on an unfolded disk with thirty-seven labels. An exact interval certificate excludes their angle equations. A comparison of logarithmic radii on a recurrent network then forces the radii and the three local degree words. We identify the entire triangulation by reducing these words to the square--octagon tiling and showing that its decoration is forced.

title: Convex combinations of strict triangular norms
abstract: We prove that a pointwise convex combination of two strict triangular norms with positive weights is associative if and only if the two norms coincide. Together with the known ordinal-sum reduction and nilpotent case, the theorem yields the same conclusion for all continuous triangular norms and, in particular, for associative bivariate copulas. It also gives a corresponding result for representable uninorms with a common neutral element.

title: Backbone Matters: Benchmarking Encoder-Decoder Networks for Semantic Segmentation of Driving Scenes on BDD100K
abstract: Semantic segmentation gives an autonomous vehicle a dense, pixel-level description of its surroundings and is a core part of scene understanding. Most segmentation networks consist of an encoder (the backbone) and a decoder, yet the backbone is often chosen without a systematic comparison. This work studies this choice on the BDD100K driving dataset. Four widely used decoders (U-Net, FPN, LinkNet and PSPNet) are combined with 13 backbones from six families (ResNet, VGG, DenseNet, Inception, MobileNet and EfficientNet), and all 52 models are trained with one common protocol. The best model, an FPN decoder with an EfficientNet-B4 backbone, reaches 62.6% mean intersection over union (mIoU), 89.8% accuracy and a loss of 0.092. Only two of the 52 models, both FPN with EfficientNet, exceed the 56.9% mIoU reported with the BDD100K benchmark. The effect of the backbone depends strongly on the decoder: the same EfficientNet-B4 gives 42.6% mIoU with PSPNet but 62.6% with FPN, and the gap between the best and the worst backbone ranges from 12.0 points (U-Net) to 42.5 points (FPN). The results and the scope of this study are discussed.

title: The LEMAITRE project: An Independent Probe of the $w-w_a$ Tension
abstract: Recent BAO, CMB, and Type Ia supernova constraints on the dark-energy equation of state show a tension with the cosmological-constant model at the heart of $Λ$CDM, partly driven by low-redshift supernova measurements. We present the LEMAITRE project, a new measurement of the dark energy equation of state, based on a distinct SN~Ia dataset (2800 from ZTF, 170 from SNLS and 300 from HSC), a dedicated calibration program, and a new, independent analysis pipeline.

title: Calibrating the cosmic distance ladder for independent dark energy constraints
abstract: Recent cosmological results presented by the DESI collaboration show a clear deviation from the $Λ$CDM model when considering a time-dependent dark energy equation of state. This deviation is strongly driven by the SNe Ia surveys, which all share the same low redshift sample. The ZTF survey provides the current larger SNe Ia sample at low redshift, which will significantly increase the constraining power. In this context, the LEMAITRE collaboration aims to provide new constraints on dark energy parameters using three independent SNe Ia datasets: ZTF, SNLS and HSC. This effort requires robust photometric calibration, with a particular focus on filter transmission measurement and star catalog calibration. The target for LEMAITRE is to control the calibration systematics on distance moduli below 0.4%.

title: Full-Color Two-loop Four-point Form Factor in N=4 SYM with Global CK-duality
abstract: We determine the full-color two-loop four-point MHV form factor of the stress-tensor supermultiplet in N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory. Using color-kinematics (CK) duality and unitarity cuts, we construct complete one- and two-loop integrands manifesting global off-shell CK duality without explicit $μ^2$ dependence. Integration-by-parts reduction to uniform-transcendentality master integrals yields purely rational numbers multiplying simple kinematic prefactors, manifesting maximal transcendentality. Expressing the form factor in terms of pentagon functions, we verify full-color infrared-pole cancellation, extract the finite remainder, and obtain new non-planar results for the two-loop triple-collinear splitting function and double-soft current.

title: A version of the Cloude/van Zyl decomposition for full/quad pol synthetic aperture radar data
abstract: Based on the Cloude/van Zyl decomposition of reflection symmetric polarimetric SAR data we present a version for full/quad polarisation data. We demonstrate both versions on X-band F-SAR data over Vejers, Denmark. Differences between the original and our version of the decomposition occur especially for very bright man-made targets. These differences come with lower entropy for our version giving an improved focus on a more pronounced dominant scattering mechanism for these objects. Interpretation of the scattering mechanism related to the full/quad pol version of the decomposition is facilitated by means of the Cloude/Pottier $\barα$ angle.

title: EmbodyAgent: Post-Training Embodied VLM Agents via Distillation, SFT, and RL
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can act as closed-loop robot-use agents (RUAs) by writing and executing control code through tool interfaces. However, turning an open-weight VLM into a high-performing embodied agent requires a complete post-training stack: out-of-the-box open VLMs fail completely at interactive tool contracts, strong frontier teachers are accessible only as black-box endpoints without exposed weights or token probabilities, and supervised imitation alone plateaus under rollout distribution shift. We present EmbodyAgent, an end-to-end post-training framework with three tightly coupled pipelines: (1) a black-box data synthesis pipeline that queries a strong teacher under a forced think-then-code contract and filters trajectories by task success; (2) an SFT pipeline that distills the explanation-and-program targets into an open-weight 9B VLM with both vision and language encoders trainable; and (3) an online RL pipeline that optimizes student-generated episodes via group-relative advantage with a runtime-error-penalized outcome reward. All three pipelines share one primitive-free Python execution tool exposing only raw visual observation and seven-dimensional end-effector control, with no action decoder and no interface shift across stages. Under a strictly separated evaluation protocol on ten LIBERO Spatial tasks (disjoint state splits, greedy test-time decoding, training-only safeguards), held-out success on 100 test states rises from 0/100 (base 9B VLM) to 14/100 (after SFT) and 84/100 (after RL), while training rollout success climbs from 8.4% to 87.7% and median model calls per episode drop from 36 to 11. We further identify a self-reinforcing runtime-error mode induced by outcome-based RL on executable code, and establish a failure-category monitoring and sampling-side curation protocol that stabilizes training.

title: Equity and Aggregate Ambiguity
abstract: Equitable resource allocations in the context of symmetric risk exposures are intuitively desirable and sometimes even expected in public planning. However, public planners generally are also concerned with mitigating risk and, more generally, uncertainty and ambiguity. We study a fundamental conflict between equity and ambiguity avoidance in public risk allocation problems. Our main results are framed and established in the setting of general symmetric aggregate losses equipped with dependence uncertainty among individual losses. Specializing to the classical model of Keeney (1980), we prove that an increase in equity is equivalent to an increase in aggregate ambiguity. We then provide a quantitative characterization of equity and ambiguity avoidance through the $α$-maxmin preference framework, establishing conditions on ambiguity and risk attitudes under which each criterion holds. Specifically, equity corresponds to ambiguity or risk proneness, while ambiguity avoidance corresponds to ambiguity or risk aversion. The analysis extends to general classes of symmetric aggregation functions, where we show that ambiguity attitude is the primary determinant of preference, though aggregation structure and risk attitude also play important roles. Numerical illustrations validate our theoretical findings and explore the equity-ambiguity tradeoff.

title: The role of complementarity and quantum correlation in the uncertainty relations and the optimum states
abstract: Uncertainty relations are used in quantum mechanics to illustrate the complementarity of two observables, assuming there is a lower bound for the product of their dispersions that depends on the first-order quantum correlation and the commutation relation of those observables in an optimum state. In this work, we demonstrate that the complex parameter of the optimum state equation has real and imaginary parts that depend on the first-order quantum correlation and the commutation relation between the observables in the optimum state, respectively. We apply our results to a two-level system, finding that the first-order quantum correlation and the commutation relation of two spin-1/2 projections in the optimum state complement each other and, finally, when the term correlation is used, a lower bound for the uncertainty principle does not depend on any parameter of the optimum state, in contrast to the usual form of the Heisenberg principle.

title: Learning to Think with Images Faithfully via Adaptive Data Selection
abstract: Thinking with images (TwI) empowers vision-language models (VLMs) to overcome perceptual bottlenecks by actively cropping and zooming into fine-grained visual details, promising both higher accuracy and interpretable, region-grounded reasoning. However, our analysis shows that the improved accuracy of TwI models does not guarantee faithful tool use; they frequently invoke tools without actually relying on the zoomed region, undermining the reliability of tool-assisted reasoning. We trace this unfaithful behaviour to the training data: when questions are answerable without zooming, the model can answer correctly while ignoring the returned evidence, and this problem is exacerbated during training as the model becomes better at answering without tools. To keep zooming useful throughout training, we adapt the training data to the model's evolving capability and train on questions where correct zoomed evidence can still help the model answer correctly. This selection is supported by a data synthesis pipeline that localises small objects and constructs verifiable questions about their fine details, and complemented by an adaptiveness reward that favours tool-free answers when zooming is unnecessary. The experimental results show that our method substantially improves reasoning faithfulness and achieves state-of-the-art performance on visual search benchmarks (+11.6% on V*, +7.9% on HR-Bench 4K, and +9.4% on HR-Bench 8K). On multimodal hallucination benchmarks, our model also outperforms the compared TwI baselines. These results suggest that improving TwI faithfulness does not sacrifice accuracy and that both can be learnt from the right training data without directly supervising the reasoning process.

title: A Three-Factor Hull-White Scenario Generator for Macro-Financial Stress Forecasting
abstract: This paper builds a scenario engine that maps a yield-curve path into a distribution of macro-financial outcomes. A three-factor Hull-White model generates arbitrage-free curves whose factors are simulated under the physical measure, with an estimated and reported market price of risk. A Minnesota-prior VARX maps the simulated curves into weekly equity returns, the federal funds rate, the Weekly Economic Index, inflation and a bank Marginal Expected Shortfall proxy, with a sign-restricted policy shock adapted to weekly data. Evaluated out of sample from 2017 to 2024, the term-structure block has the lowest forecast error in 13 of 20 maturity and horizon cells, and the density forecasts are well calibrated for the continuously moving variables. At weekly frequency the curve carries no incremental information about these variables once their own lags are controlled for, so the engine's value lies in conditioning on a specified curve path, which no benchmark can do.

title: Learn, Freeze, and Transfer an Activation Function Across Architectures
abstract: Transfer learning typically reuses knowledge acquired by a source network through its learned weights. We investigate whether a learned activation function can also be transferred and remain useful in networks trained from scratch. We study this complementary form of transfer through a learn-freeze-transfer protocol, in which the activation is optimized jointly with a source network in a single training run, and is then frozen and reused in target networks trained from scratch. A pointwise activation with globally shared parameters is independent of layer dimensions and can therefore be incorporated into networks of different architectures trained from scratch. We instantiate this protocol with FAct, a five-parameter activation represented by a two-harmonic truncated Fourier series, initialized from a Fourier approximation of GELU and learned in a Vision Transformer (ViT) on ImageNet-1K. When reused in a ViT of the same architecture trained from scratch on ImageNet-1K, the frozen activation (Frozen FAct) improves top-1 accuracy by 1.46 percentage points over GELU. Across four smaller target architectures (standard ViT, Swin Transformer, linear-attention ViT, and MLP-Mixer) and four image-classification datasets, it achieves the highest mean accuracy among eleven activation functions in 15 of 16 settings under a common training configuration, with improvements of up to 1.71 percentage points over the best conventional activation. When the learning rate and weight decay are tuned separately for each activation under the same search budget, Frozen FAct still ranks first in 11 of the 16 settings, second in four, and fourth in one. These results provide empirical evidence that a learned activation function can retain its usefulness when transferred across vision architectures, independently of the weights with which it was learned.

title: Connecting Coronal Loop Scaling Laws and Kink Wave Heating: An Analytical and Numerical Study
abstract: Turbulent dissipation of kink waves has been proposed as one of the mechanisms responsible for the observed high coronal temperatures. We test this hypothesis by examining the effect of this heating mechanism on coronal loops. The coronal loop static and dynamic behaviour is investigated under the assumption that the heating in the loop is primarily provided by kink wave dissipation. The heating term is borrowed from the recently developed UAWSoM model. Loop modelling is done in 1D using three different methods: one analytical following the principles first set in the RTV scaling laws, and two numerical: one based on the setup used to derive the RTVS scaling laws, and UAWSoM. We provide scaling laws and estimate density, temperature, and pressure, as well as kink wave heating rate and kink wave energy density needed to counteract energy loss by thermal conduction and radiative cooling. Estimates of kink wave energy density needed to heat the loop to 1 MK correspond to maximum velocity amplitudes of around 35 km s$^{-1}$ near the loop apex. Loop radius, density contrast and filling factor are found to affect the predictions significantly. The two numerical methods agree to a high degree. The analytical method predicts that $W_\textrm{k} \propto PL^{-2/3}$, while the two numerical methods show a wider range of scaling exponents which depend on the location in the loop. UAWSoM simulations suggest that loops may exhibit dynamic behaviour for a wide range of loop conditions, which may include thermal non-equilibrium cycles and periods of emerging and dissipating slow waves. Overall, estimates of kink wave energy density and scaling laws provide observational constraints on the importance of the proposed kink wave heating mechanism, with the current preliminary results suggesting that the uniturbulent kink wave heating may be a significant source of energy and heat in coronal loops.

title: Notes on non-equilibrium thermodynamics of Robinson-Trautman spacetimes
abstract: Robinson-Trautman spacetimes are determined by a parabolic heat-type evolution equation of fourth order for a scalar field on future null infinity. This equation may be re-written as an energy balance for an asymptotically time-like observer. In turn, it becomes a first law in the context of non-equilibrium thermodynamics if the non-linear memory is interpreted as heat. This leads to a local version of temperature and a manifestly increasing entropy density from the viewpoint of the environment.

title: Uninorm constructions on bounded trellises via closure and interior operators
abstract: In this paper, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions under which six closure- or interior-based operations on bounded trellises are uninorms. These operations incorporate triangular norms, triangular conorms, or both, and form three order-dual pairs. Since the underlying pseudo-order need not be transitive and meet and join need not be associative, standard lattice arguments do not apply directly. Under a fixed ambient transitivity assumption, the first pair is characterized by image, monotonicity, and compatibility conditions for the associated maps on elements incomparable with the neutral element; an additional comparison condition used in earlier sufficient constructions is shown to be redundant. Complete characterizations are also obtained for the variants with an absorbing endpoint, including both nondegenerate and degenerate interval cases. For the pair involving both a triangular norm and a triangular conorm, we derive exact comparison conditions requiring the triangular norm to take the value~$0$, or dually the triangular conorm to take the value~$1$, in the relevant cases. These conditions reduce to the usual incomparability assumptions in the absence of nontrivial zero- or one-divisors. On bounded lattices, the closure and interior conditions simplify to explicit identities or image restrictions. Finite proper-trellis examples clarify the role and limitations of the ambient transitivity assumptions.

title: Convergence of the Most Probable Transition Paths in Multiscale Systems
abstract: This paper is devoted to study the convergence behavior of the most probable transition paths in a class of multiscale stochastic dynamical systems. First, based on Euler-Lagrange equations, we establish proximity and convergence results in the space of continuous functions endowed with the supremum norm. These results compare the most probable paths of the multiscale system with those of averaged system derived from the averaging principle. Next, we utilize a variational framework and analyze the Onsager-Machlup functionals using $Γ$-convergence. Together with the equi-coercivity of the functional family, we prove the convergence of both their minima and minimizers. Specifically, we show weak convergence of the minimizers in the Cameron-Martin space $H^1$, which implies their strong convergence in $L^2$.

title: The rigidity phenomenon for weighted composition operators on the Fock spaces
abstract: We establish the rigidity of canonical sums of any finite number of weighted composition operators acting from a Fock space $\mathcal{F}^p$ into another $\mathcal{F}^q$ for all possible combinations of \(p,q\in (0, \infty]\). Specifically, we show that such a sum is bounded (compact, resp.) if and only if its summands are individually bounded (compact, resp.). In the case \(p\le q\), we present two independent approaches -- one analytic and one largely algebraic -- based on some common preliminary rigidity results. As a natural byproduct of our approach, we also obtain the Reproducing Kernel Thesis.

title: Surface sheaves on the quintic I. Expanded degenerations and virtual gluing
abstract: We study the specialization of Donaldson-Thomas virtual cycles for surface sheaves on a Calabi Yau threefold degenerating to a simple normal crossing threefold, composed of two quasi Fano threefolds glued along a common (double) divisor. The compactification of the two relative sheaf moduli spaces involves construction of suitable moduli space of sheaves on expanded degenerations of each quasi Fano variety. On a fixed expanded fiber the matching datum is an equivalence of the derived restrictions of the component sheaves. We identify the corresponding deformation complexes and give valuative and obstruction-theoretic hypotheses under which the specialized virtual class is a sum over marked joining divisors. When a marked space is the full fiber product of proper relative factors over a smooth simple boundary moduli space, its class is a refined diagonal pullback. For the case of sheaves supported on hyperplane sections of the threefold we discuss construction of the proper relative family by descending the chartwise stable loci, and identify both marked pieces, including the one with zero boundary. To provide some examples, we carry out explicit constructions for the moduli space of surface structure sheaf and its twists. We also prove valuative results for specified sheaves with noninvertible hulls. In a sequel, Part II, we use the construction of degeneration technique in this article to compare quintic invariants with the predicted S-duality modularity of "M5-brane modified elliptic genus" provided by string theorists, Gaiotto Strominger and Yin.

title: Theory of magneto-electrokinetics in unidirectional electrolyte flow: Hydrodynamic potential and Hall effect
abstract: We develop a theoretical framework for magneto-electrokinetic transport in dilute electrolytes under unidirectional flow and streaming current conditions. Unlike standard magnetohydrodynamics in liquid metals, where charge carriers are electrons and conductivity is typically uniform, electrolytes exhibit spatially varying ion densities and additional forces such as osmotic pressure. In steady state, the coupled Navier--Stokes, Nernst--Planck, and Poisson equations become analytically tractable. We derive a Boltzmann-like expression for ion distributions that incorporates both the electrostatic potential and a novel hydrodynamic potential arising from the magnetic field. This potential depends explicitly on the flow profile and is not screened close to the bounding walls. Applying the theory to Poiseuille flow, we derive expressions for the induced Hall potential and demonstrate its near-linear dependence on flow velocity and magnetic field strength, while remaining largely independent of salt concentration. To validate this one-dimensional framework, we analyze the two-dimensional spatial transients near the channel entrance. We demonstrate a separation of length scales: the Hall electric field and space charge adjust to the magnetic field almost instantaneously, whereas the macroscopic salt concentration wake develops over a much longer Graetz length dictated by the Péclet number. We also examine a similar flow with counterions only and no added salt, determining the resulting potential and ion distributions. This work offers new theoretical tools for understanding ion transport in microfluidic and electrochemical systems.

title: Observation of the electromagnetic Dalitz decay $J/ψ\rightarrow μ^+ μ^- η$
abstract: Using a data sample of $(8.998 \pm 0.039)\times10^9$ $J/ψ$ events collected by the BESIII detector at BEPCII, we report the observation of the electromagnetic Dalitz decay $J/ψ\to μ^+ μ^- η$ for the first time, with a statistical significance greater than 10$σ$. The branching fraction is measured to be $\mathcal{B}(J/ψ\to μ^+ μ^- η) = (3.05 \pm 0.14_{\rm stat.} \pm 0.13_{\rm syst.})\times 10^{-6}$. The ratio of this branching fraction to that of the corresponding radiative decay $J/ψ\to γη$ is determined to be $\mathcal{B}(J/ψ\to μ^+μ^-η)/\mathcal{B}(J/ψ\to γη) = (2.80 \pm 0.18) \times 10^{-3}$. Combining this result with the previous BESIII measurement of the $J/ψ\to e^+e^-η$ branching fraction yields $\mathcal{B}(J/ψ\to μ^+μ^-η)/\mathcal{B}(J/ψ\to e^+e^-η) = 0.219 \pm 0.020$. These results are consistent with the theoretical predictions based on the vector meson dominance model.

title: Improving the signal-to-noise ratio through postselection of coincident detections in anticounterfeiting and quantum key distribution
abstract: In quantum communications and other photon-counting applications, reliably detecting weak optical signals against a strong noise background remains a fundamental challenge. In this paper, we develop a simple idea: when a signal is carried by pairs (or more generally multiplets) of photons emitted simultaneously, postselection of coincident detections recorded on two detectors makes it possible to improve-sometimes drastically-the Signal to Noise Ratio. Essentially, this is made possible by the fact that genuine and accidental coincidences scale differently with the width of the postselection window. As long as the window remains wide enough to retain detections from the same pair, the genuine coincidence rate is approximately unchanged. In contrast, coincidences formed from independent clicks decrease linearly as the window is narrowed. The resulting signal-to-noise ratio, therefore, increases inversely with the window width. Our approach makes it possible to reveal photon-pair signals that are otherwise hidden beneath a much stronger uncorrelated background. We analyze here applications of this idea to quantum key distribution, metrology, and anti-counterfeiting.

title: SpecWM: Turning Verification into Refinement for Streaming World Models
abstract: Recently, video world models have advanced interactive generation, with large models offering higher quality and smaller models enabling faster inference. Existing speculative methods combine their strengths through fast draft generation and selective target regeneration guided by rewards on decoded frames. However, verification covers only the external scorer's evaluation dimensions and adds decoding and scoring costs. Moreover, these scores provide no correction, requiring costly target regeneration for rejected drafts. To address these limitations, we propose Speculative World Model (SpecWM), a unified, training-free inference framework for streaming world models. It verifies draft chunks using the target's latent velocity field. Verification also yields a reusable correction; two thresholds select Accept, Refine, or Reject. Specifically, one-step refinement reuses it to improve perceptual quality, while three-step refinement strengthens camera following and trajectory consistency. These findings motivate transition-aware refinement. On WBench Navigation, SpecWM improves visual quality at 1.63$\times$ speedup over the target and raises NavScore from the draft's 75.99 to 85.63, achieving the best quality-speed-control trade-off. Additionally, our LongSpecBench shows sustained quality and control over long, multi-turn rollouts, while experiments on Hy-Nomas validate SpecWM across backbones and denoising budgets.

title: The Necessity of Acceptance & Rejection in Inferential Reasoning
abstract: In this paper, we argue that acceptance and rejection constitute two fundamental positions necessary for inferential reasoning. Our central thesis is that a proposition acquires an inferential role when it is considered from a position of acceptance or rejection, rather than purely understood as propositional content. We distinguish between understanding a proposition, entertaining it hypothetically, and employing it within an inference. Particular attention is given to hypothetical reasoning and suspended judgement, which appear to challenge the necessity of adopting either position. We maintain that these cases do not undermine our thesis, since inferential reasoning can involve provisional acceptance or rejection without requiring personal belief or permanent commitment. Accordingly, the necessity of these positions should be understood as inferential rather than psychological. By examining the relationship between propositional content, inferential positions, and rational commitment, we defend the view that acceptance and rejection provide the fundamental conditions under which propositions can function within reasoning. This establishes a philosophical foundation for understanding inference through opposed rational positions.

title: Unusual increase in electrical and thermal conductivity of severely deformed CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy: Roles of disordering and nanostructuring in electron and phonon transport
abstract: This work investigates how defect engineering and nanostructuring via severe plastic deformation influence electrical and thermal transport in the high-entropy alloy CrMnFeCoNi. High-pressure torsion (HPT) for up to N = 4 turns produces a hierarchical defect structure, including deformation twins at low strains, dislocations and Lomer-Cottrell locks at intermediate strains, and a high fraction of high-angle grain boundaries at large strains. While hardness naturally increases and saturates at ~520 Hv, both electrical and thermal conductivity exhibit an unusual increase upon HPT processing (from 0.953 MS m-1 and 10.3 W m-1 K-1 after homogenization to 1.003 +- 0.005 MS m-1 and 14.4 W m-1 K-1 after N = 4). Analysis based on the Wiedemann-Franz law indicates a modest increase in electron transport (~5%) and a significant increase in phonon transport (~100%) after HPT processing. The phonon mean free path remains small on the order of 0.6-1.1 nm, and comparison with the Cahill-Pohl model shows that heat transport occurs near the minimum thermal conductivity limit, where vibrational modes are strongly scattered. This suggests that the enhancement in thermal transport is not governed by conventional defect scattering, but it is hypothesized that modifications in atomic-scale disorder, such as deformation-induced short-range ordering, are responsible for this unusual behavior. Specific heat capacity increases after HPT, consistent with stored defect energy. The linear thermal expansion exhibits a non-monotonic behavior, decreasing initially due to internal stresses and relaxation effects, and increasing at higher strains due to grain boundary-induced anharmonicity. These findings highlight the complex interplay between defects, atomic-scale disorder, and nanostructure in governing the electrical and thermal properties of severely deformed high-entropy alloys via electron and phonon scattering.

title: Cooperativity-enhanced single-photon emission in a topological quantum emitter chain
abstract: Single-photon emitters are one of the key elements in state-of-the art quantum technologies, yet optimizing and manipulating their emission requires precise fabrication of the emitter systems themselves. Here, we propose a route to tailored single-photon emission by exploiting cooperative effects in a topological single-photon emitter chain. Although the involvement of multiple emitters normally suppresses single-photon emission, we show that localized topological edge modes restore single-photon emission and protect against local perturbations. At the same time, cooperative effects occur due to the collective nature of the edge modes, leading to directional emission and linewidth narrowing. Our findings open new possibilities for tailoring single-photon emission by combining cooperativity and topological effects.

title: To predict or to persist: how decoherence shapes learning in a spin-qubit quantum reservoir
abstract: In this work we investigate how dephasing and the choice of measured observables affect learning in a simulated six-qubit spin chain with Markovian dissipation and exact expectation-value readout. For externally driven nonlinear autoregressive moving-average signals, combining single- and two-qubit observables gives better predictions than a population-only readout at comparable polynomial feature counts. Most of the configurations we tested become more accurate than a reference with relaxation and dephasing disabled, most strongly at $T_2=1\,μ$s, where total memory capacity drops, and still at $T_2=5$-$10\,μ$s, where memory is only redistributed across delays. For autonomous generation, we train the readout with scheduled sampling and iterative dataset aggregation to expose it to states reached under its own feedback. We do not find a clear systematic dependence of limit-cycle persistence on coherence across the reservoir ensemble. For chaotic forecasting, in contrast, prediction horizons at $T_2=1\,μ$s shorten in all 10 reservoir realizations relative to that reference. For the noise-driven strange non-chaotic attractor, the model produces a smooth, approximately closed orbit, and neither captures the target's scatter nor follows its trajectory pointwise. We conclude that, within this simulated reservoir, the impact of coherence depends strongly on the task.

title: Frontier models need only one text to unmask its human or AI author
abstract: Given a single text and a simple zero-shot prompt (no web access, tools, candidate lists, or writing samples), frontier models can answer "who wrote this?" at three increasingly specific levels: (1) whether an AI or human wrote it, (2) if an AI, which lab, and (3) if a human, often exactly who. The latest models (Claude Fable 5.2, GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Carbon) match trained detectors like Pangram while also explaining their predictions in natural language, and Opus 5.5 names the correct lab for 98% of texts generated by models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google. Most strikingly, Fable 5.2 correctly names the author of 55% of 15K anonymous ICML 2020 reviews that were never made public, and identifies the username behind 69% of comments from active Redditors (with >500 posts over the last year). Accuracy depends on exposure to an author's writing in pretraining data and on reasoning effort, and simply asking a model how familiar it is with someone predicts whether it can identify their writing. For anyone who has published enough writing online, frontier models present a greater threat to anonymity than commonly assumed, and defenses are limited.

title: Surface sheaves on the quintic II. Donaldson-Thomas invariants and the M5-brane modified elliptic genus in string theory
abstract: We compute Donaldson-Thomas invariants of pure two-dimensional sheaves in the hyperplane class of a smooth quintic threefold. We take advantage of two degenerating families to relate the DT geometry of Quintic threefold to geometry of pure two dimensional shaves on a quartic threefold and correction terms induced by invariants of relative Hilbert schemes of points. For this we use degeneration technique and virtual gluing formula in the prequel Part I. The marked virtual intersections, Chow specialization and complete moduli on the smooth quintic give nine coefficients of the M5-brane modified elliptic genus in string theory predicted by Gaiotto, Strominger and Yin, including its entire primitive polar part. Four geometric degrees determine the candidate in the prescribed modular space. We also construct a weight-26 period series on the complete hyperplane system and identify the contributions of twisted-cubic hulls and their point modifications on both sides.

title: MixReact: Physics-Based Reactive Humanoid Control from Multimodal Cues via a Discrete-Continuous Mixture of Transformers
abstract: Humanoid agents in everyday environments are expected to react to diverse cues as humans do, with semantically appropriate and physically executable behaviors. Existing cue-driven reaction generation methods support only a narrow range of cue modalities and are limited to purely kinematic generation, leaving the resulting reactions susceptible to physical artifacts. To this end, we present MixReact, the first unified framework for physics-based reactive humanoid control from text, audio, and video cues, integrating a Discrete--Continuous Mixture of Transformers (DisCo-MoT) for state prediction with a History-aware Action Transformer (HAT) for physical execution. DisCo-MoT couples a discrete masked-modeling branch with a continuous autoregressive diffusion branch via one-way mixture attention within a MoT architecture. Guidance from discrete context mitigates collapse into averaged behaviors in one-to-many reaction generation, while direct prediction in continuous state space bypasses the decoding bottleneck of discrete representations. HAT then maps the predicted next state and observed execution history to executable actions, enabling robust closed-loop control in physics-based simulation. Experiments across all three modalities demonstrate consistent improvements over the baselines in fidelity, diversity, and physical consistency, while ablations validate the complementary contributions of the components. Our code will be released to facilitate future research. Project page: https://binlee26.github.io/MixReact_Page/

title: CAVQS: Context-Aware Variational Quantum Circuit Synthesis via Unitary Redistribution and Dynamic Reconstruction
abstract: Variational quantum circuit synthesis jointly searches circuit structure and continuous parameters to reduce costly two-qubit gates, but block-based workflows typically instantiate blocks independently, limiting simplification across block boundaries. Moreover, fully unitary synthesis does not exploit opportunities created by permitted output measurements and classical feedforward. We present CAVQS, a context-aware variational synthesis framework that combines unitary redistribution and dynamic reconstruction. First, CAVQS uses QR decomposition to transfer unitary factors between overlapping blocks, preserving the overall transformation while reshaping local synthesis targets to enable cross-block reductions. Second, for blocks that precede permitted terminal measurements, CAVQS constructs ancilla-free dynamic implementations with a CNOT-budgeted pre-measurement search and analytic branch-unitary construction, thereby minimizing expected CNOT cost. Across random-circuit targets, CAVQS reduces mean two-qubit gate counts by 28.79%-42.52%, 2.05%-52.62%, and 30.51%-74.64% relative to QFAST, SQUANDER, and Fast-USYN, respectively, on common successful instances. On 4--6-qubit quantum algorithm benchmarks, the corresponding reductions are 27.27%-36.77%, 20.65%-69.10%, and 36.31%-71.88%, respectively.

title: Spherical Tessellation of Circular Arrays for Massive MIMO: Favourable Propagation Conditions and Spectral Design
abstract: Upper-mid-band XL-MIMO can exploit line-of-sight propagation, but periodic uniform cylindrical arrays may produce grating ridges. We analyse a spherically tessellated concentric circular antenna array with non-separable facet orientations. Under fixed normalised chord spacing and ideal facet visibility, we prove that user channels become asymptotically orthogonal and matched-filter SINR approaches the single-user SNR. Simulations confirm interference decay and SINR convergence. A spectral comparison shows that facet-normal diversity prevents the full-amplitude grating ridges of the cylindrical baseline, with the inter-facet residual decaying with array size.

title: Sightline: Calibrated Data-Flow Summaries for LLM-Integrated Applications
abstract: Programs increasingly call large language models (LLMs), filling prompt placeholders with program values and consuming the output. Such a call crosses the boundary between natural language and programming language (NL/PL). To follow data across it, an analysis needs a data-flow summary of which placeholders the output uses, but no code describes what the model does. Analyses of these LLM-integrated applications therefore taint every output with every input, creating spurious flows, or ask a second model to label each call, which is costly. We prove, and mechanize in Lean 4, that a placeholder flows to the output of a transformer, to first order, only through the attention that reads it (no reading, no flow), and that a faint reading or sensitivity cannot certify that a placeholder does not flow. Unlike reading, the log-probability gradients and Fisher signals of existing methods vanish on confident outputs, and single-span removal fails on duplicated content. Our tool, Sightline, reads a recorded call in one forward pass, learns from labels which reads are uses, and calibrates the pruning to miss at most a chosen fraction $α$ of true flows, on average over call sites, when deployment is exchangeable with calibration. On 2,103 unseen repository families and four models, Sightline is the most accurate summary against the seven closest methods and a hidden-state probe. Calibrated at $α$ = 1%, it misses about 1% of true flows and prunes 43.9-65.6% of spurious flows, 1.6 to 2.6 times as many as the best baseline, and still 43.8-60.1% when calibrated on another collection. Through an open surrogate, it reads models treated as closed about as accurately as they read themselves, without their labels. In the information-flow control of an LLM agent, it removes about half of the labels from inputs that do not flow.

title: The gravitational wave candidate S251112cm: near-complete optical coverage with ATLAS, Pan-STARRS and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory
abstract: On 2025 November 12, the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) network detected S251112cm, a compact binary merger candidate with a false alarm rate of one per four years at a luminosity distance of $93 \pm 27$ Mpc. The probability that the lighter component's mass lies below 1 $M_\odot$ is >99%, while the probability that either component lies at 1-3 $M_\odot$ is only 8%, leaving the nature of the progenitor system unclear. We present Pan-STARRS and ATLAS optical follow-up of the 90% localisation region, and quantify Vera C. Rubin Observatory target-of-opportunity observations. In the North, Pan-STARRS imaged 1084 deg$^2$ (65%) within 7 days to a median depth of 21.9 mag and ATLAS 1545 deg$^2$ (87%) within 14 days to 19.3 mag across both hemispheres; in the South, Rubin covered 849 deg$^2$ (36%) 2-10 days post-merger to median depths of 24.5 ($g$) and 23.5 ($i$) mag. They reported 173, 93 and 67 candidates respectively (269 unique), which we assess against AT 2017gfo-like kilonova and SN 1998bw-like broad-lined Type Ic supernova models using prior activity, host luminosity distance, photometric evolution and absolute magnitude. Eight survive, mainly for lack of distance information. Six of these lie in hosts fainter than any in a volume-limited comparison sample, suggesting they are background sources. AT 2025aimy declines too slowly for the AT 2017gfo-like model, and a VLT host spectrum places AT 2025alqe outside the LVK volume, leaving no convincing counterpart candidates. Pan-STARRS and Rubin together exclude both models in $\sim$80% of the 90% localisation volume: the deepest wide-area constraint on a subsolar-mass merger to date and, to our knowledge, the most complete optical coverage of a significant subsolar-mass candidate.

title: Resonant filling for long-pulse operation of EuXFEL using iterative learning based feed forward
abstract: A future operation scenario of the European XFEL (EuXFEL) is long-pulse (LP) mode, where the 800 superconducting radio frequency (SRF) cavities of the linac are energized with RF pulse lengths of up to 500ms. Compared to the current, short-pulse (SP) mode with less than 2ms, the dominant mechanical eigenmodes of the cavities at a few hundred Hertz pose a significant control challenge, as the RF pulse extends beyond a multiple of their periods. To improve energy efficiency of LP operation, cavities are operated at bandwidths in the range of tens of Hertz, a factor of 10 narrower than in SP. Due to peak power limitation of the proposed high power amplifiers, even the fill time surpasses mechanical mode periods. This paper presents experimental evaluation of two feed forward adaptation approaches to facilitate resonant-filling despite mechanical mode transients: In a single-cavity regulation setup, the RF drive phase is adjusted to match the Lorentz force detuning induced cavity phase shift. In vector-sum RF regulation systems, the incident phase cannot be adjusted to each cavity individually, so the concept is inverted by adapting mechanical cavity tuner drives to match each individual cavity resonance trajectory with a fixed common RF drive phase.

title: Obvious group manipulations in voting
abstract: We study obvious group manipulation in voting and characterize it as manipulation identifiable from a coalition's option sets alone. Our analysis focuses on two overlapping classes: tops-only rules and rules satisfying the majority criterion, including all Condorcet-consistent rules. On the universal domain with at least three alternatives, a tops-only rule is not obviously manipulable by groups (NOMG) if and only if it is dictatorial. For rules satisfying the majority criterion, NOMG is impossible when $n,m\geq3$, except with four voters and three alternatives. We quantify the coalition sizes behind these restrictions, obtaining sharp bounds for efficient tops-only rules and an exact threshold for majority-criterion rules with odd electorates. In the exceptional configuration, we characterize an interval of NOMG scoring rules containing Borda, which is also Condorcet consistent there. We further characterize NOMG with two alternatives and apply our tops-only characterization to generalized median voter schemes and voting by committees.

title: Sourcing vector perturbations in warm inflation through shear viscous effects
abstract: Vector modes are generally believed not to play a significant role in standard cosmological perturbation theory because they decay rapidly. Non-equilibrium dynamics in the radiation bath present during warm inflation can lead to shear viscous effects, requiring a description beyond the perfect-fluid approximation. We adopt the fluctuating hydrodynamic approach to account for stochastic anisotropic stress related to shear viscosity. We show that the vector mode obeys a constrained Langevin equation in an inflationary background. The resulting power spectrum, considered in the weak-viscosity regime, is proportional to the shear viscosity and it also depends on the Hubble slow-roll parameter $ε$, decaying approximately as $a^{-(1-ε)}$. This behaviour is significantly slower than the unsourced, non-viscous power spectrum, which decays as $a^{-4}$. The continuously sourced vector modes, nevertheless, decay on superhorizon scales, and the illustrative benchmark parameter choices adopted in our numerical examples give a negligible late-time vector-to-scalar ratio. Despite the absence of direct large-scale observable vector signatures, the main results establish a source of vector perturbations during warm inflation and provide a framework for studying possible secondary effects along with large-scale white noises in the vector channel.

title: The existence of generalized Steiner systems
abstract: A generalized Steiner system $GS(t,w,n,q)$ is a $q$-ary constant-weight code of length $n$ and weight $w$ that has minimum distance at least $2(w-t)+1$ and attains the Johnson-type upper bound $(q-1)^t\binom nt/\binom wt$. For strengths $t=1$ and $t=2$, such systems were known to exist for all sufficiently large lengths satisfying the necessary divisibility conditions. For general fixed parameters, Liu and Shangguan (J. Combin.\ Theory Ser.~A 209 (2025), 105955) proved that the Johnson-type bound is attained asymptotically, and asked whether it is attained with equality for all sufficiently large lengths satisfying these conditions. We answer this question affirmatively. We prove that, for fixed integers $q\geq3$ and $w>t\geq1$, a $GS(t,w,n,q)$ exists for every sufficiently large $n$ such that $\binom{w-i}{t-i}$ divides $(q-1)^{t-i}\binom{n-i}{t-i}$ for all $0\leq i<t$. Moreover, the system can be chosen so that the supports of distinct codewords intersect in at most $t$ coordinates. Our proof assigns an independent random labelling to every set of $t+1$ coordinates, which turns large support intersections into conflicts in an exact covering problem, and then applies Keevash's decomposition theorem for labelled complexes.

title: Federated Learning for Unmanned Aerial Systems: A Screened Bibliometric Census of an Emergent Sub-Literature
abstract: We census the literature at the intersection of federated learning (FL) and unmanned aerial systems (UAS) with a broad Scopus query that combines FL, UAV, and delivery/logistics terms (Computer Science and Engineering, 2022--2026). The export holds \textbf{14,965 records}, but only \textbf{7.9\%} of the 14,945 unique records mention both an FL term and a UAV term in title, abstract, or author keywords. That screen leaves \textbf{1,185 records}: 90 in 2022, 361 in 2025, and 332 already indexed for 2026. The screened share of each year's raw output stays near 7.5\%, so the growth is not an artefact of the screen. Term-definition, document-type, and complete-year checks leave the leading venue (\emph{IEEE Internet of Things Journal}, 111 papers, $h{=}30$) and the leading country (China, 628 affiliation instances) unchanged. A manual read of 30 records finds 14 of 26 full papers (54\%, 95\% CI 35--71\%) substantively about FL for UAVs, so the corpus counts keyword co-occurrence, not only focused work. Counting authors by Scopus ID gives 4,095 authors with Lotka exponent $n{=}3.15$ ($R^2{=}0.996$); name strings would merge distinct people and understate the author count by 31\%. An OpenAlex export under the same screen yields 147 records, 74\% of them in the Scopus corpus, but the two exports are not matched populations, so we do not read the volume gap as coverage alone. Finally, of 228 records with a delivery-adjacent term, only 5 (2.2\%) mention \emph{parcel}, \emph{last-mile}, or \emph{courier} (14, or 6.1\%, if \emph{package} counts); the rest reflect transportation, traffic, and generic-logistics idiom. Keyword screening alone therefore cannot isolate last-mile drone-delivery research from the surrounding UAV-networking literature.

title: Attention Head Specialization: Phase Transitions in Sample Complexity
abstract: Attention heads specialize into distinct functions during training, often emerging in stages together with sharp changes in model behavior. While this phenomenon has mostly been studied as a function of training time, we ask how head specialization depends on the amount of available training data. Empirically, we find that heads specialized to syntactic relations in BERT emerge as the dataset size increases. We then study this phenomenon in a solvable high-dimensional model of multi-head attention and establish that, in this model, head specialization is a genuine phase transition in sample complexity, corresponding to a non-analyticity in the test error and other observables. Depending on data structure and regularization, specialization can follow uninformative head differentiation or occur through a cascade of phase transitions that progressively recover weaker latent features, providing a statistical form of simplicity bias. Finally, we relate these statistical transitions to the stagewise emergence of specialized heads during online learning, disentangling statistical from dynamical origins of head specialization.

title: Sharp topological overlap in every dimension
abstract: For a positive integer $d$ let $c_d^{\mathrm{top}}$ (resp. $c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}$) be the maximum $c$ such that, for every continuous (resp. affine) map from the $n$-dimensional simplex $Δ^n$ to $\mathbb{R}^d$, some point of $\mathbb{R}^d$ lies in the images of at least $(c-o(1))\binom{n+1}{d+1}$ of the $d$-dimensional faces, as $n\to\infty$. We show that \[ c_d^{\mathrm{top}}=c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}=\frac{(d+1)!}{(d+1)^{d+1}}. \] The second equality confirms a conjecture of Bukh, Matoušek, and Nivasch, who established the upper bound. The proof was found by GPT-6 Astra, following the directions of the author.

title: Two powers, one scalar field: unified early and late dark energy
abstract: We investigate whether a single canonical scalar field can account for both early and late dark energy. We consider a double-power potential in which a steep positive-power term can generate an early peak in the scalar energy-density fraction, while an inverse-power term supports late-time acceleration. This evolution requires the steep term to dominate initially and become subdominant later. We test the model against cosmic microwave background (CMB) measurements, Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) baryon acoustic oscillations, and Pantheon+ supernova data, with the SH0ES host-distance calibration. Relative to flat $Λ$CDM, the data fit improves by $Δχ^2_{\rm data}=-6.90$, or $Δχ^2_{\rm objective}=-3.76$ when Gaussian parameter-prior penalties are included. The scalar-field model gives $H_0=69.53\pm0.26\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, compared with $68.45\pm0.24\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ in flat $Λ$CDM. This shift brings the inferred expansion rate closer to the SH0ES measurement, but does not resolve the discrepancy significantly.

title: A sensitivity-constrained polynomial method for DQC1 query complexity
abstract: The polynomial method is one of the fundamental techniques for proving lower bounds on quantum query complexity, particularly in the BQP query model. In this work, we develop an analogue of the polynomial method for the DQC1 query model. We introduce the notion of {\em sensitivity approximate degree} for Boolean functions and show that it provides a lower bound on DQC1 query complexity. We establish several basic structural properties of this new measure. As a first result, we show that every nonconstant total Boolean function on $N$ input variables has sensitivity approximate degree $Ω(N)$, and hence requires $Ω(N)$ queries in the DQC1 model. Thus, unlike in the BQP query model, DQC1 admits no asymptotic query speedup for total Boolean functions. For symmetric partial Boolean functions, we give a complete characterization of the sensitivity approximate degree in terms of the separation between oppositely labeled Hamming weight layers. This yields a tight quadratic separation between sensitivity approximate degree and standard approximate degree, and also leads to tight quadratic separations between DQC1 and BQP query complexities. We further establish quantitative average-case classical simulation theorems for DQC1 algorithms. Finally, we apply our framework to Fourier analysis, obtaining a simple proof of an $Ω(N^{1/4})$ DQC1 query lower bound for the 2-Forrelation problem.

title: Time Series Structure Learning with Local Causal Parent Discovery
abstract: Learning and inference on time series can pose significant statistical challenges, including autocorrelated observations, distribution shift over time, and the curse of dimensionality. These challenges complicate the practical application of causal discovery algorithms, which already suffer from high computational and sample complexity in the general case. To mitigate these issues, this work introduces Iterative Temporal Parent Discovery (ITPD): a sound and complete constraint-based procedure for causal structure learning on multivariate time series with causal nonstationarity. ITPD takes a local-to-global learning approach that discovers the global graph by sequentially discovering the parent set for each variable. ITPD exploits temporal structural priors, graph partitioning, and the local Markov condition to swap higher-order conditional independence tests for lower-order alternatives. With an exact oracle, ITPD performed the least number of tests and used the smallest average conditioning set sizes relative to baselines. In benchmarking simulations, ITPD sat on the Pareto frontier with respect to F1 and wall-clock time and was faster than baselines on large graphs ($\geq$ 1000 nodes). For graphs with 2000 nodes, ITPD ran $2.3\times$, $9.1\times$, and $40.9\times$ faster than iterative IAMB, DF-PC, and PCMCI, respectively.

title: Triplet adiabatic potential energy surfaces for the O($^3$P) + C$_2$(X$^1Σ_g^+$, a$^3Π_u$) reaction and quasiclassical trajectory dynamics
abstract: We present three global adiabatic potential energy surfaces (PESs) for the O($^3$P) + C$_2$(X $^1Σ_g^+$, a $^3Π_u$) to CO(X$^1Σ^+$) + C($^3$P) reaction, computed at the icMRCI+Q/aug-cc-pVTZ level. This reaction is relevant to combustion chemistry, atmospheric processes, and astrochemistry. Since the energy difference between the $^1Σ_g^+$ and $^3Π_u$ states of C$_2$ is smaller than the zero-point energy, both states mix upon interaction with the approaching O atom. Consequently, the PESs exhibit a double-well topography in the reactant valley. Beyond this feature, the three PESs display markedly different topographies. The 1 $^3A''$ PES features a deep minimum 7.16 eV below the O + C$_2$ entrance channel. In contrast, the 2 $^3A''$ and 1 $^3A'$ surfaces possess shallower collinear wells ($\approx$ 5.7 eV) and strong angular anisotropy arising from avoided crossings with higher-lying triplet states. The analytical fits reproduce the \textit{ab initio} data with root-mean-square (RMS) deviations of 0.022--0.028 eV over an energy interval exceeding 13 eV. Quasiclassical trajectory (QCT) calculations reveal higher reactivity on the barrierless $1\,^3A''$ surface compared to the $2\,^3A''$ PES, where an angle-dependent entrance barrier reduces the cross sections. Furthermore, cross sections for reactions initiated from C$_2$(X $^1Σ_g^+$) and C$_2$(a $^3Π_u$) are remarkably similar for the three PESs, regardless of the initial rovibrational state.

title: Attention Drift Regularization with Adaptive Initialization for Domain-Robust Visual Recognition
abstract: Source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) adapts a pretrained source model to unlabeled target domains without source data access, yet two critical failure modes remain unaddressed. First, attention drift: source-learned attention maps shift toward spurious or background features under distribution shift, destabilizing feature representations. Second, domain-gap-agnostic initialization: applying a single fixed source model uniformly across all target domains ignores domain gap severity, causing premature overfitting to noisy pseudo-labels under large shifts. We propose DGA-CAFC to address both failures. The Counterfactual Attention-based Feature Consistency (CAFC) module enforces feature stability by minimizing the discrepancy between representations computed under learned attention and those under counterfactual-inspired normalized perturbations, thereby promoting domain-robust features independent of spurious attention shifts. The Domain-Gap Aware Source Model Selection (DGASS) module estimates domain gap severity via target prediction entropy and selects the source model variant whose confidence level best matches the estimated gap, reducing negative transfer and stabilizing pseudo-label quality. Crucially, CAFC transfers beyond SFDA: applied as a lightweight regularizer to standard domain generalization objectives without target data. Extensive experiments across SFDA and DG benchmarks demonstrate that our method consistently improves over recent baselines, demonstrating the effectiveness and generality of the proposed framework. Project page is available at https://visdomlab.github.io/DGA_CAFC

title: Physics-Informed Feature Representations and Pretrained Tabular Foundation Models for Generalizable Melt Pool Geometry Prediction
abstract: Developing generalizable, data-efficient machine learning (ML) models for advanced manufacturing remains challenging because experimental datasets are limited and process-property relationships vary across materials and operating conditions. In laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), melt pool width, depth, and melting mode (conduction, transition, or keyhole) govern process stability and defect formation. Conventional ML models typically use dimensional process parameters, which represent laser-material interactions only implicitly and may limit cross-material transfer. This study evaluates whether two physics-informed dimensionless features, normalized enthalpy and Peclet number, combining laser processing conditions with material thermophysical properties, improve melt pool prediction over raw process parameters. We systematically benchmark seven models: four classical ML methods (Gaussian process, support vector machine, random forest, and XGBoost) and three pretrained tabular foundation models (TabPFN, TabDPT, and TabICLv2). Experiments span 316L stainless steel, IN625, IN718, and combined-material datasets, covering regression of melt pool width and depth and classification of melting modes. Dimensionless features yield comparable or superior predictive performance in most settings, with the largest gains in cross-material depth prediction (R^2 = 0.96). Tabular foundation models generally achieve stronger classification performance than classical baselines, particularly for multi-material datasets. These findings indicate that combining physically meaningful dimensionless representations with pretrained tabular models can improve data-efficient melt pool modeling and support more transferable process-window identification in LPBF.

title: Flux-induced condensation in a radial geometry
abstract: Stirring and shear usually suppress phase separation, but transport through a boundary can induce it. We study a binary mixture that is stable everywhere at rest and fills a two-dimensional annulus. The inner boundary is semipermeable and exchanges material with a permeate held at a fixed chemical potential, so that a steady flux of one component crosses the annulus. Although this driven system carries a steady current and produces entropy, within Model B dynamics its steady state is an equilibrium profile in an effective external field that is logarithmic in the distance from the center.
