As an application, we establish that, under suitable assumptions, every nonlinear generalized skew Lie \(n\)-derivation \(G:\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{A}\) admits a standard form $G(X)=ZX+D(X),$ where \(Z\in\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})\) and \(D:\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{A}\) is an additive \(\ast\)-derivation. Finally, we apply this result to several important classes of unital \(\ast\)-algebras, including unital prime \(\ast\)-algebras, standard operator algebras, and von Neumann algebras.

title: Extremal Ky Fan $p$-$k$ norms of graphs
abstract: We study a two-parameter extension of Nikiforov's extremal problems for graph norms, focusing on the quantity $$ S_{p,k}(G) = \left(\sum_{i=1}^{k}σ_i(G)^p\right)^{1/p}, $$ where $p\ge1$, and $σ_1(G) \ge \cdots \ge σ_n(G)$ are the singular values of the adjacency matrix of an $n$-vertex graph $G$. This quantity provides a common generalization of the Ky Fan $k$-norm and the Schatten $p$-norm, which correspond to the cases $p=1$ and $k=n$, respectively. We establish upper and lower bounds and characterize extremal and near-extremal graphs within specified parameter ranges. For each fixed $k \ge 4$, we determine an explicit exponent $\vartheta_k \in [1,2)$ such that the balanced complete $k$-partite graph is the unique maximizer for all sufficiently large orders, and we characterize the unique graph attaining the second-largest value. In particular, this determines the maximum Ky Fan $4$-norm for all sufficiently large orders. At these exponents, any maximizer with a fixed edge deficit from the Turán graph's edge count belongs to an explicit finite family of complete $k$-partite graphs (whenever such a realization exists), whereas a fixed edge surplus is uniquely maximized by adding a star inside a largest part of the balanced graph. Furthermore, we quantify the relation between small absolute norm deficits and graph structure, demonstrating that relative near-optimality alone does not guarantee structural proximity. We also obtain a vertex-partition lower bound featuring an optimal universal remainder coefficient and complete equality conditions. These results provide structural answers to Nikiforov's norm questions in the two-parameter setting, linking extremal values to uniqueness, prescribed edge counts, and the structure of near-extremal graphs.

title: VerifiQuant: Governance-by-Execution for Financial LLM Workflows
abstract: Large language models embedded in financial workflows fail most dangerously by emitting confident, well-formatted but wrong numbers with no signal distinguishing them from correct ones. We argue that the central deployment problem is governability: a system must determine when a question supports a numeric answer and when it should instead clarify, intercept, or refuse. We present VerifiQuant, a governance-by-execution framework that packages financial logic into inference contracts and evaluates each query through an executable diagnostic funnel before deterministic computation. This separation makes computation, clarification, and refusal structured and auditable while keeping financial arithmetic outside the language model. Against matched retrieval-and-execution baselines, and within a declared contract library, the principal benefit is not higher accuracy on well-posed questions but safer behavior when an input does not justify a number. When it finds no applicable contract, it says so instead of guessing. Coverage sweeps and failure analysis put a price on this boundary: safety is bought with coverage rather than with accuracy, and residual failures remain attributable to specific runtime frontiers.

title: The Manhattan cospectrality of the cocktail party graph
abstract: For a graph $G$ of order $N$ with adjacency eigenvalues $λ_{1}(G)\geq \cdots\geqλ_{N}(G),$ the cospectrality of $G$ is the smallest value of $\sum_{i}\left\vert λ_{i}(G)-λ_{i}(H)\right\vert $ over all graphs $H$ of order $N$ not isomorphic to $G.$ Abdollahi and Zakeri (Ars Math. Contemp. 22(1) (2022) P1.06) conjectured that the cospectrality of the cocktail party graph $CP_{n}$ is attained exactly at the graph $H_{n}.$ This graph is obtained from $K_{1,2,\ldots,2}$ by attaching a pendant vertex to the vertex of the part of size one. We prove this conjecture for every $n\geq2$ by showing that only three explicit graphs (two for $n=2$) are at distance less than $2$ from $CP_{n}.$ We work with the complement of a competing graph. First we remove its components $K_{2}.$ Then we treat the case in which its main component has a dominating vertex. The remaining cases are reduced to finitely many small graphs. The proof is computer-assisted, and all computations concern explicit finite lists of graphs.

title: Integrated Stress Responses and ABCB11 Repression in Drug-Exposed Human Hepatocytes
abstract: Drug-safety information systems must distinguish direct bile salt export pump (BSEP) inhibition from transcriptional changes in hepatic transport programs. We investigated whether repression of ABCB11, which encodes BSEP, tracks an integrated stress response (ISR) after accounting for dose and liver-identity proxies. We analyzed 197 human hepatocyte RNA-seq dose conditions for 50 compounds using compound-centered models and 2,000 compound-bootstrap resamples. The association remained negative after dose and 436-gene identity adjustment ($β=-0.288$; 95\% interval, $-0.416$ to $-0.127$), and after jointly adding global-expression, oxidative-stress and apoptosis scores ($β=-0.198$; $-0.342$ to $-0.039$). The adjusted partial correlation ($r=-0.422$) exceeded in absolute magnitude those obtained for all but 1 of 5,000 expression-matched and 16 of 5,000 expression- and variance-matched random six-gene sets. Several comparator transporters also declined, indicating that the association was not restricted to ABCB11. Adding an interpolated source-screen viability proxy to all controls retained a negative estimate but an interval including zero ($β=-0.190$; $-0.335$ to $0.009$; 152 conditions, 39 compounds). Exposure-restricted uncertainty likewise depended on identity adjustment. Published modules from 240 external microarray conditions for 80 perturbagens showed consistent stress--metabolic covariation, without gene-level replication. A separate assay/FDA audit exposed sparse joint coverage and source-dependent associations. Together, these analyses link hepatocyte stress to ABCB11 repression and provide a biologically grounded approach to integrating biochemical, transcriptional and regulatory evidence for drug-safety assessment.

title: Distributional Deep Hedging
abstract: Deep hedging learns a hedging strategy by optimising a risk preference over a neural-network policy. The preference is fixed before training, so each new preference requires a new policy and, in actor-critic methods, a new critic. We propose distributional deep hedging, in which the distribution of the hedging profit and loss is learned through its quantiles and the risk preference is applied afterwards, as a weight on those quantiles. We characterise the preferences that admit this representation, which include expected shortfall and its mixtures, and show that the entropic utility is computed from the same quantiles. At the current policy, each of these preferences is bounded below by an expected utility with the same gradient. This bound reduces risk-sensitive hedging to a sequence of risk-neutral problems, from which we derive policy-search and actor-critic algorithms. In numerical experiments, the learned hedges approach references computed by dynamic programming, and a single distributional critic trained without a preference can serve preferences chosen after training.

title: Detour different-distance sets in graphs
abstract: The detour distance $D(u,v)$ between two vertices of a connected graph is the length of a longest $u,v$-path. A set $S$ of vertices is a detour different-distance set if no vertex outside $S$ has the same detour distance to two vertices of $S$. We study the lower and upper detour different-distance numbers $\mathrm{dd}_D(G)$ and $\mathrm{DD}_D(G)$, the smallest and largest orders of maximal such sets; this is the detour analogue of the different-distance sets of Hedetniemi, Hedetniemi, Laskar and Mulder. The two notions coincide on trees, cycles, complete bipartite graphs and the Petersen graph, but differ in general: for instance, detour different-distance sets may contain triangles or induce $4$-cycles. We determine both numbers for many families, among them wheels, fans, windmills, hypercubes, helms, flowers, books, ladders, prisms, Möbius ladders, crowns, gears, Dutch windmills and complete multipartite graphs, and for joins, coronas and lexicographic products. We prove that $\mathrm{DD}_D(G)$ is at most the detour diameter; that $\mathrm{DD}_D(G)=n-1$ if and only if $G$ is a path; that $\mathrm{dd}_D(G)=\mathrm{DD}_D(G)=1$ whenever two vertices are joined by Hamiltonian paths to all other vertices; that $\mathrm{dd}_D(G)=\mathrm{DD}_D(G)=2$ for Hamiltonian-laceable graphs and, more generally, for bipartite graphs in which each part contains two vertices whose detour distances to the other part are constant; and that $\mathrm{DD}_D(G)\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ for Hamiltonian graphs.

title: Local connectivity of Julia sets of Newton maps of trigonometric and hyperbolic functions
abstract: We study the Newton maps of $\sin z$, $\cos z$, $\sinh z$, and $\cosh z$, each of which is transcendental meromorphic and has infinitely many unbounded immediate attracting basins. We first verify directly that, for the cosine Newton map $N_{\cos}(z) = z + \cot z$, the half-planes $\{\pm \operatorname{Im} z > M\}$ are repelling petals at infinity for every $M \ge 2$. These explicit petals allow us to apply the tame-basin criterion of Barański, Fagella, Jarque, and Karpińska and obtain local connectivity of the spherical boundary of each immediate basin of $N_{\cos}$. We also show that the Newton map of $Ae^{λz} + Be^{-λz}$, where $ABλ\neq 0$, is affinely conjugate to the sine Newton map $N_{\sin}(z) = z - \tan z$. The published local-connectivity theorem for $J(N_{\sin})$ therefore applies to this entire family, including the cosine and the two hyperbolic Newton maps. We describe the invariant lines and basin geometry of the four maps and illustrate the corresponding dynamical planes numerically.

title: Local cohomology module with infinitely many associated primes over ramified regular local rings of the least possible dimensions
abstract: In \cite{Ma} we have observed the example of local cohomology module with infinitely many associated primes over a 12 dimensional ramified regular local ring. In this paper we construct examples of local cohomology modules with infinitely many associated primes over ramified regular local rings of two different ring dimensions. The result of this paper is very much dependent on the result (\cite{SS}, Theorem 2.6).

title: Computing Weighted Set Covers with Heterogeneous Stochastic Oracles: Deadline-Constrained Token Complexity
abstract: We study computation in which a probabilistic Turing machine (PTM) uses AI systems, abstracted as heterogeneous stochastic oracles (HSOs), to solve Weighted Set Cover. A pilot study shows that an LLM can outperform weighted greedy. HSOs differ in capabilities, response distributions, latencies, and token costs. We study how the PTM selects HSOs to obtain, by a deadline and with a required success probability, a full cover satisfying a prescribed weight threshold, and we analyze expected token cost. For queries requesting full covers, assuming independent call successes and uninformative failures, we characterize by linear programming the minimum expected token cost for every feasible success probability. An optimal policy randomizes over at most two preselected sequences of oracle batches. Among policies attaining maximum success probability, the expected cost reduction of two-batch selection relative to querying all oracles in one batch is nonnegative and submodular. We construct an FPTAS for near-optimal cost reduction under heterogeneous response-time bounds. Computing an optimal two-batch selection is NP-hard but admits a pseudopolynomial algorithm for positive integral expected token costs. For partial-cover responses, the PTM combines returned sets across batches and turns. Once their union covers the universe, it verifies total weight directly or obtains a guarantee from LP-dual tests on retained partial covers. We give one-turn probability, token-cost, and hardness results and adaptive token-cost bounds under per-batch assumptions. A constructed instance shows that residual-guided querying can reduce expected token cost by a factor linear in the number of possible residual subproblems.

title: BitPrefill: W1.58A4 Tensor-Core Acceleration for Compute-Bound LLM Prefill
abstract: Low-bit quantization reduces large language model (LLM) inference cost, yet implementations optimized for memory-bound decode can leave compute-bound prefill on BF16 tensor cores. This gap matters for input-heavy workloads, including long-context and multimodal applications, where prefill can account for a substantial fraction of inference latency. We propose a W1.58A4 operator that quantizes weights to ternary values and activations to 4-bit, while executing the linear projection on native INT4 general matrix multiply (GEMM) tensor cores, turning prefill from a full-precision matrix multiply into a low-bit one. We deploy the operator for BitNet-b1.58 on a single RTX 4090 and a Jetson Orin Nano edge device, and report GEMM-kernel latency, end-to-end LLMs prefill latency, and task accuracy against bf16 and BitNet/BitBLAS baselines. Our proposed kernel achieves ~1.42x acceleration compared to the original BF16 prefill phase, with negligible reduction on model accuracy.

title: Analytical Modeling of Thermal Shield-Induced Tilt Noise in Lunar Regolith: Constraints on Future Lunar Seismometers and Gravitational waves Detectors
abstract: Surface features such as thermal shields, insulating blankets, and exposed rocks modify the absorption of solar radiation in the lunar regolith, producing lateral temperature gradients missed by one-dimensional thermal models. These gradients cause thermoelastic deformation that tilts surface-deployed seismic instruments, adding long-period noise. We develop an analytical framework, based on Hankel transforms in a semi-infinite regolith, that treats these features as perturbations to a laterally uniform diurnal thermal state; linearity allows multiple features to be superposed. The framework is applied to the Apollo 14 Passive Seismic Experiment, including the seismometer thermal shield and surrounding instruments. The Apollo shield is a multilayer insulation (MLI) blanket that passes a fraction of the solar-flux fluctuation to the ground. Near local noon the shadow of the instrument body shifts by 2-5 cm across this dimly lit ground. This asymmetry dominates the tilt; its median amplitude spectral density reaches 7-8 x 10^(-11) rad/sqrt(Hz) in the 1-5 mHz band, about three orders of magnitude above that of an opaque shield. Enlarging an opaque shield lowers the tilt, but the body-shadow tilt of an MLI shield does not decrease with shield radius. Thermal heterogeneity can thus generate a tilt bias, present even during seismically quiet intervals, that should be included in the noise budget of future lunar horizontal seismometers and inertial GW accelerometers, and the optical transmission of the shield and the instrument's own shadow can matter more than shield size. The analytical framework provides a computationally efficient way to evaluate thermal-shield geometry, albedo contrast, and instrument placement for future lunar seismic and inertial gravitational-wave sensor deployments.

title: Gravitational Wave Detection via Massive-Particle Interferometry
abstract: Gravitational-wave (GW) observations provide a powerful means of testing general relativity and exploring the physics of black holes and the early universe, motivating the development of complementary detection techniques. Here, we propose and theoretically investigate a GW detector based on massive-particle interferometry, in which the signal is encoded in the relative phase accumulated by a quantum particle traversing a closed-loop trajectory and a reference path. We derive the frequency-dependent GW-induced phase response and examine the parameters on which it depends. These parameters provide a means of tuning the detector response over a broad frequency range, motivating the exploration of tabletop detectors for GW signals at frequencies comparable to and below the LIGO band, in the idealized limit. By exploiting the trajectory-dependent gravitationally induced phase, the proposed scheme offers a distinct and potentially complementary approach to GW detection and motivates further investigation of its experimental feasibility and practical sensitivity.

title: An ALMA Survey of Molecular Gas in the Host Galaxies of Fast Radio Bursts
abstract: We present ALMA observations of CO(1-0) and CO(2-1) emission and millimeter continuum measurements for 9 localized fast radio burst (FRB) hosts at z=0.05-0.38. CO emission is significantly detected in 6 hosts and tentatively detected in one, yielding molecular gas masses of 2.2x10^8-1.0x10^10 Mo for a Milky Way CO-to-H2 conversion factor. All 6 detections show spatially resolved emission and large-scale velocity gradients, several consistent with ordered disk rotation. FRB positions do not necessarily coincide with the brightest CO emission, and no distinct kinematic component is identified at the burst positions at the present kpc-scale resolution. Together with published data, we assemble the largest FRB-host sample with CO measurements or upper limits to date. CO-detected hosts tend to have larger molecular gas reservoirs and longer depletion times than stellar-mass- and star-formation-rate-matched xCOLD GASS galaxies. They also tend to have higher molecular gas fractions and longer depletion times than expected from molecular-gas scaling relations. However, survival analyses including non-detections do not establish a significant difference in molecular gas mass or gas fraction. Both hosts detected in CO and HI have molecular-to-atomic mass ratios within the broad scatter of comparison galaxies. Our results highlight diverse cold-gas environments rather than a uniformly molecular-gas-rich FRB host population. At the position of the repeating FRB20201124A, the measured 98 GHz continuum flux density is above the predicted star-formation contribution and lies at the lower end of or below an extrapolation of the VLA spectrum. These results allow a compact persistent-source contribution and a possible spectral turnover between centimeter and millimeter wavelengths, although the present sensitivity and resolution prevent a firm separation from surrounding star-forming emission.

title: Möbius expansion and pointwise energy transfer over arbitrary fields
abstract: Let $F$ be a field of positive characteristic $p$, and let $A\subset F^\times$ have $N$ elements. We prove that, for every $λ\in F^\times$, \[ \card{A+λA^{-1}}\gg\min\{N^{10/9},(pN^2)^{1/3}\}. \] This improves the exponent $31/30$ to $10/9$ in the common small-set range. Over prime fields the bound strengthens to $\min\{N^{10/9},(pN)^{1/2}\}$. Analogous bounds hold for $Af(A)$ when $f$ is a Möbius transformation satisfying the stated nondegeneracy conditions. In characteristic zero, the bound $N^{10/9}$ remains valid. No subfield-avoidance condition is required.

title: Detection of GRB 261010A with GRID-11B
abstract: We report GRID-11B observations of the main emission episode of GRB 261010A. We measure $T_{90}=5.68^{+1.04}_{-0.32}$ s and a minimum variability timescale of $51.6^{+10.5}_{-9.8}$ ms. Its spectrum is described by a cutoff power law with $E_{\rm p}=1089^{+171}_{-80}$ keV. At both candidate host redshifts ($z=0.070$ and $0.785$), the low $\varepsilon$ values and their positions relative to the Amati relation suggest Type-I-like properties. These properties, despite the long duration, resemble those of GRB 211211A and motivate investigation of a possible compact-object merger origin.

title: Adding One More Agent: How AI Team Size and Formation Shape Productivity and Diversity in Human-AI Brainstorming Teams
abstract: Generative AI has improved individual productivity, but whether adding a plurality of AI partners helps or hurts remains open. We crossed AI partnership (one versus two) with behavioral formation (calibrated to average human behavior versus customized by the participant) in a brainstorming experiment ($N$=168) with human-human dyads as reference. Two-AI rooms posted more ideas to the shared board, but human-authored ideas dropped substantially. With one AI partner, formation mattered: humans paired with an average-calibrated AI posted more than any other condition. With two, this effect vanished. Humans continued talking but converted fewer ideas into board posts. AI social talk predicted more human posts, while AI posting volume predicted fewer. AI presence increased global diversity of human-authored ideas, but only a second AI increased within-session differentiation. The number of AI partners and their formation can reshape what the human contributes; single-agent results do not generalize to multi-agent teams.

title: Eigenvalues and Resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck Operator in the Large-Friction Limit
abstract: We study the eigenvalues and resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator by the methods of analytic dilation and phase-space deformation. We prove that in the large-friction limit $γ\to+\infty$, there are neither eigenvalues nor resonances away from the thresholds $γN$, and that near each threshold $γk$, there exists a bijection between the eigenvalues and resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator and those of the Witten Laplacian at the level $k$, $-Δ_V^{(k)}=-Δ_V\otimes 1_{μ_k}-dΓ_k(\operatorname{Hess}V)$. We also show that each negative eigenvalue of $-Δ_V^{(k)}$, $k\geq 1$, produces a pole of the resolvent at distance of order $γ^{-1}$ below $γk$, whose imaginary part is $O(e^{-cγ})$ for every $c<2δ_V$. Here $δ_V$ is the width of a strip of analyticity of $V$.

title: Testing Settlement Flags after Late Evidence and Process Restart
abstract: A settlement flag can survive an application restart while the economic effects remain ambiguous. We define a contract linking the fixed plan, source admission at two cutoffs, identity-keyed ledger effects and post-invocation state. We generated 504 synthetic histories, ran each through a file implementation and a separately coded SQLite implementation, and observed 672 controlled process exits. The file implementation missed 54 same-identity payment-date conflicts, including 27 that credited cash early, and a monitor using run flags, artifact presence and purchase counts accepted all 54. The same contract distinguishes a purchase awaiting closure from a correct quote wait for a single writer on a running kernel and filesystem.

title: Which Archived Results Survive a Rule Change? A Case Study in Revalidating Decisions
abstract: A research workflow can retain a correct numerical result after the evidence or approval that supported its use has expired. Common incremental build methods identify reusable computations, while deciding what remains usable also requires knowing which policy justified each approval. We examined a recorded parser migration across 312 paired research records, replayed both parsers with the same inputs, applied a calculation-file omission to the complete cohort, and evaluated current proof in a GNU Make comparison. Treating the prior projections as current would change at least one field in 11 of 312 records, and controlled cases show that even matching values can lack a current proof. The study separates numerical recovery from applicable approval and sets out the conditions under which a maintained dependency graph can preserve both.

title: Stellar activity demotes GJ 9404 b to a planetary candidate
abstract: GJ 9404 is a nearby M dwarf ($d=23.8\,\text{pc}$), around which a $13.4586^{+0.0044}_{-0.0067}\,\text{d}$ planet has been claimed in a recent study using 54 publicly available HARPS-N radial velocities (RVs). We re-analyse the spectroscopy associated with this study, and carry out a joint modelling of: (i) stellar rotation in RV, FWHM, and Mount Wilson S-index through Gaussian processes; (ii) long-term trends in all physical quantities; (iii) planetary signals in RV. Current evidence supports the existence of planets in the period range $2-100\,\text{d}$ by at most $Δ\ln Z=-0.4$ for any considered stellar-activity model, which is insufficient for a widely accepted planet detection. Additional spectroscopy is necessary to accurately quantify the stellar activity of GJ 9404 and determine whether any RV signals warrant further attention.

title: How developers split roles among them and a coding agent and what "collaboration" means
abstract: Background: Coding agents such as Claude Code become more and more competent, so that their role in the development process can grow. Objective: How do developers characterize the role-split between them and their agent? How would they ideally want to collaborate with their agent? Methods: We perform a 3-step, mixed-methods study. We apply qualitative open coding to 2025 early adopters' blog articles; perform a quantitative survey of 2026 practitioners; develop and apply a method for coding-agent-supported open coding of survey freetext responses. Results: The 2025 practitioners have the agent work in supporting roles only. Accountability was firmly human. In 2026, both are fundamentally still true. Gradually, however, the role-split is now different, with much more agent involvement. The developers' notion of collaboration has three facets: Predominantly a separation into human-only, agent-only, and collaborative work steps, with defined conditions and goals. Second, accommodating personal preferences without engineering justification. Third, a holistic view of collaboration covering the entire development process. Conclusions: Defining one's role relative to the agent will need to be a recurring activity. The different views on collaboration are likely a source of friction and conflict for teams; future work should find out how to cope with that.

title: On the number of edge-disjoint $K_r$ in $K_{r+1}$-free graphs
abstract: Gy\H ori and Keszegh [\emph{Combinatorica} \textbf{37} (2017), 1113--1124] proved that every $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices with $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+k$ edges contains at least $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint triangles. We extend this result to cliques of arbitrary fixed order. Specifically, we prove that for every fixed integer $r\ge 3$ and all sufficiently large $n$, every $K_{r+1}$-free graph on $n$ vertices with $t_{r-1}(n)+k$ edges contains at least $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint copies of $K_r$, where $t_{r-1}(n)$ denotes the number of edges in the Turán graph $T_{r-1}(n)$. Moreover, equality holds if and only if $G$ is obtained from $T_{r-1}(n)$ by adding edges within one of its parts, with the added edges forming a triangle-free graph.

title: A Solvency II-Based Framework for Pricing Structural Longevity Risk under an Affine Mortality Model
abstract: This paper develops a Solvency II-based pricing framework for structural longevity risk in incomplete longevity markets. The valuation scheme relies on the Cost-of-Capital principle underlying the Risk Margin and combines it with a continuous-time affine mortality model. Mortality dynamics are specified in calendar time, with age-dependent mortality patterns linked to a latent longevity factor driving long-term mortality improvements. The affine structure preserves closed-form survival probabilities and provides a tractable basis for repeated Best Estimate, Solvency Capital Requirement and Risk Margin calculations. We derive the conditional distribution of one-year discounted Best Estimate variations, obtaining analytical expressions for their asymmetry and Value-at-Risk under the Gaussian affine specification. Within this setting, we introduce a stress-based assessment by applying adverse shocks to the deterministic parameters governing the longevity trend. The trend-based stress is compared with a mortality-level stress and with a Value-at-Risk-based capital assessment. The methodology links stochastic mortality modelling, prudential capital valuation and longevity-linked payoff assessment within a unified actuarial framework. A numerical application based on Belgian mortality data illustrates the implementation and shows that the mortality-level stress produces substantially larger scenario-based capital-cost measures than the trend-based stress. These findings highlight the sensitivity of longevity risk valuation to the specification of adverse mortality scenarios. The approach offers a transparent and operational basis for assessing and pricing structural longevity risk under a Solvency II Cost-of-Capital perspective.

title: On the loss landscape of the linear neural network: beyond critical points
abstract: While the critical points of the loss landscape in linear neural networks have been extensively studied since the seminal work of Baldi \& Hornik in the late 1980s, a description of this landscape at an intermediate or global scale is still lacking. Such a characterization is crucial, particularly as a substantial body of literature indicates that gradient descent circumvents critical points. The present article introduces an intermediate structure, termed the critical thalweg, which encompasses all critical points and exhibits key geometric properties. Beyond providing a geometric proof of Baldi \& Hornik's results using simpler assumptions than the existing literature, this framework offers a global view of the loss landscape that can be easily visualized in a two-dimensional plane. Empirical observations suggest that gradient descent is attracted toward the critical thalweg, along which the loss continues to decrease to its global minimum.

title: Cohomological $k$-Equivalence Does Not Capture Graph Isomorphism
abstract: Ó Conghaile introduced cohomological $k$-equivalence $\equiv^{\mathbb{Z}}_k$, a refinement of equivalence in $k$-variable counting logic that is decidable in polynomial time for each fixed $k$: the local isomorphisms that survive must extend, in both directions, to compatible families of integer combinations of local isomorphisms. He asked whether, for every finite relational signature $σ$, some $k$ makes $\equiv^{\mathbb{Z}}_k$ coincide with isomorphism of $σ$-structures (Question 14 of his MFCS 2022 paper). We show that the answer is negative already for graphs: for every $k\ge 1$ there are finite simple graphs $A_k\not\cong B_k$ with $A_k\equiv^{\mathbb{Z}}_k B_k$. Every isomorphism of the pair would induce a permutation $g$ of a common index set $D$. One part of the graphs, over $\mathbb{F}_3$, admits exactly the even permutations, because $g$ acts by its sign on a nonzero class in the cokernel of the unsigned boundary map on subsets of $D$. A second part, over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and built on the Johnson graph $J(|D|,2)$, admits exactly the odd permutations. No set of at most $k$ vertices detects the parity: every local isomorphism of a common family is realised, with the same images, by permutations of both parities. We complement the main result with three observations. For the pair built from an index set of size $n$, the least width at which cohomological equivalence distinguishes the two graphs is $\log_4 n+O(1)$; so within this construction the doubly exponential size is unavoidable. The pairs are nevertheless distinguished in polynomial time by an explicit invariant that combines the class of the part over $\mathbb{F}_3$ with the parity of the part over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Finally, cohomological $2$-equivalence already distinguishes the coloured graphs with which Berkholz and Grohe show that no level of the Diophantine relaxation decides isomorphism.

title: Error analysis for the numerical approximation of the quantile hedging problem
abstract: We analyse numerical approximations of quantile hedging in complete linear markets with Markovian diffusion dynamics. The problem is formulated as stochastic control for an augmented state $(X,P)$, where the probability martingale $P$ is constrained to $[0,1]$ and controlled through an unbounded volatility coefficient. We combine control truncation with piecewise-constant policy time-stepping (PCPT), stopping controls continuously upon boundary hitting to preserve the state constraint. Using one-step dynamic programming principles and regularisation, we derive a generator inequality and explicit value-function error bounds. Under standard coefficient regularity and a Lipschitz payoff, optimising the truncation and regularisation parameters yields an error exponent arbitrarily close to $1/8$ from below, uniformly in the probability variable. For controls bounded from the outset, we obtain exponents arbitrarily close to $1/4$ from below, approaching the exponent established by Jakobsen, Picarelli and Reisinger without state constraints. We also implement a fully discrete scheme with neural-network controls. Grid-time projection onto $[0,1]$ introduces a martingale defect and a pricing bias. We quantify this bias in a toy problem and mitigate it using a state-dependent control bound. Experiments in Black--Scholes and Lipschitz local-volatility models illustrate the correction and the decrease in pricing errors under grid refinement.

title: A unified closed-form theory for elastic waves in polycrystals of any crystal symmetry
abstract: The coherent elastic wave in random polycrystals is described by the first-order smoothing approximation, whose mass operator remains an integral evaluated only numerically. Here we derive its closed form for equiaxed, untextured polycrystals of any crystal symmetry with an exponential correlation function, giving an explicit dispersion equation at all frequencies. Unlike the integral form, which fails beyond one inverse correlation radius from the real axis, the closed form holds deep in the complex wavenumber plane, where heavily attenuated roots lie. It is compact, reproduces the dispersion equations of Stanke and Kino for cubic grains, extends them to any symmetry and contains the Born and far-field approximations as special cases. It reveals the structure of the roots and their partitions of the coherent field: three roots per polarization, one from the incident wave and one from each of the two scattering channels, without and with mode conversion. It also yields closed-form limits of their velocity, attenuation and partition in the Rayleigh, stochastic and geometric regimes, which show why a single coherent wave has been observed at long wavelengths, whereas more than one can be observed at short wavelengths. These results underpin further theory and quantitative characterization of polycrystalline microstructure.

title: Uniformising random greedy maximal independent sets on graphs with at most five vertices
abstract: A random greedy algorithm scans the vertices of a finite graph in increasing order of independent exponential arrival times and accepts each vertex unless an accepted neighbour blocks it. We ask an inverse question: can strictly positive finite arrival rates be chosen so that the terminal inclusion-maximal independent sets are all equally likely? We call this exact property exponential greedy uniformisability (EGU). We establish the complete small-order classification: every finite simple graph on at most five vertices is EGU, with the unique exception of the five-vertex path $P_5$ up to graph isomorphism. A strict $2\times2$ probability minor provides an explicit obstruction for the exceptional graph; the positive cases are certified by graph-isomorphism reduction and exact constructive witnesses. We explain the independent-exponential-clock probability law and the formal Lean 4 verification, registered as Palomar PALOMAR-2026-11-19-000021 (version 1). The registration is a formal proof record, not a claim of novelty certification or journal peer review.

title: One Behavior, Out of Order: Deterministic Execution and Parallel Simulation of ROS 2 Applications
abstract: System-level simulation is widely used to validate robotic applications before hardware deployment. However, Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2), a popular middleware for such applications, uses asynchronous publish-subscribe communication, which can make application behavior depend on scheduling and the platform. The behavior can then vary across runs and machines even with the same inputs. This nondeterminism makes faults hard to reproduce and tests unreliable. In this paper, we first give ROS 2 applications a lightweight coordination scheme in which every component, including event-driven ones, reads its inputs and writes its outputs at predefined time instants. By decoupling computation and communication, the scheme makes an application deterministic, that is, it always has one behavior for given inputs. Tests are thus repeatable, but for large applications they still take a long time. To speed up these tests, we then present an out-of-order parallel simulation algorithm. From the predefined read and write instants, it knows before the run which activations of components depend on which. It starts each activation as soon as those it depends on have finished. Finally, we implement the algorithm in a simulator that runs existing ROS 2 applications without any change to them or to ROS 2. We evaluate the simulator on industrial use cases and synthetic graphs. On the industrial use cases, it is up to 2.6 times faster than synchronous parallel simulation and needs an order of magnitude less memory for messages than asynchronous parallel simulation.

title: Puzzles, People, and Publications: Measuring Shared Significance in Crosswords from 1942 to 2024
abstract: Crossword puzzles are cultural objects that encode shared significance. We use interpretable, large-scale computational methods to analyze how crossword constructors, editors, and publications have adopted and adapted language to convey significance. Focusing on approximately 2.4 million crossword clue/answer pairs published in The New York Times between 1942 and 2024, we find shifting significance and differing editorial practices to be quantitatively measurable. By computationally measuring shared significance over time in crossword puzzle production, we are able to better understand cultural changes in the United States through the 20th and early 21st centuries.

title: A posteriori estimates for inverse evolutionary problems
abstract: The paper is focused on a posteriori error analysis of evolutionary problems, which are ill-posed in the sense of Hadamard. They may have no solutions and respective approximations may be highly unstable. For these problems, the a posteriori error estimation concept applicable to well-posed problems is not valid and requires a significant reformulation. A posteriori estimates of the functional type provide the basis for addressing this issue. They generate computable quantities that estimate the distance between a function (approximate solution to the inverse problem) and exact solution of a "close" well-posed initial boundary value problem associated with the same differential equation. The solution of this close problem exactly satisfies one part of the imposed conditions and the others are satisfied approximately with the accuracy $\eps$. This idea is elaborated for several evolutionary problems generated by the reaction-convection-diffusion equation: backward parabolic problem, problem with non-local time conditions, Cauchy parabolic problem, and parameter(s) identification problem. The estimates derived not only control the accuracy of approximate solutions, but also suggest a unified approach to calculating them numerically.

title: Feynman integrals, coactions and Lie-algebra representations
abstract: We outline a link between canonical differential equations of Feynman integrals and matrix representations of flat connections taking values in certain Lie algebras. Leveraging insights from string theory and properties of periods associated with these Lie algebras, we deduce single-valued solutions to the differential equations and coactions for the integrals. We introduce a novel form of the differential equations which connects with the representation theory of the Lie algebras and may depart from $\varepsilon$-factorisation in a controlled way. We illustrate the formalism through relevant examples.

title: PLATON 7: An ultra-fast exoplanet atmospheric retrieval code
abstract: PLATON is an open source Python package for atmospheric retrieval, first released in 2018. We introduce PLATON 7, a complete rewrite of PLATON using Claude Fable 5. The biggest changes are that PLATON now uses JAX for all intensive calculations, and these calculations are now performed in single precision instead of double precision. These two changes speed up the code by a factor of ~60 with negligible decrease in accuracy, allowing it to compute a 0.8--5.3 um transmission spectrum at R=20k in 0.35 ms on a RTX 5090. We also introduce several new features, including support for two-limb retrievals, patchy clouds, and more opacities (particularly OCS and CS2). PLATON is available on GitHub at https://github.com/ideasrule/platon.

title: Lost in the Signal Model: Confusion Between Deterministic and Stochastic Gravitational Wave Signals in Pulsar Timing Array Data
abstract: With growing evidence for the presence of a gravitational wave background (GWB) in pulsar timing array (PTA) data, it is imperative to understand how this signal will act as a foreground for other GW signals, particularly those from individual supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs), which are predicted to be detected in the next decade. For PTAs, since these two types of signals are long-timescale persistent signals, a signal from an SMBHB system may already be present in the latest PTA datasets. In this work, we analyze how the presence of this signal could affect our detection statistics for the GWB, and how the presence of the GWB can affect our search for the SMBHB system. We find that individual SMBHB signals can significantly skew the recovery of the GWB amplitude and spectral index. However, when the SMBHB signals are recovered consistently, we are again able to recover the GWB power-law parameters, highlighting the importance of joint searches in future PTA searches for GWs. We also explore the rate of improvement of parameter estimation uncertainty, giving insight to the types of signals most likely to be identified well enough to enable multimessenger analyses.

title: Blazars through the eyes of REDSoX and GOSoX
abstract: Blazar polarimetric properties provide key constraints on the physical conditions within relativistic jets, offering insights into particle acceleration mechanisms, high-energy radiation processes, and jet composition. The Rocket Experiment Demonstration of a Soft X-ray Polarimeter (REDSoX) will serve as a precursor to the Globe Orbiting Soft X-ray Polarimeter (GOSoX), a state-of-the-art polarimeter designed for observations in the soft X-ray range (0.2-0.4 keV), with a planned launch for 2030. REDSoX and GOSoX will be the first (and currently only) X-ray polarimeters capable of performing observations below 1 keV, opening a new observational window into high-energy polarimetry. In this work, we investigate the soft X-ray polarimetric properties of blazars expected in the REDSoX and GOSoX band and assess the detectability of different samples of sources: one drawn from the RoboPol Monitoring Program, a statistically complete sample of gamma-ray-selected blazars spanning the low-, intermediate-, and high-synchrotron-peaked sources, and one cross-matched between the CAZ (CRTS, ATLAS, and ZTF) and eROSITA catalogs. We estimated the expected source fluxes in the selected energy bands through spectral energy distribution fitting performed with the Bjet-MCMC tool. We investigated the expected polarimetric properties under three competing emission scenarios: leptonic, hadronic, and hybrid, each one predicting distinct observational signatures. We assessed the detectability of every source by comparing our polarization degree predictions with the instrument's minimum detectable polarization function (MDP). Finally, we computed the detection probability for each source. This work offers a set of promising blazar targets for future observations with GOSoX, highlighting the mission's potential for probing relativistic jet physics through soft X-ray polarimetry.

title: Water-ice formation in Ophiuchus follows the local irradiation
abstract: Water ice only appears on interstellar dust grains beyond a certain depth into a molecular cloud. This depth has so far been quoted as one extinction threshold per cloud. We measured the threshold along 43009 sightlines through the Ophiuchus cloud with the ice color-excess method, which converts archival WISE and Spitzer photometry of background stars into the peak optical depth of the 3 $μ$m water-ice band. We sorted the sightlines by the 12 $μ$m surface brightness of the cloud at fixed extinction, a proxy for the ultraviolet field that excites the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons at the cloud surface. The onset of ice formation lies at higher extinction toward sightlines with brighter 12 $μ$m emission, ranging from $A_{K_S}^{\rm th} = 0.67$ to $1.15$ mag. It increases by 0.58 to 0.90 mag in $A_{K_S}$ per factor of ten in 12 $μ$m brightness, depending on the adopted reddening coefficient. Because the 12 $μ$m-bright and -faint sightlines lie in different parts of the cloud, we repeated the comparison within each of the five subregions, and four of the subregions show the same trend. The trend also persists among sightlines with a similar amount of diffuse material around them. A later onset in more strongly irradiated gas is expected from photodesorption by external ultraviolet light, although a comparison of its size with models requires a calibration of the 12 $μ$m brightness against the strength of the field. The extinction at which water ice appears thus varies with the local environment, which complicates comparisons between clouds. Photometric ice maps resolve this variation across entire clouds, and the SPHEREx and JWST ice surveys can test it spectroscopically.

title: Charge Exchange Illuminates Turbulent Cold-Hot Interfaces
abstract: Cold-hot interfaces are ubiquitous in the multiphase circumgalactic medium (CGM), galactic winds, and the Galactic Center (GC), yet their microscopic contact regions are difficult to observe. Charge exchange (CX), in which a highly ionized metal ion captures an electron from a neutral donor and emits soft X-ray lines, directly probes these interfaces. We develop a subgrid CX model coupled to a nonequilibrium ionization (NEI) network in hydrodynamic simulations of radiative turbulent mixing layers. CX soft X-rays are confined to a thin, highly corrugated cold-hot interface (corrugation factor $\sim10$), whereas thermal emission fills the hot phase. Turbulent transport sustains high-charge ions at $T\sim 10^4$-$10^5$ K, where they encounter neutral donors. The low-temperature O VIII fraction exceeds that in a uniformly cooling isobaric parcel, demonstrating the importance of mixing to the ionization history. CX depletes this cool ion population, while continued entrainment maintains the supply. Including a metagalactic ionizing background changes the ion distribution and enhances CX surface brightness by a factor of a few in our CGM comparison, but preserves the cool origin of most CX emission. In the limit of sufficient neutral column, CX surface brightness is ion-supply limited: higher donor density increases local emissivity but shortens the reaction layer. The system-wide CX-to-thermal soft X-ray ratio also depends on the volume-to-interface scale $V/A_{\rm int}$, making CX a potential probe of multiphase structure in the CGM, galactic winds, and the GC.

title: Little Red Dots at Cosmic Noon: Spectroscopy Reveals Declining Abundance but a Non-Evolving Luminosity Function Shape
abstract: Little red dots (LRDs) are an extremely abundant population of red, compact, broad-line objects primarily found in the early universe. At $5<z<8$, they are at least 10 times more abundant than UV-selected quasars. Yet, how this population evolves towards lower redshift is unclear. In this work, we present our search for LRDs at cosmic noon ($2\lesssim z\lesssim 4$) in nearly 20 deg$^2$ of the Deep/UltraDeep fields of the Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program (HSC-SSP). Combining multiwavelength wide-field imaging surveys from 0.3 to 4.5 $μ$m, we identify 266 photometric LRD candidates. With spectroscopic follow-up from Keck/NIRES, VLT/X-shooter, and Magellan/FIRE on 24 candidates, we identify a sample of four LRDs with broad H$α$ emission. With the purity of the photometric sample calibrated by spectroscopy, we estimate the number density of LRDs to be approximately $6.8\times10^{-7}$ cMpc$^{-3}$ at $2.10<z<2.55$---this is nearly a factor of 35 decrease from their flat number density evolution at $4\lesssim z\lesssim8$ estimated from JWST spectroscopic surveys. The knee of the LRD optical luminosity function also remains consistently at $M_{5500}\approx-22$ mag across $2<z<5$, below that of quasars. We further speculate that only the abundance of LRDs, but not the shape of their optical luminosity function, evolves with redshift, and the Roman Space Telescope will be able to test this decisively with a substantially larger sample of low-redshift LRDs.

title: Topologically Obstructed Kondo Hybridization: A Route to Kondo Semimetals
abstract: The interplay of strong correlations, topology, and symmetry can reshape the low-energy electronic structure of quantum materials and drive the emergence of novel quantum phases. In heavy-fermion systems, the Kondo effect entangles localized $f$ moments with conduction electrons, giving rise to coherent heavy-electron bands at low temperatures, typically characterized by a Kondo hybridization gap. Here we show, however, that the topology and symmetry of the conduction-electron Fermi surface can obstruct the opening of the Kondo hybridization gap at certain momenta. Treating the Fermi surface of a three-dimensional system as an effective two-dimensional manifold, we demonstrate that nontrivial topological invariants defined on this manifold impose a topological obstruction to opening a full hybridization gap, forcing the $fc$ hybridization to vanish at certain momenta on the Fermi surface. These hybridization zeros lead to crossings between $c$ and $f$ bands, giving rise to nodal points or lines near the Fermi energy within the Kondo phase. Our results establish topological obstructions to Kondo hybridization as a route to Kondo semimetals, revealing a fundamental connection between Fermi-surface topology and the emergence of correlated electronic phases.

title: A matrix model of an M5--brane on a plane--wave background
abstract: We construct the maximally supersymmetric deformation of the recently proposed $\mathcal{A}_6$ matrix model on a plane--wave background. We derive the same theory independently, by reducing the light--cone M5--brane on a five--sphere in this background to its lowest harmonics, including the dynamics of its chiral two--form and of its fermions. We then classify all its classical vacua. We show that one of them is the fivebrane giant graviton, and that its fluctuations form a single $\mathfrak{su}(2|4)$ multiplet, which reproduces the $\ell=1$ level of the spherical transverse fivebrane identified in the large $N$ limit of BMN theory. Moreover, the dynamical tensor supports new families of vacua, where the flux balances the size of the brane, and whose spectrum contains that of a fuzzy membrane. Finally, we show that BLG theory sits inside the model, both on a Coulomb branch of the massless theory and around the giant graviton of the massive one, where the two membranes are polarized into the fivebrane.

title: Agent-guided construction of Feynman integral bases
abstract: Finding bases of Feynman integrals whose differential equations are suitable for phenomenology is a remarkably verifiable task. We exploit this to design two \emph{skills} with which Claude Opus~5.5 produces novel results autonomously, working for several days. For a two-loop five-point family (with two masses and 18 elliptic sectors) and a two-loop superfamily for the radiative jet function with a K3 sector, the agent finds bases whose differential equations are free of poles in the dimensional regulator $\varepsilon$ and at most quadratic in it, and takes the jet-function one to $\varepsilon$-factorized form.

title: The MURALES survey. IX. MUSE observations and results for 3C radio sources at 0.3 < z < 0.82
abstract: This is the ninth paper in the MUse RAdio Loud Emission lines Snapshot (MURALES) project series, presenting the results of observations of 3C radio sources obtained with the VLT/MUSE integral field spectrograph. Here, we investigate the morphology and kinematics of the extended emission line regions (EELRs) of 26 radio galaxies at intermediate redshift 0.3 < z < 0.82 and their relation with the radio ejecta. EELRs are observed in all but 4 of the 26 sources extending as far as 160 kpc from the host galaxy. They show different morphologies and kinematics usually related with the radio properties. The five sources associated with the smaller radio sources show highly disturbed gas kinematics. Several EELRs have a filamentary morphology, often forming bubbles inflated by the radio lobes. The more extended EELRs usually have elongated morphologies and show well-ordered rotation. We then confirm the general results obtained from the study of the source at lower redshift: radio galaxies are surrounded by super-disks, that is, structures of ionized gas on scales of many tens of kiloparsec, whose properties depend on a combination of the evolutionary state of the radio source and its orientation with respect to the super-disks.

title: Off-diagonal long-range order and $p$-wave pairing in one dimension from critical density fluctuations
abstract: A central theme in the theory of unconventional superconductivity is that Cooper pairing can be mediated by bosonic collective modes other than lattice vibrations. However, collective fluctuations in reduced dimensions can also have a destabilizing effect on superconductivity, by suppressing long-range order or by destroying Fermi-liquid quasiparticles in the normal state. In this work, we study a one-dimensional (1D) model of spinless fermions with local interactions that exhibits a continuous quantum phase transition from a Luttinger liquid to a phase-separated state. Combining field-theoretic arguments with numerical exact diagonalization and matrix-product-state methods, we find that the quantum critical point exhibits two-particle off-diagonal long-range order and $p$-wave pairing. Our work shows that critical density fluctuations at a phase-separation instability can act as pairing glue for unconventional superconductivity in 1D, overcoming the disordering effect of phase fluctuations and the absence of long-lived fermionic quasiparticles in the normal state.

title: The cosmological lithium problem and how decaying relics still solve it
abstract: Lithium-7 in old stars is about three times below the prediction of standard big-bang nucleosynthesis, and deuterium lies slightly above it. Precise measurements of deuterium, helium-4, and the effective number of neutrino species now disfavor most previously proposed particle solutions. We find that relics that decay or evaporate with lifetimes of a few hours, mostly into electron antineutrinos of about a hundred MeV and into electrons or photons, still lower lithium-7 while respecting these measurements. Such relics include gauge bosons of $L_e-L_τ$ or $B-3L_e$ and heavy neutral leptons with a dipole coupling or mixing with $ν_τ$, with masses of a few hundred MeV, and populations of evaporating Q-balls that carry lepton number. The decaying particles substantially alleviate the lithium problem, while Q-ball populations reach the $2σ$ range of lithium-7 adopted by the Particle Data Group. These relics can shift the effective number of neutrino species by up to about $2.5$ times the precision expected from the Simons Observatory, and a future Galactic supernova can test the particles.

title: Moment bounds and UV reconstruction from curved positivity cones
abstract: The fundamental principles of the S-matrix impose positivity bounds on the Wilson coefficients of EFTs, including the SMEFT. These bounds form convex cones that often have curved boundaries when there are degeneracies among the irreducible two-particle low-energy states. Numerical approximations have previously been used to evaluate these curved cones. We develop a moment-based framework to analytically carve out these cones, particularly those associated with anomalous quartic gauge couplings in the SMEFT. The framework also allows us to reverse engineer UV models from the curved boundaries of the positivity cones.

title: Topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry
abstract: Chiral (or sublattice) symmetry describes bipartite systems such as the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain where same-sublattice A-A and B-B hoppings are forbidden, enabling the protection of topological phases. Here we identify new topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry wherein chiral symmetry is preserved on only one sublattice, as may occur with sublattice imbalance (e.g. graphene-hBN) or localized orbitals (e.g. zincblende). Unlike conventional symmetry operators described by group theory, half-chiral symmetry is an algebraic constraint on the sublattice-projected Hamiltonian such as $PHP=0$, requiring a new framework for topological protection. We develop such a framework, identifying real-space bulk topological invariants and corresponding topological boundary modes that stick to zero energy. In two dimensions we construct a half-chiral Kekule honeycomb model and show that its unusual higher-order topology protects a single zero-energy mode at a single corner.

title: Onset of quantum chaos in a family of two-dimensional conformal field theories
abstract: We exhibit random matrix statistics in the scaling dimensions of non-BPS primary operators in a family of two-dimensional conformal field theories. Specifically, we consider the sigma model with K3 target space and $\mathcal N=(4,4)$ supersymmetry in a neighborhood of the Kummer orbifold point $\mathbb T^4/\mathbb Z_2$. At the free-fermion radius, the spin-zero spectrum of the $\mathbb Z_2^4$-invariant sector is exactly degenerate at integer energies. The exactly marginal blow-up deformations that preserve this symmetry form a four-dimensional space, whose directions we parametrize by unit quaternions. Along each deformation direction, we compute the first-order splitting of the degenerate levels, i.e., the leading anomalous dimensions as the coupling goes to zero. In sectors where all exact symmetries are resolved, including a hidden $\mathbb Z_2$ at the even levels, the non-zero first-order shifts along a generic direction follow the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble (GOE), as we verify by computing several spectral diagnostics. We compare quantitatively with the well-known singlet deformation, which has enhanced symmetry: even after all its known symmetries are resolved, its first-order spectrum has exact degeneracies, its gap ratio approaches the GOE value only slowly as the energy increases, and its unfolded spectrum lacks the long-range rigidity of the GOE.

title: Thermalization and quantum chaos in a pure gauge discrete non-Abelian lattice gauge theory
abstract: Gauge theories constitute the basis of our microscopic description of fundamental physical laws, and they are a cornerstone of contemporary scientific research. Yet, how such systems thermalize far from equilibrium remains a fundamental open question at the crossroads of statistical, high-energy, and condensed-matter physics. In this work, we investigate the thermalization properties of non-Abelian lattice gauge theories, focusing on the discrete gauge group $D_3$, which is ideally suited for current qudit-based quantum simulators. Specifically, we study a linear plaquette chain in a gauge-fixed formulation that removes unphysical degrees of freedom. A numerical analysis of the Hamiltonian spectrum and expectation values of local operators shows a behavior broadly aligned with the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH). We also study thermalization through the real-time dynamics of the entanglement spectrum, confirming the emergence of random-matrix level statistics after an initial transient. Our results expand the rich phenomenology of dihedral non-Abelian gauge systems. Once the relevant symmetry structure is properly resolved, the model displays the same qualitative ETH-based thermalization scenario observed in Abelian gauge models and generic non-integrable quantum many-body systems.

title: From Binary Wind to Radio Burst: Dispersion-Measure Evolution after Accretion-induced Collapse
abstract: Secular changes in the dispersion measures (DMs) of repeating fast radio bursts probe the source-local plasma. Such DM time variability has been interpreted with spherical, single-density-profile models. Accretion-induced collapse (AIC) of a white dwarf may instead follow binary interaction and occur inside a finite, anisotropic circumstellar structure. Here, we construct an angle-dependent toy model of aspherical AIC ejecta propagating through a pre-AIC free wind, shocked-wind bubble, swept-up external shell, and polar cavity, exploring a diffuse environment (number density of $1~{\rm cm^{-3}}$, located at $10~$pc) and a compact cloud (number density of $500~{\rm cm^{-3}}$, located at $0.3~$pc), bracketing ionized and initially neutral upstream gas. The unshocked ejecta initially yield ${\rm DM}\propto t^{-2}$, while crossings of the finite wind-bubble interfaces produce breaks and curvature in ${\rm DM}(t)$. In initially neutral models, shock ionization can overcome geometric dilution: the total DM reverses from decline to growth after approximately $10$--$20$ yr and later turns over as the finite reservoir is processed. Ionized-upstream models instead generally decline or flatten. Without fitting individual sources, our models span both signs and the approximate magnitudes of the secular DM-variation rates measured among repeaters. In this dynamical framework, DM evolution is set by shock propagation through the circumsource density and ionization structure, rather than the contemporaneous burst rate, distinguishing it from photoionization-driven scenarios. Consequently, in our model, an instantaneous \(d{\rm DM}/dt\) is not a unique indicator of source age. We suggest that the observed distribution of secular DM variation slope amplitudes and signs will be important for distinguishing among different models of DM variations in repeating FRBs.

title: When the magnetic force theorem fails: dressed exchange in the induced-moment magnets FePt, FePd, CoPt, and CoPd
abstract: Effective spin Hamiltonians for itinerant magnets are commonly parameterized by magnetic-force-theorem (MFT) exchange constants, which are subsequently used to compute the behavior of complex and delicate spin textures, for example skyrmions. We show that for systems containing atoms with large spin susceptibility, such as Pd or Pt, this approach misses important parts of the energetics. For FePt, it even predicts the wrong ground state. Benchmarking against fully self-consistent spin-spiral density-functional calculations - in which the electronic structure, including the induced Pd/Pt moments, relaxes for every spin configuration - we quantify the missing energetics for the ordered L1$_0$ alloys FePt, FePd, CoPt, and CoPd. By comparing a family of models that differ only in their treatment of the induced Pt moment, including the configuration-dependent models of Mryasov and Polesya, we identify the origin: the energetics of the induced moments are governed by the exchange-enhanced (dressed) susceptibility, of which the frozen-potential MFT captures only the bare part - about one third of the Pt-mediated interaction in FePt. We derive a general bound showing that no on-site (intra-atomic) refinement can supply the missing strength. The dressing decides the magnetic ground state in FePt, where the interlayer ordering rests entirely on the Pt-mediated interactions, and shifts the Curie temperatures of the other alloys by several hundred kelvin. Computed ordering temperatures, magnon spectra and spin wave stiffness for all four compounds are provided.

title: The Simons Observatory: A Novel Design for Heat Strap at Sub-Kelvin Temperatures
abstract: We present a novel process for the fabrication of copper heat straps and a measurement of their thermal performance at sub-Kelvin temperatures. The conductance of the heat straps is consistent with the bulk conductivity of annealed copper over the range 60 mK to 1 K. We find no evidence for deviation from a linear dependence of conductivity with temperature over the explored range, indicating that the contact resistance at the strap ends is sub-dominant. Heat straps developed and validated through the described process have been deployed in both the Large Aperture Telescope Receiver and a Small Aperture Telescope of the Simons Observatory and have met thermal requirements.

title: Arinkin's sheaf and Hilbert schemes
abstract: Arinkin's sheaf gives a relative Fourier-Mukai autoequivalence of a general Beauville-Mukai system, extending the usual Poincaré bundle over the smooth locus. We provide an alternative construction of it as a deformation of the Fourier-Mukai autoequivalence on the Hilbert scheme of an elliptic K3 surface obtained by lifting the classical Poincaré kernel for an elliptic surface. As applications, we show that the $P=C$ property for a general Beauville-Mukai system is equivalent to that for the Hilbert scheme fibration, thus providing new proofs for both. We also construct an explicit deformation that connects Markman's construction of a projectively hyperholomorphic bundle on products of hyper-Kähler manifolds of K3${}^{[g]}$-type to that of Hartlieb and Shah. This answers a question of Hartlieb and Shah.

title: Held-to-Maturity Accounting: Hidden Losses and Systemic Fragility
abstract: This paper studies how accounting-induced opacity affects systemic risk in the banking system. Motivated by the buildup of unrealized losses during recent monetary tightening episodes, we develop a model in which banks hold correlated interest rate sensitive assets and are connected through an endogenous interbank network. We show that Held-To-Maturity (HTM) accounting amplifies systemic risk by delaying loss recognition, allowing losses to accumulate and become synchronized across institutions. When losses are realized under liquidity stress, the interaction of correlated exposures and network linkages generates nonlinear increases in defaults. These findings suggest that accounting regimes are not neutral from a financial stability perspective, as they influence both the buildup and propagation of systemic risk, particularly in environments with common asset exposures and strong interconnectedness.

title: Machine learning reveals new Galactic C-rich and O-rich AGB sources
abstract: Identification of carbon-rich (C-rich) and oxygen-rich (O-rich) Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB) stars is crucial to understanding the structure and dust sources of the Milky Way. We present a machine-learning (ML) classification of Galactic AGB candidates using Gaia DR3, identifying 304,090 O-rich and 4,227 C-rich sources. Our two-step approach, which involves similarity-based selection, followed by XGBoost classification that combines colour and spectroscopic features, demonstrates that a small, but high-quality training sample is sufficient for accurate identification even in massive datasets such as ~140 million sources from Gaia DR3. The ML-identified stars occupy distinct regions in colour-magnitude and Gaia-2MASS diagrams, and comparison with stellar isochrones combined with Gaia distances allows estimates of their masses and ages. Spatial distributions show that O-rich AGB stars dominate the inner Galaxy, while C-rich AGB stars are concentrated toward the anti-Galactic centre. Vertical profiles indicate that massive O-rich (5-8 M$_\odot$) stars remain near the Galactic mid-plane, whereas C-rich (2.3-2.5 M$_\odot$) and low-mass O-rich (1-1.5 M$_\odot$) AGB stars are more vertically extended, with scale heights that increase with decreasing stellar mass and increasing stellar ages. C-rich AGB stars trace the Galactic warp at intermediate ages (1 Gyr), with warp amplitudes appearing larger than those traced by Cepheids. Intermediate-mass O-rich AGB stars (~300 Myr) show tentative correspondence with several spiral arm features, while the C-rich distribution is too smooth for reliable identification with the current sample. These results highlight AGB stars as powerful probes of stellar evolution and Galactic dynamical processes.

title: Model the Annotation, Not the Noise: Semantic Annotation-Channel Prompt Learning against Noisy Labels
abstract: Parameter-efficient prompt learning has become a cornerstone for adapting pre-trained vision-language models (VLMs), yet it remains highly vulnerable to label noise in few-shot Web and retrieval scenarios. Existing noise robust methods typically rely on hard sample selection or deterministic label correction, which discard valuable semantic ambiguity and overlook how observed annotations are actually generated. To bridge this gap, we reformulate noisy prompt learning through the perspective of data generation, proposing SACP, a Semantic-aware Annotation Channel-based Prompt learning framework. Instead of suppressing noise heuristically, SACP decouples latent clean-label prediction from instance-dependent annotation generation. By integrating frozen VLM semantic priors with lightweight visual residuals, SACP constructs a structured annotation channel optimized via generalized expectation-maximization with soft posteriors. Furthermore, a posterior-aware memory is introduced to preserve label uncertainty during test-time inference. Extensive experiments across different synthetic benchmarks and the real-world noisy Food101N dataset demonstrate that SACP achieves state-of-the-art performance against its counterparts in different label noise patterns, especially under severe asymmetric noise.

title: MambaSplit: Severity-Robust and Inference-Efficient Semantic Unmixing of Fluorescence Microscopy Image Data
abstract: The number of structures fluorescence microscopy can image in one sample is limited by how few fluorophores can be separated without significant spectral overlap. Semantic unmixing circumvents this limit by imaging two structures in one fluorescent channel and computationally separating the superimposed image into one image per structure. Because pixels rarely identify their structure, unmixing requires both local and long-range spatial context. The relative brightness of the two structures is unknown and can be very uneven, so predictions must remain accurate across mixing severities, from balanced mixtures to ones where a structure is barely visible. Existing methods either process small image patches or add context through auxiliary pathways that slow inference on large images. We present MambaSplit, a hierarchical state-space encoder with a convolutional decoder that captures context across large tiles in linear time and predicts both channels in one deterministic pass. MambaSplit trains either on computationally summed channel images with random mixing ratios, where a lightweight head estimates the unknown ratio and conditions the decoder on it, or on experimentally acquired superpositions. Across five datasets and nine mixing ratios, MambaSplit achieves the highest RI-PSNR, by up to 3.0 dB, in 11 of 15 dataset-severity combinations and ties in one more, while running 5.9x faster than the strongest baseline. On acquired superpositions, fine-tuning a model pretrained on summed inputs matches or exceeds all baselines. Ablations show that accuracy and robustness come mainly from the training recipe: large tiles, mixing ratios sampled across their full range (up to 11 dB over fixed-ratio training), and independently drawn channel crops (3.9 dB on BioSR). The state-space backbone makes large tiles affordable, enabling high-content screening and event-driven smart microscopy.

title: Large deviations, effective dynamics, and dynamical phase transitions in random maps
abstract: Large deviation theory provides a natural framework to characterize rare fluctuations of time-averaged observables in deterministic and stochastic systems. Building on previous results for deterministic chaotic maps, here we extend the Doob transform to random maps, constructing an effective dynamics in which rare events become typical. This makes it possible to directly reproduce the dynamics of rare trajectories that are exponentially difficult to sample under the original dynamics. We further apply spectral large-deviation methods to characterize dynamical phase transitions in random maps. The spectral structure of the tilted operator provides insight into the mechanisms underlying these transitions and, in particular, allows us to identify the appropriate initial states that select one dynamical phase or another. Our results extend the connection between large deviation theory, spectral methods, and effective dynamics to random chaotic maps, providing a general framework to study rare events and dynamical phase transitions in these systems.

title: Certification of non-stabilizerness in multi-qubit systems via worst-case random access codes
abstract: Recent works have proposed semi-device-independent frameworks to certify non-stabilizerness, but the complexity of the stabilizer polytope makes these methods infeasible beyond a few qubits. In this work, we address this limitation by moving to partially characterized measurements in the context of worst-case random access codes. We first establish a simple condition, which we term the stabilizer pigeonhole criterion, that certifies non-stabilizerness in $m$-qubit pure states, and show how it can be applied to reduced states. As an application, we certify magic in $W$ states of arbitrary size using only eight preparations and three single-qubit measurement settings. Motivated by recent work on the stabilizer marginal problem, we then construct prepare-and-measure correlations generated by global $m$-qubit quantum states for which every $k$-qubit marginal lies inside the stabilizer polytope, yet the combined correlations cannot be reproduced by any global stabilizer mixture. Finally, we derive analytical upper and lower bounds on the worst-case bias attainable with mixed stabilizer preparations in an $m$-qubit random access code with $n$ Pauli measurements. For the complete set of $4^m-1$ non-identity Pauli measurements, we show that the optimal quantum and mixed-stabilizer biases both scale as $2^{-3m/2}$, and that their ratio is asymptotically bounded by a constant ($\lesssim 1.85$), showing that in this setting, magic in the preparations alone yields at most a constant-factor advantage over stabilizer mixtures.

title: Latent Space Planning with Sequential Monte Carlo
abstract: Planning with learned world models amounts to finding action sequences whose predicted rollouts reach a goal. Sampling-based planners often struggle at longer horizons, while gradient-based methods can become trapped in local minima. Meanwhile, model predictive path integral control (MPPI), a complementary approach, alternates between estimating an expectation under a cost-weighted distribution from samples and updating the plan from this estimate. Its samples, however, are drawn afresh at every iteration from a Gaussian proposal and reach the target distribution only through importance weights. Moreover, a target distribution favoring goal-reaching trajectories can be difficult to define directly, motivating a sequence of intermediate distributions. Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) provides a natural mechanism for evolving such a sequence through importance weighting and resampling. Motivated by this, we formulate latent-space planning as optimization guided by SMC, which moves a population of action sequences while a gradient-based optimizer updates the plan. Inspired by classical planning, we further introduce a PDE-derived cost-to-go that guides the evolution of the sample distribution using the structure of the latent state space. On navigation and manipulation tasks with visual and proprioceptive world models, our formulation outperforms gradient-based planners by $29$ and $50$, sampling-based planners by $35$ and MPPI by $7$ percentage points in average success rate, while succeeding in fewer iterations than gradient-based planners and within 4\% of MPPI.

title: Planar cut-and-project sets with interval windows are bi-Lipschitz equivalent to lattices
abstract: We prove that every cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose window is a line segment is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice: if $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^3$ is a plane which is not spanned by vectors in $\mathbb{Z}^3$, $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$, and $σ$ is a segment of any length which is transverse to $V$, then the set of points $v\in V$ with $v+x\inσ+\mathbb{Z}^3$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to $\mathbb{Z}^2$. For planes of Diophantine slope this is a theorem of Burago and Kleiner, and the point of the present paper is that no Diophantine condition on the plane is needed. We also show that the same conclusion holds when the window is a finite union of intervals. Together with the author's construction of a cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a compact window of countable boundary, which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to any lattice, this shows that for planes in $\mathbb{R}^3$ the answer to the bi-Lipschitz question depends on the shape of the window rather than on the Diophantine properties of the plane.

title: Effects of Preionisation in Radiative Shocks IV. A Spectral Grid Library of fully Radiative Shock Models with Time--Dependent Precursor
abstract: Here we present an extensive set of shock models calculated using an improved version of the MAPPINGS shock and photoionization code. The new version of MAPPINGS, namely MAPPINGS V, has a greatly improved treatment of the precursor emission, a more robust adaptive-mesh shock solver (Sutherland & Dopita 2017), and new atomic data compared to MAPPINGS III, which was used by Allen et al. (2008) to create their widely used shock model grid. The new shock model library covers the shock velocity range 50-1000 km/s, and a wide range of initial conditions and updated abundances. We highlight how the newer models compare to the earlier grid, and discuss where the shock models are most likely to approximate conditions for various types of astrophysical objects.
