On a fixed-wing UAV benchmark, the corrected operator matches the accuracy of a batched Adam solver and an Ipopt solver at equal sample size and is 8 times faster than the Adam solver on the same GPU at a few hundred scenarios and 15 times faster than Ipopt on a CPU.

title: Do Companies Deliver on Their IPO Claims?
abstract: Initial public offering (IPO) filings describe what a company does and what it intends to become. Yet whether individual forward-looking claims are subsequently realized is difficult to assess. We introduce Vision Follow-Through (VFT), a benchmark and agentic pipeline that separates claim extraction, category assignment, verifiability, and evidence-grounded follow-through assessment. \vftclaims{} contains 5,066 human-annotated claim spans from 50 IPO filings, while \vftverify{} adds verifiability tiers, follow-through outcomes, and cited later evidence for 1,000 claims. Across language models, classifying human-annotated claims is substantially easier than extracting claims from full filings. Extraction coverage also varies sharply by category, with Organizational/Culture claims recovered far less often than Market Opportunity claims. Follow-through assessment poses a separate challenge: model judgments diverge from human assessments in different ways rather than exhibiting a single consistent bias. These results show that reliable assessment of corporate follow-through requires both finding the relevant claims and grounding subsequent judgments in later evidence.

title: Nonlinear Shrinkage for Higher Moments Estimation in Large Portfolios
abstract: Portfolio risk is not limited to the variance of returns. The moments of portfolio returns depend directly on the covariance matrix and higher-order co-dependences (coskewness, cokurtosis, etc.). In practice, however, these objects are extremely noisy, especially for large portfolios. Here we introduce filtering methods based on tensor decompositions that extend cross-validated covariance cleaning and the Average Oracle methodology to even-order co-moment tensors. Using returns on historical Russell 1000 constituents, we find that the proposed filters improve out-of-sample estimation accuracy relative to sample estimators, both for correlation and cokurtosis tensors, as measured by relative squared Frobenius errors. These improvements translate into lower relative errors on portfolio volatility and kurtosis, and into lower out-of-sample volatility and kurtosis when the portfolio objective penalizes both variance and the fourth moment.

title: On the Delandtsheer Conjecture
abstract: We prove the Delandtsheer Conjecture of 1988 that a line-primitive automorphism group of a finite linear space is point-primitive.

title: From data pencils to image representations of continuous-time LTI systems
abstract: The continuous-time fundamental lemma describes the set of all trajectories of a linear time-invariant system by a Gramian matrix built from measured input--output data and their derivatives. The jet of a trajectory is represented as the Gramian applied to a nonunique parameter satisfying a differential-algebraic equation. We determine the complete Kronecker structure of the associated data pencil for multiple-input multiple-output systems. This enables the construction of a polynomial image representation of the input--output behavior directly from the data. The resulting image matrix has column degrees equal to the controllability indices, and its latent variable is free and serves as a flat output of the system. The computation relies on an orthogonal staircase reduction followed by basis reconstruction using polynomial kernels. We also propose a structure-preserving preconditioning of the Gramian to improve its condition number and facilitate rank decisions in the reduction. We illustrate our approach on a chain of mass-spring-damper systems.

title: Stratum: A Hardware-Software Co-Design Framework for SNN Inference on RISC-V
abstract: Efficient spiking neural network (SNN) inference on RISC-V processors requires tracing implementation costs back to the compiler and hardware decisions that produce them. Training environments, compilers, and cycle-level simulators, however, typically operate as distinct tools, making this attribution difficult. This paper presents Stratum, a framework that integrates an snnTorch-trained SNN, an MLIR-based compiler stack, and a cycle-level gem5-based RISC-V model into a unified workflow. Stratum exposes two optimization levers, software decisions in the generated code and hardware configuration choices in the simulated core, and uses stage-level cycle measurements to identify performance bottlenecks. We demonstrate Stratum on a two-layer N-MNIST network with three controlled comparisons: (i)~dense vs.\ spike-gated lowering of \texttt{snn.linear}, (ii)~output-outer vs.\ spike-major weight layout with spike-gating enabled in both binaries, and (iii)~L2 cache capacity with both layouts. Our spike-gated lowering reduces simulated inference time by $64\times$ (453.2\,ms to 7.04\,ms), and our spike-major layout cuts it by a further 37.2\% (to 4.42\,ms) at 4\,MiB L2, with the predicted class unchanged. The layout speedup grows from $1.59\times$ to $1.88\times$ when L2 shrinks to 1\,MiB. These results show that Stratum enables rapid early evaluation of design choices at both the software level (compiler stack) and the hardware level (cycle-level gem5 simulation).

title: Data Informativity for Robust Feedback Rectification of Switched Linear Systems
abstract: Feedback rectification is a method for switched linear systems that constructs a mode-dependent state feedback such that the closed-loop subsystems share a common eigenvector basis. If the assigned eigenvalues lie inside the unit disk, this yields a common quadratic Lyapunov function and guarantees exponential stability under arbitrary switching. In this paper, we study robust feedback rectification from input-state data affected by bounded disturbances. Using the concept of data informativity, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for approximate feedback rectification without requiring full row-rank of the collected input-state data. If the rectification error is smaller than the stability margin of the prescribed eigenvalues, we obtain global exponential stability under arbitrary switching in the disturbance-free case, and practical global asymptotic stability under bounded disturbances. The approach is illustrated by a mass-spring-damper chain with varying stiffness, where prescribed poles are assigned in every mode from data that do not determine the system matrices uniquely.

title: Hamiltonian symmetry behind the vanishing of four-wave interactions at non-trivial resonances for one-dimensional deep-water waves
abstract: The unexpected cancellation of non-trivial resonant four-wave interactions is the foundation of several compact and accurate models for one-dimensional deep-water waves. The reasons for this cancellation are not yet fully understood. An additional integral of motion would account for it, but to our knowledge no corresponding symmetry has been identified. Here it is shown that in real canonical variables with the cubic terms eliminated, the fourth-order Hamiltonian is invariant under a sign-dependent phase rotation generated by the Hilbert transform. The corresponding Noether charge is the action imbalance between right- and left-moving waves, conserved exactly although number-changing quartic terms remain. The symmetry confines the quartic kernel to the sector with two wavenumbers of each sign, which contains no non-trivial resonance, so the cancellation follows without calculation. In complex normal variables the symmetry is the vanishing of the reduced Zakharov kernel whenever the product of the four wavenumbers is non-positive, and the known closed form of that kernel follows directly. The symmetry is the fourth-order instance of a selection rule valid at every order in these variables: no term of the Hamiltonian has a single wavenumber of the minority sign. The rule rests on the holomorphic structure of planar deep-water flow and on its square-root dispersion relation.

title: Bridging Badiou's Gaps: Topos Theory and the Bodies of Mathematical Expression
abstract: This article develops a second stage of an argument begun in 2013, revisiting Alain Badiou's use of topos theory in Being and Event and Logics of Worlds. The previous article diagnosed Badiou's reduction of topos theory to its atomistic, localic form as the scientific scapegoat in his attack on 'democratic materialism'. Now I ask what follows when this logicist illusion is dispelled and the categorical alternative is taken seriously, particularly with respect to forcing, semantic expression, and mathematical subjectification that constitute the key elements of Badiou's earlier work. I thus reconstruct Badiou's own arguments in a corrected form, while transferring them to a categorical framework. The aim is not to introduce new mathematical results, but to identify what is conceptually lost through their reduction to set-theoretic formalism. In particular, I describe Cohen's forcing argument in the context of Grothendieck topoi and Kripke-Joyal semantics, thereby explicating the geometric structures implicit in Badiou's thinking. This reconstruction further brings into view a different way of understanding Badiou's concepts of subject, body, and change. Rather than treating a topos as merely a formal container for mathematical objects, I propose reading it as a body of mathematical expression, aligning with Johnstone's characterization of a topos as a 'universe of discourse'. At the same time, the geometrization of logic allows Badiou's own four-fold typology of change - when applied to topos theory itself as a mathematical 'event' - to be anchored to various historical definitions of a topos. In this way, the article bridges Badiou's two major works while clarifying how his own limited expression of mathematical formalism embodies his 'dialectical', ultimately singular concept of the event, and the way it clouds his philosophical understanding of locality and temporality.

title: GAAFormer: Geometry-Anchored Attention Transformer for Joint Point Cloud Denoising and Upsampling
abstract: Point cloud denoising and upsampling require samples that accurately recover the underlying surface from noisy or sparse observations. A central challenge in both tasks is preserving surface coverage while refining point locations. We introduce GAAFormer (Geometry-Anchored Attention Transformer), a unified generative octree transformer that performs both tasks with a shared network. Its decoder anchors attention neighborhoods to geometry, providing spatial context for occupancy prediction and point generation. Fixed voxel windows and alternating shifts preserve the grouping of surviving nodes as the output tree changes. The design retains the encoder, positional encoding, prediction heads, and parameter count of a serialized-attention backbone. We establish a deletion-consistency property of the neighborhood rule and evaluate both tasks using the same model. On PUNet, GAAFormer achieves a mean Chamfer distance (CD) of $6.0643\times10^{-5}$, reducing CD and Hausdorff distance by 3.35% and 19.34%, respectively, relative to the serialized backbone. For upsampling, it achieves CD values of $0.8475$, $1.7057$, and $1.0147$ ($\times10^{-5}$) on PU-GAN, PU1K, and Sketchfab, respectively, with improvements in CD, Hausdorff distance, and point-to-surface distance over the same backbone on PU-GAN and Sketchfab. These results establish a single architecture for point cloud denoising and upsampling. Within the shared encoder-decoder, the same geometry-anchored attention module improves both noise removal and dense point generation without task-specific redesign or additional parameters.

title: HermiteTwin: Bicubic Hermite Shell Digital Twins for Contact-Rich Deformable Manipulation
abstract: While existing methods for reconstructing deformable object manipulation have made impressive progress, they typically represent a thin object with a single particle set that must serve two purposes at once: modeling bending, and resolving contact with the robot. To bridge this gap, we present HermiteTwin, a framework that reconstructs a physical digital twin of a thin deformable object from multiview video of a robot manipulating it. Our key idea is to represent deformation and contact separately, each at its own resolution. The object is simulated as a bicubic Hermite shell, a coarse grid of $C^1$ elements whose nodal positions and derivatives define a smooth surface with Kirchhoff--Love bending, while the gripper acts through dense samples in material space that are captured, clamped, and released, and whose attachment forces reach the shell through the Hermite basis. This decoupling keeps the physical state compact while contact stays fine-grained. We identify effective material and contact parameters with CMA-ES followed by adjoint-based refinement, and drive a reconstructed Gaussian appearance model with the simulated shell. In experiments on real cloth and foam manipulation, HermiteTwin outperforms the state-of-the-art spring--mass twin across reconstruction, resimulation, and future prediction.

title: DermKG: A Concept-Centric Knowledge Graph for Interpretable Skin Disease Diagnosis from Dermatological Morphology
abstract: Dermatologists describe lesions with a standardized morphological lexicon, which makes concept-based models attractive for interpretable skin disease diagnosis. How much diagnostic information these concepts actually carry, however, is rarely quantified. We present DermKG, a concept-centric knowledge graph built on the expert-annotated SkinCon subset of Fitzpatrick17k (3,230 images, 48 concepts, 113 diseases). DermKG has 3,452 nodes of 8 types and 19,365 edges of 11 relation types, and encodes disease concept profiles, concept co-occurrence, a three-level diagnostic hierarchy, and 20 clinical morphology rules, all of which are supported by the training data (15 strong, 5 moderate). An information-ceiling analysis shows that the 3,230 lesions collapse onto only 813 distinct concept vectors, bounding concept-only top-1 accuracy at 38.9\% for diseases and 77.6\% for the nine categories. Within this bound, DermKG-Net, a graph neural network that scores lesions against disease prototypes and aggregates them along the hierarchy, raises category-level balanced accuracy from 0.257 to 0.411 over the strongest of 11 baselines (paired bootstrap difference $+0.150$, 95\% CI $[0.073, 0.231]$) and more than doubles minority-category recall. Ablations show that most of this gain comes from the hierarchical prototype objective, with a smaller contribution from graph structure. DermKG further yields rule-based reasoning chains and concept-level explanations for individual predictions.

title: The Four-Cycle Extremal Number of the Seven-Cube
abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that the largest number of edges in a four-cycle-free subgraph of the seven-dimensional hypercube is 304. In a hypothetical 305-edge subgraph, three-star counting and a local computational lemma force every degree to be four or five. A square-counting identity and an inequality for opposite facets then reduce the proof to five candidate facet profiles, excluded by two further local statements. The three computational statements concern only six-dimensional cubes and are certified by 21 propositional refutations.

title: SIR-Agent: Skill-Augmented Image Restoration Agent with Recursive Self-Improvement
abstract: Agents for Image Restoration (IR) aim to leverage Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to autonomously perceive image degradation and invoke IR tools. However, existing IR agents typically rely on fine-tuning MLLM parameters to adapt to new IR tasks, leading to catastrophic forgetting of IR knowledge. To address this limitation, we propose a skill-augmented IR agent, dubbed SIR-Agent, that maintains IR knowledge in a scalable skill library and uses Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) to facilitate efficient skill-library evolution. Specifically, we design a Chain Feedback-driven Skill Revision (CFSR) to evolve the skill library. The CFSR analyzes restoration chains to identify and revise weak operations in existing skills. The compatibility of a revised skill with known tasks decides if it replaces the original skill or is appended independently. Furthermore, to advance CFSR's skill-library evolution, we present an RSI-driven skill meta-learning mechanism, which identifies CFSR's inefficient operations and autonomously refines its revision strategy. Extensive experiments across 14 IR benchmarks, covering 6 single-degradation and 8 mixed-degradation scenarios, demonstrate SIR-Agent's superior IR performance. Further evaluation on 7 unseen tasks validates SIR-Agent's generalization to new IR tasks.

title: Belief-State Management Meets Rubric Rewards for Agentic Forecasting
abstract: Current large language model (LLM) agents still struggle to forecast real-world events. This stems from two primary limitations: i) standard ReAct harness accumulates reasoning and evidence within one growing context, and ii) outcome-based rewards in forecasting lead to a slow and noisy signal that cannot distinguish sound reasoning from lucky guesses. To address these, we introduce a forecasting training framework including harness design and post-training. For the harness side, we propose Proactive Belief-State Management (PBM), equipping agents with a fold tool to compress lengthy context into compact belief states and reset the context for subsequent exploration. For the training side, we develop SEIPH, a five-dimensional, outcome-blind rubric, providing process-quality rewards. Using the rubric-based reward, we post-train a 35B model with PPO and GRPO, yielding DeepForecaster-PPO and DeepForecaster-GRPO. Theoretically, we prove that idealized fold-based stopping converges and calibrated local rewards reduce segment-level gradient variance. Empirically, DeepForecaster-PPO (35B) achieves the best Brier score on both ForecastBench and Polymarket-Sim, outperforming frontier agents based on DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1.6T), Kimi-K2.6 (1T), and GPT-5.5. DeepForecaster-GRPO ranks second on both FutureX metrics. Ablations reveal that PBM also improves the untrained base model without any training. Calibration analysis shows that DeepForecaster-PPO makes more accurate high-confidence predictions than Qwen3.6 and GPT-5.5. Trajectory analysis further shows that forecasts generally improve from the first to the final belief state as agents gather evidence and revise their judgments.

title: GRADPlace: Geometry-Based Routing-Augmented Differentiable Placement for Routability Optimization
abstract: Routability-driven placement needs gradients that show how cell movement redistributes routing demand. Cell inflation exploits routing feedback only indirectly, and differentiable methods rely on black-box congestion predictors or on virtual-cell congestion fields frozen between routing updates. We present GRADPlace, which represents probability-weighted candidate routes as movable horizontal and vertical segments. Routing feedback sets their probabilities, while their geometry and expected demand evolve with cell coordinates. An electrostatic routing objective propagates gradients through this geometry to connected cells, complementing cell inflation. On the ISPD 2015 benchmarks, our reproduced Xplace-route and published DCGP results have on average 3.37x and 2.56x as many design-rule violations as GRADPlace, with more vias and comparable routed wirelength.

title: Preserving Pretrained CFG Structure in RL for Diffusion Models with Conditional Contrast Regularization
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has become an important component in the post-training of diffusion models. In practice, however, standard RL often improves the target reward without reliably preserving holistic generation quality, leading to unstable reward-quality trade-offs that we view as a form of reward hacking. Since Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) is known to improve visual clarity, prompt alignment, and perceptual quality in generation, we investigate whether its underlying structure can serve as a useful prior during RL. We present a unified geometric view that interprets both CFG and RL as correction vectors in a common prediction space, and identify the projection of the RL-induced correction onto the pretrained CFG correction as a useful diagnostic of quality-related structural preservation. Geometric analysis and rotation intervention further show that the pretrained CFG direction carries information useful for generation quality that reward-driven RL updates do not necessarily preserve. Based on this insight, we propose Conditional Contrast Regularization (CCR), which uses the frozen reference model's conditional contrast as a local structural prior during RL. Experiments across multiple reward settings and backbones show that CCR more consistently preserves generation quality while maintaining competitive reward, yielding a better reward-quality trade-off than standard RL and generic regularization methods.

title: InterBand-EMG: A Cross-Band Foundation Model for Generalizable Hand-Pose Estimation
abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG) enables continuous hand-pose estimation, but learning representations that generalize across users and movements remains challenging. We introduce InterBand-EMG, which combines band-specific quantization with cross-band reconstruction and structured masked code prediction to learn transferable EMG representations for hand-pose tracking. We also introduce SynapMyo, an eight-channel EMG-to-pose dataset comprising 1,227.74 hand-hours from 499 users across 68 movement categories. Experiments on emg2pose and SynapMyo show that InterBand-EMG outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in joint-angle accuracy across all three generalization settings on both datasets. The source code and the SynapMyo dataset will be publicly released upon acceptance of this paper.

title: EgoLAM: Learning Latent Actions from Hand and Head Motion
abstract: Latent action models let a robot policy learn from video by turning the change between two frames into a training target. In egocentric video, a cup can move across the image because a hand pushes it or because the wearer turns. Both changes help predict the next frame, but only the first describes manipulation. During training, EgoLAM supervises the action code with measured wrist motion and supplies camera motion separately to the forward model. Even when the wearer turns while pushing a cup, the training target still describes how the hand pushed it. The action encoder pools object slots around each hand, and wrist translation and rotation can be decoded from the code in a common reference frame. Extracting a code then requires only two RGB frames. Alongside LARYBench classification and regression, we measure how much wrist motion a frozen code retains and how strongly it responds to a synthetic view or lighting change. EgoLAM has the highest hand-motion decoding score among eight evaluated models. Across three LIBERO suites, policies pretrained on its codes and fine-tuned on expert demonstrations achieve 79.38% mean success, 28.73 points above expert behavior cloning and 9.76 points above the strongest other latent action model in each suite on average.

title: Half-integrality and an upper bound for slopes of Drinfeld cuspforms of level $Γ_1(t^r)$
abstract: Let $p$ be a rational prime, let $q>1$ be a power of $p$ and let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be the field of $q$ elements. Let $k\geq 2$ and $r\geq 1$ be integers. Let $S_k(Γ_1(t^r))$ be the $\mathbb{C}_\infty$-vector space of Drinfeld cuspforms of rank two, level $Γ_1(t^r)$ and weight $k$ over $\mathbb{F}_q(t)$. In this paper, we prove that every finite $t$-adic slope of the Hecke operator $U_t$ on $S_k(Γ_1(t^r))$ belongs to $\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z}$ and is at most $k-2$. If $q$ is odd, then every such slope is an integer.

title: Two-phase visco-elastic FENE-P model: Thermodynamically consistent modeling, sharp interface limit analysis and unconditionally energy stable numerical scheme
abstract: Although mathematical modeling and numerical simulations for two-phase Newtonian flows have been extensively studied for many years, relatively little work has focused on developing thermodynamically consistent models for two-phase Non-Newtonian viscoelastic flows, and to the author's best konowledge, no structure-preserving numerical methods have been reported for such models. In this paper, we focus on modeling the two-phase non-Newtonnian visco-elastic FENE-P model based on the energetic variational approach (EnVarA). In the model, a phase-field function is introduced to describe the diffuse interface which satisfies the Cahn-Hilliard (CH) equation. And all the physical variables can be connected smoothly. We conduct a matched asymptotic analysis for the sharp interface limit, which shows the diffuse interface model will converge to the sharp interface model when the interface thickness trends to zero. We then reformulate the model in an equivalent form that facilitates the construction of the numerical scheme. A weakly decoupled scheme is proposed for the resulting FENE-P-CH system, and its unconditional energy stability is proved theoretically. Finally, a series of numerical experiments is conducted to validate the model and assess the performance of the proposed scheme.

title: A Vision-Based Framework for Manual Assembly Verification and Adaptive Operator Assistance
abstract: Manual assembly remains difficult to monitor because operator actions, components, and task progress must be interpreted together. This paper presents a modular framework based on a single overhead red-green-blue (RGB) camera, combining object detection, hand-motion tracking, region-aware interaction detection, finite-state verification, task-specific pose classification, and configurable visual guidance. The system was evaluated during pneumatic-piston assembly and disassembly with eight participants under three assistance conditions: full, mid, and no guidance. Mixed-effects analysis identified an association between assistance condition and a composite measure of motion quality, with lower estimated scores under mid and no guidance relative to full guidance. However, the condition-by-trial interaction was not statistically significant, and the estimated differences in learning trajectories remain descriptive. No condition differences were detected in completion time or failed-stage counts. The study demonstrates the integration of visual perception, procedural verification, and configurable operator feedback in a single-camera workflow. Selecting assistance according to operator expertise remains a design objective for future investigation.

title: HookEvo: A Framework for Coordinated Plugin Evolution on Hook-Enabled Agent Runtimes
abstract: Repairing failures in tool-using agents can require coordinated changes to how the harness interprets tool receipts, assembles context, and checks actions. We introduce HookEvo, a framework that uses an existing agent runtime's lifecycle hooks to evolve task-specific harnesses. We instantiate HookEvo on DeepSeek Harness. In each round, a separate improver diagnoses failures from execution traces and proposes a candidate. HookEvo evaluates the candidate against the current harness on matched tasks and carries the retained version into the next round. A single candidate can jointly edit executable plugin handlers and the state they share within a task, allowing a tool receipt to inform context and control a later action. Using a frozen Qwen3-4B executor, the selected harnesses lead the reported Qwen3-4B comparisons, achieving 95.41% on ALFWorld, 70.56% on DBBench, 48.17% on WebShop, and 41.67% on OSBench. Across three improvers and three edit scopes, from skill text to single-component and coordinated executable edits, GPT-6.1 Sol shows the largest average gain from the broadest scope. Our code is available at https://huangshengzebluesky.github.io/hookevo/.

title: Consecutive Supersymmetric Quantum Mechanical Algorithms for Resolving the Spectra of Legendre-type Differential Operators
abstract: Quite comprehensive iterative algorithms based on consecutive supersymmetric quantum mechanics (SUSYQM) have been constructed heuristically, for resolving the eigenspectra of the Legendre operator and its associates parametrized in various coordinates, \emph{without receiving any input from traditional analytical methods}. On building these algorithms, the two symmetries \text{--} supersymmetry and shape invariance symmetry \text{--} hidden in these operators are brought to the fore as the only two governing principles, with the aids of the newly devised algebraic techniques such as the \emph{active supersymmetrization transformations}, \emph{momentum operator maps} as well as plain and \emph{higher-order spin matrix maps}. In view of their algebraic simplicity and elegance, high efficiency, as well as independence of traditional methods, some of these algorithms become the promising candidates to supplant the popular power series approach to the eigenspectra of Legendre-type operators.

title: Strong Functional Observability and Strong Functional Detectability: Applications to Functional Observer Design for Systems with Unknown Inputs
abstract: This paper investigates strong functional observability, strong functional detectability, and strong$^*$ functional detectability for continuous-time linear systems with unknown inputs in both the state and measurement equations. Extending Kratz's finite algebraic approach \cite{26}, zero-output trajectories are characterized through the projected kernel of a finite matrix, without differentiating the unknown inputs. This characterization yields a necessary and sufficient rank condition for strong functional observability. For strong functional detectability, a frequency-dependent rank criterion involving only the original system matrices is derived, along with an equivalent finite test based on reduced zero-output dynamics. Strong$^*$ functional detectability is then characterized by an additional algebraic rank condition, and its relationship with the existence of stable functional observers is examined. A constructive observer design procedure based on constrained Sylvester equations is also developed. Particular cases and a numerical process example illustrate the theoretical results.

title: Chern classes, Poincaré polynomials, and Bernstein-Sato polynomials of plane curves
abstract: We show that the Poincaré polynomial of a reduced plane curve $C$ is the Chern polynomial of the dual of the bundle of Jacobian syzygies of $C$. Using the Zeuthen-Segre formula, we prove that its value at $t=-1$ equals the Euler number of the complement of $C$ up to the correction term $μ(C)-τ(C)$, so the two numbers coincide if and only if all singularities of $C$ are quasi-homogeneous. As applications, we show that the defect in a combinatorial inequality for free $d$-arrangements is the square of the difference of the exponents, extend the addition technique to arbitrary reduced plane curves, and locate the roots of local Bernstein-Sato polynomials at ordinary singular points.

title: Development and control of Görtler vortices in the SD-2 serpentine diffuser
abstract: This study investigates and controls the flow through a serpentine diffuser using wall-modeled large-eddy simulations (WMLES), with emphasis on the formation of streamwise vortices, their contribution to flow distortion, and their suppression using opposition control. Following Agrawal et al., AIAA Journal (2026), simulations are performed at three Mach numbers, $Ma_{AIP} =0.36, 0.46,0.54$. Adverse pressure gradients and centrifugal forces induced by geometric features of the diffuser promote flow separation and lead to the formation of counter-rotating Görtler vortices. Downstream of the second bend, the transition from an elliptical to a circular cross-section drives these vortices toward the centerline along the spanwise direction, ejecting low-momentum fluid from the near-wall region into the core. A steady opposition-control strategy using wall-normal velocity forcing is employed to attenuate the streamwise vortices. The control strategy increases pressure recovery, reduces flow distortion, and substantially suppresses total-pressure fluctuations across all three Mach numbers. The maximum flow distortion is reduced by $\approx 50\%$ at the two lower Mach numbers and by $34\%$ at $Ma_{AIP}=0.54$. The variance of the total-pressure fluctuations is reduced by approximately two orders of magnitude near the center of the AIP and by a factor of two near the periphery. An input-output power analysis further shows a net positive power gain at all three Mach numbers, with a maximum control efficiency of approximately $65\%$ at the lowest Mach number, although the power efficiency decreases significantly at higher Mach numbers due to the larger actuation amplitudes required.

title: Re-JEPA: Coupling Representation Prediction and Signal Reconstruction for State-Conditioned EMG Tracking
abstract: Improving continuous hand tracking from surface electromyography (sEMG) requires generalization across users and motion types while maintaining sensitivity to subtle movements. Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn latent representation spaces through contextual prediction, but their effectiveness for tracking depends on which motion-relevant details these representations preserve and how those details are interpreted as the hand state evolves. We introduce Re-JEPA, a tracking framework that couples representation prediction with signal reconstruction and incorporates state-conditioned motion decoding. During pretraining without kinematic labels, Re-JEPA predicts continuous latent targets at multiple levels from visible EMG patches and reconstructs masked amplitude and phase attributes from the fused predictions. Signal reconstruction imposes an additional constraint on the contextual predictor, encouraging its outputs to retain information needed for signal recovery. For downstream tracking, the Gated Persistent Motion (GPM) decoder conditions EMG-token readout on recurrent state tokens and motion history, then generates continuous trajectories through gated state updates and incremental pose prediction. Under the emg2pose tracking protocol, Re-JEPA reduces angular MAE after full fine-tuning by approximately 10.3%, 19.3%, and 14.9% relative to vemg2pose on the cross-user, cross-stage, and joint cross-user-stage splits, respectively.

title: Symplectic Matroids, Stabilizer Codes, and Quantum Secret-Sharing
abstract: An $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear $[[n,k]]_q$ stabilizer code is represented by a totally isotropic subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$ of dimension $n-k$, whose full-rank generator matrix has nonzero maximal minors on admissible column sets forming the bases of a representable symplectic matroid. Sarvepalli asked whether graphical symplectic matroids introduced by Chow give stabilizer codes with good parameters, when a Lagrangian matroid induces a quantum access structure, which code realizes it, and which polynomial carries the weight enumerator. We answer these questions. For a $3$-connected simple graph, every representation of a graphical symplectic matroid, over any field, gives a stabilizer code of distance exactly $2$, so the girth is not a lower bound. For a represented Lagrangian matroid and a dealer, we construct the dealer-shortened stabilizer code, its logical operators, an encoding isometry and explicit recovery maps, and we show that this is the code implemented by the stabilizer state through teleportation. A set of players recovers the secret, learns nothing, or learns part of it according to a rank formula on pairs of columns, which equals its mutual information with the dealer; for graph states it becomes a cut-rank condition. Over $\F_2$ a symplectic matroid of any rank has only one representation, so the code, its access structure and its weight enumerators depend on the matroid alone; for $q\ge3$ even the enumerator does not. Circuit-induced authorized sets always reconstruct when the matroid is self-dual, but not in general, and a six-qubit graph state shows that the two access structures can differ even then. Finally, a polynomial in the ranks of column pairs determines both weight enumerators.

title: Observed, Curated, Reused: Observation Bias in Clinical AI Evaluation
abstract: Clinical AI evaluations are vulnerable to observation bias embedded in routine medical documentation, which captures only what clinicians notice, test, and record rather than a complete clinical picture. As this evidence travels into publications and reference knowledge graphs, crucial distinctions disappear: unexamined symptoms blur with confirmed negatives, and chronological disease progression is lost. Surviving evidence can also enter both the benchmark query and the reference knowledge base, creating a self-referential loop where a patient is evaluated against clues derived from their own published case report. To quantify this bias, we tracked 6,503 clinical cases across six historical Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) releases (October 2021-June 2026) to identify when HPO first cited the publications describing them. This yielded a confirmatory cohort with an observable "source ingestion" event, where HPO cited a case's source publication as target-disease evidence. Diagnostic rankers depended heavily on these source publications: for our primary semantic ranker (Resnik), publication-weighted mean reciprocal rank rose from 0.26 before paper ingestion to 0.84 upon inclusion in HPO, but collapsed to 0.05 when source-linked assertions were counterfactually removed. Two additional rankers (IC-cosine and LIRICAL) reproduced this trajectory, and control experiments confirmed the diagnostic jump was driven by the patient's publication rather than background HPO growth. Clinical AI systems may therefore score well because their knowledge base contains evidence linked to the test case's source publication, rather than through generalization. Modern knowledge is not the problem; evaluation evidence must match the claim. Trustworthy benchmarks must separate patients, source-linked evidence, and time: historical tests should use only knowledge available at the intended decision time.

title: Can Reasoning and Image Description Enhance Yes/No Visual Mathematical Understanding?
abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on general visual tasks, yet their ability to understand mathematical images remains limited. This paper investigates whether explicit reasoning and textual image descriptions can enhance VLMs' performance on binary yes/no visual mathematical questions. To achieve this, we curated a paired evaluation set to benchmark prominent open-source VLMs under varying prompt and input conditions. In particular, we leverage Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting and use textual descriptions, either replacing or augmenting visual inputs, to isolate and evaluate mathematical comprehension. Our results show that explicit reasoning improves performance, especially in paired consistency accuracy, while textual image descriptions do not consistently help and may degrade performance. These findings suggest that reasoning is important for stable visual mathematical judgement, whereas description-based intermediates require more careful design.

title: Interstellar extinction estimates for nearly 90 million stars based on synthetic photometry from Gaia XP spectra
abstract: Accurate stellar extinction measurements are essential for recovering intrinsic stellar properties and investigating the three-dimensional distribution of interstellar dust. We present reddening estimates for 87,270,425 stars using synthetic SMSS gri photometry derived from corrected Gaia DR3 XP spectra, combined with Gaia BP and RP, 2MASS JHKs, and WISE W1 photometry. Stellar extinction is determined through empirical SED fitting based on reference stellar loci constructed separately for dwarfs and giants. Comparisons with three external extinction catalogs show good overall agreement, with dispersions of 0.049-0.075 mag in E(B-V). The catalog covers approximately 99.99% of the sky. Using stars with sigma_d/d < 0.2, we further construct reddening maps in four distance ranges from 0 to 5 kpc, revealing prominent molecular clouds and large-scale Galactic dust structures. Extinction-corrected color-absolute-magnitude diagrams show significantly tighter stellar sequences and consistent red-clump features in different Galactic fields. The resulting catalog provides a homogeneous data set for stellar extinction correction and studies of Galactic dust structure.

title: PepDeTech: Anonymous Occupancy Monitoring on a Battery-Powered 2.3k-Zone dToF LiDAR Node with On-Chip Processing and Bluetooth LE Reporting
abstract: As populations grow, society is increasingly required to shift towards systems of shared resources, which allow space, energy and time to be optimised. Facilitating this transition depends on data: how many people are present, when and where. From such information, schedules can be organised more efficiently and resources allocated where they matter. At the same time, privacy concerns and energy consumption limit deployment: cameras are frequently unacceptable, while simpler sensors miss people and cannot provide the full picture. This paper presents PepDeTech, a compact, battery-powered occupancy node that combines a 54 x 42-zone direct Time-of-Flight (dToF) Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) (VL53L9CX) with a Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) System on Chip (SoC). Three deterministic algorithms, background subtraction, motion history and a track lifecycle, run on-chip and count the people simultaneously, providing real-time occupancy monitoring. No trained model is involved, and setup takes less than a minute. Over three scenarios, background subtraction reaches a per-frame +-1-person accuracy of 83.6 % (mean absolute error (MAE) 0.70 persons), tested with up to five people present. At a 30 s interval the node draws only 3.1 mW, lasting 60 d on a 1200 mA h cell. Several weeks of deployment on a single charge make the node usable as a survey instrument for facility management: a room can be characterised for a measurement campaign without cabling, network provisioning or a camera, and the resulting occupancy record is what ventilation, lighting, cleaning and space-allocation decisions are argued from, ultimately resulting in more efficient resource allocation.

title: ManipScope: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Instruction Following and Generalization in Robotic Manipulation
abstract: Completing a manipulation task does not establish that a robot follows the requested goal rather than a familiar routine. ManipScope is an evaluation-only diagnostic benchmark for robotic instruction following under changed task requirements. Built on RoboTwin 2.0's simulation resources, it specifies 48 held-out scenes across six task families with explicit source-task links; policies are trained on unmodified RoboTwin 2.0 demonstrations, and no demonstrations of the scenes are provided, so success requires reusing skills under a changed request rather than fitting supplied examples. Beyond task success, ManipScope provides a chain of diagnostics in which each step tests one explanation of a failure. For twelve policy checkpoints, 84.6% of failures in 13,200 episodes on eleven selection scenes displace a distractor, and gripper records show that failed episodes usually grasp a non-target. When the target is reassigned among the candidates on identical initial states, ten checkpoints follow every instruction on 3.9% of 1,000 states, below the 16% of an instruction-blind chooser, while a GPT-6 agent run as positive control reaches 88%. The failure recurs on unmodified training tasks and is not explained by missing manipulation skills, so success in these scenes largely reflects instruction-independent preferences; two checkpoints trained on the same data nevertheless follow color instructions. In a feasibility test, letting an agent select the target and the policy execute partly restores instruction following. Case studies with future-video and internal-intervention probes further show that forecasts and execution can agree on the wrong target and that action changes need not transfer the goal. Success, consistency, and sensitivity must each be checked against the requested goal.

title: $γ$-Scape: An Agent-Centric World for Mobile Embodied Intelligence
abstract: Recent embodied agents construct and adapt robot behavior through executable programs, tool use, and interaction feedback. Studying these systems in mobile manipulation calls for physical worlds that connect agent-directed execution with its physical consequences and reusable interaction experience. We introduce $γ$-Scape, an agent-centric simulation and benchmark platform for mobile embodied intelligence. Agents compose motion tools and learned skills to carry out complete tasks that combine navigation and manipulation in a persistent physical world. BenchForge grounds structured objectives in physical task instances with instructions, reference programs, and goal evaluators, defining task goals while preserving agents' choice of valid solutions. An agentic collection harness further enables agents to produce demonstrations by carrying out contact-rich interactions through sustained control and physical feedback. Assisted reference execution and human guidance provide complementary experience. The resulting tool traces and aligned observation-action records support program refinement and policy learning, with common task-goal criteria for subsequent evaluation. We benchmark representative agent systems on complete tasks and demonstrate contact collection and trace-informed program revision. Together, these workflows provide infrastructure for research on embodied recursive self-improvement.

title: Numerical tests of 5D APS $η$-invariant phases for 4D chiral fermions
abstract: We calculate the phase of a 4D chiral fermion determinant from the 5D Atiyah--Patodi--Singer (APS) $η$-invariant. We study the anomaly-free $SU(5)$ representation $\mathbf{10}\oplus\overline{\mathbf 5}$ on a four-torus, using gauge fields independent of one coordinate. For these backgrounds, the 4D phase can be calculated independently from a 3D Dirac spectrum. For an Abelian background embedded in $SU(5)$, two different 5D bulk extensions reproduce the 4D phase within $0.03\%$ in the tested heat-kernel extrapolations. One extension changes the spatial gauge field along the fifth direction and requires a coupled 5D spectral calculation. An independent single-charge check reproduces the Chern--Simons anomaly coefficient within $0.3\%$ using quadratic extrapolations. We also calculate 5D APS phases for non-Abelian backgrounds in the $SU(4)\times U(1)$ subgroup. For a background generating the full $\mathfrak{su}(4)$ algebra, the 5D phase with a fixed spatial field agrees with the independent 4D phase within $0.5\%$ over the six heat-kernel parameters examined. We further study a varying-field 5D extension for an embedded $SU(2)$ background. These results show that the 5D APS calculation reproduces a nonzero chiral phase after anomaly cancellation.

title: Frontier Voltage Boost Laplacian Path Planning
abstract: This paper introduces Frontier Voltage Boost Laplacian path planning. The method inherits many of the attractive features of earlier Harmonic Potential Field planning methods, including absence of local minima and smooth paths, while improving the original. The piecewise approach we introduce is able to solve larger maps and handle narrow passages more quickly than earlier Harmonic Potential Field methods. After explaining the algorithm, we experimentally characterize its cor- rectness, performance, and path smoothness as a function of map size. Code is available at https://github.com/vpritamani/FrontierVoltageBoostLaplacianPathPlanning

title: Stochastic Differential Equations on the Simplex
abstract: We propose a framework for simplex-valued diffusion processes, formulated as solutions to stochastic differential equations driven by antisymmetric Brownian motion. Our edge-wise representation includes the multivariate Jacobi processes and the general class of continuous simplex-valued polynomial diffusions. Also, it allows bounded, locally Lipschitz state-dependent drift rates and edge weights. We establish weak solutions, as well as global strong existence and pathwise uniqueness for strictly positive initial states under a sufficient boundary non-attainment condition.

title: The geometric expansion of the coarse trace formula of GL(4)
abstract: We study the non-semisimple terms in the geometric side of Arthur's trace formula of $\rm{GL}(4)$ for the further study of the invariant trace formula. After modifying the zeta function and Arthur's definition of the weighted orbital integrals, we compare the two ways to calculate the distributions $J^T(f)$ of the geometric side, we can obtain that the distributions can be written as the linear combanition of the weighted orbital integrals. In particular, we get the coefficients $a^M(S,γ)$, for all $γ\in \rm{GL}(4,F)$, expressed by the measure and zeta functions.

title: Composite Dielectric-Loaded Metallic Metagratings for Dual-Polarized Transmissive Beam Manipulation
abstract: We present and experimentally demonstrate a comprehensive analytical suite for the design of transmissive metal-based metagratings (MGs) for dual-polarized anomalous refraction. Considering a composite configuration of perforated metallic slabs with controlled dielectric loading, we develop a rigorous mode-matching formulation tying the various MG degrees of freedom to the various reflected and transmitted Floquet-Bloch modes, enabling efficient beam deflection for both transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) polarizations. Inherently versatile, the analytical framework accurately models single-layer and double-layer constructs with multiple rectangular perforations per unit cell, each potentially loaded with dielectric material. We harness this degree-of-freedom abundance to devise diverse polarization-sensitive transmissive MGs, ranging from all-metallic single-layer and double-layer structures for single-polarized (TM or TE) perfect anomalous refraction, to dielectric-loaded architectures implementing dual-polarized routing of the incident wave. Beyond highlighting concrete paths to address TE-polarized fields in such formations, our results, validated via full-wave simulations and experiments at K band, showcase the great potential of metal-based MGs for manipulating fields in transmission, facilitating effective synthesis of durable dual-polarized beamforming superstrates for environmentally demanding and high power antenna applications.

title: A Geometric Approach to the Classification of Locally-APN Niho-Type Power Functions
abstract: Let $q=2^m$ with $m\geq 2$. We develop a geometric approach to the classification of locally-APN Niho-type power functions over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. Our approach begins with a characterization of $\mathbb{F}_q$-homogeneous functions: the conditions $D_F(a,F(a))=q$ and $D_F(a,b)\leq 2$ for every $a\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^*$ and $b\neq F(a)$ hold if and only if the projective graph of $F$ is a $(q+1)$-arc in $\mathrm{PG}(3,q)$. For Niho-type power functions, this differential condition is equivalent to the locally-APN property. Applying the classification of $(q+1)$-arcs and the description of their stabilizers, we prove, for $m\geq 3$, that $F_s(x)=x^{s(q-1)+1}$ is locally-APN if and only if $s\equiv(2^k+1)^{-1}\pmod{q+1}$ for some $1\leq k\leq 2m-1$ satisfying $\gcd(k,m)=\gcd(2^k+1,q+1)=1$. Together with the known case $m=2$ and the sufficient condition of Xie et al., this gives the complete classification and confirms the conjecture of Cui, Luo, and Xiang.

title: A Framework for AI-Ready Data in Earth and Environmental Science
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), specifically machine learning (ML), is increasingly integral to Earth and environmental research, yet the suitability of current research data infrastructures for supporting AI workflows remains poorly defined. While the FAIR principles provide a foundation for scientific data management, they do not explicitly address several requirements arising when datasets are used for training, evaluating, and deploying AI models. This article presents a practically motivated framework for assessing and improving AI-readiness of research data within distributed Earth and environmental data infrastructures. The framework was developed through a structured, community-driven process, beginning with a review of existing literature and readiness frameworks combined with feedback from a limited survey of scientists applying ML methods. Its main aspects were shaped by a multidisciplinary expert group representing data providers, infrastructure developers, data managers, and AI practitioners. It identifies 25 criteria covering data preparation, data quality, documentation, access, and supervised learning targets. The criteria emphasize aspects particularly relevant to AI applications, including provenance, treatment of missing data, bias documentation, uncertainty characterization, machine-actionable metadata, efficient access formats, and the quality and reproducibility of target generation. Application to a broad range of representative environmental use cases highlights how the relevance of individual criteria varies by application. We argue that AI-readiness should be understood primarily as a property of transparency and fitness for purpose rather than as a fixed level of data quality. The framework lays a foundation for communication and community-driven action to advance AI-ready data and support next-generation AI-enabled scientific workflows.

title: Electronic Wichmann-Kroll correction to the energy levels of muonic hydrogen-like atoms
abstract: Using modern multiloop calculation methods, we obtain correction to energy levels of muonic hydrogen-like atoms due to the leading-order ($\proptoα(Zα)^3$) Wichmann-Kroll electronic potential. Our result is expressed in terms of generalized polylogarithms. As a byproduct, we also obtain the Wichmann-Kroll potential in momentum space in terms of the same functions.

title: Smoothed Conformal Testing with Small Calibration Sets
abstract: A small calibration sample restricts split conformal $p$-values to a coarse rank grid. Randomization removes this discretization, but its effect depends on both the smoothing interval and the allocation of auxiliary random variables. Independent tie-block randomization is exactly valid under null exchangeability. When calibration and null scores are jointly exchangeable conditional on the alternative scores, we prove positive regression dependence and hence Benjamini--Hochberg false discovery rate control, including for atomic score distributions. Smoothing over calibration-dependent rank cells agrees with tie-block randomization when calibration scores are distinct and no test score ties a calibration score, but can fail marginal validity with atoms. Assigning sorted random draws according to score order can invalidate even a single null $p$-value. An exact two-test example violates the usual $π_0α$ bound, and simulations with continuous scores exhibit false discovery rates above the nominal level $α$. Finally, conditional moment identities and normal-model illustrations show that removing the rank grid does not remove calibration uncertainty. Randomization can produce additional discoveries, including when ordinary conformal testing cannot reject at all, but it does not generally substitute for a larger calibration sample.

title: BioCL-POS: Biological Completer-aware Learning with Predictive Observation Selection - A Wild Ginseng Study
abstract: Growers and traders rely on root morphology to assess wild ginseng, yet breakage can obscure important structural traits. We study point cloud completion to provide geometric references for morphological analysis. Does providing more observed points always improve 3D completion? We test whether selected subsets improve recovery of the original missing region while keeping the pretrained completer fixed. We introduce BioCL-POS, an external selector that predicts how the completer responds to candidate inputs. For each candidate, we predict the displacement and distance from shared spatial locations to the nearest points in its completion. We use these spatial responses to estimate recovery quality and supervise them with measurements from actual completions. At inference, we select an input from the observed geometry and run the completer once. We evaluate four frozen completers on controlled gaps in ginseng and tree data at 5%,10%, and 20% omission, and examine 30% omission on ginseng. At 5--20% omission, we outperform full-input completion and all five alternative selectors on both datasets with all four completers. We achieve lower mean reconstruction error and higher mean F-score and coverage. We thus show that selecting observations can improve geometric recovery without retraining the completer, providing more accurate geometric references for subsequent morphological analysis.

title: Do Language Models Know Which Words Steer Their Reasoning?
abstract: While chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting elicits intermediate reasoning steps from language models, it is unclear which words in the context actually steer the CoT. We identify Phantom Context Influence (PCI): language models are disproportionately steered by semantically irrelevant context words, even as the same models deny those words' relevance when asked. To localize PCI, we introduce Leave-One-Out Word JSD analysis, which removes one context word at a time from the otherwise intact context to isolate its marginal effect on the next-token distribution; words whose removal flips the prediction (pivot words) are passed to the same LLM to self-judge whether it recognizes this predictive dependence. Across four models and three benchmarks, language models largely do not know which words steer their reasoning, a mismatch we call the Generation-Judgment Contradiction. Inspired by this phenomenon, we propose Online KV Suppression: it scores every prompt word's influence over the whole chain of thought in a single pass, then zeroes the KV-cache entries of the highest-influence word the model itself judges inert and redecodes. This single-word intervention improves CoT accuracy across four models and five reasoning benchmarks, by up to 8.9 percentage points on math reasoning benchmark.

title: Conservative Implicit and Explicit Solvers for Reactive Conformable Transport with Multirate Memory
abstract: In this article, we analyze conservative implicit and explicit schemes for reactive transport with a conformable time scale and multirate exchange. The conformable derivative defines a local change of time coordinate, while exchange with immobile regions supplies the memory. Positive Gauss--Jacobi quadrature approximates the prescribed exchange spectrum by finite compartments. Both schemes use conservative finite-volume fluxes. Forward Euler gives the explicit update; backward Euler initializes the implicit second-order backward differentiation formula (BDF2). Eliminating the compartment states reduces each implicit step to a tridiagonal system. Under stated mesh and regularity conditions, we prove implicit solvability, conditional explicit positivity and stability, and discrete mass balance. A cell-average error estimate separates spatial, compartment and temporal contributions. Its proof accounts for the boundary fluxes and the BDF2 startup error. Source-specific bounds make the temporal and memory prefactors uniform under mesh and compartment refinement. For a broader positive-history model, continuous residual estimates have coefficients independent of memory strength and kernel mass. Local coercivity gives a sharper coefficient. Manufactured tests recover second-order spatial convergence, first-order Euler convergence and second-order BDF2 convergence. Separate experiments examine the memory and combined estimates. In a prescribed porous-medium application, the finest numerical states differ by $3.57\times10^{-5}$ in relative space--time $L^2$. Independent resolution checks support the computed pulse attenuation, immobile storage and release after injection ends.

title: SAVIOR: Sample-efficient Adaptation of Vision-Language Models for OCR Representation
abstract: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) pipelines and vision-language models exhibit high accuracy on standard OCR and document-understanding benchmarks, yet they systematically underperform on document patterns that are operationally critical in financial workflows. These patterns include vertical or rotated text, logo-embedded vendor names, fine-print regulatory clauses, degraded scans, and complex multi-column layouts. While underrepresented in public datasets, they constitute a substantial portion of real-world failure cases. We introduce SAVIOR, a sample-efficient data curation methodology that targets such high-impact failure scenarios to adapt vision-language models for robust financial OCR. We further propose PaIRS, a structure-aware evaluation metric that measures layout fidelity by comparing pairwise spatial relationships between tokens. Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-VL-Instruct with SAVIOR-Train achieves a word recall of 0.93. When the resulting layout-aware OCR output is used as context for document question answering, it attains an F1 score of 0.89, outperforming both open- and closed-source models such as GPT-4o, Mistral-OCR, PaddleOCR-VL, and DeepSeek-OCR.

title: Bring Cloud-Native Networking to FreeBSD Jails: Porting Calico from Linux
abstract: While Linux containers benefit from a rich ecosystem of Container Network Interface (CNI) plugins such as Calico and Cilium, FreeBSD Jails lacked native, standardized solutions for advanced networking. As a result, users have relied on manual, error-prone configurations, limiting scalability and integration with modern orchestration platforms. This paper introduces porting Calico, a widely adopted CNI plugin, to the FreeBSD operating system. Our approach replaced Linux-specific components with FreeBSD-native equivalents: iptables with ipfw, netlink sockets with routing sockets, and Linux network namespaces with FreeBSD's vnet. This work aims to bridge the gap between Linux and BSD container networking. By providing scalable, policy-driven capabilities that are compatible with existing Linux-centric infrastructure, FreeBSD can participate more fully in the broader container networking ecosystem.

title: Gap-label bounds and optical reconstruction of Landau-subband quantum geometry
abstract: We derive a magnetic gap-label lower bound on the internal quantum weight of Landau subbands that remains nonzero even when the occupied Chern number vanishes. Using the second fundamental forms of nested subbundles to decompose the quantum geometric tensor, we isolate the constraint imposed by the uniform parent curvature and show that the excess quantum weight above the bound equals twice the weaker circular transition weight. For a noninteracting parabolic band with a periodic scalar potential, Landau-level mixing preserves the integrated relative curvature while the occupied direct gap remains open. Nevertheless, uncorrected sub-cyclotron absorption need not satisfy the projected bound. Using exact circular-dipole relations, we reconstruct the low-frequency guiding-centre weight and signed dichroism from circularly polarized absorption. This reconstruction removes the first-order orbit-polarization contribution. For an insulating filling of an isolated lowest-Landau-level-derived cluster, a potential-gradient estimate bounds the omitted remote-transition weight quadratically at weak coupling. This yields a finite-window lower bound on reconstructed quantum weight and bounds the deviation of reconstructed dichroism from the integrated relative curvature.

title: Spiking Neural Networks Incrementally Track Firing-Rate Networks
abstract: Understanding how spiking neural networks (SNNs) efficiently process data streams is key to (i) studying how biological brains conserve energy for lifelong predictions and (ii) enabling efficient continuous AI inference. In this work, we propose a theory on how an SNN incrementally tracks its corresponding firing-rate network, a continuous-valued neural network (ANN). We prove that the output of a discrete SNN continuously tracks the instantaneous ANN output implicitly determined by the SNN input. Based on this principle, we develop LIF-Stream, a conversion framework for efficient SNN inference over unbounded data streams. It enables the converted SNN to reuse its prior activation state and compute only the activation updates between frames, thereby reducing the average number of time steps needed per frame. Specifically, LIF-Stream controls the SNN to continuously track the reference ANN output, which gives a high-accuracy prediction for every frame. Evaluation on three large-scale streaming inference benchmarks with distinct modalities shows that LIF-Stream achieves the best efficiency-accuracy trade-off compared to high-accuracy SNN techniques.

title: Cruella: A Unified Microscaling and Floating-Point Dot-Product Unit for LLM Inference on FPGAs
abstract: The number formats that accelerators execute natively are fixed at fabrication, yet large language model (LLM) checkpoints are released with MXFP4 weights in the Microscaling (MX) formats standardized in 2023. FPGAs adopt new formats through bitstreams. However, to the best of our knowledge, no deployed FPGA LLM accelerator executes MXFP4 weights alongside BF16 products. We characterize the decoding of MXFP4 checkpoints, whose layers alternate between MXFP4$\times$BF16 products and BF16$\times$BF16 products of attention and BF16 layers. With a BF16 KV cache, BF16$\times$BF16 products take 56%-77% of the datapath time, during which a separate MXFP4 unit idles. We present Cruella, whose unified dot-product unit (UDPU) executes both product types on one DSP array and reduction pipeline. First, per-group pre-alignment keeps this pipeline at the BF16 width and changes perplexity by at most 0.7%. Second, pre-adder packing places two signed MXFP4$\times$BF16 products in one DSP48E2 multiplier with an exact correction. On an Alveo U55C, the UDPU needs 23% fewer DSP slices and 36% fewer LUTs than separate MXFP4 and BF16 units of equal throughput. On this board, MXFP4 weights speed up decoding by 1.15$\times$-1.87$\times$ over BF16 weights, and an NVIDIA A40 GPU decodes faster but spends 0.92$\times$-2.01$\times$ the board's energy per token.

title: A resolution-based framework for coherent and decoherent jet energy loss in NLO pQCD
abstract: We investigate the role of medium resolution and color decoherence in jet energy loss in high-energy heavy-ion collisions. Within an NLO pQCD framework, implemented using NLOJet++, we calculate inclusive jet production in $pp$ collisions and extend the calculation to $AA$ collisions by incorporating nuclear PDFs, Glauber geometry, and medium-induced jet energy loss in the Higher-Twist formalism. To account for the finite resolution of the QGP, we introduce a sequential coherent clustering procedure based on the pairwise invariant mass of final-state partons. The resulting coherent clusters act as independent color sources when resolved by the medium, with the transition governed by an effective resolution scale $Q_{\rm med}$. We validate the coherent clustering procedure using PYTHIA simulations and investigate the nuclear modification factors of inclusive jets, reclustered jets, soft-drop $r_g$, and jet mass in Pb+Pb collisions at $s_{NN}=5.02$ TeV. Comparison with the ATLAS measurements yields $Q_{\rm med}=10-20$ GeV. While coherent energy loss alone systematically underestimates the observed suppression at high jet $p_{\rm T}^{\rm jet}$ and fails to reproduce the substructure dependence of jet quenching, incorporating decoherent energy loss provides a consistent description of these observables. Our results demonstrate that accounting for the medium's ability to resolve jet substructure is essential for a consistent description of jet quenching in heavy-ion collisions at the LHC.

title: A fast automatically adaptive integral equation solver for nonlinear two-point boundary value systems
abstract: We present a fast, high-order, automatically adaptive integral-equation solver for nonlinear two-point boundary value systems. The method builds on the fast direct solver for linear second-kind integral equations and completes the mathematical formulation needed for general boundary conditions, including cases in which the simplest background Green's function is singular and cases with genuinely rank-deficient boundary conditions. Nonlinear problems are written as nonlinear second-kind integral equations and are solved by combining this fast adaptive linear solver with Newton iteration and user-specified continuation. In this way the nonlinear solver inherits the full strengths of the linear integral-equation method: a fast direct solver, arbitrary order accuracy, and automatic adaptive resolution with only a small overhead over a solve on the final mesh. The resulting algorithm is particularly effective for problems with localized or multiscale structure, including boundary layers, dense oscillations, transition regions, hypersensitive optimal-control systems, and singular perturbations. The same framework also provides a computational foundation for future studies of bifurcation and solution-branch exploration.

title: Reasoning in Fewer Tokens: Concept-Normalized Multilingual Scratchpads and Reversible Model-Adaptive Reasoning Codes
abstract: Chain-of-thought prompting significantly improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) but incurs high inference costs due to lengthy autoregressive decoding. While previous efficiency approaches reduce costs by discarding tokens or utilizing continuous latent representations, these lossy methods fundamentally sacrifice interpretability and auditability. In this work, we introduce a novel compression framework for intermediate reasoning. We apply Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) to reasoning corpora to learn a compressed vocabulary of Private Use Area (PUA) tokens, each representing frequent semantic spans. After expanding the LLM's vocabulary, we fine-tune the model via strictly 1:1, our method is lossless. We evaluate our approach on Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-14B, and Qwen2.5-32B across four diverse benchmarks. Our method reduces total generated tokens by 14.7% on average with reasoning trace lengths dropping by up to 27.1%, while incurring a negligible average accuracy cost of 1.6 percentage points. Crucially, this approach is orthogonal to existing lossy methods, allowing practitioners to stack lossless and irreversible compression techniques. We demonstrate that a compressed intermediate language provides a highly efficient computational resource that accelerates inference while fully preserving the transparency of LLM reasoning.

title: Embodied Interaction Policy: A Unified Model for Full-Duplex Human-Robot Interaction
abstract: Real-time human-robot social interaction requires continuous coordination between speech and physical behavior. Existing systems often separate interaction agents from motion generation, complicating coordination as conversational states change. We propose \textbf{Embodied Interaction Policy (EIP)}, a unified streaming framework that couples an Audio-Interaction expert with a motion expert through layer-wise joint attention. This allows motion generation to directly access the evolving interaction context. A chunk-wise causal mask prevents access to future context, while a vocal token encodes speaking state and the semantic emotion of the response. We construct \textbf{Embodied Interaction Dataset (EI-Data)} from co-speech and dyadic interaction data and train our model in two stages to learn state-adaptive and emotion-conditioned behavior. Combined with the frozen interaction expert, EIP supports continuous robot motion during proactive responses and interruption-aware turn-taking. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate improved motion quality over representative gesture-generation baselines. Compared with a representative cascaded system, EIP achieves higher interaction success and reduces warm-start latency by 64\%. Physical deployment and user studies further demonstrate improved motion naturalness and interaction comfort.

title: 60-cm-long In-vacuum Zerodur Optical Cavity for Optical Lattice Atom Interferometry
abstract: Optical cavities are widely used in atomic physics experiments to control the spatial geometry and spectral properties of atom-light interactions. Recently, an optical lattice generated by the pristine mode of an optical cavity was utilized to hold and extend the quantum coherence of atomic spatial superpositions. Here, we describe an in-vacuum optical cavity designed to enhance the spatial and temporal coherence of optical lattice atom interferometers to one millimeter wavepacket separations and one minute measurement durations. The cavity uses a rigid Zerodur spacer to suppress the negative effects of thermal drift and mechanical-acoustic vibrations on the atomic motional state. The 60 cm-long cavity spacer provides ample optical access for the laser beams and imaging optics necessary for the preparation, quantum control, and read-out of the atomic state, as well as room for various source mass configurations for localized gravitational measurements. An integrated differential pumping structure enables compatibility with ultrahigh-vacuum operation and optical interferometry allows for in-situ vibration monitoring. The performance of the optical cavity is methodically characterized: we measure mirror vibration noise with amplitude below 5 nm/$\sqrt{\rm Hz}$ in a wide frequency range of 2 Hz - 100 kHz and a slow 15 MHz thermal drift of the cavity resonance over 47 hours, which can be readily stabilized with an integrated piezo. The optical cavity supports both 852-nm light for Raman transitions and 1064-nm light for the optical lattice, with a free spectral range matched to an integer divisor of the cesium ground-state hyperfine splitting.

title: H-MSAE: Hierarchical Sparse Concept Coverage for Efficient and Diverse Instruction Data Selection
abstract: Large instruction-tuning corpora contain substantial semantic redundancy, motivating the selection of compact subsets that preserve useful supervision while reducing training cost. Existing diversity-aware selectors often rely on generated semantic tags and explicit graph structures, introducing considerable annotation and preprocessing overhead. We introduce H-MSAE, a hierarchical sparse instruction selection framework that organizes multi-resolution concepts learned by a Matryoshka sparse autoencoder into a coarse-to-fine hierarchy. Quality-weighted, diminishing-return coverage with ancestor propagation promotes high-quality and non-redundant semantic coverage, while pool-relative length constraints regulate subset composition. We motivate this design through a local quality-diversity analysis of subset SFT utility and examine it using example-quality and representation-space diversity diagnostics. On Tulu 3 data pool, H-MSAE achieves the highest Final Avg among the evaluated 50K selectors across scales and initialization. The selected subset also exhibits the highest mean quality and effective rank among the evaluated methods. By avoiding full-pool generative tagging and supporting efficient sparse selection, H-MSAE reduces measured end-to-end runtime by approximately $5\times$ relative to MIG.

title: GGDriver: Glance at What Is Shared, Gaze at What Differs for Perception-Free Planning
abstract: A planner deciding whether to turn left or continue straight needs to inspect different parts of the scene for each maneuver. Yet many end-to-end driving planners evaluate every candidate trajectory against the same compressed scene representation. We let each candidate select the visual evidence used to refine and score it. A global glance first produces trajectory hypotheses from shared scene features. We then project a corridor around each trajectory into the camera views and use the resulting mask to attend to patch features at the backbone's native resolution. After refinement, the scorer projects each final proposal again and ranks it using evidence along its own path. This geometric selection requires only the predicted trajectory and camera calibration. On three planners with different scene representations (learned registers, a perception-supervised bird's-eye-view grid, and a coarse image-token grid), adding this gaze improves planning scores. In ablations, path-aligned patches outperform both a matched number of randomly selected patches and attention over all patches. Using the gaze for ranking yields larger gains than using it for refinement alone. With a ViT-S backbone and no perception labels, GGDriver achieves a rater feedback score of 8.110 on the WOD-E2E test set, 94.2 PDMS on NAVSIM-v1, 48.6 EPDMS on NAVSIM-v2, and a closed-loop Driving Score of 72.18 on Bench2Drive.

title: The non symmetric Hikita conjecture
abstract: We construct local and global comparison maps for the Hikita conjecture in quiver gauge theories and study their analogues for finite non symmetric Cartan pairs. The construction uses quiver Hecke description of Coulomb branch and microlocal geometry. It yields comparison maps from B-algebras to the cohomology of some Lagrangians of quiver varieties. For arbitrary symmetric types, the local and global comparison maps are surjective and are isomorphisms under a B-algebra dimension bound. In finite non symmetric types, the local image is the image of the Kirwan map, i.e., the tautological subalgebra. It can be proper. Under some assumptions we also construct a non symmetric global comparison map. Crystal theoretic methods identify the set of nonempty Lagrangians with the set of isomorphism classes of simple modules of the category $\mathscr O$ of the Coulomb branch, and proves that the Lagrangians are nonempty for $\ell$-dominant $\ell$-highest weights. The proof uses microlocal modules of Coulomb branches that we define. We prove they form integral bases of the Grothendieck group of the category $\mathscr O$, with Jordan-Hölder multiplicities given by characteristic cycles. In symmetric type we prove an isomorphism between based quasimap modules at homogeneous polarized points of quiver varieties and co-specialized microlocal modules. The proof uses hyperbolic restriction and Braden's theorem. We conjecture an extension to all homogeneous points and a relative version.

title: Thermal photon production in massless boost-invariant gases: hydrodynamization without thermalization
abstract: We study hydrodynamization and thermalization in ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions using relativistic kinetic theory.
