An example over Z/4 shows that chain generation cannot be dropped. A chain system over Z/8 with short exact rows, whose maps commute only up to homotopy, shows that homotopy-exactness cannot be weakened to distinguished triangles in the derived category. Under finiteness conditions the model is finitely generated. The proof combines a derived horseshoe lemma with induction over the lattice, and yields a short proof and extension of Franzosa's connection matrix theory.

title: Metadata-Private Voice Communication over Tor using Post-Quantum Key Encapsulation
abstract: Encrypted voice communication systems commonly protect call content but expose significant metadata, including the network identities of both parties, call timing, and traffic patterns. Simultaneously, advances in quantum computing threaten the asymmetric primitives underlying conventional key exchange, creating a harvest-now, decrypt-later risk for long-lived sensitive communications. Existing systems address at most one of these concerns: secure VoIP applications such as Signal and Wire rely on centralized infrastructure and classical cryptography, while anonymous communication tools built on the Tor network support only text messaging and lack post-quantum key encapsulation. This paper presents SAPEC (Secure Anonymous Peer Exchange Communicator), a peer-to-peer voice communication system that simultaneously addresses anonymity, decentralization, and quantum resistance. SAPEC routes all traffic exclusively through Tor hidden services, concealing the IP addresses of both parties, and augments the standard TLS handshake with a custom protocol layer that performs ML-KEM-1024 key establishment, a settle on AES-256 symmetrical keys and mutual Dilithium identity verification before any audio is transmitted. All audio is subsequently encrypted under AES-256. A removable Crypto Ignition Key prevents identity key material from being stored on the device. Empirical evaluation across 45 independently circuit-rebuilt test runs yielded a median one-way audio delay of 355 milliseconds and a median connection setup time of 7.61 seconds on same-region Tor circuits, demonstrating that interactive voice communication over onion routing is practically achievable.

title: Decision Columns as an Index: Interpretable Embeddings for Explainable Entity Matching and Search
abstract: Business data systems must determine whether records refer to the same entity and retrieve records satisfying requests whose decisive properties are implicit. As agents act on these records, both tasks require auditable reasons. Dense embeddings perform well but offer opaque coordinates, cannot be filtered by meaning, and require corpus re-encoding to add new properties. We propose interpretable embeddings built from decision columns: each column stores a decision model's calibrated answer to a natural-language question, with outcomes yes, no, or not stated. A record's embedding is its answers across an ordered set of questions. Similarity decomposes exactly into per-question contributions, and new questions add coordinates without altering existing ones. On public product benchmarks, question-space retrieval matches dense candidate generation statistically in a retrieve-then-verify entity matcher, while providing exact explanations for accepted matches. Questions derived from retrieval failures triple mean reciprocal rank without re-encoding prior answers. For search, inferring the attributes of a suitable result outperforms encoding only the literal request, and combining question-space and dense scores improves retrieval, though not at our prespecified confidence threshold. A single small neural network predicts the full interpretable vector from an existing dense embedding, enabling corpus backfilling from a few thousand labeled rows at roughly 1/200 the cost. We position interpretable embeddings as a complementary, readable retrieval channel for explaining matches, filtering on attributes, and extending indexes as failures expose missing facts.

title: Functional Depth Is Learned: Isolating the Computation That Layers Produce Only Together
abstract: Transformer performance scales with depth, but layer count merely counts the opportunities for sequential computation: layers could still behave as nearly independent refinements that barely depend on one another. We study how transformers develop functional depth during pretraining, introducing an exact inclusion-exclusion decomposition that isolates the connected component, i.e., the computation that appears only when a specified set of layers acts together under identity ablation. Tracking this quantity across public checkpoints of Pythia, OLMo, and Amber yields three findings. First, write-relative connected coordination strengthens from its initialization or earliest-checkpoint baseline as pretraining proceeds, across all measured interaction orders. Second, these connected components are behaviorally consequential under direct intervention: deleting them damages perplexity more than deleting a norm-matched random direction at the same site in all 35 measured model-order cells. Third, pairwise representation similarity is consistently negatively correlated with pairwise connected coordination across seven models, yet the two signals are not interchangeable: similarity- and coordination-based block-removal criteria often agree in Pythia but diverge on Amber. Together, these results suggest that architectural depth provides the opportunity for sequential computation, while pretraining progressively organizes cross-layer dependencies within that depth.

title: Submanifolds, restriction of differential operators and Schouten-Nijenhuis bracket
abstract: In this article, we present new formulas for restricting the Hodge operator, the codifferential and the Hodge Laplacian to a submanifold. These formulas are concise, thanks to the use of tools for differential forms (Schouten-Nijenhuis bracket and generalized interior product). They also facilitate explicit calculations for practical applications.

title: Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances
abstract: Detecting individual instances is crucial for many segmentation problems. However, expert instance annotations are often unavailable, so instances are approximated heuristically (e.g., as connected components of semantic maps), which can merge touching objects or split fragmented ones. Even when expert annotations exist, expert disagreement or structural delineation biases can yield split or merged reference instances, corresponding to over- or under-segmentation, respectively. Panoptic Quality (PQ) and related metrics capture both segmentation and detection quality while weighting all instances equally, regardless of size. Yet when the references are biased, these metrics can neither detect split or merged instances nor distinguish valid from invalid overor under-segmentation. We present Star Panoptic Quality (StarPQ), a novel evaluation ramework, which closes this gap in two steps: First, we construct a so-called star forest in the bipartite graph whose clean, merge, and split stars isolate different failure modes. Second, we calculate the final metric by individually weighting each failure mode, allowing practitioners to account for instance delineation biases. Across various experiments, we demonstrate that StarPQ not only enables targeted penalization or eniency towards specific failure modes, but also serves as a diagnostic tool to reveal their prevalence.

title: The moments and asymptotic spectral distribution of the Grassmannian ensemble
abstract: In this paper, we study random density matrices constructed by taking partial traces of projections onto random subspaces of a bipartite Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B}$ distributed according to the pushforward measure of the action of the unitary group on the Grassmannian $\text{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B})$. This ensemble models a `typical' quantum subspace. All tracial moments of the density operator, as well as mixed tracial moments of reduced density operators, are computed explicitly using Weingarten calculus. There are several consequences of these results. In particular, we prove that the empirical spectral distribution of the density operator converges almost surely to a rescaled Marchenko-Pastur law. We also prove that this ensemble can be written as a sum of asymptotically free random density operators, leading to an alternative proof of the convergence of the spectral distribution. Finally, we compute the asymptotic expansion of the average entanglement entropy.

title: StereoVLM: Binocular Vision-Language Models for Metric 3D Spatial Reasoning
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong semantic understanding but remain limited in their ability to reason about metric 3D space in the physical world. Existing VLMs typically infer 3D scene structure from one or more images without known camera calibration or cross-view geometric constraints. This makes metric 3D inference inherently ambiguous and leaves it unclear whether their spatial predictions are grounded in visual evidence or driven primarily by semantic priors. In contrast, calibrated stereo provides explicit cross-view geometry that resolves this ambiguity and offers a more reliable foundation for metric 3D perception and geometric generalization. We investigate how VLMs can learn transferable 3D representations directly from calibrated binocular observations. To this end, we introduce StereoVLM, the first geometry-aware binocular VLM for metric 3D spatial reasoning. StereoVLM follows a hierarchical learning paradigm spanning from cross-view correspondence and disparity estimation to calibration-conditioned metric depth perception and semantic spatial reasoning. We further find that disparity supervision generalizes substantially better than direct binocular depth supervision on unseen environments. To evaluate these capabilities, we introduce Stereo3D-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark across three levels, from point-level geometry to object-level spatial reasoning. StereoVLM-8B achieves 95.17% depth accuracy ($δ_1$) and a 66.98 average object-level score on Stereo3D-Bench. Intervention results further indicate that the model's performance on Stereo3D-Bench benefits from valid cross-view geometry and cannot be explained solely by additional visual tokens or semantic priors. Hierarchical geometric supervision also yields average gains of 3.54 points across five spatial benchmarks and 4.3 percentage points in RoboCasa manipulation success.

title: Large orbits of $p$-groups on conjugacy classes of arbitrary finite groups
abstract: Let $P$ be a $p$-group that acts faithfully and coprimely on a finite group $H$. In a previous paper it was shown that if $H$ is solvable, then there exists a conjugacy class $c$ of $H$ whose stabilizer in $P$ has order at most $|P|^{1/2}$, and that this bound is best possible. In this paper we remove the hypothesis that $H$ is solvable. As a consequence, there always exists an irreducible character of $H$ whose inertia group in $P$ has order at most $|P|^{1/2}$. The proof depends on the classification of finite simple groups. Its main new ingredient is a result on quasiprimitive linear actions of $p$-nilpotent groups which shows that the elements acting as field automorphisms can be ignored when one looks for vectors with small stabilizers. We also present a new family of examples, with nonsolvable $H$, in which the bound is attained.

title: Augmentation of cardiovascular flow measurements with generative diffusion models
abstract: Cardiovascular imaging offers several ways to measure blood flow, but each provides an incomplete, resolution-limited, or noisy view of the underlying dynamics. Reconstructing the missing information is inherently ambiguous because several flow fields may be compatible with the same observation. Here, we investigate generative diffusion models as tools for cardiovascular-flow generation and reconstruction using a fully controlled state-of-the-art dataset from a digital twin of a healthy human left heart. First, we show how unconditional samples reproduce the changing anatomy and the highly fluctuating statistical properties of the flow throughout the cardiac cycle. Second, we test the conditional inference of our generative model by reconstructing an entire 2D planar section of geometry and flow configurations from a limited portion. Repeated reconstructions allow us to represent a range of plausible completions, going beyond a single deterministic estimate, while their mean retains the principal features of the reference flow. Comparison with a Gaussian process regression baseline on the same reduced domain highlights the main advantage of diffusion models: their reconstructed ensembles capture a broader range of velocity and gradient fluctuations, better encompassing ground-truth features that the baseline distributions can miss. Our results provide a quantitative proof of concept for probabilistic reconstruction of incomplete cardiovascular-flow measurements and demonstrate the potential for groundbreaking applications to the augmentation of in-vivo cardiovascular imaging data.

title: The Benefit of Migration in Throughput Maximization on Unrelated Machines and under Restricted Assignment
abstract: In preemptive throughput maximization on parallel machines, jobs have release dates, due dates and weights, and the goal is to maximize the total weight of the jobs completed by their due dates. We study the benefit of migration, i.e., by what factor the optimal weight can increase when a preempted job is allowed to resume on a different machine. By a classic result of Kalyanasundaram and Pruhs, on identical machines the migratory optimum is at most $O(1)$ times the nonmigratory optimum. We give, for the first time, bounds for unrelated machines and for restricted assignment. We show that on unrelated machines, when every eligible machine can complete a job by itself, the migratory optimum is at most $O(\sqrt n)$ times the nonmigratory optimum, where $n$ is the number of jobs. Under restricted assignment it is at most $O(\log n)$ times the nonmigratory optimum. We provide instances which show that both bounds are best possible up to constant factors, even when the jobs have unit weights. Since our proofs are constructive, we obtain the first nontrivial approximation algorithms for migratory throughput maximization on unrelated machines and under restricted assignment.

title: SUAF: Spectral Universal Advantage Features for Zero-Shot Policy Improvement
abstract: Reward-independent representations enable reinforcement learning agents to reuse knowledge across tasks, but limited representation capacity raises three fundamental questions: what statistical dependence should these representations capture, which components of that dependence should be retained for policy improvement, and how does discarding the remaining components affect decision-making? We address these questions through canonical dependence analysis. For a reference policy, we construct an action-centered, positive-lag canonical dependence matrix (CDM) that isolates the additional predictive contribution of the current action beyond the current state. Its singular value decomposition yields Spectral Universal Advantage Features (SUAF), paired features that recover delayed advantage through linear reward projections. We show that the spectrum quantifies mutual information between current action and future state-action visitation conditioned on current state and determines reward specific approximation errors. Retaining the leading modes gives optimal rank-constrained approximations under both isotropic average-case and reward-uniform minimax criteria. Separating the immediate reward contrast also avoids the spectral floor arising from direct compression of the full advantage operator. To learn SUAF from reward-free data, we develop an action-centered Soft-HGR objective with bidirectional temporal-difference estimation. We further connect spectral approximation errors to sufficient conditions for policy improvement. Finite-state experiments validate the spectral predictions and feature-learning method, while zero-shot evaluations on discrete tasks and continuous-control benchmarks demonstrate the utility of the learned representations across rewards.

title: Autonomous Parameter Surgery: How LLMs Implant Selective Backdoors into Language Models
abstract: Neural network weights are usually treated as opaque artifacts of gradient descent. Recent work on weight space programming, however, suggests that large language models can inspect and rewrite another network's parameters directly. In this paper, we ask whether a general language model can turn a natural language backdoor specification into persistent, selective weight edits on its own, without gradient training, layer hints, external corpora, or a prescribed editing formula. Using DeepSeek Flash at low reasoning effort inside a restricted workspace that blocks local CPU simulation, we test three open models (Qwen3.5-0.8B, Llama-3.2-1B, SmolLM3-3B) across two review domains (IMDb and Yelp; 18 independent sessions). Evaluated in fresh processes with the editor removed, the modified checkpoints reach 99.2% mean attack success on the editing domain and 97.6% transfer success on the unseen domain, while preserving clean accuracy, low control drift, and general capabilities within 1.7 points of the base models. Our traces show that the model converges on edits in the final layer in 17 of 18 runs and discovers both dense rank-one orthogonalization and single neuron weight surgery at an average cost of \$1.74 per run.

title: ESSI: Computationally Efficient Semantic Search for Sparse Autoencoder Concepts
abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) decompose diffusion model activations into interpretable features, but steering a model with them requires identifying which features map to a given semantic concept, if any. Existing methods for this concept to feature task are expensive, relying on grid searches or repeated passes through the frozen UNet. We propose Efficient Semantic Sparse Identification (ESSI). Using segmentation masks to label SDXL activations as concept or non-concept, ESSI ranks SAE features and binary-searches for the smallest set on which a linear classifier still separates positive from negative samples while not falling below a performance threshold, then reuses that classifier to calibrate the steering strength. We evaluate the same selected features on both concept insertion and object unlearning. Compared with prior work, ESSI is as cheap or cheaper, and performs well on both insertion and removal.

title: Sharp Last-Iterate Bounds for the Stochastic subGradient Method
abstract: We determine the worst-case expected optimization error of the last iterate of constant-stepsize projected Stochastic subGradient Method on convex Lipschitz objectives. The upper and lower bounds match up to universal constants for every stepsize, horizon, dimension, and conditional noise moment of order $p\in[1,\infty]$. With bounded noise and a fixed positive bound on the initial distance to a minimizer, the best constant stepsize gives worst-case error after $n$ iterates of order $1/\sqrt n$ on the line and $\sqrt{\log n/(n\log\log n)}$ in every fixed dimension at least two.

title: The Fiscal and Economic Implications of Green Mandates: a Boltzmann Approach to Public Governance
abstract: Public authorities increasingly need to translate multifaceted policy objectives into concrete fiscal and investment choices while accounting for their socioeconomic consequences. A credible ex-ante impact assessment should report downstream implications attributable to the historical baseline and specified policy targets, without introducing discretionary assumptions about unknown administrative, socioeconomic or other physical processes. Bringing the large-scale perspective of statistical physics to public governance, we construct such an ex-ante impact assessment. Its scope encompasses policy objectives that condition a finite number of generalized moments of observables in the historical baseline, which comprises a sufficiently large collection of projects or public programmes. As a proof-of-principle application, we consider the green transition in the energy-generation sector using the historical baseline of many infrastructure projects from the World Bank. Our earlier results deriving closed-form expressions for coarse-grained combinatorial probabilities enable a tractable statistical and downstream assessment. We assess the statistical compatibility of the historical baseline with different levels of green-power surplus and demonstrate how the same statistical-physics construction can estimate any downstream metric expressible through arbitrary functions of generalized moments of the baseline observables. In the absence of more detailed knowledge about the processes forming the historical baseline, large-scale universality, whenever many unknown influences on collective phenomena become negligible, unambiguously offers a principled route to a self-contained ex-ante impact assessment.

title: BioEmu2: Scalable Emulation of Biomolecular Dynamics
abstract: Despite major advances in structure prediction, modelling the motions and interactions that drive biomolecular function at scale remains a central challenge. We introduce BioEmu2, a generative model for atomically resolved biomolecular structures combining static structure prediction, equilibrium sampling and time evolution, that samples orders of magnitude faster than molecular dynamics (MD). Trained on experimental and synthetic structures and extensive MD data, it supports multi-component systems containing proteins, nucleic acids, modified residues, ligands and ions. Structure-prediction accuracy is comparable to top open-weight biomolecular folding models, and a context parallel mode enables prediction of megadalton complexes. Equilibrium distributions approximate MD references with free-energy errors near 1 kcal/mol across tested proteins and complexes. Time propagation predicts long-timescale dynamical trajectories and kinetics of binding and conformational changes. Generated structures can be controlled by conditioning on residue contacts or steering with user-defined bias potentials. Enhanced sampling enables free energy calculation involving rare states. BioEmu2 makes the study of biomolecular ensembles and dynamics scalable.

title: The Thurston algorithm for general entire maps on the complex plane: Existence and uniqueness
abstract: We prove that a marked topological entire Thurston map $(f,A)$ of stable parabolic type is Thurston equivalent relative to $A$ to a postsingularly finite entire function if and only if it has no Levy cycle relative to $A\cup\{\infty\}$. Here $A$ is a finite forward-invariant set containing the postsingular set. In the realizable case, the entire function is unique up to complex affine conjugacy, and every orbit of the Thurston pullback converges to its fixed point. We establish a Wolff--Denjoy type estimate for nonexpanding self-maps $T$ of the Teichmüller space of any connected orientable surface of finite type without boundary. If $T$ has an unbounded orbit, there are a nonzero measured foliation $G$ and a constant $C$ such that $\operatorname{Ext}_{T^k x}(G)\le C\operatorname{Ext}_x(G)$ for every $x$ and $k\ge0$. For a fixed-point-free transcendental Thurston pullback, this supplies the foliation used in the existence proof. A central tool is a fixed finite measure obtained as the total-variation limit of renormalized pushforward measures transported back along a Teichmüller ray. It allows us to select a cylinder at a late time and compare the mass of the same marked region at different times. If $G$ has a cylinder, a four-point extremal-length estimate and the Thurston matrix force a Levy cycle. Otherwise, in the absence of a Levy cycle, cluster rescaling shows that cylinders of large modulus carry almost all the fixed measure at all late times. Following a cylinder of definite mass until its modulus decreases gives a contradiction. We compare this geometric argument with the proofs for real entire maps and exponential maps.

title: A quasi-tree expansion of the Homfly polynomial
abstract: The Homfly polynomial is one of the best-studied invariants of oriented links. Here, building on work of Jaeger and others, we present a new method of computing it. Terms in the expansion are algebraically simple and they are indexed by certain quasi-trees of the Seifert graph of an (almost) arbitrary link diagram. The quasi-trees, in turn, depend on a single basepoint along the link but no more auxiliary data. This allows us to streamline the proofs of some old results and to find new ones as well, such as an upper bound on the total degree in terms of directed joins of the Seifert graph.

title: Transpilation-Aware Multi-Vendor QPU Scheduling with Predicted Post-Transpilation Fidelity
abstract: Cluster schedulers already choose nodes, GPUs and accelerators for submitted workloads, enforce quotas and spread load. QPUs from several vendors are now schedulable resources in the same clusters, yet the user still names the device, usually the one with the best average fidelity. For a given circuit that choice is often wrong: compiling onto each device's qubit connectivity adds gates, so a job can meet its required success probability on one device and miss it on another with similar error rates, and checking this exactly by compiling for every candidate is too slow for a scheduling decision. We let the scheduler choose the QPU in two stages. A training-free estimate predicts, in milliseconds and without compiling, the success probability on every candidate and filters out those that would miss the requirement; only the chosen device then compiles the circuit, re-checks it, and binds the job or rolls back. The estimate matches compiling every candidate at about 25x lower latency in simulation, ranks measured success on IBM hardware as well as the post-compilation estimate (Spearman rho = 0.95), reduces requirement violations from tens of jobs to a few, and avoids them under contention without piling jobs onto one device. Across vendors it works when error rates are comparable (IBM and IQM) and fails when published figures overstate a device.

title: From Giant Vortex States to Bright Solitons in Rapidly Rotating Bose--Einstein Condensates with Attractive Interactions
abstract: We study the ground state of a Bose--Einstein condensate (BEC) with attractive interaction of strength $ a_Ω$, confined by a two-dimensional anharmonic trap rotating at angular velocity $ Ω$. We prove the occurrence of a phase transition, as $ Ω\to\infty $, from an annular giant vortex state to an angularly localized bright soliton. More precisely, we distinguish three regimes according to the relative sizes of the radial and angular concentration scales. In the weak coupling regime $ a_Ω= \mathcal{O}(Ω^{-1/2}) $, the limiting angular profile is governed by a variational problem on the unit circle showing rotational symmetry breaking: below a given sharp threshold, the condensate remains uniformly distributed in the annulus and has a giant vortex profile with a vortex-free bulk and macroscopic circulation; above it, rotational symmetry is broken. In the intermediate coupling regime $ Ω^{-1/2} \ll a_Ω\ll 1 $, the condensate localizes at a point on the unit circle with radial and angular widths of order $ Ω^{-1/2} $ and $ a_Ω\sqrtΩ)^{-1} $, respectively. After rescaling, the limiting profile factorizes into the ground state of the one-dimensional harmonic oscillator in the radial variable and a one-dimensional bright soliton in the angular variable. In the regime $ a_Ω= a \in (0,a^*) $, corresponding to stable attraction below the collapse threshold $ a^* $ both the radial and angular widths are of order $ Ω^{-1/2} $; consequently, the limiting profile is no longer a product but rather a genuinely two-dimensional localized state.

title: Optimal High-Dimensional Martingale CLTs over Rectangles
abstract: We prove Gaussian approximation bounds over rectangles for high-dimensional martingale sums, with lower bounds showing optimality up to powers of $\log n$. The results cover bounded increments, conditional and marginal sub-Gaussian and sub-exponential tails, and uniform $q$th-moment bounds on the largest absolute coordinate for $2<q\le3$. The predictable quadratic variation $Q$ may be random; the comparison Gaussian has deterministic covariance $Σ=\mathbb{E}Q$. We assume $Σ_{jj}=1$ and $\max_j\sum_k|Σ_{jk}|^s\le M$ for fixed $s>0$ and $M\ge1$, allowing $Σ$ to be singular, and quantify the error due to $Q-Σ$. Conditional tail bounds yield the same dimension threshold as boundedness, whereas marginal tail bounds give smaller thresholds. We also establish necessary and sufficient conditions for uniform convergence in all these classes; under the uniform moment assumption, the criterion holds for every fixed $q>2$. When $Q=I_d$, the bounded and marginal light-tail rates have no additional factors in $\log n$ if $\log(ed)\ge\{\log(en)\}^2$; the same holds for the finite-moment rates with $2<q\le3$ in every dimension, for all sufficiently large $n$.

title: A Coats-Based Formulation for Multiphase Reactive Transport Accounting for Aqueous Phase Disappearance
abstract: As part of the energy transition, underground hydrogen (H2) storage in porous media has emerged as an alternative solution for large-scale energy storage to salt caverns. Assessing the feasibility of such systems and ensuring their operation requires accurate modeling of the geochemical processes that may alter the composition of the stored gas. This results in a highly nonlinear coupled system of partial differential equations, ordinary differential equations, and algebraic constraints, calling for robust and specialized numerical strategies. In this work, we adopt a Globally Implicit Approach (GIA), as sequential solution algorithms are known to introduce splitting errors due to the decoupling of flow and geochemical processes. In addition, most splitting-based methods implicitly assume the persistent presence of the liquid phase, an assumption that may be violated during gas injection or withdrawal owing to aqueous phase vaporization and mineral precipitation in the vicinity of wells. We extend Coats' formulation to multiphase reactive transport with a rigorous and fully implicit management of aqueous phase disappearance and reappearance. The proposed approach introduces new molar concentration unknowns for basis species that track the re-appearance of the aqueous phase and guarantee the nonsingularity of the Jacobian matrix. Additionally, the appearance of the liquid phase is managed using a multiphase flash calculation algorithm. The proposed algorithm is validated against the CO2 storage benchmark problems. Finally, the approach is applied to an underground H2 storage in an aquifer under cyclic injection and withdrawal conditions.

title: DiTraR: Diverse Scorers and Transcript-Guided Re-ranking for Video Corpus Moment Retrieval
abstract: Video corpus moment retrieval asks a system to find, in a large collection of untrimmed videos with subtitles, the video and the time interval that a natural-language query describes. We find that most top-ranked errors of a strong corpus-level scorer come from choosing the wrong video, not from imprecise boundaries, and that re-weighting the evidence the scorer already uses does not fix them. We present DiTraR, which addresses video selection from two complementary directions. A witness-interval scorer decomposes the query into probes and scores every candidate interval of every corpus video exactly; a multi-scorer energy ensemble averages the energies of independently trained scorers before one exhaustive search; and a transcript verifier, a frozen language model that reads the time-stamped dialogue of the highest-ranked videos, re-orders the moments without changing their boundaries. With all settings frozen on development data and a single evaluation, DiTraR reaches 24.36 and 13.55 R@1 at IoU 0.5 and 0.7 on the TVR validation split. The ensemble improves queries about visual content, the verifier improves queries about dialogue, and their gains largely add up.

title: Interactive Semi-Parametric On-Track Learning for Vehicle Dynamics in Autonomous Racing
abstract: Autonomous racing requires an accurate vehicle dynamics model near the limits of handling, yet a mismatch between the nominal and actual dynamics inevitably remains. To reduce this mismatch, existing methods learn from on-track data, i.e., data collected while the vehicle drives on the track under racing conditions, by adapting the physical parameters of the nominal model or by learning a residual that captures the remaining mismatch. However, these on-track learning methods typically handle either the physical parameters or the residual separately, which restricts their ability to resolve the mismatch. To address this limitation, we propose an interactive semi-parametric learning framework that learns both the physical parameters and the residual under a single shared prediction-error objective. Since updating one changes the learning target of the other, they are recursively updated in turn, each guided by the other's latest update. Each update is then accepted only if it does not increase the shared objective, so that the objective is guaranteed to be non-increasing and convergent over the recursion. Numerical simulations and hardware experiments show that the proposed framework outperforms the baselines. Compared with the nominal model, it reduces the one-step prediction errors of lateral velocity and yaw rate by 90.0% and 81.6% in simulation and by 54.0% and 59.4% on hardware.

title: Mammalian gonadal development: origins, specification and differentiation of ovary and testis cell lineages
abstract: Testicular and ovarian development requires the coordinated formation and assembly of multiple cell types that enable these organs to fulfill their roles in sexual differentiation, reproduction, and endocrine function. A defining feature of gonadal development is that both testes and ovaries arise from a common bipotential primordium, the genital ridge, composed of multipotent progenitors. In this Review, we synthesize current knowledge on the origin, specification, differentiation, and function of the major fetal gonadal somatic lineages, drawing primarily on mouse and human studies. We describe how the adrenogonadal primordium (AGP) gives rise to the gonadal primordium (GP), how coelomic epithelium-derived progenitors generate the supporting, steroidogenic/stromal, and supporting-like cell lineages, and how these progenitors become progressively fate-restricted. We highlight recent evidence for early lineage priming within spatially organized domains of the coelomic epithelium. We further examine the molecular pathways and cellular processes governing sex-specific differentiation of these lineages and discuss remaining gaps in our understanding of how bipotential gonads differentiate into testes or ovaries, and their implication for human health.

title: The Power of Sampling for Finding Far-Apart Bases in Matroids
abstract: We study the geometry of matroids via the \emph{diameter} and \emph{dispersion} of the metric space of their bases. Given a matroid $M$, we ask if the diameter of its basis-exchange graph $\mathcal{G}(M)$ can be approximated by sampling two uniformly random bases. As our main result, we show that their expected distance is always at least $1/16$ of the diameter of $\mathcal{G}(M)$. While this might appear to follow from the edge-expansion properties established by Anari, Liu, Gharan and Vinzant (STOC'19), we show that this inutition is false by constructing a graph $G$ with edge-expansion at least $1$ for which sampling two random vertices does \emph{not} give a constant-factor approximation to its diameter. We turn to finding $k\geq 2$ maximally-diverse bases of a matroid, the $k$ (max--min) diversity problem. When $k=2$, the problem is solvable via matroid intersection. However, for $k\geq 3$ no polynomial-time approximation or hardness is known, even for diverse spanning trees. We show that sampling $k\geq 3$ bases provides a tight $Θ(\log k)$ approximation. We then combine structural insights about the local density of $\mathcal{G}(M)$ with classical LP-rounding techniques to obtain a polynomial-time $1/6$-approximation algorithm for the $k$-diversity problem in arbitrary matroids, the first constant-factor polynomial-time approximation for max--min diversity on any matroid. A key ingredient for our result is the \emph{Farthest Matroid Basis} problem: given a collection of bases, find a new basis as far as possible from all of them. We give a polynomial-time $1/3$-approximation algorithm for this, which is our main algorithmic primitive for $k$ max--min diversity. We also show it is $W[1]$-hard when parameterized by the optimal distance. We also improve the $1/6$-approximation for $k$-diversity, for partition matroids and graphic matroids of constant arboricity.

title: Ehrhard-Type inequalities for radial measures
abstract: We study Ehrhard-type inequalities for convex sets under rotationally invariant probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge2$, described by a radial density profile $φ$. We give sufficient conditions on the profile that apply to Gaussian and multivariate Student measures, including the Cauchy measure, and to a family of mixtures of two Student measures. We also prove necessary conditions on the profile and its tails. Together, these conditions determine the exact parameter range for this mixture family and characterize the rotationally invariant stable measures satisfying the inequality.

title: Star Triangulations
abstract: We study full triangulations of planar point configurations consisting of $n$ points in convex position and one point in the interior, assuming that no three points are collinear (star configurations). Our main contribution is a classification of the star configurations up to combinatorial equivalence. We show that there are $2^{n-1}-n$ equivalence classes, by establishing a bijection between a star configuration and a particular Young diagram. By transforming each such Young diagram to a binary sequence, we manage to also give a combinatorial description of the orbits of these star configurations under the dihedral group action, encoding each such orbit through a black-and-white bracelet. For each star configuration, we derive an explicit formula for the number of its full triangulations, expressed in terms of Catalan numbers and the parts of the associated Young diagram. Additionally we derive a formula of these full triangulations expressed only in terms of Catalan numbers and the bead structure of the associated bracelet. Finally, we let the points move freely under the restriction that they stay in a star configuration and show that there exist $\binom{2n-3}{n-3}$ topologically distinct full triangulations.

title: Intervals of limit points for $B_α$-spectral radii
abstract: For a finite simple graph $G$, let \[ B_α(G)=αA(G)+(1-α)L(G)=(1-α)D(G)+(2α-1)A(G),\qquad 0\leq α\leq 1. \] We study the limit points of the spectral radii of these matrices. Put $a_α=1-α$, $b_α=|2α-1|$, and $w_α=a_α+b_α$. We prove that, for every $α\neq 1/2$ and every integer $d\geq 3$, the interval \[ \left[a_αd+2b_α\sqrt{d-1},\,w_αd\right] \] consists entirely of $B_α$-limit points. All these points are realized by connected bipartite graphs of maximum degree at most $d$. We extend the induced-subgraph interpolation of Alon and Wei from $A$ to $aD+bA$, and obtain a unified proof using bipartite Ramanujan graphs. Consecutive intervals overlap for large $d$; hence the set of $B_α$-limit points contains a half-line for every $α\neq 1/2$. At $α=1/2$, one has $B_{1/2}=D/2$, and the set of spectral radii is discrete. Combining uniform edge subdivisions with generalized Bethe decorations, we improve the Laplacian and signless Laplacian half-line to $[29/5,\infty)$, verified by an exact rational certificate. We also treat two complementary tree constructions. For the starlike trees $T_{1,m,m}$, the limiting $B_α$-spectral radius is the unique solution above the path threshold of an explicit unsquared equation. More generally, letting selected arms of a starlike tree tend to infinity produces ordered limit points with tree realizations. Finally, we give the exact affine relations among $B_α$, the $A_β$-matrix, and the deformed Laplacian. These identify which tree and caterpillar results are reparametrizations of earlier work. The interval theorem also yields half-lines of $A_β$-limit points for every $0\leβ<1$, and of deformed-Laplacian limit points for every nonzero deformation parameter.

title: Group-III doping of the p-type oxide SnO
abstract: Al-, Ga-, and In-doped tin monoxide (SnO) films were grown by molecular beam epitaxy. Hall measurements reveal acceptor character of all investigated group-III dopants in SnO, which correspond to theoretical calculations and previous experiments for Ga and In, but contradicts theoretical calculations predicting donor character for Al in SnO. Doping concentrations of 10e18-1e22 cm-3 were tested and maximum hole concentrations of 2e19, 3e19, and 1e19 cm-3 with doping efficiencies of 3 percent, 9 percent, and 1 percent were found for Al, Ga, and In, respectively. The observed doping limit in the mid e19 cm-3 aligns with the limits observed in literature for different dopants, hinting to fundamental aspects of the SnO defect chemistry. Due to the unexpected Al acceptor behavior, we hypothesized Al1+ being present instead of Al3+. To stabilize the higher Al3+ oxidation state, another sample series of Al-doped SnO was grown in an oxidizing atmosphere. Despite the oxidizing atmosphere, these samples showed p-type character. A more complex defect chemistry is thus expected to explain the Al acceptor character.

title: What Must a Model Tell a Planner? Outcome Interfaces for Risk-Aware Planning After Robot Damage
abstract: When a robot is damaged, it must decide which routes it can still afford, and the amount of risk it may accept can change from one mission to the next. We argue that whether a learned model helps such a robot depends on its decision interface, that is, on what the model hands to the planner. A decision policy tells the planner what to do, whereas an outcome model, a kind of world model, predicts the consequences of each route. We study simulated Unitree Go2 quadrupeds and H1 humanoids with weakened motors, added payloads, or reduced foot friction. We compare four interfaces. The first is a decision policy, and the second is the same policy trained with fixed penalties for infeasible routes. The third is an outcome model that predicts the feasibility and travel time of each route. The fourth, which we call a capability contract, is an outcome model that predicts the chance of success and the travel time of the robot on each terrain and composes them along a route. All share the same collected experience, matched tuning and risk calibration, and an uncertainty guard. Two comparatively low-risk probes let the capability contract rank hazardous terrains about as well as four new trials on every hazard. At a calibrated 5% limit on selecting empirically infeasible routes, outcome models cut declined missions from about 32% to 7-8% on Go2 and from 57% to 35-36% on H1 compared with the plain policy. Fixed penalties narrow this gap, but the best penalty changes with the risk target. Predicting outcomes lets the planner preserve missions by changing routes as risk requirements tighten.

title: Well-posedness and finite-time breakdown for Euler-alignment systems with diffusive chemotaxis
abstract: We investigate a recent class of pressureless Euler systems arising in biological contexts, in which the velocity evolution is driven, besides the nonlocal alignment interaction, by the gradient of a concentration self-produced by the population. We first establish local existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, in a class requiring no spatial derivative of the initial population density, together with a continuation criterion. We then derive sufficient conditions on the initial data for finite-time breakdown in the multidimensional setting, with an explicit upper bound for the maximal time of existence. Numerical simulations complement the analysis and illustrate the transition between regular and singular regimes, and the role of the chemotactic strength in the onset of blow-up.

title: Effects of sinusoidal pitch amplitude and phase on power extraction and pitching-energy exchange in a single-blade vertical-axis turbine model
abstract: Sinusoidal blade pitching can improve vertical-axis turbine performance, but whether a blade could follow the same motion passively depends on the energy exchanged through pitching. This study experimentally examines 480 prescribed-pitch conditions using a single-blade model following a circular trajectory in a water channel at four tip-speed ratios (TSRs) from 1.25 to 3.14. The amplitude associated with the highest measured power decreases from 16° to 12° and then 8° as TSR increases, with the corresponding phase shifting from 0 to pi/4. At TSRs of 1.25 and 3.14, the cycle-averaged power coefficient increases from 0.0047 to 0.1037 and from 0.4698 to 0.5948, respectively. Pitching-energy maps show nearly neutral net hydrodynamic pitching work for the highest-performing motions at the two lower TSRs and net energy transfer from the flow to pitching at the two higher TSRs. Virtual damping narrows the positive-energy region, although the higher-TSR best-tested motions retain an energy surplus at nonzero damping. However, net energy transfer from the flow to pitching also occurs for motions with substantial power losses. At the lowest TSR, phase-resolved force measurements and particle image velocimetry link the gain to delayed dynamic-stall-vortex formation and shedding, prolonged favorable loading, and reduced subsequent negative power. At the highest TSR, the flow and loading change locally, with little alteration of the main power-producing event. The joint maps identify performance-enhancing motions with an energetic margin against assumed dissipation, providing candidates for further passive or assisted pitching studies.

title: A Microwave-Photonics Formulation of the Rydberg-Atom Receiver
abstract: The performance of Rydberg-atom receivers is seldom stated as a radio-frequency (RF) link budget. The receiver is shown to be an intensity-modulated direct-detection analog optical link whose modulator is the laser-driven vapor. The transmission of a warm vapor is derived in closed form by averaging the four-level response over atomic velocities. The conversion gain, noise figure, bandwidth, intercept points, and spurious-free dynamic range follow from this one function. For a weak probe the instantaneous bandwidth is half the width of the transparency window in two-photon detuning. The local-oscillator beat places the second-order intercept near twice the local-oscillator field, so the local oscillator sets the even-order linearity. For a rubidium transition at 17.04 GHz the closed forms agree with a velocity-resolved density-matrix model to 1% for the slope and the intercepts and to 10% for the bandwidth. They underestimate the group delay by a third. The response is tied to atomic constants, and the sensing volume escapes the Chu limit. However, the noise figure of a warm vapor rules it out as a general replacement for an antenna and low-noise amplifier.

title: Freedom is all you need
abstract: The functional calculus allows for the rigorous analysis of functions of matrices or even operators. The free functional calculus gives the natural class of functions over any category. We initiate the representation theory for taking a generic free functional calculus to the classical nc functional calculus going back to Taylor, Voiculescu and many others, with an eye towards learning of categories. The functional calculus on direct sum closed and locally similarity (i.e. change of coordinates) invariant domains inherits the niceties of complex analysis and large-scale parallel networks, such as automatic analyticity, free universal monodromy, which gives a hypothetical explanation for beneficial overfitting.

title: Probing CP violation in weak radiative and dielectron decays of $Λ$ and $Ξ^-$ hyperons
abstract: The rare decays $Λ\to ne^+e^-$ and $Ξ^-\toΣ^-e^+e^-$ can serve as sensitive probes of $CP$ violation, especially that induced by interactions from beyond the standard model. We demonstrate that this is so because the dominant long-distance components of these processes provide sizable absorptive phases that can give rise to significant $CP$ violation via interference with potential new-physics effects. Treating the new contributions model-independently, we find that this leads to $CP$-odd rate asymmetries that are currently allowed by kaon and hyperon data to reach the 10% and 20% levels in the $Λ$ and $Ξ^-$ cases, respectively. Interestingly, we obtain comparable outcomes for the related weak radiative modes $Λ\to nγ$ and $Ξ^-\toΣ^-γ$. These results are testable at future high-statistics hyperon facilities.

title: One partition function call to rule them all: Efficiently computing the equilibrium landscape of multiple nucleic acid strands
abstract: In the nearest neighbour model of DNA/RNA binding, the partition function (PF) is a sum of Boltzmann-weighted free energies of the exponentially large set of secondary structures. Dirks et al. [SIAM review, 2007] gave a polynomial time PF algorithm for $O(1)$ strands, generalising McCaskill [Biopolymers, 1990] single-stranded case. Despite the intuition that PF may somehow encode the entire state space, thus far different approaches were required to solve various energy-landscape prediction problems. For example: finding the minimum free energy (MFE), structure(s) for $O(1)$ strands was open since 2007, and we recently solved [ICALP, 2025] via new techniques. We asked if there is a magnifiable PF algorithm [DNA31, 2025], which we answer here in the affirmative. We give an $O(N^3(c-1)!)$ time, $O(N^2)$ space algorithm, for $c=O(1)$ strands of $N$ bases, the same overhead as Dirks et al. (non-magnifiable) algorithm. However, we show that magnification allows for efficient decoding of the entire landscape, concretely: a single call to the magnifiable PF efficiently solves and improves upon a large number of problems, giving: - MFE in $O(N^3(c-1)!)$ time, $O(N^2)$ space; a considerable improvement over our $O(N^4(c-1)!)$ time, $O(N^4)$ space result [ICALP 2025]. - The first polynomial time algorithm for the multi-stranded density of states problem, in time $O(N^3(c-1)!),O(N^2)$ space. - The first polynomial time algorithm outputting the entire list of energy levels occupied by at least one structure (in time $O(N^3(c-1)!),O(N^2)$ space), and the first algorithms for various energy landscape and counting problems. Our approach unifies the field of energy landscape prediction showing that a single, general, algorithmic framework neatly unifies a large collection of problems that practitioners care about, and required distinct techniques with worse time bounds.

title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Agnostic PAC Learning for Partial Concept Classes
abstract: Let $\mathcal H\subseteq\{-1,+1,\star\}^{\mathcal X}$ be a partial concept class of finite VC dimension $d$. We construct a deterministic agnostic PAC learner that, for every $\varepsilon,δ\in(0,1)$, uses $O((d+\log(1/δ))/\varepsilon^2)$ i.i.d. examples from an arbitrary distribution $\mathcal D$ over $\mathcal X\times\{-1,+1\}$ and returns a total concept $\hat h:\mathcal X\to\{-1,+1\}$ satisfying $\text{er}_{\mathcal D}(\hat h)\leq \min_{h\in\mathcal H}\text{er}_{\mathcal D}(h)+\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-δ$, where $\text{er}_{\mathcal D}(h)=\mathbb P_{(x,y)\sim\mathcal D}[h(x)\neq y]$. This establishes the optimal sample complexity, matching the lower bound of Alon et al. (FOCS 2021).

title: Perceived Differences in Activity and Experience Between Developing Software With and Without AI
abstract: The fundamental changes in software engineering driven by generative AI will have profound effects not only on the number of available software engineering jobs but also on what software engineering itself looks like. As the career evolves, questions arise about what the skillset and interests of the next generation of software engineers will be and whether long-time engineers will continue to be attracted to the career. In this paper, we contribute to answering these questions by studying how software development with AI tools is perceived to differ from traditional development and how the differences are modulated by years of programming experience. We find that, in terms of programming activities, engineers report less talking with peers about technical problems, less decomposition, less searching of documentation, and less using a debugger, while they report more task switching. We also find experiential differences, including less deep focus and less sense of control over code and design. We call these the different craft results, in contrast to core code-production activities such as writing, refactoring, and fixing code, which show only small mean differences. We also find that these differences are amplified by years of programming experience (an experience gradient), with software engineers who started programming before the age of generative AI perceiving greater changes in both activity and developer experience. We discuss our findings and their implications on training of the next generation of engineers and on engineers who may have difficulty transitioning to the AI-infused world of software engineering.

title: Minkowski Correlation Functions (MCF): Long-range, robust shape descriptors for point patterns
abstract: A morphometric analysis of point patterns using Minkowski functionals is short-sighted, whereas correlation functions do not provide robust, i.e., additive shape descriptors. To combine the advantages of both standard techniques and to overcome their weaknesses, we introduce ring-based Minkowski correlation functions (MCFs) as robust and sensitive descriptors of disordered point patterns. By assigning to each point a spherical shell and quantifying the resulting two-phase morphology via Minkowski functionals, MCFs capture structural information across multiple length scales, remain sensitive at radii where conventional disk-based Minkowski functionals have saturated, and implicitly encode higher-order correlations beyond the pair correlation and structure factor. We present an exact and efficient algorithm for planar patterns extending the established disk-based morphological approach to long ranges. Applications across scales -- active colloids (Quincke rollers), longleaf pine trees, and the Hubble Ultra Deep Field -- demonstrate clear and systematic deviations from homogeneous Poisson references, with distinct responses of covered area, boundary length, and Euler characteristic. The approach combines short computation times, robustness to noise, and straightforward edge handling with clear interpretability as low-dimensional functions of the outer ring radius.

title: Weighted sum commuting maps with the $(f,g)$-Aluthge transform
abstract: Let $\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ denote the algebra of all $n\times n$ complex matrices, where $n\geq2$, and let $Δ_{f,g}$ be the $(f,g)$-Aluthge transform associated with nonnegative continuous functions $f,g$ on $[0,\infty)$ satisfying $f(t)g(t)=t$ for all $t\geq0$. In this paper, we characterize all surjective maps $Φ:\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C}) \to\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ satisfying\[Φ(Δ_{f,g}(αA+βB))=Δ_{f,g}(αΦ(A)+βΦ(B))\]for all $A,B\in\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$, where $α,β$ are fixed nonzero real numbers. Without assuming additivity or linearity, we prove that when $f$ is nonconstant, $Φ$ must be of the form $Φ(A)=cUAU^*$ or $Φ(A)=cU\overline{A}U^*$ for all $A$, where $U$ is a fixed unitary matrix, $\overline{A}$ denotes the entrywise complex conjugate of $A$, and $c$ is a nonzero complex scalar. Moreover, we completely determine the possible values of $|c|$, which form either $\{1\}$, $q^{\mathbb{Z}}$ for some $q>1$, or $(0,\infty)$. When $f$ is constant, we show that $Φ(A)=S(A)+D$ for all $A$, where $S$ is a surjective $\mathbb{Q}(α,β)$-linear map and $D\in\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ satisfies $(α+β-1)D=0$.

title: Yau's pinching problem and vanishing of Betti numbers
abstract: We prove that a closed connected Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq4$, satisfying $\sec>\frac{\operatorname{Scal}}{n(n+2)}$ at every point has vanishing real cohomology in degrees $1,..., n-1$. It is consequently a rational homology sphere if $n$ is odd or the manifold is orientable. Complex projective space shows that the coefficient is optimal and that the strict inequality is necessary in every even dimension. The required estimate for the Weitzenböck curvature term is established by integrating restricted Ricci operators over orthonormal frames and combining complementary degrees using Hodge duality. This also allows us to replace sectional curvature pinching by intermediate Ricci curvature bounds. For a nonflat metric, the weak Yau inequality, $\sec\geq\frac{\operatorname{Scal}}{n(n+2)}$, gives the same cohomology vanishing unless the manifold is isometric, up to scaling, to a quotient of complex projective space with its Fubini-Study metric. This also holds using the second intermediate Ricci curvature in place of sectional curvature. More generally, a nonzero Betti number in the range controlled by an intermediate Ricci bound forces local symmetry. We also derive sharp Hodge eigenvalue estimates and a scalar spectral vanishing criterion.

title: Topology Hub Optimal Transport: Eliminating Long Context Dilution at Flash Speed
abstract: Long-context models use sparse or structured attention to avoid quadratic cost, yet retrieving a small set of relevant facts embedded among hundreds of thousands of distractors degrades as normalization mass disperses with length. Hub-and-spoke optimal transport (OT) replaces the dense $L \times L$ matrix with a linear-size graph over local windows and $K$ shared hubs balanced by Sinkhorn scaling. Building on block-wise tail refinement and fixed-support transport topology (arXiv:2605.08123, arXiv:2609.07954), we introduce Topology Hub Optimal Transport (THOT): (1) bounded-support capacity gating via simplex sparsemax ($O(L\log L)$) or sorting-free token-local thresholded ReLU ($O(L)$), driving excess distractor mass to zero; (2) a three-sweep $1+2$ annealed row-closed Sinkhorn schedule that damps bipartite residuals; (3) an exact rank-$(D+2R+1)$ One-Reference-Tile adjoint in batched split-factor Triton kernels (BF16 Tensor Cores, FP32 potentials); and (4) a chunked exclusive-prefix causal variant with verified zero future leakage. On NVIDIA L4, sparsemax THOT trained at $L=128$ reaches 97.40% zero-shot recall of fixed bindings at $L=262{,}144$ under pure task loss ($α=0$) and 98.83% at $α=0.05$ (matched by $O(L)$ thresholded ReLU at $α=0.05$, vs. 80.60% at $α=0$), while softmax-gated hub OT drops to 3.52%. In bidirectional operator microbenchmarks, our kernel runs forward+VJP in 100.1 ms at $H=8, D=64, L=262\mathrm{K}$ (2.2x faster with 4.0x smaller compiler temporaries than latent softmax) and 1.34 ms vs. 4.37 ms for cuDNN FlashAttention at $L=4{,}096$; multi-layer LM runs use the unfused path. Zero-shot WikiText-103 multi-needle retrieval hits 100.00% (128/128 queries at $L=65\mathrm{K}$) vs. 0.78% for short-trained RoPE FlashAttention, and compact 4-layer WikiText-4K runs show modest causal and masked LM gains.

title: Atmospheric parameters and chemical abundances of young stars with APOGEE -- II. Carbon, Nitrogen, Oxygen, and Sulphur abundances in Orion
abstract: We derived the abundances of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, sulphur, and iron in young G-, K-, and M-type stars (effective temperatures of 3500--5900 K) using APOGEE-2 infrared spectra. Our final sample comprises 195 slow rotators ($v\sin i$ $\leq$ 30 km~s$^{-1}$) in the Orion complex (Orion A, B, OB1, and $λ$~Ori). The abundances were determined using MARCS model atmospheres, atmospheric parameters derived with \tona, and the \bacc\ code. We obtained median abundances of $ε$(C) = 8.37$\pm$0.10, $ε$(N) = 7.35$\pm$0.16, $ε$(O) = 8.63$\pm$0.08, $ε$(S) = 7.19$\pm$0.18, and $ε$(Fe) = 7.45$\pm$0.05. Nitrogen is subsolar ([N/H] $=-0.48$), whereas carbon, oxygen, sulphur, and iron are within 0.1 dex of the solar values. We find no spatial structure within the Orion subgroups, and the only significant difference is a 0.29 dex lower nitrogen abundance in Orion A than in Orion OB1, which does not extend to the other elements. Compared with 430 nearby main-sequence stars analysed in the same way, Orion shows carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen abundances lower by 0.1--0.2 dex, although consistent within the errors, whereas sulphur and iron differ by less than 0.07 dex. We also compare our abundances with nebular abundances of HII regions and star-forming galaxies: the stellar abundances of oxygen, sulphur, and iron are higher, with the largest offset in iron, although the agreement in abundance ratios improves when temperature inhomogeneities and dust depletion are taken into account.

title: Real-time neuromorphic audio and vision perception for autonomous robotic applications: Integration and experimental evaluation on a rover platform
abstract: Neuromorphic sensing and computing offer a promising alternative to conventional deep learning pipelines for mobile robots, where perception must run continuously under tight latency and energy constraints. However, most neuromorphic solutions are still evaluated offline or on isolated benchmarks, and their integration into complete robotic systems remains largely unexplored. In this technical report, a four-wheel rover platform is presented that combines three real-time perception pipelines: a classical audio tagging pipeline based on Pretrained Audio Neural Networks (PANNs) running on an NVIDIA Jetson GPU, a neuromorphic audio pipeline in which a spiking neural network (SNN) is deployed on the SynSense Xylo Audio~2 chip, and a neuromorphic vision pipeline in which events from an event-based camera are processed by the SpikeYOLO spiking detector for traffic cone detection. On the Xylo chip, the whole processing chain---from the microphone signal to the classification of low- and high-pitched sounds---is performed on-chip, while the host only configures the device and reads the output neurons. All models are deployed as containerised services and integrated through ROS~2, and a configurable action dispatcher maps the detected classes to robot behaviours, closing the loop between perception and actuation. The platform is demonstrated in a proof-of-concept scenario in which the robot reacts to sound classes detected by both audio pipelines and detects traffic cones with the event camera, showing the feasibility of integrating neuromorphic hardware into a multimodal robotic platform operating in real time.

title: Recovering buoyancy-glitch parameters in low-luminosity red giants from global stellar properties with machine learning
abstract: Buoyancy glitches in red giants provide localized information on the interior structure near the base of the convective envelope, but their properties are typically inferred from dedicated seismic modelling rather than global properties, limiting large-sample applications. We investigate whether the buoyancy-glitch amplitude ($A_g$), location ($W_{\rm g}^{\star}$), and width ($D_g$) can be recovered from global stellar properties using gradient-boosted tree regressors (XGBoost and LightGBM). The models were trained on a grid of 12580 synthetic stellar models of low-luminosity red giants, with target parameters derived from fits to the local buoyancy frequency profile. We find that $W_{\rm g}^{\star}$ and $D_g$ exhibit excellent recoverability, achieving test-set $\mathcal{R}^2$ values of 0.98 and 0.97, respectively. In contrast, $A_g$ shows moderate recoverability overall ($\mathcal{R}^2=0.68$). This reduced recoverability of $A_g$ is concentrated in the large frequency separation range $Δν= 4.6$--$18.9\,μ$Hz, where the glitch resides in the evanescent-zone transition between the convective envelope and the gravity-mode cavity, increasing intrinsic scatter. SHAP analysis shows that $ν_{\rm max}$ and $T_{\rm eff}$ dominate the predictions across all targets, indicating that the regressors rely primarily on evolutionary state. While $W_{\rm g}^{\star}$ and $D_g$ are tightly constrained by global evolutionary trends, the lower recoverability of $A_g$ reflects localized structural complexity associated with red-giant evolution. Overall, for the synthetic grid adopted here, these results indicate that global properties provide a direct estimate of the buoyancy-glitch parameters and a way to prioritise dedicated mixed-mode inversions for large asteroseismic samples such as Kepler and PLATO.

title: Molecular structure breaks universality in screening behavior of electrolyte solutions
abstract: Electrostatic screening is one of the most fundamental phenomena in electrolyte solutions. While dilute electrolytes are described by the universal Debye--Hückel theory, recent experiments have reported an apparently universal scaling law for screening lengths in concentrated electrolytes, fueling ongoing debate over anomalous underscreening. Yet, liquid state theory has been unable to determine whether molecular details of the solvent, the ions, or both should preserve or break such universality. Using machine-learned classical density functional theory, we compute numerically exact decay lengths across a hierarchy of electrolyte models of increasing molecular complexity. We find that molecular details qualitatively reshape screening: solvent attraction generates a new monotonic decay mode, solvent polarity produces re-entrant behavior, and ionic structure alone can drastically alter screening-length exponents. Consequently, no single scaling law describes screening universally across these molecularly distinct electrolytes. Our results challenge equilibrium interpretations of experimentally observed universality in concentrated electrolytes.

title: Cluster Editing in Subexponential Fixed-Parameter Time
abstract: Cluster Editing asks whether at most $k$ edge additions and deletions turn a given $n$-vertex graph into a disjoint union of cliques. For more than a decade, the fastest algorithm for it was the golden-ratio algorithm of Böcker with running time $O(1.62^k+n^{O(1)})$. Cao and Chen had conjectured that the subexponential running time $2^{o(k)}\cdot n^{O(1)}$ is possible, but this contradicts the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH). Recently, the breakthrough algorithms for 3-SAT of OpenAI and Anthropic refuted ETH itself. Our main result transfers running times from 3-SAT to Cluster Editing. If 3-SAT on formulas with $m$ clauses can be decided in time $T(m)$, then there is an algorithm that, given a graph with $n$ vertices and integers $k$ and $r$ with $2\le r\le k^{1/3}$, decides Cluster Editing in time $2^{O((k\log r)/r)}\cdot T(2^{O(r^2\log r)}\cdot k)\cdot n^{O(1)}$. Combined with the breakthrough algorithms for 3-SAT, this proves Cao and Chen's conjecture, as it solves Cluster Editing in time $2^{O(k\cdot(\log\log\log k)^{3/2}/\sqrt{\log\log k})}\cdot n^{O(1)}=2^{o(k)}\cdot n^{O(1)}$. The key ingredient is a sparsification theorem for Cluster Editing, the counterpart of the Sparsification Lemma for satisfiability: In time $2^{O((k\log r)/r)}\cdot n^{O(1)}$, it reduces a given instance to $2^{O((k\log r)/r)}$ weighted instances with $O(rk)$ vertices and degree $O(r)$, each of which is equivalent to a 3-SAT formula with $2^{O(r^2\log r)}\cdot k$ clauses. Conversely, by a known reduction with linear blow-up, every saving in the exponent for Cluster Editing is, up to constant factors, a saving for 3-SAT.

title: Load-Following Dynamics of an SMR-Powered All-Electric Ship with Battery Energy Storage
abstract: Small modular reactors (SMRs) are being considered as compact, high-energy-density power sources for future all-electric ships. In such systems, propulsion-load variations can propagate through the electrical network, turbine-generator set, steam generator, and reactor, producing coupled nuclear, thermal, mechanical, and electrical transients. This paper presents an integrated dynamic load-following analysis of an SMR-powered all-electric ship with and without battery energy storage system (BESS) support. The model couples an integral pressurized water reactor, a once-through moving-boundary steam generator, a simplified turbine model, a synchronous generator, an AC shipboard electrical network, an asynchronous propulsion motor, and a grid-connected BESS. A propulsion-load reduction is applied through the motor torque command, and the responses of the SMR-alone and SMR+BESS configurations are compared. The results show that, without BESS support, the sudden decrease in propulsion motor power creates a temporary surplus between turbine mechanical power and electrical demand, causing a large over-frequency transient and rapid steam-cycle adjustment. With BESS support, the battery absorbs excess electrical power during the transient, reducing the frequency peak from approximately 61.1 Hz to about 60.06 Hz. The BESS also indirectly smooths the upstream steam-cycle and reactor responses, including steam flow, steam-generator pressure, feedwater flow, coolant temperature, reactivity, reactor thermal power, and steam-generator region lengths. These results demonstrate the importance of modeling nuclear-powered electric ships as coupled multi-domain systems and show that BESS integration can improve short-term load-following performance.

title: Differential Transmutations and First-Passage Expansions for Monomial Brownian Boundaries
abstract: Let $P_t=\exp(t\partial_x^2/2)$ be the heat semigroup and let $F(t)=ρt^p$, where $p\ge2$ is an integer. Previous transported-zero theory associates with this boundary a constant-flux solution annihilated by a polynomial-coefficient differential operator of order $2p-1$. We show that the same differential structure contains the complete formal perturbation expansion of the Brownian first-passage density to $F$. For $N=2p-1$ we construct graded spatial operators \[ \mathcal A_r^{(p)}x^n= \frac{(-1)^r}{r!} \frac{\prod_{j=0}^{pr-1}(n+2j+1)} {\prod_{j=1}^{Nr}(n+j)}x^{n+Nr} \] and prove the Laplace conjugacy \[ \mathscr L\mathcal A_r^{(p)}\mathscr L^{-1} =\frac{(-1)^r}{r!}k^r \left(-\frac1k\frac{d}{dk}\right)^{pr}. \] Consequently, the inverse spatial transmutation applied to a reflected Dirac mass generates, coefficient by coefficient, the unique formal solution of the exponential-martingale transform equation for first passage. The cubic case is developed explicitly and checked algebraically through fifth order. We also explain how this differential construction and the independently developed Wright--Volterra generalized-image construction represent the same first-passage law in different coordinates. The present result is formal at all orders; convergence of the resulting perturbation series is left as a separate analytic problem.

title: Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization
abstract: Hyperparameter optimization (HPO) is essential for high predictive performance, but its computational cost becomes prohibitive when candidate configurations require repeated training on large datasets. This paper proposes a ranking-preserving coreset (RPC) selection framework for accelerating evolutionary HPO. The method constructs a compact coreset that preserves the relative ranking of hyperparameter configurations observed on the full training data. Coreset selection is formulated as an evolutionary optimization problem that maximizes Spearman rank correlation between full-data and subset-based configuration rankings while penalizing subset size. The selected coreset is then used for HPO with three evolutionary algorithms: Genetic Algorithm (GA), Cross-generational elitist Selection, Heterogeneous Recombination and Cataclysmic Mutation (CHC), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Experiments on seven tabular, two text, and two image benchmark datasets show that RPC substantially reduces HPO time while maintaining test accuracy comparable to full-dataset HPO across decision tree, text classification, and image classification tasks. Across datasets and optimizers, HPO-stage speedups range from approximately 1.14x to 8.80x, while the one-time coreset construction cost is accounted for separately through end-to-end runtime and break-even analysis. On 20 held-out configurations excluded from coreset construction, RPC achieves higher ranking correlation than same-size random sampling on 8 of 11 datasets (dataset-level Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p = 0.014). These results show that ranking preservation extends beyond the configurations used during selection. The one-time construction cost can be amortized when the coreset is reused across HPO runs.

title: Receptor Abundance Alone Underpredicts Red Blood Cell Adhesion in Gaucher Disease
abstract: Red blood cells (RBCs) in Gaucher disease (GD) adhere abnormally to vessel walls and carry more Lutheran/basal cell adhesion molecule (Lu/BCAM), a laminin receptor. Whether receptor abundance sets this adhesion is untested. We simulated RBCs carrying stochastic Lu/BCAM-laminin bonds, calibrated a population on control donors, and predicted GD adhesion from the 1.3-fold receptor rise. On laminin and endothelium the data exceed the prediction 1.6- to 1.7-fold. Matching them requires 2.4- and 4.6-fold more binding-competent receptors, compatible with the estimated 5.7-fold rise in phosphorylated receptors. Neither a stiffer membrane nor higher bond affinity removes the shortfall at high shear stress. In sickle cell disease, given active-receptor counts, the model predicts the fall in adhesion under hydroxyurea within 1.4-fold, while total receptors rise. Adhesion likely follows receptor state more than abundance. Stiffening instead retains cells at a splenic slit.

title: Explicational statistics: research for an AI age
abstract: AI is dramatically changing the statistical research landscape. I argue that production of a distinct category of statistical knowledge, which I refer to as explicational statistics, is actually becoming more valuable as AI increasingly automates other parts of the research process. I define explicational statistics, contextualize it in terms of other forms of statistical knowledge, and explain why I think the rise of AI makes it more valuable. I demonstrate my framework by first developing a new dimension reduction method, Ambient Embedding Projection, that can simultaneously visualize the intrinsic geometry of a data manifold along with how that manifold is embedded into ambient space. I then use my new method to conceive of a new statistical property of a collection of manifolds, related to metric distortion, that in single-cell biology can capture the ensemble behavior of cell populations. I apply these ideas to single-nuclei RNA-seq data from the brains of mice from different behavioral conditions to reveal potential cellular mechanisms of chronic social defeat stress.

title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology
abstract: Machine learning has largely kept separate the choice of architecture and the process of training. A classic Transformer, for instance, trains a fixed set of attention and MLP sublayers at every layer, in the same order, and optimizes the weights within. This uniformity is a convention rather than a principled design choice, and it is likely suboptimal: the best architecture for a given task may be smaller, more efficient, and far from uniform. We believe that, ideally, training itself should shape the model's topology. To this end, we introduce Model Carving, which learns both a Transformer's weights and its architecture in a single run. By applying learnable, scalar gates to each sublayer, we allow the training loss to remove the model's own components during training -- freeing a smaller heterogeneous network inside. We evaluate Model Carving by pre-training standard Transformers from 140M to 2.7B parameters and looped Transformers from 140M to 1.3B. At equal training compute, carved models reach a lower validation loss than dense models trained with up to 1.7 times more compute. Furthermore, carved models also outperform size-matched models produced by pruning or distillation, suggesting that the best way to obtain small models for edge devices is to carve them during training, not to compress a large one afterwards. This advantage both grows with scale and carries over to downstream tasks such as few-shot evaluation and generation. Because the removed sublayers no longer run, carved models also cost up to 34% fewer FLOPs per token and decode up to 1.6 times faster without cost in quality. Our results show that architecture, like weights, should be learned and not fixed in advance, and that inside every large transformer is a smaller, faster, stronger one waiting to be carved out.

title: Non-penetrating World Models
abstract: We study a new problem of preventing object penetration in interactive video world models. To understand how existing models handle this, we introduce NoPeBench, a benchmark that evaluates how world models respond to physical obstacles. Our evaluation reveals that none of the open-source models can reliably prevent such failures. Surprisingly, however, these models already encode the information needed to predict such violations. We find that the hidden states of diffusion transformers (DiTs) can predict whether a candidate action will penetrate an obstacle. Building on this, we introduce NoPeWorld, a lightweight framework that detects and prevents penetration. Specifically, we train a small prediction head on top of a frozen DiT's hidden states to read out if a candidate action is safe or not. Unsafe actions are then replaced with safe ones that best preserve the original intent. Despite its simplicity, NoPeWorld substantially reduces the physical violation rate, averaged over six video world models, from 74% to 16%. Remarkably, our method shows zero-shot generalization to open-domain imagery, third-person viewpoints, and moving obstacles. We publicly release our code, the NoPeBench benchmark, and model weights. Project Page: https://nopeworld.github.io .

title: Your Camera Can Hear You: Side-Channel Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Metadata
abstract: To prevent motion sensors from acting as covert microphones, Android 12+ caps SensorManager gyroscope and accelerometer rates at 200 Hz by default, requires HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS for higher rates, and throttles sensors back to 200 Hz when the microphone toggle is off. We show that Android's Camera2 subsystem bypasses these defenses. During an active Camera2 session, Camera HAL stabilization pipelines record high-rate gyroscope measurements and export them via vendor CaptureResult metadata.
