Loudspeaker speech excites chassis vibrations that couple into this path. Across 50 smartphones (2020-2026) from 10 vendors, 37 expose gyroscope metadata via Camera2, and 26 exceed 200 Hz--including six flagship models at 800-1000 Hz, double SensorManager's 400-500 Hz ceiling. This channel requires neither RECORD_AUDIO nor HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS and defeats privacy switches: turning off the microphone toggle does not throttle metadata, and turning off the camera toggle blanks only video frames while 800-1000 Hz metadata keeps streaming. To build a zero-profiling attack that generalizes to unseen phones, we introduce Source-to-Leakage Learning (S2L). Prior attacks train on real sensor traces, entangling speech with a specific phone's mechanical resonances and sampling rate. S2L decouples speech content from hardware acoustics using a physics-constrained forward simulator. Trained exclusively on simulated leakage without target-phone traces, our universal recognizer CamEar achieves 52.1% mean word accuracy (up to 61.8%) and 74.3% character accuracy (up to 80.7%) across the six 800-1000 Hz phones. In contrast, ISpyU models fine-tuned on real target-phone data drop to 25.9% word accuracy on unseen phones; CamEar improves cross-device accuracy by 101.4% and outperforms ISpyU's same-device models on every tested phone.

title: Recognizing $k$-inducible Digraphs is NP-complete
abstract: A digraph is k-inducible if its arcs correspond to the pairwise majority relation of a preference profile with k voters. By McGarvey's theorem, every asymmetric digraph is k-inducible for some k, but for every fixed k there are digraphs that are not k-inducible. Whether a digraph is 1-inducible or 2-inducible can easily be decided in polynomial time. The complexity of deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible for every fixed $k\geq 3$ has been a long-standing open problem. We prove that deciding whether a tournament is 3-inducible is NP-complete and then leverage this result to show that deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible is NP-complete for every fixed $k\geq 3$. Our results imply that, unless P=NP, k-inducible digraphs cannot be characterized by finitely many forbidden induced subdigraphs.

title: All stable Schoen--Wolfson cones are minimizing
abstract: In the late nineties, R.~Schoen and J.~Wolfson studied the problem of minimizing the area among Lagrangian surfaces in a Riemannian symplectic $4$-manifold. In their parametric approach, they showed that minimizers are smoothly branched-immersed away from a discrete set of points, where there exists a nonflat tangent cone minimizing the area among Lagrangian disk competitors. They also classified the stable singular cones into a family $C_{p,p+1}$ indexed by a positive integer $p$, but left open the question of which of them are globally minimizing. We settle this question by showing that for each $p \geq 1$, $C_{p,p+1} \cap B_1$ minimizes the area among Lagrangian disks spanning its boundary with degree one.

title: Task2Hand: A Contact-Grounded Skill for Parametric Dexterous-Hand Morphology Design
abstract: Dexterous hand design demands repeated expert work across geometry, robot-description code, collision debugging, grasp initialization, and policy training. We present Task2Hand, a Skill: a specification package that turns a functional manipulation brief into a parameterized hand model and routes every candidate through cost-ordered contact, dynamics, and learning gates. Each gate returns a status and an evidence record; on failure, the Skill records the earliest blocker, revises one bounded parameter group, and reruns the cheaper gates. The agent generates, validates, and trains autonomously within declared bounds, and escalates trade-offs, plateaus, and conflicting evidence to a human who sets the next design direction. An evidence-driven design trajectory for bidirectional in-hand manipulation yielded SAGE Hand (Skill-Aware Generative Embodiment): four fingers, 16 actuated DoF, an integrated guiding palm, compact roots, cylindrical tips, and a collision-cleared opposable thumb. Under a matched training protocol, SAGE Hand reaches 45.6% task success on a hexagonal prism against 37.3% for the LEAP hand, and 70.8% on a bicolor cylinder against 51.6%. Dense simulated tactile input more than halves the cylinder drop rate. In a controlled iteration study, the Skill path preserves capture at 164/165 trials while the path without the Skill degrades to 14/165, confirming that the gates act as a regression guard during refinement. Accepted candidates pack with URDF/MJCF, metrics, checkpoints, and a provenance manifest.

title: A proof of the polygonal Faber--Krahn inequality
abstract: We prove that, for every integer $n\ge3$, the regular $n$-gon uniquely minimizes the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, up to congruence, among simple polygons of prescribed area with at most $n$ sides. We also obtain the optimal linear correction when fewer than $n$ sides are present. The proof combines a partition into convex cells with a mixed boundary comparison. Among convex polygons of fixed area and fixed sum of base angles less than $π$, the isosceles triangle minimizes the first eigenvalue with Dirichlet conditions on the base and Neumann conditions elsewhere. A comparison of Fourier transforms of conformal area densities proves this inequality and the corresponding upper bounds for inverse spectral moments of integer order at least two. We prove strict log-convexity of an interpolation of the eigenvalues of regular polygons of unit area for real parameters at least four. We then derive sharp hexagonal bounds for periodic convex polygonal tilings and asymptotic bounds for convex polygonal partitions of a fixed convex polygon, with an explicit correction for boundary junctions.

title: Convergence of a finite element Chorin projection method for the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations
abstract: We analyze a fully discrete finite element projection method for the stochastic incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and multiplicative noise. We show solvability and uniform moment estimates for the intermediate and the corrected velocity approximations under the assumption that the initial data is square-integrable and divergence free, and that the deterministic forcing term is bounded in $L^{q}(0,T;H^{-1}(D))$ for a sufficiently large $q$. Under standard stability and approximation assumptions on the finite element spaces and a coupling condition on the spatial and temporal discretization parameters, we prove convergence of a subsequence to a martingale solution of the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations. The analysis combines the complementary spatial and temporal estimates of the predicted and the corrected velocity approximations and uses the numerical dissipation to identify their common limit. We establish tightness of the piecewise constant temporal interpolations of the velocity field approximations using Aldous' criterion combined with the uniform discrete moment estimates. The convergence result holds in two and three space dimensions as it does not rely on any additional regularity of the limiting martingale solution beyond the one naturally available from the energy inequality. Finally, we demonstrate the performance of the scheme in numerical experiments in two space dimensions for smooth and vortex sheet initial data.

title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is a neurodevelopmental condition that can affect attention, activity and impulse control. Electroencephalography (EEG) records brain activity as children and adolescents perform cognitive tasks. However, comparing features derived from these recordings requires consistent signal preparation, shared analysis windows and documented quality decisions. We curated 669 existing BALLADEER recordings from 156 participants across five task conditions so that researchers can compare seven EEG feature families on the same time intervals for each participant and task. The dataset links continuous signals to precomputed measurements from 115 feature definitions or templates and records the quality decisions made for each recording. Analyses must still account for repeated measurements within participants, residual artefacts and differences between acquisition systems. Technical validation covered signal integrity, numerical checks on feature estimators and completeness of the released files. In every task, the median proportion of recording time retained after preprocessing was 100%. To illustrate reuse, we report saved participant-held-out evaluations comparing XGBoost using all seven families on eight-second windows with a predictor based only on recruitment-group prevalence in the training fold. Recruitment-group discrimination was stronger in Robots than in the three Slackline conditions. These descriptive results from overlapping cohorts do not establish diagnostic validity. The dataset, curation software and aggregate results for the predictive example are publicly available.

title: Soft--hard Bayesian inference in heavy-ion collisions
abstract: Bayesian analyses of jet quenching commonly constrain jet--medium interaction parameters using a fixed quark-gluon plasma (QGP) background obtained from a soft-sector calibration. This approach neglects uncertainty in the medium and prevents hard observables from providing additional constraints on its properties. We investigate these effects in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.76$ TeV using sequential Bayesian inference in a reduced three-parameter space. We vary the initial normalization and nucleon width of the medium together with the jet--medium coupling, combining JETSCAPE medium evolution with MATTER+LBT calculations of high-$p_T$ hadron and inclusive-jet suppression. We first constrain all three parameters using the hard observables alone, then incorporate a projected soft-sector posterior through sequential inference. We find that the hard observables are sensitive to the medium properties and reveal substantial correlations with the jet--medium coupling, reflecting their compensating effects on jet quenching. Propagating the soft-sector information shifts the preferred coupling relative to a fixed-medium extraction, with the update driven primarily by hadron-suppression measurements. Despite substantial differences in the medium parameters and coupling favored by hard-observable-only and sequential inference, their suppression predictions remain similar over much of the measured range. These findings highlight the difficulty of distinguishing changes in the QGP medium from changes in microscopic jet--medium interaction strength using inclusive suppression measurements alone.

title: Localization of weakly integral objects in braided fusion categories
abstract: An object $X$ of a braided fusion category is called weakly integral if $\mathrm{FPdim}(X)^2$ is an integer. We prove that every nonzero weakly integral object admits a localization, that is, a Yang-Baxter operator $R$ on a finite-dimensional vector space $W$ such that, for every $n$, the algebra homomorphisms from the group algebra of the braid group $B_n$ to $\mathrm{End}(W^{\otimes n})$ and to $\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})$, defined by $R$ and by the braiding, have the same kernel. The operator $R$ can be chosen unitary when the braided fusion category is unitary. This proves the 'if' direction of a conjecture of Rowell and Wang, motivated by topological quantum computation, which states that a simple object admits a localization if and only if it is weakly integral. For a simple weakly integral object of a unitary braided fusion category, the operator $R$ that we construct has an enhancement in the sense of Turaev, and the resulting knot invariant is the Reshetikhin-Turaev invariant of knots colored by $X$.

title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
abstract: Deploying large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon and continual interactions requires maintaining reusable memory states for future inference, posing challenges for existing architectures. Standard Transformers accumulate layer-wise, token-level KV caches, incurring linear GPU memory growth and quadratic computational complexity as the context expands. In contrast, linear-time architectures compress history into fixed-size states, but struggle to retain fine-grained details. We introduce MemOnce, a foundation architecture that learns scalable memory states for language models. MemOnce is based on two core designs: (a) Memory encoder-decoder: it caches only a small subset of final-layer hidden states as compact memory representations and dynamically decodes them back into KV caches for attention layers; (b) Memory sparse attention: for each continual input, MemOnce adaptively retrieves relevant memory representations, with the sparse indices computed only once across layers. Coupling these two designs enables efficient on-the-fly memory loading and KV cache decoding, drastically reducing the GPU memory footprint and achieving linear-time complexity. We conduct extensive experiments to show that MemOnce outperforms Transformers and other architectures across varying model sizes, context lengths, and training paradigms (pretraining and post-training adaptation). In particular, adapting Qwen3.5-4B with MemOnce reduces memory state cache by 1313$\times$ and prefill latency by 6.9$\times$ at 1M context, and improves throughput by 3.5$\times$ and overall memory performance by +5.77%. Finally, MemOnce generalizes zero-shot to downstream representation tasks, achieving competitive results against specialized models.

title: Hölder continuity of meromorphic functions and equisingularity
abstract: For a complex analytic variety and an exponent between zero and one, we study the sheaf of meromorphic functions that are locally Hölder continuous with that exponent for the outer metric. It sits between the structure sheaves of the seminormalization and of the Lipschitz saturation of Pham and Teissier. We prove that these sheaves are coherent and that only finitely many of them are distinct, the exponents at which they change being rational numbers governed by the Rees valuations of the ideal of a certain diagonal. Each exponent defines a Hölder saturation of the variety. We show that a variety whose Hölder saturation is smooth for some exponent larger than one third is itself smooth and that one third is sharp. For reduced curve germs we compute the Hölder saturations from the characteristic exponents of the branches and give explicit thresholds, in terms of classical invariants, at which they become the seminormalization, the Lipschitz saturation, or a curve of the same multiplicity. We prove that homeomorphic curves are bi-Hölder homeomorphic for some positive exponent, whereas bi-Hölder homeomorphisms with exponent close enough to one preserve the multiplicity. We then introduce the relative Hölder saturation of a family and prove that it specializes to the saturations of the fibers over a dense Zariski-open subset of the base. This leads to two notions of equisingularity for families of complex analytic varieties, Hölder equisingularity, defined by a bi-Hölder trivialization, and the stronger Hölder equisaturation, defined by the triviality of the relative saturation. For families of reduced curve germs we show that they interpolate between topological, Whitney and Lipschitz equisingularity, with explicit exponents depending only on the invariants of the special fiber.

title: Nonperturbative Bounds on the Ground-State Energy of Lattice QED
abstract: We establish nonperturbative bounds on the ground-state energy of lattice quantum electrodynamics with naive fermions in Coulomb gauge, within the Gaussian photon approximation. Our central result is a spectral comparison theorem showing that, in the thermodynamic limit, the minimum fermionic energy density over all link configurations coincides with that of the trivial gauge configuration. The proof exploits a logarithmic determinant representation and dimensional reduction, without relying on reflection positivity, and applies to lattices of either parity. Combining this result with the positivity of the electromagnetic and Coulomb Hamiltonians, we derive an explicit lower bound on the interacting ground-state energy. Finite-lattice counterexamples show that the thermodynamic limit is essential.

title: Observation of rotonic density enhancement at the boundary of a uniform dipolar superfluid
abstract: The collective excitations of a quantum liquid lie at the heart of its emergent behaviour. In many systems, the variation of excitation energy ${\varepsilon}$ with wavevector $k$ exhibits a softening at a characteristic lengthscale, which plays a key role in thermodynamics and transport. These excitations, termed rotons, often reflect an underlying tendency of the liquid to crystallize into a competing symmetry-broken state, such as the solid state of helium or the Wigner crystal of electrons in a magnetic field. More than $50$ years ago, it was predicted that rotons should manifest as emergent density oscillations at the fluid's boundary, but this effect has not been observed. Here, we realize an ultracold dipolar superfluid confined in a homogeneous trapping potential and directly confirm the emergence of rotonic density enhancement at its edge. This is accompanied by rotonic density fluctuations across the bulk, which are linked to the static edge structure via the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. Increasing the dipolar character leads to an azimuthal density modulation of the fluid's boundary, which we show to be analogous to the behaviour of a quasi-one-dimensional fluid confined in an annular optical potential.

title: No Polynomial-Time Algorithm For Tarski Fixed Points Unless Cryptographic Assumptions Fail
abstract: We study the time complexity of finding a Tarski fixed point. We provide a subexponential-time reduction from the Unique End of Potential Line (UEOPL) problem to the problem of finding a Tarski fixed point. Using a range of known cryptographic lower bounds for UEOPL, our reduction implies a range of conditional lower bounds on the running time of any algorithm that finds a Tarski fixed point. The strongest of these give quasi-polynomial-time lower bounds for the problem. We also obtain a similar quasi-polynomial-time lower bound for Tarski based instead on a weak exponential-time type hypothesis for UEOPL. These running time lower bounds match the recently discovered quasi-polynomial query lower bounds for the problem.

title: A Methodologically Rigorous Benchmark of Linear Regression,RNN, and LSTM for S&P 500 Forecasting:Identifying Sources of Performance Inflation in Financial DeepLearning
abstract: This study examines one-day-ahead forecasting of the S&P 500 closing level using a 2006-2025 dataset that includes fundamental price data, macroeconomic indicators, and engineered technical features. We benchmark three model families, namely linear regression, vanilla recurrent neural networks (RNN), and long short-term memory networks (LSTM), within a unified preprocessing and chronological evaluation pipeline. A central contribution of this work is a methodological audit of common practices in the deep-learning-for-stock-prediction literature. We identify three sources of result inflation that frequently appear in published methodologies: wavelet-denoised evaluation targets, the absence of a naive persistence baseline, and best-of-N replicate reporting. We then re-evaluate all model families under a corrected protocol that controls for each. Performance is reported using root mean squared error, mean absolute percentage error, and the Pearson correlation coefficient, averaged across N = 30 independent replicates per configuration. We compare models on accuracy, stability across replicates, and architectural depth sensitivity, using the naive persistence forecast (predicting today's close as tomorrow's close) as a primary baseline against which all candidate models must demonstrate improvement.

title: Nearly pristine gas and hard ionizing radiation one billion years after the Big Bang
abstract: The first stars formed out of light elements (H, He, and Li leftover from Big Bang Nucleosynthesis) and began the chemical enrichment of the Universe. Identifying this first-generation population of stars, known as Population III, and understanding their properties is one of the most ambitious goals of modern extragalactic astrophysics. We report the detection of He and H emission lines and extremely low Oxygen abundance in AMORE6, a strongly magnified galaxy at redshift z = 5.725, i.e. approximately one billion years after the Big Bang, with deep James Webb Space Telescope spectroscopy. He II lambda1640 and lambda4686 emission lines are detected at 16.7 sigma and 4.0 sigma significance, respectively. The observed He II-to-Hbeta ratios are consistent with predictions for extreme ionizing radiation fields and the low chemical compositions typical of Population III stars. Oxygen abundance of the interstellar medium is estimated to be 8 x 10^-4 solar from weak [OIII]lambda4363 and lambda5008 lines, consistent with an almost pristine environment, perhaps enriched by the Pop III stars themselves. Although we cannot exclude alternative sources of hard ionizing radiation, such as accreting black holes, these observations offer the first view of the extremely low metallicity environment where the Universe's first stars are predicted to be born. The data show that such pockets of pristine gas still exist one billion years after the Big Bang and that they are dominated by very massive stars.

title: Structure and relaxation of long-lived odd-parity modes in two-dimensional Fermi liquids
abstract: In two-dimensional Fermi liquids, odd-parity deformations of the Fermi surface relax anomalously slowly at a rate $\sim T^4$, where $T$ is the temperature. However, the leading-logarithmic prediction for the magnitude of this rate $\sim m^4 \ln m$, where $m$ is an angular harmonic index, exceeds exact-diagonalization results and the $\ln m$ scaling is not observed. We resolve this discrepancy by evaluating the 2D Fermi-liquid collision integral for general regular isotropic potentials to leading order in $T/T_F$, including the nonlogarithmic term beyond the $\ln(T_F/T)$ term. We find that the local temperature modulation of the odd mode, which we call the thermal dressing, suppresses relaxation by collinear scattering, with residual relaxation set by large-angle scattering. Such large-angle processes give corrections of order $\ln m/\ln(T_F/T)$ that are not small and must be resummed. We benchmark our results against exact-diagonalization calculations for constant interactions and find agreement over a range $m^2 T/T_F \lesssim 0.4$, and we provide closed-form results for the slowest odd-mode relaxation rate of a spin-polarized dipolar gas.

title: Thermopower overshoot from collinear scattering in two-dimensional Fermi liquids
abstract: Electron transport is typically described in terms of relaxation times, which measure how quickly Fermi-surface deformations decay. We show here that the thermopower of a two-dimensional Fermi liquid instead probes the structure of these deformations in the form of their local temperature change, which we call the thermal dressing. This structure leads to an overshoot of the thermopower over its hydrodynamic value $- s/(ne)$ with increasing wave vector, before it falls to half that value in the ballistic limit. At low temperatures, the excess thermopower does not have the linear-in-temperature scaling expected of a Fermi liquid, but decreases only logarithmically as $1/\ln(T_F/T)$ at optimal wave vector. The overshoot is caused by collinear scattering, which redistributes energy over the Fermi surface and induces the thermal dressing, the strength of which grows with the angular harmonic index $m$ of the deformation. In contrast to tomographic effects in the charge conductivity, this overshoot does not rely on an odd-even effect in quasiparticle lifetimes and defines a distinct thermographic transport regime. The thermopower overshoot survives realistic disorder and should be detectable in a thermocouple with high-mobility samples.

title: Quantum Many-Body Scars from Operator Size
abstract: We present a general construction of approximate many-body scar states in two copies of a system using a bilocal size interaction that couples one site to its partner on the other copy. For an uncoupled two-sided Hamiltonian whose terms have fixed size in an operator basis, we identify polynomially many Krylov basis states that it annihilates and that, in the thermodynamic limit, become concentrated on a single size sector. The size operator splits them into a tower of equally spaced levels that gives rise to coherent revivals characterized by collective oscillations of energy across the two copies. We provide a concrete realization of this construction in two copies of a general $q$-body nearest-neighbor spin chain, and the SYK model.

title: Optimal Linear Regression Without a Variance
abstract: We study high-probability linear regression in the infinite variance regime, wherecthe regression noise has only a finite conditional $α$-moment $ν$ for some unknown $α\in(1,2)$, and the covariates may only have finite moments up to a given order (e.g., 4th moment). We give a black-box reduction that converts finite-variance regression procedures into weak-moment procedures. The reduction is based on empirical residual pruning and is agnostic to the moment exponent, the noise scale, the covariance, and the design moment. Under a finite fourth-moment condition on the covariates, any finite-variance subroutine attaining the sub-Gaussian rate yields the following when the number of samples $n$ is above a suitably defined threshold: Without knowing $α$ or $ν$, we have with probability at least $1-δ$ that $ \|\widehatθ-θ^*\|_Σ \lesssim_α ν^{1/α} \big(\frac{d+\log(1/δ)}{n}\big)^{\frac{α-1}α}, $ where $d$ is the dimension, $Σ$ is the covariate covariance matrix, and $\|v\|_Σ:=(v^\topΣv)^{1/2}$. We further prove a matching minimax lower bound that holds under the same conditions. The reduction is computationally efficient whenever the finite-variance subroutine is. We also obtain a distribution-free prediction guarantee under a bounded raw $α$-moment assumption on the response, and give an analogous $α$-agnostic reduction for mean estimation.

title: On the non-uniqueness of solutions of the axi-symmetric swirl-free Navier-Stokes equations, II
abstract: We prove optimal non-uniqueness of Leray solutions of the unforced incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in 3D within the class of axially symmetric swirl-free flows. More precisely, we construct two solutions $u_1,u_2$ that have the same initial data $u_1(0)=u_2(0)$, are smooth for every positive time, satisfy the energy identity, and satisfy \[ u_1,u_2\in C_tH_x^α\cap L_t^2H_x^{α+1}\,\,\text{ for every }\,\,0\leqα<1/2,\qquad u_1,u_2\in L_t^\infty L_x^{3,\infty}\cap L_t^{2,\infty}L_x^\infty. \] Thus non-uniqueness holds in optimal Sobolev spaces and critical Ladyzhenskaya-Prodi-Serrin weak spaces, even in a symmetry class where smooth solutions are globally regular. The proof relies on a computer-assisted construction of a linearly unstable forward self-similar solution, starting from the numerical profiles identified in our preceding paper (arXiv:2606.07501). We combine explicit asymptotic expansions and global residual estimates with weak coercivity inequalities stabilized by finitely many functionals. Approximate solutions of auxiliary linear equations yield quantitative inverse bounds, allowing us to correct both the stationary profile and its unstable eigenpair by contraction arguments. The instability and localization theorem proved in arXiv:2606.07501 then produces the non-unique solutions.

title: Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?
abstract: It is commonly stated in the literature that T violation is zero in neutrino disappearance channels. We show this claim is not general: it holds only for symmetric matter profiles or when the T/CP-violating phase ($δ$) is 0 or $π$, that is, when the Jarlskog invariant is zero. The $ν_μ$ and $ν_τ$, but not the $ν_e$, survival probabilities carry a $\sinδ$-dependent term that is non-zero in asymmetric matter and constitutes a genuine T asymmetry. The confusion arises from an improper T test that subtracts a probability from itself: a mathematical identity, not a physics result. In this paper, we clarify the distinctions between a proper and an improper T test as well as the proper and improper CP and CPT tests, for a general, arbitrary matter profile. For a toy model consisting of two different layers of constant density, we find that the maximum T-violation is obtained when one layer is close to the solar resonance, and the other is close to the atmospheric resonance. We address whether the matter asymmetry for DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande experiments is sufficiently large to allow the $\sinδ$ dependence to be probed in $ν_μ$ survival probability. We also discuss future experimental scenarios that could probe T/CP-violation in $ν_μ$ survival probability.

title: Ohmic warm inflation
abstract: We show that Warm Little Inflation is anomalous, lacks a suitable inflaton potential, and cannot sustain the thermal bath, as the quasi-static approximation over-estimated the dissipated power. To address these issues, we propose a new friction mechanism and new anomaly-free models based on one fermion charged under a U(1) gauge group in one extra dimension. The four-dimensional lattice version is a ring of $N$ U(1) groups with one fermion at each site, reducing to an anomaly-free version of the warm little inflaton model for $N=2$. The inflaton is a Wilson line, protected for $N\ge5$. Large $N$ allows a suitable monodromy inflaton potential. In the continuum limit, $N\to\infty$, the inflaton velocity becomes a five-dimensional electric field and friction becomes Ohmic dissipation, which seems able to sustain warm inflation compatibly with observations.

title: Empirical Limits of Risk-Averse Reinforcement Learning versus Gas-Aware Routing in Deterministic DeFi Execution
abstract: The migration of order execution to Automated Market Makers (AMMs) introduces two deterministic frictions absent from classical microstructure: closed-form constant-product slippage and Maximal Extractable Value (MEV) sandwich attacks gated by gas costs. We construct an end-to-end execution environment calibrated to live Uniswap V2 reserves, an EIP-1559 AR(1) gas process, and real Swap events, utilising stress-volatility gas shocks to make the MEV trigger informative. A Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) agent with a Rockafellar-Uryasev Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) penalty and a dual-head Chow-Ghavamzadeh critic is trained for one million steps across five risk-aversion levels and seeds, benchmarked against a myopic gas-aware oracle. We document a reproducible specification-gaming pathology: prior to a patch, a forced terminal liquidation routed through a no-MEV code path artificially inflated returns threefold and was preferentially exploited by higher-$λ$ runs. On the corrected environment, the strongest PPO variant captures 79\% of the myopic gas-aware oracle (46,542 $\pm$ 673 vs 58,786 $\pm$ 616 USDC), and extending the observation with three blocks of gas history fails to close the gap. We find no empirical evidence that the tested model-free MLP policies dominate this myopic gas-aware oracle, which can be evaluated in $\mathcal{O}(\log ε^{-1})$ time per block. This result is robust to a $\sim$16x trunk-capacity expansion and a variance-controlled gas-history ablation. Code and reproducibility materials are available upon request.

title: The Limits of Behavioral Early Warning for Copy-Trading Blow-Ups: A Pre-Registered, Full-Universe On-Chain Study (Hyperliquid)
abstract: A common, rarely-tested assumption behind copy-trading risk controls is that "behavioral monitoring catches blow-ups": that a master trader's conduct drifts before the equity damage that wipes out followers. We test this on real on-chain money over the full public Hyperliquid leaderboard: 37,895 addresses, filtered to 10,395 "master-worth-copying" accounts, yielding 2,621 genuine loss-driven idiosyncratic blow-ups across 48 independent crash-days. On a model-free panel of 2,477 blow-up masters, behavioral drift leads equity for only 9% (216 masters); 69% blow up with no gradual behavioral signal at all, and the overall median lead is negative (-8 days): when conduct moves, it typically lags the equity rather than leading it. A purpose-built three-axis mixture-SPRT detector, pre-registered with its operating point frozen on a disjoint tuning split and read once against a sealed test set, confirms the boundary rather than beating it: it achieves chance-level discrimination (AUC 0.49) at 2% recall. It does post the lowest false-positive rate of any method (0.040, ~1.9x below a leverage tripwire), but at negligible recall that precision is of little practical use. Behavioral early warning is therefore not a viable general safety net for copy-trading blow-ups: most are sudden, a plain equity / drawdown stop fires as early on them, and the residual behavioral signal (gradual over-leveraging) precedes fewer than one blow-up in ten.

title: Ethereum as a Relative Asset-Pricing Problem Across Numeraires: Baseline Evidence from Triangular Pricing Consistency
abstract: This paper studies Ethereum pricing as a relative asset-pricing problem across numeraires. The core restriction is triangular consistency among ETH/USD, ETH/BTC, and BTC/USD: the direct ETH/USD price should equal the synthetic price implied by the other two legs. Using a single-venue Coinbase true-USD triangle at hourly frequency from January 2022 through June 2023, I measure the log wedge between direct and synthetic prices. The wedge is close to zero on average, ADF diagnostics reject the unit-root null, and first-order persistence is low, while its absolute magnitude rises during stress episodes, especially around the FTX collapse. Supporting evidence from a Binance USDT triangle shows a tighter unconditional wedge, suggesting that venue liquidity and arbitrage efficiency also matter for wedge magnitudes in this sample. A Gate.io order-book extension for the Terra/Luna, FTX, and USDC-SVB windows uses hourly bid and ask snapshots to construct executable triangular round trips; across 524 common event-hour observations, no positive after-fee executable breach is observed. The results support a conservative interpretation: Ethereum prices generally align closely with triangular consistency, while stress-state deviations are best understood as relative pricing wedges within market frictions rather than as persistent intrinsic misvaluation.

title: Quantum-Inspired Risk Portfolio Optimization via Exponential Tilting
abstract: Financial portfolio optimization is often framed through mean-variance objectives, yet real profit-and-loss (P&L) scenario distributions are typically discrete and non-Gaussian. To explore realistic P&L distributions, we propose an objective function based on exponential tilting and certainty equivalent under constant absolute risk aversion. We then derive a second-order approximation, recovering a quadratic optimization problem solvable through mixed integer quadratic programming (MIQP) and quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO). Constraints in the QUBO formulation are incorporated via Lagrangian relaxation and slack variable approaches, enabling a direct comparison between classical constrained MIQP and quantum-inspired methods. In order to study how exponential tilting affects mean, standard deviation, and tail-risk measures such as Value at Risk and Conditional Value at Risk, we design an experimental protocol based on scanning a grid of tilt parameters and solving the associated optimization problems. The results on a realistic trading portfolio show how the tilts can be tuned to optimize different risk-return profiles while remaining competitive with those found using other state-of-the-art approaches. Moreover, performance analysis suggests that, even using classical solvers, the QUBO formulation with Lagrangian relaxation scales better than the MIQP approach, providing the best constraint encoding strategy.

title: ParliView: An Experiment-Driven Platform for Parliamentary Transparency
abstract: ParliView is a modular, agentic retrieval-augmented generation platform for querying European Parliament records. It provides a natural language interface for citizens to explore parliamentary debates and activities, and a controlled experimentation environment in which different users can be exposed to systematically varied system behaviours. This enables rigorous study of how design choices, such as verbosity, interactivity, and source presentation, affect user trust, comprehension, and reliance. We describe the system architecture and demonstrate its two core interfaces.

title: Per-Prediction Uncertainty Is Not a Regime Detector: A Detectability Bound and Two-Level Deployment for Cross-Sectional Equity Rankers
abstract: Quantitative finance is increasingly exploring AI-native and agent-mediated allocation: when should an allocator trust a cross-sectional ranker after a silent regime shift that volatility controls miss? Aleatoric scaling addresses market noise; it does not detect epistemic invalidity when ranking structure breaks without a volatility footprint. Building on Sanderink (2026), "When Alpha Breaks" (arXiv:2603.13252), which established per-stock epistemic uncertainty, rank-geometry coupling, and a two-level gate on a walk-forward LightGBM US AI-exposure panel, this paper asks whether per-stock scores can be pooled into portfolio-wide health, or whether strategy-level abstention must condition on realised outcomes. RQ1 (Separation): Does epistemic uncertainty capture model-specific failure distinct from volatility? RQ2 (Decision value): Does a two-level architecture beat baselines on risk-adjusted return and drawdown? RQ3 (Robustness): Do answers hold across regimes, a second ranker, falsification tests, and a universe-readiness gate? We prove a detectability bound: score-only aggregates of per-prediction error predictors cannot beat chance under strict concept shift. CIFAR-10-C confirms the covariate-versus-concept dichotomy (AUROC 0.955 vs 0.500); equity cross-sectional aggregates stay near chance (bad-day AUROC ~0.55) despite valid per-stock signals. The constructive escape is Y-conditioning: partial-horizon RankIC CUSUM (k=5; AUROC 0.796) and a matured-RankIC regime-trust index. Falsification tests and a universe-readiness stop verdict bound allocator claims. Rank-geometry coupling (rho=0.616) forces a discrete tail-cap and strategy gate. Evidence is historical walk-forward simulation on one thematic universe (N<=100) through February 2025; the validated object is reliability architecture, not transportable alpha.

title: Growth versus equity in a stochastic multiplicative wealth model: The cost of redistribution and the emergence of an inequality Laffer curve
abstract: A stochastic multiplicative wealth model with taxation and redistribution is extended to include two channels through which fiscal policy can reduce the economy's average growth rate: productive disincentive (a tax-dependent mean return) and administrative inefficiency (loss of part of the collected revenue). For uniform redistribution, the stationary density of normalized wealth remains an inverse-gamma law, but its shape parameter acquires a richer dependence on the tax rate. The central finding is the emergence of an "inequality Laffer curve": when the disincentive is sufficiently strong, the Gini coefficient first decreases, reaches a minimum at a finite tax rate, and then increases again as taxation intensifies. In the extreme limit the stationary state collapses back to the condensed phase, restoring the oligarchic transition. Both channels also create a direct trade-off between inequality and long-run average wealth, giving rise to a welfare-maximizing tax rate. The two channels are combined into a single analytically tractable model, and all predictions are validated by agent-based simulations. The results show that the qualitative existence of an optimal tax rate is robust whenever the aggregate growth rate responds to fiscal policy, while the inequality Laffer curve is a specific prediction of the productive-disincentive channel.

title: Rethinking Edge-Device Collaborative LLM Inference for 6G AI Edge: An Empirical Evaluation
abstract: 6G ubiquitous intelligence requires generative AI capabilities that far exceed the compute, memory, and energy budgets of mobile terminals. By pushing large language model (LLM) inference to proximate network edge, 6G is shifting to the AI Edge era via four edge-device collaborative paradigms: edge inference, model routing, model split, and speculative decoding. However, existing evaluations are predominantly conducted in idealized datacenter settings, masking the practical challenges posed by heterogeneous hardware and stochastic wireless channels at 6G AI Edge. This article presents the first unified, hardware-in-the-loop empirical study that re-examines these paradigms under practical network conditions. Our stage-wise latency evaluation reveals that network dynamics can inflate Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) by up to 6x, while massive tensor transmissions delay speculative decoding by 246 ms and consume over 150 ms in model split. Because no single paradigm universally dominates across all performance dimensions, we advocate for a context-aware adaptive orchestration framework that dynamically selects collaboration strategies based on network conditions, terminal capabilities, and task semantics, and outline a research roadmap toward 6G AI Edge deployment.

title: Unveiling the Eigenvector 1 Sequence in BZQ Blazars. I. Mg II and Ultraviolet Fe II Emission in the UV Main Sequence
abstract: We investigate the location of flat-spectrum radio quasars confirmed as blazars (BZQ-C), Fanaroff-Riley type II radio-loud (RL) quasars (FRII-Q), and radio non-detected quasars within the ultraviolet (UV) Eigenvector 1 (E1) plane defined by the Mg II line width (FWHM Mg II) and the UV Fe II strength (RFeUV). This represents the first systematic comparison of BZQ blazars with their proposed parent population in the UV E1 framework. To minimize selection biases, we construct statistically representative control subsamples and perform matched-subsample analyses in redshift and Mg II luminosity. Population differences are assessed using one- and two-dimensional non-parametric tests, including the Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Anderson-Darling, Mann-Whitney U, and Fasano-Franceschini statistics. We find that the three AGN populations occupy statistically distinct regions of the UV E1 plane. The dominant separation is driven by FWHM Mg II, with BZQ blazars systematically exhibiting narrower line profiles than FRII-Q quasars, while radio non-detected quasars lie between both populations. In contrast, RFeUV provides only limited discrimination between the RL subclasses, although it separates radio-loud from radio non-detected quasars at the population level. The observed ordering demonstrates that the UV E1 plane preserves the physical sequence expected from RL AGN unification. Inclination-dependent projection provides a natural first-order explanation for the Mg II line-width ordering. Additional differences in intrinsic BLR structure or accretion properties may contribute to the observed distributions, although the present analysis does not allow these effects to be separated independently from orientation.

title: Participant-Independent Validation of Smartphone Video and Wearable Inertial Sensing for Coach-Rated Running-Form Classification
abstract: Automated running-form assessment could make technique feedback more accessible outside professional coaching and laboratory settings. We evaluated a low-cost pipeline combining side-view smartphone video with wearable inertial measurement unit (IMU) acceleration for coach-rated running-form classification. The dataset comprised 294 labeled recordings from 20 runners and 1,555 windows across four cues: landing position, suspension, triple extension, and upper-body posture. The primary analysis used 100 repeated four-runner holdout splits, recording-level aggregation of window predictions, and LightGBM models with hyperparameters fixed from prior modality-specific searches. Video-only LightGBM achieved mean macro F1 of 0.310, versus 0.168 for a majority-class baseline. Adding IMU features reduced macro F1 to 0.267, a paired mean difference of -0.043. Robustness analysis with Logistic Regression, Linear SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM found that video-only models had higher mean performance than the majority baseline, whereas fusion effects depended on model family: Linear SVM showed a small positive effect, Logistic Regression was approximately neutral, and tree-based models showed lower performance with fusion. These results indicate a modest participant-independent signal in smartphone pose features. However, apparent IMU-fusion gains depended strongly on validation design, model family, and target category. The gap between recording-level and participant-independent performance underscores the need for runner-holdout evaluation and suggests that simple feature-level fusion does not reliably generalize to unseen runners.

title: MemVanta: Memory-Efficient CPU Inference for Quantized GGUF Language Models
abstract: Deploying large language models on commodity CPUs is often constrained not only by computational throughput but also by the resident memory required to execute quantized models within fixed system budgets. We present MemVanta, an experimental C++20 inference runtime for quantized GGUF language models that treats memory residency as a first-class systems objective. MemVanta combines memory-mapped model access, bounded tensor caching, quantized execution paths, paged key-value state, and explicit memory-pressure validation. We evaluate MemVanta against a pinned llama.cpp baseline using the same OpenLLaMA 7B v2 Q4_0 GGUF under CPU-only execution. Across five measured runs following warm-up, MemVanta records a peak resident set size of 3,983,412 KiB compared with 7,586,960 KiB for llama.cpp, corresponding to a 47.50 percent reduction in peak RSS. This memory reduction involves a substantial throughput trade-off: MemVanta achieves 3.15 +/- 0.04 tokens/s for prompt processing and 1.52 +/- 0.02 tokens/s for token generation, compared with 45.82 +/- 0.96 and 7.76 +/- 0.09 tokens/s, respectively, for llama.cpp. In a separate Linux cgroup-v2 experiment with swap disabled, MemVanta completes execution at a tested 3584 MiB memory ceiling, while llama.cpp is OOM-killed at that ceiling and first succeeds at the tested 3840 MiB level. These results position MemVanta as a memory-efficiency research prototype rather than a throughput competitor. We analyze the architectural mechanisms underlying this trade-off and discuss reproducibility, correctness, limitations, and opportunities for memory-constrained CPU and edge inference.

title: Faculty Experience with Generative AI Integration into the Teaching and Learning Process
abstract: This study was conducted to enhance our knowledge and understanding of the lived experiences of faculty regarding generative artificial intelligence (AI) in teaching and learning within the English and Communication Program at the American University of Armenia. This phenomenological qualitative research study used face-to-face, in-depth, open-ended interviews with five faculty members from the program. Faculty expressed different levels of conflict, voicing both positive and negative issues and concerns regarding their experiences with generative AI in the teaching and learning process. Five categories and 11 themes emerged from the analysis of these interviews, including concerns about academic integrity and student learning, as well as a lack of faculty AI training, understanding, and experience. Emergent themes indicated that faculty need additional support, including training and leadership guidance, in order to better understand the importance and benefits of effective AI utilization and AI literacy development. Faculty lacked sufficient experience with and understanding of generative AI capabilities and ongoing developments. Overall, faculty perceptions and attitudes toward generative AI within teaching and learning can be characterized as a mix of reservation and optimism.

title: Why High-Spin Prograde MAD States Are Not Realized for AGN in Nature: Consequences for AGN Phenomenology
abstract: Quasar-like and other bright active galactic nuclei are typically radio quiet despite strong evidence that many host rapidly spinning black holes. In contrast, general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations show that high-spin prograde black holes in magnetically arrested disk (MAD) states produce the most powerful relativistic jets. We show that these results are not in conflict but instead correspond to physically distinct and mutually limiting evolutionary pathways. If accretion proceeds through radiatively efficient thin disks, then as the innermost stable circular orbit decreases with increasing prograde spin, radiative output and radiation pressure rise sharply, driving strong disk winds that remove the conditions required for effective jet formation. In this branch, high-spin prograde systems are therefore expected to be jet-suppressed. Alternatively, if accretion transitions to radiatively inefficient flows capable of producing MAD states, then the spin-up to near-maximal prograde rotation proceeds on timescales that exceed the age of the universe for the relevant systems, preventing the realization of the extreme high-spin prograde MAD configurations explored in GRMHD simulations. Within this framework, powerful jets need only be produced efficiently in counterrotating systems, not maximized there, preserving the time-dependent spin evolution central to the counterrotation versus corotation paradigm of Garofalo et al. (2010). We thus reconcile GRMHD results with observations and provide a unified interpretation of the radio-loud/radio-quiet dichotomy and the cosmic evolution of powerful radio sources.

title: Construct Validity of AI-Administered Cognitive Assessment: Psychometric Validation of a Nine-Dimension Process-Oriented Evaluation Instrument
abstract: Process-oriented evaluation of large language models requires psychometrically defensible instruments, yet the measurement tools used in AI cognitive assessment have received little formal validation. This paper reports the construct validation of a 54-item, nine-dimension instrument operationalizing the Multi-Dimensional Assessment for AI Cognition framework through a repeated six-component AI-administered adjudication architecture. The validation program combined conceptual audit, schema-integrity testing, confirmatory factor analysis, and targeted revision across multiple versions, each validated on a fresh cohort of roughly 1,800 to 2,200 scenario-response pairs. The best current version (v4.7, n = 1,774) achieves acceptable to good psychometric properties across all nine dimensions. All meet internal consistency thresholds, with Cronbach's alpha from 0.770 to 0.922. Confirmatory factor analysis shows four dimensions at good fit and four at acceptable fit, with 53 of 54 items loading at or above 0.40 on their parent factor. Schema enforcement yields perfect structural integrity, confirming the six-component architecture as stable. One item, Hallucination Control Q6, remains below threshold but improved materially under v4.7's evidential calibration redesign, surpassing prior versions without reaching target. The instrument is publishable as a largely validated assessment with one sub-threshold component and a deferred tools-enabled comparison reserved for future work. The program also yields a five-category taxonomy of item-level failure modes, including ceiling and floor compression, construct drift, proxy-formula failure, condition confounding, and fundamental mismatch, that may generalize to other AI evaluation contexts.

title: Social-Qwen: From Individual Nonverbal Cues and Emotion to Multiparty Social Dynamics Understanding with Instruction Tuning
abstract: Effective participation in multiparty scenarios requires robots to move beyond individual toward understanding group-level social dynamics, which are inherently complex due to the interplay of nonverbal cues, internal states, and interaction context. Existing approaches often rely on end-to-end deterministic models, while recent state-of-the-art methods such as large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) address this issue to some extent but remain limited by their size and computational cost for real-time applications. Moreover, both approaches are constrained by the scarcity of multiparty interaction data and annotations, which describe how individual nonverbal cues and emotional states contribute to social dynamics which describe collective outcomes such as group engagement. We hypothesize that explicitly modeling individual-level states is essential for accurate group-level understanding. To this end, we present Social-Qwen, a two-stage framework that first analyzes each participant's nonverbal cues and emotions, then infers group-level engagement using instruction-tuned representations. To mitigate the lack of individual annotations in group datasets, we employ knowledge distillation to transfer supervision signals. Experiments on the OUC-CGE dataset show that Social-Qwen significantly outperforms prior end-to-end baselines and achieves state-of-the-art performance in group engagement analysis, demonstrating the promise of instruction tuning for scalable social intelligence in robots. We further evaluate robustness by testing generalization to (1) an in-house dataset spanning multiple social activities and (2) estimating other social dynamics such as group harmony. Results suggest consistent performance, highlighting Social-Qwen as a promising approach toward real-time social intelligence for intelligent agents.

title: Environmental Interaction: Recognizing Capability within Everyday Actions
abstract: Systems designed to support everyday capability consistently ask people to do something additional: track activity, follow programmes. For those who need such support most, this ask is often too high. We propose a different approach: environmental interaction. Through four probe deployments with older adults we show that everyday actions are themselves generative sites for interaction design, and that engagement depends less on sensing and guidance than on revealing in that action that it is polymorphic. A chair sit-stand is also a box squat; a door pull also a row. Each time participants encountered this second frame, the response was surprise, delight, and "I can do that!" The paper contributes environmental interaction as a design space, a serial probe methodology, and empirically grounded design considerations - including invitation over instruction, recognition before extension, and interaction as presence - centered on recognition as a generative design challenge.

title: Scrub Data: A Framework for Reproducible Data Curation with AI Coding Agents
abstract: Data curation---the process of collecting, cleaning, and joining raw datasets for unified analysis---is a time-consuming yet crucial part of any data science project. With the emergence of powerful agentic coding tools, it is tempting to "vibe curate"---i.e., to prompt AI agents to perform data curation operations and blindly trust their outputs in order to finish work more quickly. However, this can exacerbate two key challenges that already plague manual data curation workflows: reproducibility---the ability to trace the exact set of modifications applied to raw datasets---and verifiability---the ability to audit changes and confirm that data is processed properly. To address these issues, we introduce Scrub Data, a framework that enables the use of AI agents in data curation workflows while transparently maintaining both reproducibility and verifiability. The framework involves an interactive data curation loop between a user and an AI agent, backed by a data provenance graph that tracks and versions all dataset updates. The data graph requires that all updates are formatted as self-contained executable steps, allowing any version of a dataset to be reconstructed from raw data by playing forward the transformations stored in the graph. This workflow takes place within a lightweight web application that is designed to be modified by users and agents in real-time to create custom visualization tools for identifying data curation needs and verifying outcomes. We demonstrate the usefulness of the framework with a real data curation use case from animal movement ecology. Starting with 89M raw GPS coordinates, we use the framework to curate a benchmark dataset of 2.5M coordinates to be used for machine learning or statistical analysis. The framework is available for use and extension at https://github.com/justinkay/scrubdata.

title: Constellations of Colour: Mapping Semantic Neighbourhoods in CLIP
abstract: How do vision-language models organise the cultural and perceptual dimensions of colour language? This pictorial presents a research-through-design visualisation of colour semantics in CLIP, a pretrained vision-language model. A dataset of 2,500 named colours is embedded with CLIP's text encoder, projected to a 2D map, and connected via a thresholded minimum spanning tree to create disjoint "constellations" of related colour terms. The resulting maps offer a model for navigating the semantic and perceptual relationships between colour terms. The visualisations reveal gradients along familiar axes (hue, lightness, chroma), as well as semantic neighbourhoods, including botanical language (hyacinth, cornflower, tulip), fictional references ("Robin Hood green", "warlock purple"), and food (butterscotch, toast, toffee). These visualisations give designers and creatives a map for exploring colour linguistically and building palettes by semantic association, pointing towards interpretable, artist-facing colour tools derived from foundation models.

title: Towards Objective Estimation of Physical Functioning Status in Breast-Cancer Patients using Real-World Data
abstract: Breast cancer is the most common invasive cancer in women, accounting for about one third of cancer cases. As with all cancers, its treatment may introduce side-effects like fatigue and reduced physical functioning, leading to a downward spiral of subsequent issues and severely affecting patient quality of life. On the positive side, physical functioning can be improved via personalized targeted interventions, tailored to the particularities of each case. However, continuous and objective monitoring of patients is a difficult task, owing to the limited clinical resources and the lack of appropriate tools. In this paper, we introduce a methodology for objectively estimating the physical functioning status of breast cancer patients from wearable smartwatch data. We show that features derived from longitudinal walking and heart rate measurements correlate significantly with phys- ical functioning scores of established patient-reported outcome measures. In doing so, our work takes a first step towards developing novel validated digital biomarkers for estimating physical functioning in breast cancer patients, thus reducing the need for self-reported measures and costly clinical evaluations.

title: Measuring Human Resilience to Unreliable AI Assistance: A Stress-Test Framework for Human-AI Interaction
abstract: As AI increasingly mediates human decisions, users must remain effective not only when assistance works as expected but also when its quality deteriorates. Human--AI research has developed rich measures of trust, reliance, and calibration, while human--autonomy research has examined resilience at the team and system levels. A missing measurement level is the human decision maker: how much task function is preserved or recovered when AI advice becomes unreliable? We introduce the Resilience Stress Test, a challenge-conditioned HCI framework that measures performance relative to a prechallenge baseline and summarizes functional loss and recovery. Four construct-validation tests draw on five public human--AI studies comprising 1,074 analytic participants. A controlled decline in AI quality produced sharp degradation followed by partial adaptation; misleading advice reduced performance in art and dermatology; baseline adjustment substantially attenuated the apparent complexity gradient in trip planning; and a logical-reasoning tutorial improved self-assessment calibration while challenged performance remained stable. The framework makes human resilience to unreliable AI operational as a functional outcome distinct from competence, calibration, and reliance, and provides a prospective protocol for comparing interfaces under reproducible AI reliability stress.

title: The Agent Is Not Your Driver: Clarifying the Implied Capabilities of In-Vehicle Anthropomorphic Agents
abstract: This position paper considers how the gap between an anthropomorphic agent in an autonomous vehicle and the automated driving system of the vehicle can create psychological risks if the agent inaccurately presents itself as integrated into the driving system. This gap is under-explored both because of the evolving nature of these agents and because of study limitations in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) research. Nevertheless, this gap may cause the agent to misrepresent itself as more knowledgeable about the car than it is, creating a risk of dependence and, in the worst case, betrayal if the occupant feels that the agent has misled them. This paper proposes a research agenda for future work to understand the psychological risk that exists in the gap between agents and driving systems and to narrow this gap in a manner aligned with safety assurance. As these agents evolve to hold greater capabilities and increased anthropomorphism, future research must investigate risks which may emerge from richer interaction with them. The impact of how an agent presents itself and its knowledge becomes greater.

title: Psychological State Monitoring Methods Based on Multimodal Emotion Recognition
abstract: The computer-Based Multimodal Emotion Recognition System needs to increase the accuracy and reliability of psychological state monitoring. A hierarchical framework was proposed in this paper to integrate facial images, speech signals and other physiological indicators of emotion in time and space for more complete analysis of human emotions. Synchronously sample data streams from webcams, microphones and wearable sensors, and then preprocess and extract features specific to each type of data. A high-end fusion architecture is adopted to combine early- and late-fusion methods and thus robustly integrate cross-modal information. Experimental validation in a real-world stress-response dataset showed good performance. The overall recognition accuracy and mean F1-score of the fused multimodal system are both about 91% and 0.88, respectively, which are superior to the best unimodal approach (face, 88% accuracy and F1-score 0.88). Temporal analysis shows that the groups for stress tracking are not uniformly adapted and resilient, and ablation experiments have determined which modules contribute significantly to the stability of the system. According to all kinds of quantitative evaluations of precision, recall, accuracy and F1 scores, the proposed method shows good balance and is practical and generally applicable. The research has provided an engineering-feasible, data-driven solution for precise emotion inference and offered methodological support for intelligent mental health assessment and human-centered system design.

title: Evaluating the Participation of Proactive Scouting Agents in Real-time Human Team Meetings
abstract: An open research question is whether the addition of conversational AI agents to real-time discussions among human teams enhances group performance. This study tested the value of adding proactive scouting agents to teams engaged in collaborative forecasting tasks. These agents were designed to (i) monitor the groupwise discussion in real-time, (ii) identify critical information gaps in the group deliberation, (iii) autonomously find and retrieve relevant information, and (iv) express the acquired content into the conversation using emulated groupwise human etiquette. In a controlled set of trials, small human teams of 4 or 5 members were tasked with collaboratively predicting the outcome of 34 Major League Baseball (MLB) games, either by forecasting the winning team or by predicting the total number of runs scored. In half the trials, the groups were assisted by proactive scouting agents. The other half were human-only deliberations. When tasked with predicting the winning team, the addition of proactive scouting agents to the group discussion significantly increased forecasting accuracy, reducing the predictive mean-absolute error by 25% (p=0.006) and improving raw predictive accuracy from 60.0% to 76.4% (p=0.050). When predicting the total number of runs scored across both teams, the addition of proactive scouting agents yielded no statistical change in group performance. It should be noted that the human participants in this study were significantly worse at predicting the number of runs scored. This may have led to random outcomes in those forecasting trials. Still, the results of this study demonstrate that deploying proactive scouting agents can significantly boost forecasting accuracy during real-time team deliberations when participants possess baseline forecasting skill.

title: Beyond Code and Pixels: Co-Generating Editable and Visually Rich Presentations
abstract: Generating PPTX presentations is a structured task that requires semantic planning, visual composition, precise layout, and editability, motivating collaboration among specialized agents. However, programmatic methods offer editability but often produce rigid designs, while image-based methods provide visual richness but flatten content into difficult-to-edit pixels. A hybrid system can combine these strengths, but must coordinate interdependent decisions across content, layout, and appearance. To address this challenge, we propose SlidesWeaver, a hybrid multi-agent system that coordinates language and vision agents through shared deck- and slide-level states. Specifically, it uses staged multimodal commitment, diffusion-based composition planning, and two generation schedules for different priorities between composition freedom and accurate text preservation, while preserving native text and geometry. Across 1,728 generations spanning 24 system-model configurations, SlidesWeaver achieves consistently superior overall quality across all evaluated dimensions while maintaining structural control, editability, and practical generation efficiency.

title: Neurosymbolic Human-AI Collaboration: Foundations, Conceptual Framework, and Applications
abstract: The growing adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across workplaces and industries, ranging from manufacturing plants to healthcare facilities, has paved the way to the design of systems in which humans and AI collaborate on shared tasks. The first developments of Human-AI Collaboration (HAIC) were driven by advances in Machine Learning (ML), which enabled the automation of numerous tasks, including large-scale data processing, image analysis, and speech recognition. However, ML automation have proven insufficient for certain applications due to methodological, safety, and ethical concerns. In such cases, researchers argue for integrating human expertise into operational workflows to improve performance, relying on the complementary skill sets of humans and AI. Despite long-standing research, the field of HAIC has not yet reached full maturity, largely due to the intrinsic difficulty of ensuring a seamless communication between humans and AI. This challenge is partially addressed by Explainable AI methods, which aim to make internal model reasoning more transparent through human-understandable explanations. Recognizing the need for a shared interface between humans and AI in collaborative settings, we propose a novel conceptual framework, NeSy-HAIC, that leverages Neurosymbolic AI (NeSy AI) to bridge the semantic gap between machine representations and human-understandable symbolic concepts. The framework builds on current research in NeSy AI and HAIC, supports multiple interaction paradigms, including Human-In-The-Loop and Human-On-The-Loop, and is characterized through its enabling methodologies and two illustrative use cases in semi-autonomous driving and security alert prioritization. We argue that the integration of data-driven learning and symbolic reasoning can substantially enhance human-AI interaction and mitigate limitations of collaborative systems.

title: Social sycophancy differs across access modes of large language models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can display sycophancy, a tendency to excessively praise, agree with, or validate a user. Existing studies have tested LLMs for sycophancy primarily through application programming interfaces (APIs) rather than the consumer user interfaces (UIs) through which the public commonly interacts with LLMs. Access mode (API vs. UI) may affect observed sycophancy rates. However, it remains unknown to what extent prominent models show API-UI differences in social sycophancy, which includes behaviors potentially more likely in UIs (e.g., softening warranted criticism). We tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek through both APIs and UIs on four dimensions of social sycophancy. Across models, UI access was generally associated with greater social sycophancy, with odds ratios up to 7.56 (95% CI [6.22, 9.20]). However, UI-API differences varied significantly across models for all sycophancy dimensions, including a pronounced reversal for DeepSeek moral sycophancy (43% UI vs. 82.3% API). Overall, our results suggest that API-based LLM evaluations may underestimate the prevalence of sycophancy in corresponding consumer-facing systems, making access conditions consequential for the external validity of LLM evaluation. To facilitate research on access-mode effects, we release 57,000 model responses and SycoUI, a browser-automation pipeline for standardized cross-interface LLM evaluation.

title: Do as I Say, Not as You Do: Assessing Public Versus Practitioner Perspectives on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and Language Technologies
abstract: With the public awareness of artificial intelligence (AI) applications such as large language models (LLMs) and generative text-to-video models reaching unprecedented levels, there is an increasing need to reconcile the perspectives held by informed practitioners, who research and develop these technologies, with the interests and opinions of the general public, who constitute the majority of people impacted by technological developments. In this work, we survey practitioners (i.e., academics and industry professionals) alongside members of the general public on perspectives relating to pertinent areas of artificial intelligence, including perceived benefit and risk, the ability for models to achieve consciousness and output art, and the use of copyright protected material for model training. Alongside comparisons of diverse perspectives on these topics, we additionally contextualise the findings with a discussion of relevant literature that supports and refutes the myriad observed stances.

title: Spectral evolution and secular shift of the Z source GX 340+0: an interpretation in the spreading layer paradigm
abstract: We present a comprehensive spectral and timing study of the bright neutron star low-mass X-ray binary and Z source, GX 340+0, using broadband X-ray observations with AstroSat in 2020 and 2024, focusing on the evolution of physical parameters along the Z track and the origin of secular shifts of this track across different epochs. The spectra are consistently described by the same model, comprising blackbody emission from a spreading boundary layer near the neutron star surface, an accretion disk, and a Comptonizing corona. We observe a significant decrease in the blackbody temperature from ~1.2 keV on the horizontal branch (HB) to ~1.0 keV on the normal branch (NB), which likely contributes to the harder spectra on the HB and softer spectra on the NB. At the same time, the blackbody normalization varies substantially from ~440-860, indicating changes in the effective emitting area. Within the spreading layer framework, this evolution reflects changes in the extent of theradiating layer, while the large absolute normalization values suggest an additional contribution from the boundary layer. We also detect variations in the absorption column density, suggesting structural changes in the inner accretion disk, possibly linked to radiation driven puffing-up. The Comptonized flux shows a branch-dependent behavior, remaining relatively stable along the HB but decreasing along the NB. We interpret these results within a unified framework where the boundary layer, corona, and inner disk evolve coherently with accretion rate, explaining both the Z-track behavior and its secular shifts.

title: Misalignment Between Educators' Testing and End Users' Behavior: What 17,000+ Chatbot Messages Reveal About AI Literacy Training for Teachers
abstract: AI literacy training for educators is expanding rapidly, but its effectiveness rests largely on self-report, knowledge tests, or interviews, revealing little about whether learning carries into practice or affects students and colleagues who use what educators build. We implemented AI for Learning, an asynchronous online course that trained 87 higher-education educators to recognize AI's capabilities, limitations, and ethics; apply prompt engineering; and evaluate AI outputs. Its central assignment asked educators to build, test, and voluntarily deploy chatbots for their practice on an educational chatbot authoring platform. Using LLM-assisted qualitative coding validated against human annotation, we analyzed the resulting 214 chatbots and their builder-bot, peer-bot, and end user-bot conversations, 17,000+ messages spanning 1.5 years. Educators 1) specified what bots should do more often than what they should not; 2) adopted templated prompt components but rarely untemplated strategies; and 3) tested routine use but seldom iterated, leaving 74% of end users' adversarial use untested. Still, 36 bots (17%) reached end users and 63 (29%) were adopted by peers. We contribute two successes and two lessons spanning the lifecycle of educator AI literacy training.

title: Cultural and Regional Influences on Global AI Apprehension
abstract: The discussion surrounding artificial intelligence (AI) is primarily influenced by Western viewpoints, often neglecting the cultural, regional, and socio-political factors that affect global perceptions of AI. This study examines how these factors shape AI apprehension in various regions, including Africa, Asia, Latin America, and the Middle East. A qualitative literature review was conducted, analyzing peer-reviewed articles, policy reports, and gray literature from multiple regions. The study used a comparative approach to assess the cultural, political, and economic contexts shaping AI perceptions. It found significant regional differences in AI concerns: Western countries emphasize privacy, surveillance, and ethics, while regions like Africa and Asia focus on technological dependency, state control, and socio-economic issues, such as job displacement. Brazil and Argentina were noted for their AI governance models, while South Africa and Kenya leverage AI to tackle socio-economic challenges. The findings underscore the need for inclusive AI governance frameworks that respect diverse local contexts and values. These frameworks would contribute to a better understanding of AI's global impact and inform future policy development.

title: When Modalities (Dis)Agree: How Decomposing Multi-Modal AI Advice Shapes Appropriate Reliance
abstract: Multi-modal AI systems integrate diverse data streams into unified advices, but this fusion conceals how individual modalities contribute to the final output. Consequently, decision-makers cannot observe whether underlying sources aligned or contradicted one another when assessing the provided advice. To test whether revealing this structure supports appropriate reliance, we conducted a pre-registered experiment (N = 240) in which participants evaluated used-car prices with multi-modal AI support. In a 2x2 between-subjects design, we varied the disclosure of modality-level outputs and natural-language explanations, crossed with within-subjects modality agreement. Revealing modality-level outputs increased reliance, while explanations improved decision accuracy independently. However, this occurred only when modalities agreed: visible consensus acted as a persuasive cue that generally amplified adherence, rather than helping participants override errors under conflict. Thus, decomposing multi-modal advice can make AI advice more persuasive without making errors easier to detect.

title: Monte Carlo Power Analysis for Small-System A/B Trials: Detecting Differences in Newsletter Engagement
abstract: Good experimental practice and predicting the scientific usefulness of an experiment or experimental platform require power analysis: estimating, *a priori*, how likely the experiment is to detect the intended effect if indeed it exists. While simple experimental designs admit well-understood power analysis methods, more sophisticated experimental designs and settings often require bespoke techniques to avoid either over- or under-estimating experimental power. We present the Monte Carlo method we use to estimate the power of experiments intended to increase user engagement with personalized e-mail newsletters of recommended news articles.

title: Light Shining Through the Moon: A Lunar-Occultation Helioscope for Solar Axions
abstract: We propose a lunar-occultation helioscope in which the Moon suppresses the direct solar x-ray beam before solar axions enter the terrestrial magnetosphere, where they may reconvert into keV photons. We evaluate the conversion with a geomagnetic model combining the IGRF-14 internal contribution and the Tsyganenko T89 external magnetospheric contribution, retaining the two signed transverse components in the oscillation amplitude. As an explicit realizability test, we propagate a circular near-600-km polar orbit through the 12 August 2026 occultation. A $4'$-radius region around the solar center remains lunar occulted for about $470$ s while the sunward line of sight stays clear of the Earth; the coherent magnetic lever arm spans $69.1$--$96.4~\mathrm{T\,m}$ with $\mathcal I_{B,\mathrm{rms}}=76.9~\mathrm{T\,m}$.
